title: Jesse Minter does not address Lamar Jackson's injury, says he'll keep conversations with QB private
summary: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026.
full_text: Over the weekend, reporting emerged that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he intends to return to play in 2026. Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, however, was not inclined to give any update on the star QB in his Monday press conference. Jackson is reportedly out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb. He is currently on injured reserve. Minter was asked what the chance is that Jackson will be able to return this season. “You know, I’m going to keep most of the conversations between Lamar and I between Lamar and I ,” Minter said. “Again, just like before, it’s a guy when you’re dealing with something, that no one wants to be on the field more. He’s probably going to do everything he can to put himself in position [to play]. But I’ll leave it at that.” Minter also did not say whether or not Jackson requires or already has had surgery. “I’m going to keep all that stuff between me and him,” Minter said. Does that mean the public won’t know the nature of Jackson’s injury and if he can return? “You may know, but that’ll come from him,” Minter said. There was one more follow-up in the press conference, with Minter being asked if it’s accurate to say Jackson’s thumb was fractured and dislocated. Minter chuckled before saying, “Again, that is specifics. I’ll keep it between me and him.” Jackson has technically started five games this season. But he played just a half against Tennessee and threw only one pass against Buffalo before having to exit due to injury. Jacoby Brissett is now set to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback with Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Aaron Glenn on giving up defensive play-calling: I'm looking at everything
summary: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn took over as the team's defensive play-caller this season and things got off to a pretty good start in September.
full_text: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn took over as the team's defensive play-caller this season and things got off to a pretty good start in September. The Jets only allowed 30 points over the first two weeks of the season, but they've allowed 193 in the last seven games. That includes Sunday's 35-point performance by the Chiefs and the Jets have only won one of those seven contests to drop to 2-7 on the season. On Monday, Glenn was asked at a press conference if he would consider handing off the play-calling role to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in the second half of the season. "Well, I would say this, and listen, we have not played really good defense the last couple of weeks, and I am very aware of that," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "But again, there's been evidence of us playing really good defense throughout this season and listen, I will never say never to anything, but I do know this: I'm looking at everything and I'm looking of ways of us to improve, and whatever that is for us to get better, you can best believe I'll make those changes. And I think I've done that throughout my career to be able to do that is I'm not afraid to make a change. I'm not saying that is going to be the change, but I'm looking at everything." Given the Jets' record, it's hard to imagine too many little tweaks that are going to lead to a major change in circumstances for the team. It's also hard to imagine Glenn doing much to improve his chances of sticking around after a 5-21 start to his tenure, but we'll see if anything looks different when the Jets face the Bills at home in Week 10.
author: Josh Alper

title: Andy Reid on Harrison Butker: I haven’t made any decisions yet
summary: The Chiefs have a clear and obvious kicking problem.
full_text: ''' The Chiefs have a clear and obvious kicking problem. Harrison Butker officially missed one more field goal on Sunday, sailing a 51-yard attempt wide right. But everyone also saw him miss from 56 a snap before — a play that didn't count because of a Jets penalty. Butker has now missed 17 kicks over the last two seasons, which is a league-high. Kansas City has Justin Tucker on its practice squad, and he would ostensibly be the next man up. But in his Monday news conference, Reid told reporters that he wasn't ready to commit to any changes at kicker. "With Butker, I haven’t made any decisions yet," Reid said. "I’m going to evaluate everything and go forward from there. Again, I haven’t decided on reps during practice, I haven’t done any of that right now. Just going through it, evaluating. And we’ll go from there." Butker has made just 12-of-19 field goals so far this season. He’s also missed an extra point. We’ll see if Reid has more to say about his kicker situation when the Chiefs start their practice week on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Lions agree to acquire S Andre Cisco from Jets
summary: Detroit is bringing in some secondary help.
full_text: ''' Detroit is bringing in some secondary help. The Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports. Cisco, 26, is in the final season of his contract. Cisco has appeared in nine games with four starts this year, recording 23 total tackles with two tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble, and a pass defensed. A third-round pick in the 2021 draft, Cisco played his first four seasons with the Jaguars. In 80 career games with 59 starts, he’s tallied eight interceptions, 26 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, and six tackles for loss. With the trade, Cisco is now in line to potentially play 18 games this season. The Lions had their bye in Week 6 and the Jets are not slated to have theirs until Week 13.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Zac Taylor: Bengals are good where we are, expect nothing at the trade deadline
summary: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor says nothing is happening in Cincinnati at the NFL trade deadline.
full_text: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor says nothing is happening in Cincinnati at the NFL trade deadline. Asked today what he expects to happen between now and tomorrow at 4 p.m., Taylor said he doesn't expect anything to happen. "Nothing. That's a bunch for everybody to talk about, but we're good," Taylor said. Asked by another reporter whether there are positions he thinks his team still needs help at, Taylor said he likes the roster he has. "No, I feel good about where we're at," Taylor said. The Bengals are 6-2 and in the thick of the AFC playoff race, and Taylor has his team right where he wants to be.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bills-Vikings game carries major significance for both teams
summary: The Bills and Vikings have identical 0-4 records in the Super Bowl.
full_text: ' The Bills and Vikings have identical 0-4 records in the Super Bowl. They enter Monday night's game with identical 6-1 records. And the stakes are very high for both teams. For Buffalo, which hopes to force the January road to SoFi Stadium through the open-air new venue in Western New York, it's important to maintain distance between the 6-2 Jaguars and 7-2 Broncos. (The division is looking like the Bills' to lose, with the Patriots now at 5-4.) For Minnesota, their status as the last unbeaten team in the NFL could dissolve to being the last team out of the NFC playoff picture. The NFC North, which now has a 20-3 record outside the division, has the Vikings at 6-1, the Lions at 6-2, the Bears at 6-2, and the Packers at 6-3. (Combined, they've lost as many games as the 0-8 Chargers.) Last week, when the Vikings picked up their first loss of the season, the Lions, Bears, and Packers won. This week, the Lions, Bears, and Packers have won. A loss by the Vikings would conclude a two-week window in which the Vikings are 0-2, and the rest of the division is 6-0. It gets worse. The 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams each won on Sunday. In the end, five playoff berths will go to the four teams of the NFC North and top three teams of the NFC West. Two of those teams will be left out. And, frankly, the Vikings seem destined to be one of them. Even with a 6-2 record, if they lose to the Bills. Because even though the defense is good enough to win a Super Bowl, the offense isn't good enough to win a playoff game. It could be just bad enough to keep the team from making the playoffs. It was one thing for the Vikings' defense to not gripe when the end result of each game was victory. If the second game of a four-week gauntlet doesn't go Minnesota's way (the Packers and 49ers are up next), things could get even more awkward in the locker room. The problem is that, despite plenty of speculation and chatter, the Vikings don't seem to be inclined to pull the cord on the emergency option of trading for Daniel Jones or Kirk Cousins. The organization's chronic "just good enough is just good enough" vibe remains palpable. Which means it all comes down to Carson Wentz against the Bills. Could Minnesota win? When Buffalo last visited Minnesota in 2018, the Vikings entered the game as 17-point favorites. The Bills, fueled by then-rookie quarterback Josh Allen throwing for 196 yards and a touchdown and rushing for 39 yards and two touchdowns (including a hurdle over linebacker Anthony Barr ), won the game easily, 27-6. (Last week, Allen said the leap over a linebacker was the moment he realized " I do belong here .") Four years ago, the Bills were favored by 6.5 points over the Vikings. Minnesota won a crazy game in overtime, 33-30, with Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson making the catch of the century on a fourth-down, game-on-the-line play. Tonight, in many respects, the season is on the line for the Vikings. Especially if they won't be trying to upgrade the most important position on the team, which in recent weeks has been the weakest on the roster.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kevin Stefanski on Jessie Bates trade: Falcons aren't punting on the season
summary: The Falcons traded veteran safety Jessie Bates to the Jaguars today, which some might see as a sign that the Falcons don't see themselves as contenders and are looking ahead at 2027.
full_text: The Falcons traded veteran safety Jessie Bates to the Jaguars today, which some might see as a sign that the Falcons don't see themselves as contenders and are looking ahead at 2027. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski says that's not the case. Stefanski did acknowledge that the Falcons are building for the future, but he also noted that in the NFC South, Atlanta remains very much in contention at 3-6. "You guys know how I feel about Jessie the person, Jessie the player," Stefanski told reporters. "But at the same time, this is football, where sometimes you have one foot in the short term, one foot in the long term. There's things like this that make your team better in the long run. Draft picks are the life blood of an organization. That's something we believe in. Stefanski said he wants fans to know that they still are going to compete to win the NFC South. "Our fans are smart enough to know that in no way, shape or form would we punt on this season. We have three wins, just like the rest of our division. Obviously not where we want to be, we want to play better, but we're in the thick of this thing and we trust in the guys we have," Stefanski said. The Falcons might not be punting on the season, but they are deciding to move on from a player who can help them this season and get draft picks for future seasons. The Falcons still might win the worst division in football, but today's trade is not the trade pf a team that thinks it's a Super Bowl contender this year.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Greg Olsen accuses media of putting "words in my mouth" about Malik Nabers
summary: After Sunday's win over the Eagles, Giants receiver Malik Nabers had some things to say about things Fox's Greg Olsen had to say about Nabers during the game.
full_text: '' After Sunday's win over the Eagles, Giants receiver Malik Nabers had some things to say about things Fox's Greg Olsen had to say about Nabers during the game. On Monday, Olsen had some things to say about how the New York Post and USA Today characterized the things he said. Olsen accused those publications of making up quotes and putting "worlds [sic] in my mouth." In order to avoid any doubt about what Olsen (and others on the Fox broadcast) said — and didn't say — about Nabers, we went to the video (and audio). Early in the fourth quarter of the Giants-Eagles game, after Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a pass behind an open Nabers who was running right to left, the Fox cameras showed Nabers waving an arm in apparent frustration. Said Fox's Joe Davis, regarding Nabers: "His body language has been terrible today." "It's just not good," Olsen said. Olsen revisited the subject a little bit later. “You brought up Malik Nabers," Olsen said, "and you never know exactly what’s being said. It’s easy for us to sit here and interpret body language. When we asked [offensive coordinator] Matt Nagy about him, he said, ‘Listen, he’s very vocal. When he didn’t get the ball to start the year, he let everyone know it.’ He said, ‘Me and Malik have a good understanding right now. What’s perceived as being negative, what’s perceived as being a distraction, I think we both have an understanding of each other that allows it to coexist.’ And just certainly is something to keep an eye on." Not long after that, the booth threw to Fox sideline reporter Pam Oliver for more on Nabers. "Yeah, you guys talk about his body language," Oliver said. "I can tell you a little more about his mindset. I talked to him. And he told me, 'I just demand excellence out of everybody around me. Anybody that has a hand in my career. Because you only get one shot. It's your life, it's your career.' It's fueled by a great sense of urgency in that hard-fought return to the field from that knee injury. Nabers said — told me, 'I'm not going out there running all these routes not to get the ball.'" Said Davis in response, "I totally get it. But when your teammate scores the go-ahead touchdown and you still have that look? Not great." "Yeah, listen," Olsen said, "there's a fine line. I played with a lot of really good wide receivers. A lot really good players. There’s never been a great wide receiver who hasn’t demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. There is a few exceptions to guys that are just a different personality and a different approach. "But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That’s great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can’t still be worried about your targets. So that’s the fine line. He's a talented, young, really good player. He's just got to keep it in check.” That same drive included a third-down throw to Nabers in the end zone. Nabers couldn't make the reception, leading to a field goal. “Listen, you want to demand the ball — you can’t throw that ball any better,” Olsen said after Nabers failed to catch the pass. “That’s a touchdown. You’re a premier player in this league. You’ve got an opportunity there, you’ve got to catch it.” That's the full extent of everything that was said on the Fox broadcast during the relevant exchange. The problem is that too many outlets don't type quotes precisely. Some will mash pieces of different sentences together. Even if the overall message is the same (and, frankly, it seems as if Davis and Olsen were being critical of Nabers, with Davis being more pointed than Olsen), the absence of accuracy opens the door for criticism of the message. In this case, Olsen never called Nabers a "bad teammate." However, Olsen explained that there's a "fine line" between "being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things" and "tak[ing] away from the success of your teammates." Which basically is one of the hallmarks of being a bad teammate. That's why all outlets that are going to pass along quotes made on broadcasts should strive to get the quotes right. It eliminates any ambiguity as to what was said — and it prevents a subsequent attack regarding the accuracy of the quote. Especially when the accurate quote tends to lead to the same place.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Saints agree to trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars
summary: The Jaguars weren't done trading when they swung a deal to acquire safety Jessie Bates on Monday morning.
full_text: The Jaguars weren't done trading when they swung a deal to acquire safety Jessie Bates on Monday morning. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that they have also agreed to a trade with the Saints for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. Other reports indicate a 2028 sixth-round pick will head back to New Orleans. Bates is joining the team in a trade with the Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. Godchaux appeared in all eight Saints games this season and he made five starts before moving into a reserve role for the last three contests. He had 15 tackles and a tackle for loss in those appearances. Godchaux was in his second season with the Saints. He previously played for the Patriots and Dolphins. He and Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile overlapped with the Dolphins during the 2020 season. The Jaguars lost DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending quad injury in Week 8 and Godchaux gives them another experienced option to help fill the void. UPDATE 1:46 p.m. ET : Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the 2028 sixth-round pick is a conditional one. The Jaguars currently do not have a 2027 sixth-rounder, but will send one to the Saints if they acquire one at some point ahead of the draft.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL moves Jaguars-Giants game in Week 11 to a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff
summary: The NFL announced a couple of changes to kickoff times for Week 11 of the 2026 season.
full_text: The NFL announced a couple of changes to kickoff times for Week 11 of the 2026 season. The Jaguars and Giants were originally scheduled to start their game at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on November 22, but the game will now get underway at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Steelers' visit to Philadelphia to face the Eagles was set for that time and it will now take over the 1 p.m. slot. Both games will still be broadcast by CBS and the Jaguars-Giants contest is now set to be the network's national game during that window. It's a sensible change as both teams are leading their divisions while the Eagles, who have a bye in Week 10, will carry a seven-game losing streak into their matchup with the Steelers. A Raiders-Broncos game in Denver will also start at 4:25 p.m. ET and the Jets-Chargers game in Los Angeles will be the lone 4:05 p.m. ET start that weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline live updates: Tracker, deals, news, rumors, analysis
summary: Jeffery Simmons, DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson and more big-name NFL players are on the move.
full_text: '' The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and PFT has you covered with news and analysis of every trade, potential trade, rumor of a trade and trade that won’t be happening. Here’s what’s happening on the NFL trade front: Falcons agree to trade S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars : The Falcons will pick up most of Bates's remaining salary in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Saints agree to trade DT Davon Godchaux to the Jaguars : The Jaguars doubled down on defensive additions. Jonathan Taylor trade appears likely : The Colts are expected to take the best offer they get for Taylor. Jets LB Will McDonald requests a trade : The 2023 first-round pick would like to be on a new team. Colts may trade more players : Indianapolis has told teams it wants more than a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs . Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones could both be traded, perhaps both to the Vikings . Jacoby Brissett is headed to Baltimore : The Ravens and Cardinals announced a deal sending the veteran quarterback and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick. Derrick Henry says he's not thinking about changing teams : The Ravens star expressed a desire to help the team improve after a fourth-straight loss. Jonathan Taylor wants to know where he'll finish the season : Taylor said no one likes uncertainty when asked about talk that the Colts will trade him. Chargers say they're not trading Khalil Mack : Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said, " I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here ." Jeffery Simmons to Bears : Chicago receives Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Tennessee will receive 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-round pick in 2027. Quenton Nelson to Seahawks : The Seahawks will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick back to Indianapolis. DeForest Buckner to 49ers : Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from San Francisco. Jonathan Taylor trade talks have picked up : The Colts may not be done making deals. The Jets have reportedly rebuffed Garrett Wilson trade interest : The Jets are not expected to deal their top wideout. The Colts are open for business : Indianapolis is building for the future after firing General Manager Chris Ballard. Jonathan Taylor hasn’t requested a trade. Josh Downs says he's " open to whatever. " Budda Baker's name surfaces in trade rumors : Baker says he hasn’t asked to be traded from Arizona and also hasn't asked not to be traded. Brian Thomas is a name to watch : The Jaguars trading Thomas frequently comes up in trade rumors . Garrett Wilson wants to remain a Jet : The talented receiver says he is hoping not to get traded .
author: Michael David Smith

title: Malik Nabers: Fox tried to "create a narrative" about me being a bad teammate
summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took to social media on Sunday night to express his displeasure with how he was portrayed during the Fox broadcast of his team's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
full_text: '' Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took to social media on Sunday night to express his displeasure with how he was portrayed during the Fox broadcast of his team's 19-11 win over the Eagles. In a post to his Instagram story that was later taken down, Nabers took particular issue with Greg Olsen's characterization of him. After quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a pass behind Nabers in the fourth quarter, Fox showed Nabers gesturing with his hands and Olsen said he was letting the quarterback know to put the ball in front of him. Play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said Nabers's "body language has been terrible" throughout the game with Olsen agreeing that it wasn't good. The broadcast also showed Nabers slamming his helmet on the sideline at one point and sideline reporter Pam Oliver discussed Nabers's desire to have the ball come his way. Olsen went on to say that there is "a fine line" between receivers demanding the ball and being overly worried about your own touches that it detracts from the success of others. Nabers responded to what he believes was an implication that he's a bad teammate. "Y'all be trying [to] create a narrative on me soo bad, it's actually crazy!! If you [don't] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE! But [Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy! My face the same way if I'm havin a good game, bad, winning or losing," Nabers wrote. "If it's a problem. 1. Keep the camera off of me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple." Nabers finished the game with five catches for 43 yards, which snapped a four-game streak with at least 111 receiving yards. He said in his postgame media session that he was frustrated with how the offense played at points in Philadelphia, but his frustration with Olsen and Davis might have been even greater.
author: Josh Alper

title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
summary: Reid said he had seen Mahomes on Monday and the QB was in "good spirits."
full_text: ''' While Patrick Mahomes' elbow injury looked bad when it happened on Sunday, he was able to finish the game, helping power the Chiefs to a 35-12 win over the Jets. It sounds like he might not miss any further playing time either. "Patrick, he is really day-to-day right now ," head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Monday news conference. "It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of some rehab in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. And we’ll just see where it goes from there. "But he’s in good spirits today — I have seen him today, so he’s in good spirits today." Mahomes suffered the injury late in the first half. In the third quarter, he completed 7-of-10 passes for 81 yards. He was 5-of-6 for 41 yards in the fourth quarter. Additionally, Reid mentioned Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and Jaylon Moore (ankle) are day-to-day with their respective injuries. The Chiefs will be on the road to play the Falcons in Week 10. The first injury report of the week will be issued on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Tom Brady: "There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today"
summary: The quarterback with a statue outside the stadium returned for the first time to call a game in his capacity as a broadcaster for Fox.
full_text: The quarterback with a statue outside the stadium returned for the first time to call a game in his capacity as a broadcaster for Fox. (And also to keep his eyes and ears open in his capacity as an owner of the Raiders.) After the Packers blew out the Patriots at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, former Patriots quarterback Tom Brady made an observation about the current Patriots quarterback. "There was some deli meat given out by Drake Maye today," Brady said to Packers safety Evan Williams in a post-game interview. Replied Williams: "I'm not gonna say that, but he was giving us some gifts, for sure." It was funny and light-hearted. And, frankly, not inaccurate. The "deli meat" insult has recently become a thing. After the Rams' Week 8 win over the Chargers, Rams safety Quentin Lake said Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was throwing " deli meat ." Lake later apologized . More generally, the comments highlight one of the basic realities of Brady calling NFL games while owning a piece of the Raiders. To date, he hasn't called a Raiders game. One of these days, he likely will. What if Fernando Mendoza gives out "deli meat"? What if the head coach makes a questionable decision? What if any of the Raiders players do something that would invite scrutiny and/or criticism? For now, Fox and the NFL can stickhandle the scheduling to keep Brady out of the delicate spot of working a Raiders game. It would become unavoidable only if the Raiders make it to the Super Bowl in a year that Fox will be broadcasting the game. That's a very narrow needle to thread. Especially since the Raiders have only been to the playoffs twice since 2002 — and haven't won a postseason game since then.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sam Darnold ruled out for Week 10, Drew Lock in line to start
summary: Sam Darnold will be out for at least another week, but the Seahawks' regular backup quarterback should be able to play in the Week 10 matchup against the Raiders.
full_text: Sam Darnold will be out for at least another week, but the Seahawks' regular backup quarterback should be able to play in the Week 10 matchup against the Raiders. Head coach Mike Macdonald said in his weekly interview with Seattle Sports 710's Brock Huard and Mike Salk that Darnold will miss another game with his quad injury. But the team is planning to start Drew Lock again, even though he was injured during Sunday's win over the Cardinals. "Good exam for Drew," Macdonald said, via Andrew Destin of TheAthletic.com. "He's dealing with an oblique. And, I think it’s something we can manage ." Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards with a touchdown in the 17-3 victory over the Cardinals. he also rushed five times for 16 yards. He did not miss an offensive snap. While Lock has also been dealing with an elbow issue, the Seahawks kept him limited on the report for all three days last week before he had no game status and started against Arizona. The plan could be similar for Lock in Week 10. Jalen Milroe is Seattle’s third quarterback, though he has not appeared in a game so far in 2026.
author: Myles Simmons

title: John Harbaugh says it "looks like" QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) will be able to play on Thursday
summary: The NFL has fully embraced a full slate of Thursday night games, justifying the health-and-safety realities by pointing to in-game injury rates when a team has a full week to rest and when it has a four-day turnaround.
full_text: '' The NFL has fully embraced a full slate of Thursday night games, justifying the health-and-safety realities by pointing to in-game injury rates when a team has a full week to rest and when it has a four-day turnaround. That selective statistical focus overlooks the basic reality that some players injured on one Sunday would be ready by the next Sunday, but won't be ready by Thursday. For Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the three extra days to recover from the hip pointer he suffered on Sunday would be useful. As it stands, the clock is ticking toward Thursday night's game against the Commanders. Coach John Harbaugh told reporters on Monday that McCarthy is "doing well," and that it “ does look like he’s going to play ” on Thursday night. Even if he's not playing, there's strategic value in keeping the Commanders in the dark about whether it will be McCarthy or Jameis Winston. Either way, it would be wise for Washington to be ready for both guys, since McCarthy could aggravate the injury or suffer a new one. That's the reality of rolling with McCarthy. His fearlessness means he'll take hits. The more hits he takes, the more likely it is that he'll be hurt. Winston did well during the brief time McCarthy went to the locker room, presumably for a quick visit with Dr. Needle. Winston completed six passes for 71 yards and a touchdown — half of the total passes McCarthy completed in the rest of the game. In the end, the Giants got another win. They're 5-2-1. And they're taking control of the NFC East, especially with the Eagles at 2-7, the Commanders at 2-5-1, and the Cowboys at 4-5. McCarthy has a higher floor than Winston. Winston, when things are clicking, could have a higher ceiling. And he seems to be better when he enters a game cold, giving the Giants the best of both worlds as they try to turn a season that seemed lost seven weeks ago tonight into something special.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants expect Cam Skattebo to play on Thursday night
summary: The Giants played without running back Cam Skattebo in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles, but they do not expect his absence from the lineup to linger.
full_text: '' The Giants played without running back Cam Skattebo in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles, but they do not expect his absence from the lineup to linger. Head coach John Harbaugh said at a Monday press conference that the expectation is that Skattebo will be "full go" for Thursday night's game against the Commanders. Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury late in the Giants' Week 7 win over the Texans and missed practice for two days coming out of the bye week. He returned on Friday and Harbaugh said he was close to being ready for the Eagles, but that the team had the quick turnaround in mind when making a plan for managing his health. Devin Singletary was the lead back for the Giants against the Eagles and he ran 21 times for 31 yards. Gregory Desrosiers had 20 yards on three carries.
author: Josh Alper

title: Maxx Crosby on trade deadline: I expect to play for the Raiders
summary: Earlier this year, Maxx Crosby was supposed to be traded from the Raiders to the Ravens.
full_text: ' Earlier this year, Maxx Crosby was supposed to be traded from the Raiders to the Ravens. As is well known, that deal came off the table when Baltimore had concerns about Crosby's physical. With the trade deadline approaching, Las Vegas could, in theory, look to trade Crosby again. But the star edge rusher said after Sunday's loss to the 49ers that he isn't looking to leave. " I play for the Raiders ,” Crosby said, via Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . “I expect to play for the Raiders. That’s all that matters. I love this team, and I plan on being here for a very long time.” While Crosby pushed for a trade in the offseason, he’s now on board with the direction of the franchise. “We’re right in the mix,” Crosby said. “We’re 4-5. We had a tough loss today, but when we’re at our best, we can beat anyone. We know it’s going to be a tough challenge. We’ve got a lot of football left and we have to take them one at a time. We’re right in the middle of it. This is the best time of the year. This is what you’ve worked so hard for.” Crosby added he’s not looking for there to be any ambiguity about his desire to remain with the franchise that drafted him. “There’s always narratives and always people that supposedly have all this inside information,” Crosby said. “I speak very clearly because everyone has an opinion, but nobody really (knows anything). Everyone that has these random things that come out of nowhere is just trying to get some attention and clickbait. So it’s just part of the game. It comes with being a player of my stature and comes with the nature of the business. “I don’t pay attention to it. I just hear through the grapevine what’s going on. [I just try to] be present. Focus on what I need to do. Be a great leader, great player and win games in the silver and black. That’s what I plan on doing for a long time.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Browns to start Deshaun Watson against Texans
summary: Watson did not play Sunday, but the team is expected to turn back to him in Week 10.
full_text: Browns head coach Todd Monken wasn’t interested in answering questions about the team's quarterback plans for Week 10 after Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints, but it seems the team has done some thinking about their plans. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that the plan is for Deshaun Watson to return to the starting lineup against the Texans. Watson cleared concussion protocol on Saturday, but was inactive after missing two practices during the week. Shedeur Sanders got the start and went 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Monken said after the game that he was proud of Sanders's performance after spending the first two months of the season on the bench, but declined to answer whether it was enough for him to consider making a lasting change. Monken hasn't confirmed the team's plan, but it appears the team will return to the status quo as they try to keep pace in the AFC playoff race.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots don't expect Ben Brown to play in Week 10, waiting for Rhamondre Stevenson MRI results
summary: The Patriots expect to be without guard Ben Brown when they face the Lions in Germany in Week 10.
full_text: The Patriots expect to be without guard Ben Brown when they face the Lions in Germany in Week 10. Brown injured his knee during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers and head coach Mike Vrabel said at a Monday press conference that he doesn't think Brown will be in the lineup for that game. Brown started at left guard and he was replaced by Walter Rouse. The Patriots have been hit hard by injuries at guard. Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker are both on injured reserve, which has pushed Matt Pryor into the starting lineup. Vrabel also said that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is getting an MRI on his knee and that the team does not have an update on his condition at this point. TreVeyon Henderson is out as he looks for answers to a neurological condition, which leaves Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as the team's healthy backs. Wide receiver A.J. Brown missed his second straight game with a knee injury and Vrabel said the team is unsure if he'll be able to play in Munich.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaguars announce Jessie Bates trade
summary: The Jaguars announced their trade for safety Jessie Bates on Monday.
full_text: The Jaguars announced their trade for safety Jessie Bates on Monday. Bates is headed to Jacksonville to strengthen a position that's been hit by injuries this season. Eric Murray will miss the rest of the year with an elbow injury and Antonio Johnson missed Week 8 with an ankle injury before returning for last Thursday's win over the Ravens. "Jessie has been a proven playmaker on the defensive side of the ball for the last 8+ seasons," Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone said in a statement. "His skillset complements our style of play and the person he is aligns with our culture. We look forward to integrating Jessie into our team as we prepare for the back half of the season." The Jaguars are sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to the Falcons. The Falcons also agreed to pay the bulk of Bates's salary for the rest of this season. Bates is set to be a free agent in March. Bates was a second-team All-Pro for the third time in his career last season. He has one interception this season and had 14 in his three-plus years with the Falcons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson benched Zavion Thomas after 15-yard penalty
summary: Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas hasn't had a lot of production so far this season, and he may have even less after head coach Ben Johnson benched him during Sunday night's win over the Buccaneers.
full_text: Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas hasn't had a lot of production so far this season, and he may have even less after head coach Ben Johnson benched him during Sunday night's win over the Buccaneers. In the second quarter, with the Bears at the Buccaneers' 6-yard line, Thomas got into a shoving match with Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish and was flagged for unnecessary roughness, moving the Bears back to the 21-yard line. On the next play, Caleb Williams threw an interception, on a play that wouldn't have been called if the Bears were still at the 6, ending a promising drive. Johnson was not happy. Asked after the game whether he said anything to Thomas, Johnson answered, "Yeah, I don't know that he played on offense after that." Johnson didn't need to say any more than to tell Thomas he wouldn't be going back into the game on offense. (Thomas did keep playing on kickoff returns.) Thomas is a speedy receiver and a talented playmaker, but Johnson wants him to know that he's not good enough to get away with committing 15-yard penalties.
author: Michael David Smith

title: ESPN, CFP strike deal to expand college playoff to 24 teams
summary: For any business, there are two ways to maximize profit.
full_text: For any business, there are two ways to maximize profit. One, reduce expenses. Two, increase revenue. As to the former, the NCAA (working in cahoots with ESPN, among others) hope to use the wolf-in-sheep's-clothing of the Protect College Sports Act to reduce the booster's billions that are currently being diverted to NIL collectives. (The PCSA appears to be DOA , which is good news for the players.) As to the latter, the NCAA and ESPN have agreed to double the size of the playoff field to 24 as of 2027. Under a five-year, $1.7 billion deal, there will be more postseason games that matter — and fewer postseason Pop Tart/mayonnaise bowl games that don't. Along the way, four postseason games that matter plenty are going the way of the dodo bird. The conference championship games for the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, and Big 12 will end. Under the new schedule, "Week Zero" becomes Week 1. And the regular-season ends on Thanksgiving weekend. The top eight teams in the CFP rankings will secure byes. The first round (with No. 9 through No. 24 playing games against each other) will cut the field to 16. In round two, there will be blowouts. The No. 1 seed will play the winner of the game between No. 16 and No. 17. The No. 2 seed will play the winner of No. 15 vs. No. 18. There also will be new pressure on players who are draft-ready to keep playing, in pursuit of a potential championship. As illusory as that goal may be. And the players, by all appearances, once again had no seat at the table. More games? No problem. Then, the powers-that-be will keep griping about the chaos that comes from the players having the right to pursue market value, when the fat cats aren't otherwise counting the money. Whether chaos exists in college football is a matter of perspective. Whether ESPN will be force-feeding an uptick in non-competitive games to folks who love football (even when it's bad football) is undeniable. There aren't, in any given year, 24 teams that are good enough to win a championship. In the second round, some of the teams that managed to win in the first round will become cannon fodder for the elite programs. And the best players on the lesser teams will be fully expected to risk an injury that could eventually cost them millions in draft stock. Regardless of the amount of chaos that will bring to their own personal business interests.
author: Mike Florio

title: Baker Mayfield: Bears barked out the Buccaneers' cadence, causing a false start
summary: The Buccaneers were flagged for five false starts on Sunday night, and quarterback Baker Mayfield said at least one of them was caused by an illegal tactic by the Bears.
full_text: The Buccaneers were flagged for five false starts on Sunday night, and quarterback Baker Mayfield said at least one of them was caused by an illegal tactic by the Bears. Mayfield said left tackle Tristan Wirfs jumped when Bears players yelled Mayfield's cadence, something that is a penalty when the officials notice it but is hard for the officials to know. Mayfield said he's not sure what else the Bucs could have done. "I don't know," Mayfield said. "The last one, I know they were barking out the cadence, which you can't do that. It's tough for the refs to call that because they're not right there at the line of scrimmage. They called that on Tristan, but you can't do that." That last false start Mayfield referenced came during a brutal stretch for the Bucs' offense: Immediately after that false start, Mayfield was hit while throwing an incomplete pass, and on the next three plays Mayfield was sacked, although one of the sacks was wiped out by a penalty. The Bucs' offensive line looked out of sorts, and Mayfield thinks the Bears' cheating was a contributing factor.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tee Higgins thinks Joe Burrow has "another step in him"
summary: The Bengals extended their winning streak to four games against the Falcons in Madrid on Sunday and they continued to use their aerial attack to fuel their success.
full_text: The Bengals extended their winning streak to four games against the Falcons in Madrid on Sunday and they continued to use their aerial attack to fuel their success. Joe Burrow was 24-of-29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the 34-17 win and he has thrown for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns over the last four games. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been the main targets for Burrow and Higgins was asked after Sunday's win if this is the best he's ever seen Burrow play. "No. I know he got another step in him, for sure," Higgins said, via a transcript from the team. Higgins said the same for the offense as a whole because there are things they could improve to find their "best form." That prospect should be a chilling one for opposing defensive players and coaches as they try to draw up ways to slow down a red-hot Bengals offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drew Lock and the Seahawks earn an easy win over the Cardinals
summary: As he has been all season, Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock was a steady hand running the offense.
full_text: Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock did today what he's done three times this season: Played mistake-free football and led Seattle to a win. Lock, playing once again for an injured Sam Darnold, was steady and efficient as the Seahawks controlled the game and beat the Cardinals 17-3. Is Lock a better quarterback than Darnold? Probably not, but Lock might be better for what the Seahawks need right now, which is a quarterback who can play mistake-free football and let the defense win the game. Darnold has thrown nine interceptions this season, while Lock has thrown none. Today Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and one touchdown. Not spectacular numbers, but the key numbers were zeroes: Zero interceptions, zero fumbles, zero sacks. Darnold has far more negative plays than Lock does this season, and that's one of the reasons the Seahawks are 3-0 in the three games that have been primarily quarterbacked by Lock, and 2-4 in the six games that have primarily been quarterbacked by Darnold. At 5-4, the Seahawks aren't the team they hoped to be heading into this season, but they're very much in contention. And they might just have a better chance of making the playoffs and getting an opportunity to defend their title if Lock keeps playing.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Saints hang on to defeat Browns in overtime, 23-22
summary: The Browns and Saints were tied at 6-6 midway through the fourth quarter.
full_text: The Browns and Saints were tied at 6-6 midway through the fourth quarter. But the game then became a barn burner in the final period and overtime, with a failed Cleveland two-point conversion allowing the Saints to escape with a narrow 23-22 victory. New Orleans had taken a 9-6 lead with Charlie Smyth’s 48-yard field goal with 5:38 left in the contest. But the Browns immediately responded with a 64-yard touchdown catch by rookie KC Concepcion, who burned the defense off the line. It was Concepcion’s first career touchdown. The Browns, however, couldn’t hold the late lead. The team’s four-minute offense couldn’t convert enough first downs, leaving the Saints with time to get down the field. They were able to get in the end zone with Audric Estime’s 2-yard touchdown with 58 seconds on the clock, going ahead 16-13. But Shedeur Sanders — playing after Deshaun Watson spent most of the week in concussion protocol — connected with Jerry Jeudy for a key 30-yard gain. The outstanding throw and catch set up Andre Szmyt for a game-tying 51-yard field goal to send the contest into overtime. Juwan Johnson capped New Orleans’ OT possession with a 15-yard touchdown reception. But Harold Fannin’s terrific catch-and-run put the Browns in position to tie it or win it with a 39-yard touchdown. Browns head coach Todd Monken elected to go for the win instead of settling for — at best — a potential tie. But Sanders’ throw to Denzel Boston was incomplete. Even if it had been caught, the Browns were flagged for holding. Sanders finished the contest 19-of-31 for 297 yards with a pair of touchdowns. On the other side, Tyler Shough was 21-of-35 for 265 yards with a TD. Notably, New Orleans center Erik McCoy had to depart the game with an elbow injury. The Saints have put themselves right back in the NFC South conversation at 3-5. They will have a chance to gain more ground in the division next Sunday, as they’ll play the Panthers at home. The Browns have now dropped two in a row, falling to 5-4. They will play the Texans at home next Sunday before a Week 11 bye.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Robert Saleh: Calvin Ridley's airport incident was "a very minor miscommunication"
summary: News emerged on Sunday night that Titans receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident over the weekend at Nashville International Airport.
full_text: News emerged on Sunday night that Titans receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident over the weekend at Nashville International Airport. Few details about the incident have been made public, which continues to be the case after head coach Robert Saleh’s news conference on Monday. "With regards to Calvin, we’re aware of everything that’s happening,” Saleh said. “From my understanding, it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport . Unfortunately, law enforcement has it, and that’s about as far as I can go with commenting.” It’s been a rough 2026 for the Titans so far, as they’ve won just one game and have dealt with multiple off-the-field incidents. Saleh said he wouldn’t call these situations “frustrating,” “Ultimately, when you’re losing, everything is kind of exacerbated,” Saleh said. “But all 32 buildings deal with things throughout the season. It’s unfortunate with what happened, but I’m sure we’ll move on with business as normal.” Coming off their Week 9 bye, the Titans will host the division-rival Jaguars in Week 10.

title: Luther Burden scores 56-yard touchdown, Bears lead Bucs 14-0
summary: The last time the Bears played at home, Luther Burden went off for 130 yards.

Caleb Williams connected with Burden on third-and-8 with a short pass over the middle, and Burden turned on the jets to outrun the Tampa Bay defense and score a 56-yard touchdown. It’s the fourth touchdown reception of the season for Burden. So far, the Bears have converted all three of their third-down attempts on their first two drives. The Buccaneers went three-and-out on their opening possession. After going 0-of-3 passing last week in heavy rain, Baker Mayfield completed his first passing attempt of the day for a 3-yard gain.

title: Jaguars agree to trade for Falcons S Jessie Bates

The Jaguars will send a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons in exchange for Bates. Bates was named a second-team All-Pro for the third time in his career last season and he has 60 tackles, an interception, three forced fumbles and a fumble return for a touchdown in nine games this season. title: Jaguars-Falcons trade grades: Jacksonville acquires All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to bolster defense
summary: Bates, who is in the final year of his contract, heads to Jacksonville in exchange for two future draft picks
full_text:
On the eve of Tuesday's trade deadline, dominoes are starting to fall across the league with Week 9 largely in the books. And now, the Jaguars have acquired All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons , according to ESPN . As Bates heads to Duval County, the Falcons receive a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in return.
Bates is in the final year of his contract and is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. While this is looked at as a rental, the 29-year-old should prove to be a key addition to Jacksonville's secondary as it looks to make a serious postseason push following a 6-2 start to the regular season.
In nine games played for the Falcons this season, Bates has recorded one interception, three forced fumbles, and 60 total tackles. The veteran has also allowed a 78.3% completion percentage to go with a 115.2 passer rating in coverage, per TruMedia.
Bates entered the NFL as a second-round draft choice of the Bengals in 2018 out of Wake Forest. After spending his first five years of his career in Cincinnati, he inked a four-year, $64.02 million contract with the Falcons in the spring of 2023 and has been lurking in their secondary ever since.
Bates is tied for the second-most interceptions (28) in the NFL since coming into the league and has been named a second-team All-Pro three times, including in 2025.
Atlanta spent last offseason inking several veterans to extensions, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London . Bates was not among them, and after dropping to 3-6 on the season with a loss to the Bengals in Madrid on Sunday, they're electing to move off of the talented safety for future draft capital.
Jacksonville gave up quite a bit to land Bates. Two picks -- particularly a second-rounder in 2027 -- is a hefty price to pay, especially considering that Bates is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. I do wonder, however, whether that price indicates that Jacksonville views Bates as more than just a rental. After all, the organization does have a history of extending players that they've acquired in midseason trades. For instance, after trading for wideout Jakobi Meyers around last year's deadline, they later signed him to a three-year, $60 million extension. I'll be curious to see if Bates follows a similar path.
Regardless of whether he's with the Jags for the next few months or years, it's a great move for the 2026 squad. Bates is one of the best safeties in the NFL. In fact, he's the player in the past 40 years with at least 800 tackles and 25 interceptions before age 30. He comes in as a premier piece for the secondary, while also deepening a safety room that has been hit by injuries, most recently losing Eric Murray for the rest of the season to an elbow injury.
Give Atlanta the slight edge here. While they are losing a blue-chip player in their secondary, they were probably going to lose him anyway in free agency later this offseason.
The Falcons spent the bulk of last offseason extending key pieces to their core, and that did not include Bates. While the team is technically still in the division race despite a 3-6 record, it doesn't feel like this season will see them making a sizable push if/when they reach the postseason. With that in mind, it's the more prudent move to move off of Bates, get worse in the secondary in the immediate, but collect legit draft capital to position yourself better down the road.
Getting a second-rounder as part of this deal is nothing to turn your nose up at and is better than any sort of compensatory pick they'd receive if Bates walked in free agency.
