title: Vikings vs. Bills prediction: Josh Allen faces NFL's top defense on Monday night
summary: Josh Allen and Buffalo's explosive offense face Brian Flores' dominant defense, while Carson Wentz replaces the injured Kyler Murray
full_text:
In the Week 9 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings host the Buffalo Bills . Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season after starting the year with six straight wins. The Vikings turn to Carson Wentz to start in place of Kyler Murray , who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Minnesota sports arguably the NFL's best defense, and it will be put to the test on Monday night against the Bills.
Buffalo has won three consecutive games to improve to 6-1, and last week beat up on the Baltimore Ravens following an injury to Lamar Jackson on the Ravens' first snap of the game. Buffalo is in first place in the AFC East behind its efficient and explosive offense, which has helped offset a defense that has been highly vulnerable this year.
Will the Vikings bounce back, or will the Bills continue to roll? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
This is going to be one of the most fascinating matchups of the season, as arguably the NFL's best quarterback ( Josh Allen ) will do battle with arguably the NFL's best defensive play-caller (Brian Flores). We know the state of play: the Vikings are going to blitz on damn near every snap, and the Bills are going to have to figure out how in the world to deal with all the extra bodies the Vikings send against both the run and the pass.
Last week, the Vikings totally shut down one of the best offenses in the league during the first half, holding the Lions to a mere 154 total yards (on 36 plays, an average of 4.3 per play) and only six points prior to the break. They frustrated Jared Goff and the passing game with their heavy blitzing and they limited Jahmyr Gibbs and company to a 25% rushing success rate.
Buffalo has been one of the best running teams in the NFL, averaging 4.8 yards per carry, which ranks fourth in the league. The Bills can lean on James Cook, who, after leading the NFL in rushing last year, is actually averaging nearly six more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. Buffalo likes to get downhill runs with schemes like duo that create double teams inside, which is tough to do against the Vikings, but can lead to big gains if you can block them up front. Whether the Bills can do that is obviously another question.
It's important to note that Allen has been blitzed on exactly a third of his dropbacks, per Tru Media, meaning he's faced the 11th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. He's 46 of 70 for 587 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions on those plays, and he's been sacked six times. That's all led to him checking in fourth in yards per attempt (8.4) and seventh in passing success rate (50.0%) but only 15th in EPA per dropback thanks to the interceptions.
The Bills will need to get the ball out quickly against the blitz, which could mean underneath targets like Khalil Shakir and passing-down back Ty Johnson are heavily involved. It might be a lighter game for the likes of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox , as teams often keep their tight ends back in pass protection against Flores' blitz-happy defense.
It might also be tough for DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to get open down the field, but there could be opportunities for big plays if the offensive line does hold up on any given snap. The Vikings have given up the occasional deep shot this year because they send so many men after the quarterback and it leaves them shorthanded on the back end at times.
The Vikings have struggled to move the ball pretty much all season. Their 4.7 yards-per-play average is tied for third-worst in the NFL. Their 1.71 points-per-drive average is fifth-worst in the NFL. And their -0.14 expected points added per play average is second-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media.
They've yet to gain more than 364 yards in any game, and they've been at 275 or fewer in five of their seven contests. They've scored more than 23 points just one time, and it was back in Week 1 when they had touchdown drives of 28, 1 and 14 yards late in the game against the Green Bay Packers .
Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of Kyler Murray, who has completed 64.9% of his passes at an average of just 6.6 yards per attempt, with a mere five touchdown passes and three interceptions. Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of the run game, where the backs have combined to average south of 4.0 yards per carry. Jordan Mason missed four games, but it's not like he's been effective when he's been on the field, having averaged 3.9 yards a pop.
Murray won't be on the field on Monday night. It'll be Carson Wentz under center in his place. Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in one-plus games in relief of Murray earlier this year. He seemed to have more command of the offense and more chemistry with Justin Jefferson than Murray does, at the very least. Jefferson went for eight catches for 92 yards and two scores during Wentz's relief appearance back in Week 1, and he was on the receiving end of seven of Wentz's 19 pass attempts in that game. (Wentz's start the following week came in a driving rainstorm in Chicago and doesn't provide much room for analysis.)
If the Vikings can keep Wentz well-protected, there should be some opportunities for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson to find openings in what has been a very leaky back seven. The Bills have been solid against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry. Given the Vikings' struggles on the ground, it seems unlikely that they'll have much in the way of success running the ball here.
You can't ask me to buy into this Minnesota offense right now — not even against Buffalo's leaky defense. We just saw the Vikings put up a relatively limp offensive performance against the Lions. And if there's a team out there that can run the ball on Minnesota the way the Lions did, it might be the Bills with Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo can win a low-ish scoring game here by doing just that.
Prediction: Bills 20, Vikings 14
author: Jared Dubin

title: Josh Jacobs breaks finger during Packers' win, will undergo surgery and could miss a maximum of three weeks
summary: Jacobs hopes to play through the issue, but grip struggles could force Green Bay to pursue running back help before Tuesday's trade deadline
full_text:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs told reporters he broke the ring finger on his right hand during the 45-27 victory over the New England Patriots . Jacobs rushed four times for five yards in the first quarter before exiting the game with what was described as a hand injury. Kaleb Johnson ended up leading the Packers in rushing with 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. Pierre Strong Jr . chipped in with 22 yards on eight carries.
Jacobs is set to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks , according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
Jacobs appeared to get one of the fingers on his right hand stuck in the face mask of Patriots safety Craig Woodson during a rushing attempt. He says they will find a way to play through it, but Jacobs struggled to grip the ball.
In three games this season, Jacobs has rushed 36 times for 80 yards and one touchdown. The Packers actually recorded the fewest rushing yards (485) by a winning team through eight games in NFL history, according to CBS Sports Research.
With Jacobs out, it does throw an interesting wrinkle into Tuesday's trade deadline. Green Bay entered Sunday with the worst rushing offense in the NFL at 60.6 yards per game. Could the Packers be interested in acquiring Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts or Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans ?
The Packers' rushing offense has been a disaster, but Green Bay's passing attack is on fire. Jordan Love threw for 373 yards and three touchdowns against the Patriots, while Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and one touchdown, and Matthew Golden 10 passes for 164 yards and a touchdown. They became the fourth duo since 2000 to have 160 yards receiving and a receiving touchdown each in a game, and the first since Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle of the Miami Dolphins in 2022.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Latest deals, grades as Andre Cisco heads to Detroit
summary: Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Chicago's blockbuster addition of Jeffery Simmons and the Colts' trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
full_text:
A steady stream of blockbuster moves in advance of the 2026 NFL trade deadline redistributed some of the league's top talent at numerous positions. Even more impactful transactions could be on the way before Nov. 10, but in the meantime, the Chicago Bears are the biggest winners of the deadline thus far with their highly fruitful acquisition of Jeffery Simmons , while the Indianapolis Colts emerged as the most aggressive sellers in dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner .
Trade watch continues for a myriad of stars on struggling teams, including Jonathan Taylor , Khalil Mack , George Pickens and others. At the same time, teams battling for position at the front of the postseason race must decide how much to invest in those standouts who are available on the trade market.
There is only one more game until the trade deadline, so this year's contenders and pretenders are about as clear as they will be before it is too late to buy and sell. It is safe to expect a flurry of moves in the next 24 hours as those franchises gear up for the home stretch or look ahead to the future.
Below is every in-season trade ahead of the NFL's 2026 deadline.
The Lions should be better off than they were before in the defensive backfield with the addition of Cisco, but by how much? Cisco arrives in a unit that ranks dead last in stopping the pass at 260.9 yards per game. He slipped from his status as an every-week starter and was at the top of the Jets' depth chart for just four of nine games this season, so while he remains productive, this is not a home-run transaction for a Detroit team that has to be better on his side of the ball in order to achieve its goals. This could age much better if and when Kerby Joseph returns to the lineup, because Cisco would be a pleasant depth option behind both Joseph and Brian Branch .
New York will have to wait a year to reap the benefits of this trade. It is a success to get something in return for a player who started fewer than half of his games this season, but the Jets need all the draft capital they can stockpile in order to pull themselves out of their rebuild, and 2028 is a long way away.
Jacksonville entered the week with needs at safety and defensive tackle and filled both of them in a matter of hours. Shortly after acquiring Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars made a play for Godchaux, boosting a defense that may already be Super Bowl-caliber. This is a necessary addition for general manager James Gladstone after he watched DaVon Hamilton go down with a torn quad in Week 8 and one that should keep the NFL's No. 5 run defense in the top echelon.
The pick heading to New Orleans will become a 2027 sixth-round pick if the Jaguars acquire one, according to ESPN . They do not currently own one but are projected to receive two compensatory picks, according to Spotrac . Even with the caveat on the return, the Saints upgraded in the deal considering they spent a seventh-rounder to acquire Godchaux in a trade last year. He was a questionable fit in a run defense that ranks fifth-worst in the NFL, anyway.
The Jaguars secured a rental for their secondary and an impactful one at that. Bates is a perennial All-Pro safety who not only beefs up the starting lineup with renowned playmaking ability but also adds depth to a group that is dealing with injuries and just lost Eric Murray for the year with an elbow issue. Jacksonville is right in the midst of its contention window and is in play for the AFC's No. 1 seed, so any move that strengthens its Super Bowl chances is justifiable, even if it gives up quite a bit in the way of draft picks to pull it off.
Those picks make this deal a beneficial one for the Falcons, too. Atlanta should have expected to lose Bates in free agency this coming offseason, since he was not among the many players it extended this past summer. The second-round pick is better than any compensatory pick that would have come with his departure, and the 2028 fifth-rounder sweetened the deal even further. Now is the time for the Falcons to turn expiring contracts into future assets, because, at 3-6, they are unlikely to contend for anything beyond a potential first-place finish in the NFL's weakest division.
Baltimore agreed to trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett and completed the deal over the weekend after its "Thursday Night Football" loss. This was an expected move for the Ravens, because their quarterback situation went from bad to worse in Week 8. The highly anticipated return of starter Lamar Jackson lasted just one play. Jackson suffered a thumb injury and is now on injured reserve. Tyler Huntley , who started in place of Jackson, took over but also went down. He is out for the season with a turf toe injury. The team relied on emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano to finish the game and started him on Thursday.
Brissett spent the last two seasons with the Cardinals, who benched him in his final game with the team and turned instead to Gardner Minshew . The return of draft capital for a quarterback who lost his job, was unhappy all offseason about his contract situation and projected as a bridge to an eventual first-round pick is a huge success for a rebuilding Arizona team.
In giving up two first-rounders to secure a perennial All-Pro defensive tackle , the Bears went all-in and opened their Super Bowl contention window. The transaction paid immediate dividends when Simmons logged a sack and led the team with six tackles in his Chicago debut: A commanding 34-17 road win over the Seahawks . Mortgaging so much of their future first-round capital showed that the Bears trust their roster, as currently constructed, to compete at the top of the league, and Simmons is the kind of game-changing talent worth the steep price. His production in the pass rush and in run defense could help Chicago maximize its high-octane unit on the other side of the ball led by Caleb Williams .
This move sends the Titans deeper into their rebuild. Questions lie ahead about whether to stick with Cam Ward at quarterback, and with the first-round picks they acquired from dealing Simmons, there will be curiosity as to whether they will use one to land a new signal-caller. Regardless of how they use the picks, moving on from one of the greatest players in franchise history shows how bleak the present is in Tennessee and that all eyes are on the future.
The seemingly nonstop onslaught of injuries hit the 49ers' defensive line, resulting in CJ West landing on injured reserve with a bone chip in his knee and Alfred Collins being ruled out for the year with a torn patellar tendon. That heightened the need for immediate help in the trenches, so the 49ers brought Buckner back after his six-plus years in Indianapolis . The 49ers selected Buckner in the first round of the 2016 draft, and the best years of his prime came during his time in San Francisco, so this is a welcome return for someone the franchise remembers fondly. Buckner remains one of the NFL's top pass-rushing interior defensive linemen and will aid in the 49ers' Super Bowl push.
Buckner's exit marked the second trade in one day for the slumping Colts, who are in the midst of tearing things down with multiple star players on the move and former general manager Chris Ballard out the door. There is an argument to be made that a Day 3 pick was an underwhelming return, but for a 32-year-old veteran on an expiring contract, the Colts were content to get at least something of value for a player who was likely to leave in free agency anyway. Buckner grew publicly frustrated with Indianapolis' struggles, which heightened the anticipation for his trade or an eventual departure at the end of his contract.
Seahawks general manager Jon Schneider is keen to make big-time moves ahead of the trade deadline. This is the fourth consecutive year in which Seattle made a play for an impactful midseason addition to its roster . Nelson is as stellar of an offensive lineman as there is on the trade market…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Lions-Jets trade grades: Detroit bolsters secondary with Andre Cisco, Jets acquire a late-round pick
summary: It wasn't the splashiest of moves, but Detroit nonetheless strengthened its secondary ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline
full_text:
The Detroit Lions and New York Jets have pulled off a trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline. Detroit is giving New York a 2028 sixth-round pick in exchange for veteran safety Andre Cisco , according to multiple outlets.
Cisco, 26, was drafted by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft . He spent his first four seasons in Jacksonville before he signed with the Jets ahead of the 2025 season. Cisco made 12 starts in 17 games in New York.
The 6-foot, 210-pound Cisco has made four starts across nine games this season. He had 23 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and one pass breakup this season for the Jets, who are off to a disappointing 2-7 start.
Cisco is going to a Lions team that is 6-2 and vying for their third playoff appearance in the last four years. He will look to help a Detroit secondary that is currently last in the NFL in both passing yards (2,087) and touchdown passes (18) allowed. The unit has been playing better in recent weeks, however. The Lions have held each of their last three opponents (the Packers , Vikings and Dolphins ) to 17 or fewer points. Detroit's secondary allowed an average of just 200 passing yards per game over that span.
Who won the trade? Let's find out.
This is a pretty vanilla trade for the Lions and GM Brad Holmes. This is certainly not a splashy trade that will generate much excitement among Lions fans. This trade looks like it was at least partly done so that Holmes can say that he did something to improve the secondary at the trade deadline.
If Holmes is looking for credit, he should get it, even if the praise should amount to a polite golf clap. As the numbers above illustrate, the Lions' secondary has taken its lumps this season. And while the unit has displayed signs of growth in recent weeks, it's fair to point out that the last two quarterbacks they faced ( Kyler Murray and Malik Willis ) aren't exactly setting the world on fire this season. They did contain Jordan Love back in Week 7, though, so the Lions have had success in recent weeks against a top-tier passer.
If nothing else, Cisco can provide depth for a unit that sorely needs it. The bottom line is that the Lions are better for making this trade.
A bland trade merits bland grades. Jets GM Darren Mougey gets some credit for getting something in exchange for a player who was playing out the final year of his contract. The return, however, is the issue here.
Cisco isn't a star, but it's fair to question whether or not the Jets could have gotten more than a 2028 sixth-round pick, especially when you look at where the Lions' pass defense currently ranks among the rest of the NFL. The Jets could/should have gotten a pick in this year's draft for Cisco. Instead, they won't be able to reap the benefit of this trade until 2028.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Jaguars agree to trade for Saints DT Davon Godchaux in second defensive trade of the day, per report
summary: Jacksonville is among the most active buyers ahead of the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
Mere hours after they acquired All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III , the Jacksonville Jaguars agreed to a trade with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux . According to The Athletic , the Jaguars will send a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Saints in exchange for the veteran lineman. That pick can turn into a 2027 sixth-rounder if those conditions are met.
It should be noted that the Jaguars do not currently have a 2027 sixth-round pick, moving it in a trade with the Giants for offensive lineman Daniel Faalele in August. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , if the conditions are met to upgrade the pick, any 2027 sixth-round pick the Jaguars eventually acquire would go to New Orleans. Jacksonville is currently projected to receive two sixth-round compensatory draft picks, according to Spotrac .
The Jaguars had been in the market for a defensive tackle in the wake of DaVon Hamilton's injury. The starting tackle suffered a torn quad in Week 8, which produced an opening in the middle of the defensive front. This move fills that gap, just like the Bates deal sealed a hole in the secondary, where Eric Murray was lost for the season due to an elbow issue.
Jacksonville's defense may already be Super Bowl-caliber, so the Godchaux acquisition should prevent any drop-off and keep the Jaguars in the hunt for the AFC's No. 1 seed. The unit ranks No. 5 against the run at just 89.3 yards allowed per game and is second-best in scoring at 15.1 points per game.
Godchaux heads to the fourth different team of his career since his arrival in 2017 as a fifth-round pick and will primarily make his impacts in run defense. He has not recorded a sack since 2022 but remains proficient against the rush and owns 15 tackles on the season with one of them coming in the form of a tackle for loss.
Godchaux started five of the Saints' first eight games and could slot directly into the Jaguars' lineup upon his arrival ahead of the Week 10 road game against the Tennessee Titans . Coach Liam Coen could either insert Godchaux into action or have him come off the bench in favor of Ruke Orhorhoro , who would have likely started if not for the trade. Arik Armstead remains the other starting interior defensive lineman.
The Jaguars are going for it. General manager James Gladstone is busy ahead of the trade deadline and successfully plugged two holes on the defense to keep Jacksonville squarely in the championship hunt. Godchaux is no game-changing addition but one who will do exactly what the Jaguars need, which is to plug gaps in run defense. What's more, they conditionally traded a draft pick they do not even own yet, which is some savvy negotiating on Gladstone's part. Since the Jaguars are projected to secure two compensatory sixth-rounders in 2027, that pick will likely vest and go to the Saints, but they will still have one left over.
The Saints own the fourth-worst run defense in the NFL , so Godchaux was clearly not working for them. The pick they got in return for him is decent compensation for a non-impact player. Plus, when they traded for Godchaux a year ago, they gave the New England Patriots a seventh-rounder, so they got that back and a little more by parting with him. It is only a slight upgrade in draft capital, but anything helps for a team that might not even make the playoffs in the league's worst division.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 11 schedule flex: Giants-Jaguars moves to 4:25, Steelers-Eagles shifts to 1 p.m.
summary: New York and Jacksonville will receive a larger Week 11 spotlight as the league swaps their start time with the intrastate matchup between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia
full_text:
The NFL has moved the Week 11 Philadelphia Eagles ' home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers from 4:25 to a 1 p.m. ET start on Nov. 22. In a corresponding move, the New York Giants ' home game against the Jacksonville Jaguars has been moved from 1 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. Both games will be shown on CBS.
The league's decision to switch these starting times is obvious. New York (5-2-1) and Jacksonville (6-2) lead their respective divisions, and while Pittsburgh (6-2) also leads its division, Philadelphia (2-7) has lost seven straight games and is sitting in last place in the NFC East.
The NFL is also probably banking on the Steelers-Eagles game still getting decent viewership. It's an intrastate rivalry with a compelling storyline: Aaron Rodgers will try to lead the Steelers to the franchise's first win in Philadelphia since 1965.
The time swap will give Liam Coen's Jaguars an opportunity to showcase their talents before a larger audience. It also represents an opportunity for the Giants to get another big win in what has been a surprisingly successful first season for John Harbaugh in the Big Apple. On Sunday, Harbaugh led the Giants to their first win in Philadelphia since 2013.
The upcoming Jaguars-Giants game could be coined the "Tom Coughlin Bowl." Coughlin, the first coach in Jaguars history, guided Jacksonville to AFC title game appearances in 1996 (the franchise's second year of existence) and 1999. As the Giants' coach, Coughlin led New York to a pair of upset wins over the Patriots in the Super Bowl .
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Seahawks plan to start Drew Lock in Week 10 despite oblique injury, Sam Darnold to miss another game
summary: Lock will make his third start of the season as the Seattle quarterback group battles multiple injuries
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks might have avoided a worst-case scenario in their quarterback group. Although Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury and broken rib, Drew Lock has a good chance to recover enough from his oblique injury to play against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10.
Coach Mike Macdonald said on his weekly radio show on Monday that Darnold will miss another week but that the team will enter their matchup with the Raiders with a "similar plan" to last week. That is, Lock will operate as the starter with Jalen Milroe backing him up. Macdonald said that Lock had a "good exam" on his oblique and that it is "something that we can manage" as he gears up to make his third start of the season.
Lock briefly entered the sideline medical tent during the Seahawks' win over the Arizona Cardinals with an oblique issue that initially made his Week 10 status uncertain. He also dealt with elbow tendinitis in the lead-up to his start against the Cardinals. Although he was effective, completing 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, Lock was visibly short of 100% health. The Seahawks had only a modest day offensively against a Cardinals defense that entered Week 9 allowing the fifth-worst defensive EPA/play in the league, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.
"I was pressing to do everything I possibly could all the time, and [the fans] were able to pull me back a little bit," Lock said after the game . "Jalen did a fantastic job throughout the week in practice filling in for me. It was a collective effort from everybody to get to Sunday, and shoot, here we are 17-3. Go Hawks."
Holding Darnold out for another game essentially gives him a free week to recover, because the Seahawks will hit their bye after the matchup with the Raiders. That sets him up to return for a critical NFC West showdown on the road against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. So long as Seattle can get there without any setbacks, it will be a massive opportunity for the reigning champions to draw within striking distance of the division lead.
Lock is 2-0 in his two starts this season, both of which came against the Cardinals. He operated the offense tremendously in Week 2 when the Seahawks put up 31 points on their division rivals and has done everything Seattle could ask of him. This is still Darnold's offense, though, and he figures to rejoin the lineup on the other side of the bye week as the locked-in starter.
In the event that Lock's oblique or elbow prevents him from playing, Milroe will be waiting for the opportunity to make his first appearance of the season. The former third-round draft pick has not thrown a pass in his career but handled three carries for four yards in three games as a rookie in 2025. Seattle also has Adrian Martinez on its practice squad.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Cam Skattebo injury update: Giants RB 'full go' for Thursday night vs. Commanders
summary: Cam Skattebo is set to return from a hamstring injury as the NFC East-leading Giants prepare for a rematch with the Commanders
full_text:
Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday that running back Cam Skattebo will be "full go" for New York's "Thursday Night Football" game against the Commanders to open Week 10.
Skattebo missed the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Texans . Harbaugh said the second-year back was "very close" to playing, but with a short week ahead, the team opted to play it safe.
With Skattebo out and Tyrone Tracy Jr . (hamstring) on IR, the Giants struggled to get much going on the ground in Philadelphia. Devin Singletary shouldered a heavy workload with 21 carries but turned that into just 31 yards (1.5 yards per carry). Still, New York managed to grind out a win to get to 5-2-1 without its top back.
Skattebo's return should provide some significant juice to an offense that needs it. Furthermore, it sounds like New York will have its current top quarterback-running back battery available, with Harbaugh saying he expects J.J. McCarthy (hip pointer) to play . McCarthy briefly left Sunday's game against the Eagles after taking a hit to the ribs, and Jameis Winston led the team's lone touchdown drive.
Skattebo leads the Giants in carries (98) and rushing yards (418), both by a wide margin, but it hasn't necessarily been the easiest year for the bowling-ball former Arizona State star. After a solid start to the year, Skattebo had a crucial fumble in Week 5 against the Commanders, a game that ended in a tie. He was a complete non-factor the next week, receiving zero touches on minimal snaps. He responded from that, though, with a 124-yard, one-touchdown day in an impressive win over Houston to right the ship. Now, he'll be in line for another busy day as the Giants look to extend their NFC East lead.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: JJ McCarthy injury: Giants QB is on track to face Commanders on 'Thursday Night Football'
summary: McCarthy suffered a hip injury during Sunday's win over the Eagles but returned to play
full_text:
The New York Giants ' first win in Philadelphia since 2013 included a gritty performance from quarterback JJ McCarthy , who temporarily left the game after taking a shot to the midsection early in the second half. McCarthy missed one series before returning to the game and helping the Giants record a 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles .
McCarthy's injury has been labeled as a hip pointer. On Monday, Giants coach John Harbaugh said that McCarthy is "doing well" and that it "does look like he's going to play" in Thursday night's home game against the Washington Commanders .
The Giants are now 2-0 in games that McCarthy has started. On Sunday, McCarthy went 12 of 19 for 127 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions. In his first start with New York, McCarthy went 20 of 28 for 252 yards with no touchdowns and no picks in an overtime win over the Houston Texans .
New York's only touchdown on Sunday occurred during the series that McCarthy missed. Jameis Winston , who went 2-1-1 as the Giants' this season before he was replaced by McCarthy, gave New York the lead for good on a five-yard touchdown pass to tight end Isaiah Likely with 2:30 left in the third quarter. Winston went 6 of 8 for 71 yards on the Giants' 14-play, 76-yard drive that took nearly eight minutes off the clock.
McCarthy returned on the Giants' ensuing possession and led a 13-play, 54-yard scoring drive that included two third-down conversions by McCarthy: an 11-yard completion to Malik Nabers on third-and-5 and an 11-yard run on third-and-10 that got New York in field goal range.
With the win, the Giants maintained their sole possession of first place in the NFC East division. Thursday will mark nearly one month since the Giants and Commanders tied after Washington botched the final seconds of overtime.
author: Bryan DeArdo

Everyone on the internet loves to overreact, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Zach Pereles looked at several things that happened during Week 9, so decide for yourself whether we're all overreacting.
Statement: The Browns should stick with Shedeur Sanders as their starting QB. Overreaction or reality: Reality. The 23-22 loss to the Saints will leave a bad taste in the mouth after what was otherwise a solid performance, especially given the circumstances. Cleveland's offensive line was abysmal, as it has been much of the year, and the run game didn't help at all. There were also multiple drops.  But Sanders delivered several things Deshaun Watson simply doesn't. How about three completions on 30-plus-yard throws downfield? Watson has one ... all year! Sanders also did excellently in several moments navigating the pressure. Coaches rarely bench players due to injury, so I wouldn't be surprised if Watson returns to the lineup. Todd Monken refused to talk about it postgame . But in this writer's eyes, Sanders should keep the job.
Statement: Matthew Stafford is holding back the Rams . Overreaction or reality: Reality. The Rams are above .500 for the first time this year after outlasting the Commanders, 20-13. The Rams force-fed Puka Nacua (19 targets for 14 catches, 150 yards and a touchdown) and got just enough for the run game. Myles Garrett came back in full force with three sacks and a forced fumble. The Rams can still be a good team, but at some point, they will need Stafford to play like his 2025 self, and it just doesn't look like he has that anymore.

McCarthy wasn't good, but he didn't have any huge mistakes. That's enough against a team like the Eagles . Dallas lost a pair of fumbles in awful moments, committed several terrible penalties, and seemed to spend half the game trying to give it away. But they won and now sit at 4-5. Yes, that's 2.5 games back of New York, but it's not impossible. I don't think the Cowboys are very good, but they might not need to be very good to win this division. title: Browns QB update: Todd Monken hasn't decided between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders for Week 10
summary: Sanders' performance against the Saints might earn another chance to start Sunday vs. the Texans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns ' quarterback situation has once again become a topic of conversation. Deshaun Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 start before an injury sidelined him for Sunday's overtime loss to the Saints . Shedeur Sanders , in defeat, played well in what was his first start of the season.
While ESPN has reported that the Browns plan to go back to Watson this Sunday against the Texans , Browns coach Todd Monken said that he was not ready to accnounce which quarterback would start vs. Houston.
"I really haven't thought through it other than getting through this morning's tape," he said. "We just got done meeting with the guys. They'll flush the game, and then we'll have a chance to meet offensively more extensive a little bit later today."
Monken was asked directly if a player can lose his job after getting injured, which would essentially be the case if Sanders stays in the starting lineup.
"I don't know what that means," he said. "Each week we put the best players on the field that give us a chance to win."
Sanders got a chance to start this past Sunday after Watson suffered a head injury during Cleveland's Week 8 loss to the Steelers . Watson, who returned to practice last Friday as a limited participant, was sacked eight times during last week's 27-6 loss. He briefly left the game early in the first quarter after taking a big hit from Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker .
Sunday was arguably Sanders' best NFL game to date. He went 19-of-31 passing for 297 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions while posting a career-high 114.6 passer rating. Sanders' big day included a 64-yard touchdown pass to rookie wideout KC Concepcion and a 39-yard scoring strike to tight end Harold Fannin Jr . in overtime. The Browns lost the game after Sanders failed to connect with Denzel Boston on Cleveland's ensuing 2-point attempt.
Sanders, a 2025 fifth-round pick, attempted just three passes during Cleveland's first eight games. Last season, he was selected as an alternative for the Pro Bowl while making seven regular-season starts. He went 3-4 as a starter while completing 56.6% of his passes with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
"Well, I'm awfully proud of him," Monken said of Sanders. "It's been 10 weeks, you know, since he had reps with the ones. ... I thought he battled. I thought he showed composure in the pocket, getting to his checkdowns at times. He made plays with his feet, and escaping. ... So there was a lot there to like. Certainly a lot to clean up, and that would be expected from a player that, you know, hasn't really had [much time] with the ones. And I thought there was a lot to build on."
If Watson gets the start, this would be his first start against his former team. The Houston Texans traded Watson to Cleveland back in 2022 in a blockbuster trade that saw Cleveland send three future first-round picks to Houston.
Watson, 31, beat out Sanders for the starting job this summer. While his play has been shaky at times, Watson has played well enough to help Cleveland get off to a surprising 5-3 start. Watson is credited with leading five game-winning drives this season, the second-most among quarterbacks this season behind only Bo Nix (6). The Browns are third in the AFC North standings behind Pittsburgh (6-2) and Cincinnati (5-2).
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Nick Sirianni says Eagles could make coaching changes as struggling offense enters bye week
summary: Philadelphia has lost seven straight games, and Nick Sirianni is evaluating everything
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have not scored more than 24 points in a game this season, and their offense has regressed even further into despair during their seven-game losing streak. As the Eagles enter their bye week in last place as the NFL's third-lowest-scoring team, coach Nick Sirianni says everything is on the table when it comes to potential changes, including shakeups on the coaching staff.
The first task for Sirianni between the Week 9 loss to the New York Giants and his next outing on Nov. 22 is to determine where the issues stem from. He took accountability for his team fielding the worst offense in the NFC East and could thus go down with the ship, but if he determines the crux of the scoring troubles falls on someone else, now would be an opportune time to make a change.
"We'll talk," Sirianni said after the 19-11 defeat. "Obviously right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there. My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches. Anything I can do to help this team win games, we'll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don't think you just change just to change."
As a first-year play-caller and the orchestrator of the system, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is under the microscope. His arrival in the offseason was supposed to help the Eagles return to prolific status on his side of the ball, but the team has done anything but that.
Sirianni deflected some of the blame directed at Mannion, though, and noted that all coaches have their hand in the offense. The Eagles will look for ways to simplify the offense during the bye week, whether or not that includes changes in leadership.
"Obviously none of us offensively have done a good enough job," Sirianni said. "We're not going to sit here as coaches -- and it's not Sean; it's all of us, and it starts with me. The correct question there, to me, is 'Do you think you've done a good enough job?' Obviously I haven't done a good enough job. We all have things we have to get better at."
Perhaps the biggest question guiding the decision-making process on potential staff changes is whether Philadelphia's woes are more a product of dysfunctional coaching or of deep personnel deficiencies. For instance, how much blame can Mannion reasonably shoulder when he is forced to call plays for backup quarterbacks in Jalen Hurts ' absence? Devonta Smith's extended absence with a hamstring injury and the loss of numerous starting offensive linemen put Mannion in a tough spot, too.
In the weeks since Hurts was shut down for the year due to blood clots, the Eagles scored 14 points, 21, 10 and 11. They lost all of those games by eight points or more. They were hardly a high-scoring team with their starting quarterback, but they are even less so without him.
"Whether it's on us as coaches or whether it's an execution thing, it's still on us as coaches," Sirianni said. "It starts with me. It's always on me. Every product that's on that field is my responsibility. There was an execution error on this play or that play. Well, did I put him in every position I could possibly put him into to go out and execute that? I'm always going to look internally first and look at myself first."

Bates would not be the first player to appear in 18 games since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, but the list is quite short.
Played 18 regular-season games since merger

Traded from Saints to Seahawks
Traded from Jets to Steelers

Of course, Bates needs to continue his excellent run of availability to join the list, but that's the track he's on now.

title: Andy Reid noncommittal on Harrison Butker's Chiefs future after another missed field goal
summary: Butker has made a career-low 63.2% of his field-goal attempts this season, while five-time All-Pro Justin Tucker waits on Kansas City's practice squad
full_text:
Andy Reid had no interest in addressing the status of Harrison Butker following the Kansas City Chiefs ' 35-12 win over the New York Jets . Butker missed another field goal (two if you count the one negated by a penalty) and was loudly booed by fans inside Arrowhead Stadium as the Chiefs went to the locker room at halftime.
Butker's initial 56-yard attempt hit the upright before he had another crack five yards closer following a penalty. His 51-yard kick with two seconds left in the second quarter sailed wide right.
"I'm sure I'll be asked about Butker. I'll address that as we go throughout the week," Reid said, unprompted . "I'll look at everything, and no need to ask. That'll be the answer that you get. I'm not making any decisions right now today."
Butker said after the game he didn't take the boos personally.
"The fans are passionate. They want [us] to win games," he said. "They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. I've got to be better."
Harrison Butker misses back-to-back attempts in similar fashion following a penalty. Chiefs fans boo loudly as they head to halftime pic.twitter.com/F1BfHbIiPT
Butker is 12-of-19 on field goal tries this season (63.2%), easily the worst accuracy rate of his 10-year career with the franchise. Butker's seven missed field goals is the most in the NFL and according to ESPN , his 17 missed kicks since the start of the 2025 season — 12 field goal tries and five PATs — also leads the league.
"I feel confident, I'm excited for the kicks, and I've just got to do better," Butker said. "Week after week, saying the same thing. Guys support me. They've seen what I've done in my 10 seasons, and they want me to be at my best. I know who I can be. I've just got to make them go in."
Butker, who's been apart of Kansas City's three Super Bowl wins during his tenure, has the support of franchise quarterback Patrick Mahomes during his season of struggle.
"We have confidence in him," Mahomes said. "That's pretty much it. I've seen him make field goals at the biggest stages that you can make in this league. I want him to know I have as much confidence in him as I've ever had, just trying to give him that vote of confidence."
The Chiefs signed veteran kicker and five-time All-Pro Justin Tucker last month to their practice squad. Tucker missed the entire 2025 season while he served a 10-game suspension following an investigation into alleged inappropriate behaviors during massage sessions.
Tucker became eligible to sign with a new team this offseason and reportedly fielded calls from several teams. After a perfect tryout, Kansas City added him, this coming after a competition with Harrison Mevis and Ben Sauls .
Chiefs special teams coordinator Dave Toub stuck by Butker after Tucker's signing last month.
"We're trying to improve Butker. We're trying to get Butker right," Toub said. "That's what this whole thing is about."

title: Bears overcome Caleb Williams' interceptions for 'SNF' win; resetting CFP race after Week 10
summary: Plus, NFL trade deadline is a day away, and we project AP Top 25 after college basketball's opening week
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Wide receiver play was off the charts to begin the third month of the NFL season. The Bengals and Packers showed off two of the best groups in the league when their top standouts went nuclear. Ja'Marr Chase, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson were among the three most impactful players in the league on Sunday when they combined for nearly 500 yards and three touchdowns.
Chase enjoyed a historic first half in Cincinnati's 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid as he racked up eight catches for 142 receiving yards in the opening half hour. Golden nearly matched those numbers in the first quarter of the Packers' rout of the Patriots alone, and he and Watson closed the day as the first pair of Packers teammates with 150 yards and a touchdown apiece in the same game since 1942.
Another one of this week's best performances actually came in a losing effort. Shedeur Sanders played some of the best football of his career in his first start of the season and made a case to remain the Browns' No. 1 quarterback , as our Zach Pereles explained.
Unfortunately, the injury bug was about as contagious this week as it has been at any point this season. Each of these big-name players dealt with something on Sunday:
November college football just hits different. An absolutely loaded Week 10 slate produced de facto College Football Playoff eliminators and shook up the front of the national championship race , so there is a lot to unpack. The projected CFP bracket now sees another new No. 1 seed and features a first-round bye for Utah , which topped BYU in a riveting top 10 rivalry battle . We gave the Utes a "B+" on our Week 10 report card for their 28-20 win, which kept them undefeated and in control of their own postseason destiny.
The biggest winner of the week, though, has to be Notre Dame . Not only did the Fighting Irish secure a cathartic win over the team that sneaked into the CFP field over them last year (leaving Miami 's Mario Cristobal furious with the officials in doing so), but they also cemented their 2026 playoff case in the process and earned a signature win for their Heisman Trophy-contending quarterback , CJ Carr . Our Shehan Jeyarajah painted the picture for Carr's award campaign.
The SEC, meanwhile, is home to one of Week 10's most significant losers. This conference is so cannibalistic that every team now owns a transitive loss to every other program, and LSU now also owns a head-to-head loss to Alabama . All of the hype around this Tigers squad has run its course now that it is 0-3 against ranked opponents. Does Lane Kiffin have a Crimson Tide problem? That might be a little bit of an overreaction , but our Brandon Marcello did point out some damning history.

title: Caleb Williams unfazed by four-interception game in Bears win: 'I don't get gun shy'
summary: Williams threw four interceptions for the first time in his football career but responded by putting Chicago in position for a game-winning field goal
full_text:
Prior to Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , quarterback Caleb Williams had never experienced a four-interception outing at any point during his football career, which includes his decorated stint at USC and several five-star high-school seasons.
And there's no need to panic, according to the Chicago Bears ' franchise player, who says he'll keep slinging it like he always has moving forward, with plenty of rounds still left in the chamber.
Unfazed by his litany of mistakes against the Bucs, Williams put Chicago in game-winning field goal position in the final seconds after a 38-yard hookup with Colston Loveland . Cairo Santos ' 38-yard boot as time expired lifted the Bears to their seventh victory.
"I'm going to throw until I can't throw anymore," Williams said . "That's how I live. I work my tail off to be in this position. I'll never not throw the ball. I could throw 100 picks in one game. If it comes down to it, I'm going to throw that pass that I did to Colston, or if it's (a) tighter window, I'm going to rip it in there. That's how I grew up. That's who I am. I don't get gun-shy. That's not me, that's not my identity, that's not who I am. With that, I'm going to keep grippin' it, keep rippin' it, and Coach calls it, it's time to go make a play."
Williams, who finished 22-of-37 for 279 yards and two scores despite four turnovers, was blitzed throughout by Tampa Bay's defense after an early 14-0 lead for Chicago quickly evaporated.
Williams suffered interceptions on three of the Bears' next four possessions — all coming in the second quarter — before he began to settle down. His fourth giveaway, an ill-advised tipped ball that was picked off by linebacker Alex Anzalone , came late in the third quarter with the Bears leading, 17-13.
Chicago pushed out front 24-13 entering the fourth after a defensive touchdown, but a couple stalled drives and a lost fumble from wideout Luther Burden led to Tampa Bay tying the game with 2:51 to play after Bucky Irving 's six-yard touchdown run was followed up by Baker Mayfield 's successful two-point conversion.
"Despite the displeasure I might be presenting right now, there's a lot of good in terms of building this team that comes from a win like this because it's like I said, one, it's hard to win under those circumstances," Bears coach Ben Johnson said. "We really haven't been in that situation where in the fourth quarter with little time left, needing to go and field goal, touchdown, whatever that is. It just hasn't happened a whole lot this year.
"And yet I feel like our guys, we are prepped for that and we're ready for it. That's what I know now after going through that. I know as a playcaller, I certainly felt great. It was as calm as I felt on calling plays there that last drive as I was all game long."
Chicago's win was only its third since 2000 with five turnovers.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Cover 32: What every team should do at NFL trade deadline, plus game balls and gaffes from Week 9
summary: Tyler Sullivan analyzes which contenders should go all-in and who needs to sell before it's too late
full_text:
There was an elephant in the room during Week 9: the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
Was it just me, or did Tuesday's deadline loom over everything? With each development, it felt as if it crystallized whether or not a team should buy, sell, or hold at the deadline. Moreover, it was hard not to watch these games through the lens of which players could be dealt and playing on a new squad by this time next week. That's what makes this weekend -- the week before the trade deadline -- so fascinating.
There's an odd finality that takes over as there are no more games to further analyze a team for what they need or should sell off. Now, it's all in the hands of the front office to either improve themselves for the stretch run or potentially move an expendable piece to help themselves down the line.
As we wrap up Week 9 and barrel towards the deadline, now is as good a time as ever to give some snap impressions on every team in the NFL and how I think they should operate before 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Chase was unstoppable in Madrid in Cincinnati's convincing 34-17 win over the Falcons. No matter what Atlanta tried to do to slow down the Bengals star receiver, they were left in the dust. This was his second straight game with at least 10 catches, 100 yards receiving, and a touchdown. That also gives him 13 such games in his career, which is the second-most in NFL history.
BURROW. JA'MARR. TOUCHDOWN. CINvsATL on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxTp4hwro5
Lamb had another prolific day as the Cowboys fended off the Colts in Indy. The wideout was targeted 16 times and turned that into 195 yards receiving, which is the second-most receiving yards in a game this season (most on the road). This was Lamb's fourth career game with at least 180 receiving yards, which is tied with Bob Hayes for the most in Cowboys history.
CEEDEE TD 🔥 📺: #DALvsIND on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/QRTQGv4NZd
Welcome back, Myles Garrett ! In his first game back since undergoing a procedure on his knee after the Week 1 opener, Garrett made his presence felt immediately. He took down Jayden Daniels three times in the 20-13 win, making the ninth career game he's tallied at least three sacks. Garrett also punched the ball free on one of those sacks on Daniels, which resulted in a Rams field goal drive right before halftime.
Myles Garrett strip sack! LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5RBIONmDIR
After cooling off over the past two weeks, Walker heated right back up in Kansas City's Week9 win over the Jets. The Chiefs back accounted for three total touchdowns in the win, which tied his career-high (2024 at Lions). Walker is the first player with five multi-touchdown games through eight games since Terrell Davis in 1998. Already, Walker is up to 1,044 scrimmage yards and 11 scrimmage touchdowns this season.
Mahomes to Walker again! NYJvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9NbsfKzOBB
We talked about this a few weeks ago ; C.J. Stroud is balling out. The Texans quarterback has reestablished himself as a top quarterback in the NFL and just tossed five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Chargers. This was the second career game that Stroud posted at least five passing touchdowns and is just the second quarterback in franchise history to have multiple five-plus passing touchdown games.
C.J. Stroud and Kayshon Boutte with a 63-yard TD 👏 HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d6CjZxnTHH
Jordan Love and the Packers steamrolled the Patriots in Foxborough, 45-27. The Green Bay QB totaled four touchdowns in the winning effort and was dialed in from the jump. His 372 passing yards were the third-most in any game of his career. He's also just the second Packers quarterback with at least 270 passing yards in five straight games, joining Aaron Rodgers (did it four times).
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
CeeDee Lamb makes a diving catch He doesn't get touched Gets up and picks up several yards Fumbles while getting tackled Colts recover it after the play is reviewed FOOTBALL DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ApA5vJgMM4
One of the wildest plays of Week 9 came in the Cowboys-Colts matchup in the early seconds of the fourth quarter. Dak Prescott completed a deep ball to a sliding CeeDee Lamb , but Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris didn't touch him. Lamb realized he was untouched, got up, and ran all the way to the Indy 13-yard line. That's when Lamb fumbled, and the loose ball was recovered by the Colts.
Dan Quinn made another puzzling late-game decision. Thanks, in part, to a 42-yard catch-and-run by Stefon Diggs, the Commanders had the ball at the Rams' 31-yard line with seconds left in regulation and down by seven. One would think that Jayden Daniels would drop back and throw a prayer to the end zone in hopes of tying the game and forcing overtime, particularly as they were well within throwing range.
Instead, Daniels threw underneath for tight end Chig Okonkwo over 10 yards away from the end zone. After a lateral, the ball was fumbled and recovered by the Rams for the win.
The final play of Rams vs. Commanders featuring some laterals pic.twitter.com/9M7WYnoC2w
This is Washington simply getting too cute. At that point in the game, opt for the Hail Mary and hope for the best. Not even attempting a touchdown was ... interesting, to say the least.
Harrison Butker's struggles continued in Week 9 and included one of the major blunders of the slate. Just before halftime, the Chiefs lined up for a 56-yard field goal, but Butker's attempt was no good to the right. However, the Jets were called for an offsides penalty, which not only gave Butker another chance to put up points, but also inched him even closer for a 51-yard attempt. Despite the second attempt, he again missed wide right.
Harrison Butker misses back-to-back attempts in similar fashion following a penalty. Chiefs fans boo loudly as they head to halftime pic.twitter.com/F1BfHbIiPT
Butker has missed a total of 17 kicks since the start of last season, which is the most in the NFL over that span.
If you are a fantasy football manager that has Jonathan Taylor on your squad, you were vultured by Seth McGowan in the most peculiar way. During Indy's second possession of the day, Taylor brought the Colts to the Dallas 2-yard line after a 6-yard line. On the play, Taylor lost his shoe, which required him to go to the sideline. McGowan came in and scored on the ensuing play.
Jonathan Taylor loses a shoe, giving Seth McGowan a chance at a goal line carry which he converts into his first NFL touchdown! Awesome for him. Horrible for fantasy managers. pic.twitter.com/mil6bMm4mA
That was McGowan's first career touchdown.
The Saints first-round pick made his NFL debut on Sunday, but had a rookie blunder amid the team's overtime victory over the Browns. Tyson recorded his first career catch on a second-and-10 pass from Tyler Shough at the Cleveland 11-yard line, and it looked like he might score. As he dove towards the goal line, however, Tyson didn't protect the football well enough, and Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger punched the ball free.
Carson Schwesinger punches the ball loose for a Browns takeaway! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/t5eYGIrmOM
Tyson finished his debut with four catches for 30 yards to go along with that fumble.
During halftime of the Broncos-Panthers matchup, Bank of America Stadium held a corgi race. However, after the festivities, one of the dogs went rogue and was running all over the field. The corgi, named Lennox, bobbed and weaved a number of would-be tacklers before ultimately being run down.
Corgi loose on the pitch in Carolina! 🐾…

title: NFL Week 10 early odds: Trade deadline could shake up lines for Chiefs, Colts and more
summary: A Jonathan Taylor trade or a Chiefs acquisition could reshape several spreads, adding another layer of uncertainty
full_text:
When it comes to betting on the NFL, it's sometimes advantageous to jump on lines early. While that can remain the case for Week 10, there is another variable that bettors need to account for this go-around: the trade deadline. Between now and when the action kicks off on Thursday between the Commanders and Giants , a slew of trades will have gone down. And lines will move.
For instance, Jonathan Taylor is currently a member of the Indianapolis Colts , but will that remain the case by 4:01 p.m. ET on Tuesday? If he's dealt, how much does that shift Indy's line with the Dolphins , where they're slotted as a 2.5-point favorite at home? What if the Kansas City Chiefs make a move for a wide receiver? That would almost certainly shift the line in their matchup with the Falcons , where they are currently a 3.5-point road favorite.
It's those types of moves that take center stage and could have the midweek lines moving more than they have the entire season. With all that in mind, let's dive into these early odds to see how the oddsmakers are stacking up Week 10 prior to Tuesday's deadline.
Note : Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, and Tampa Bay are on the bye in Week 10.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Commanders at Giants (Thursday)
Commanders +105, Gaints -125
Patriots at Lions (in Germany)
Panthers -120, Saints +100
Vikings +142, Packers -170
Seahawks -166, Raiders +140
Steelers +142, Bengals -170
Chargers at Ravens (Monday)
Chargers +154, Ravens -185
New York sits as a slim 1.5-point favorite in this NFC East matchup with the Commanders. Of course, these two clubs tied earlier this season, but the Giants are a different team this time around. Jameis Winston was under center for that contest, and now it'll be J.J. McCarthy , who briefly exited Sunday's win with a hip injury . The Giants are 6-2 ATS on the season, which includes a 3-1 ATS record at home. Washington is 2-1 ATS on the road.
New England opened as a 1.5-point favorite for this international game in Munich, but that has since changed. In the aftermath of a blowout defeat at the hands of the Packers at Gillette Stadium, New England finds itself as an underdog to Detroit, who is now laying 2.5. Neither of these teams has been particularly strong clubs to back this season, as the Lions are 3-4-1 ATS while the Patriots are 3-5-1 ATS. The Over might be the play for this game, however, as it's 11-6 between them entering Week 10.
Both teams are well rested. The Jags initially opened as a 10-point favorite, but that has ticked down to -9.5. Liam Coen's team is 5-3 ATS this season, including a 2-1 ATS mark on the road. Meanwhile, Tennessee hasn't defended Nissan Stadium that well in 2026 as they're 1-3 ATS at home.
Carolina is a 1.5-point road favorite over the division rival Saints in what will be their first of two matchups this season. The Panthers are looking to snap a three-game losing skid after losing to the Broncos at home. They are 2-2 ATS on the road so far in 2026, while New Orleans is still looking for its first ATS victory at the Superdome this season. Coming into Week 10, the Saints are 0-4 ATS at home.
Houston came out of its bye week looking like a true playoff threat, despite a 3-5 record, after C.J. Stroud tossed five touchdowns in a win over the Chargers. Now, they're gearing up as a 4.5-point road favorite against the Browns. Houston is 2-1 ATS on the road this season, and all of those games saw them as road favorites. Still, this won't be an easy task for them in Week 10 as the Browns are a perfect 3-0 ATS at home this season.
Buffalo opened as a 7.5-point favorite, and that line has since moved to -8.5. Of course, this line could move again depending on how the Bills matchup against the Vikings on Monday night unfolds, but enter that game 5-2 ATS. As for the Jets, they're looking to snap a four-game losing streak, with the most recent defeat coming in Kansas City, where the Chiefs put up 35 points while the Jets mustered 12. New York is 4-4-1 ATS on the season and is 2-2 ATS at MetLife Stadium. The one advantage that the Jets will have is that Buffalo will be playing on the road on a short week.
This line could move depending on whether the Colts decide to trade Taylor, Daniel Jones , or even Josh Downs before the deadline, so you may want to proceed with caution here. That said, they are 2.5-point favorites at home against Miami. The Dolphins are 2-2 ATS on the road this season, while Indy is 2-2 ATS at Lucas Oil Stadium. The latest reports state that Jones will stay in Indianapolis.
Minnesota still has its Monday night matchup with the Bills, so this game could see some movement. That said, Green Bay has opened as a 3-point favorite after a dominating road win over the Patriots. Jordan Love totaled four touchdowns in the win, but should face much tougher sledding against a stout Vikings defense. In the Week 1 opener, the Vikings beat the Packers at home, 39-22. In that defeat, Love committed two turnovers. With this game being played at Lambeau Field, it's worth noting Green Bay is 3-1 ATS at home this season. However, Minnesota is 3-1 ATS on the road.
Kansas City picked up the hook and is now laying 3.5 points to the Falcons as a road favorite after initially opening as a 3-point favorite. Despite the confidence of the oddsmakers, the Chiefs are just 1-3 ATS on the road this season. However, Atlanta is coming back from an international game in Madrid on Sunday, which certainly contributes to this line. The Chiefs are also just a better club and seemingly dodged a bullet with Patrick Mahomes after he injured his elbow in Week 9 but finished the game, and MRI results showed no damage.
Seattle is a 3-point favorite on the road in Las Vegas, and this is another game to keep an eye on from a trade deadline perspective. While it sounds like it's unlikely, if the Raiders trade Kirk Cousins , that'd put Fernando Mendoza in for his first-career start. Under that circumstance, one would imagine this line moving even further in the direction of the Seahawks. However, the defending champions are dealing with QB injuries. After missing Week 9 with a quad injury, Sam Darnold is reportedly not a lock to return in Week 10. Meanwhile, top backup Drew Lock is dealing with an oblique injury that he suffered in Week 9, which has his status up in the air as well. The Seahawks are 1-2 ATS on the road this season, while the Raiders are 3-1 ATS at home.
Los Angeles opened as an 8.5-point favorite, but that has since come down to -7. That could be due to the uncertain status of Puka Nacua , who sustained a knee injury on the Rams' final offensive play of the day in their win over Washington. If he misses time, it further dents their offense, which was already without Davante Adams . L.A. is 3-1 ATS on the road, while the Cardinals -- who could trade pieces before Tuesday's deadline -- are 0-3 ATS at home.
San Francisco is a 4.5-point road favorite as they gear up for a matchup against the Cowboys. Both clubs are coming off of wins in Week 9, with San Francisco taking down the Raiders while Dallas fended off the Colts. As a road favorite, the Niners are 0-1 ATS. Overall, they're 2-1 ATS on the road. Meanwhile, Dallas is just 1-2 ATS at AT&T Stadium, but has yet to be a home underdog this season. Last season, the Cowboys were 3-0 as a home underdog.
Cincinnati's offense has been on a tear in recent weeks, thanks in large part to Joe Burrow looking like an MVP candidate. That's, in part, why they are a 3.5-point favorite as they host the Steelers. However, as good as the Bengals offense has looked in recent weeks, this is a tough spot for them. Despite being favorites, the Bengals are coming home after playing in Madrid and will face a Steelers team that was just on its bye, creating quite the rest disparity. Cincinnati is 1-2 ATS at home this season, while Pittsburgh is 1-2 ATS on the road, so something will need to give.
Baltimore will likely start Jacoby Brissett for this…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Who's buying, who's selling, plus biggest names, led by Jonathan Taylor
summary: Plus, there are a few wild cards in play ahead of Tuesday's deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, and the hours until then will be filled with anticipation and landscape-shifting moves. This season has already seen the Bears acquire defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans , the Seahawks acquire guard Quenton Nelson from the Colts and the 49ers acquire defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Colts. That's a combined 15 Pro Bowl selections on the move. Add in trades for Jacoby Brissett ( Cardinals to Ravens ), Marvin Harrison Jr . (Cardinals to Texans ) and Joey Porter Jr . ( Steelers to Cowboys ), and it's been hectic already.
It will get even more hectic. Last year, both Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams got dealt on deadline day, and those were just the headliners. As the deadline nears, we delve into buyers, sellers and teams who could go either way.
Potential adds: WR, OL, CB
Chiefs GM Brett Veach told NFL on CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson that Kansas City is looking to acquire a wide receiver . Considering Patrick Mahomes has not completed a pass 20+ yards downfield since Week 4, when Tyquan Thornton got hurt, the Chiefs could have their eye on a serious threat. Kansas City's group has been among the least productive wide receiver units across the league this year, with former first-round pick Xavier Worthy struggling to produce and Rashee Rice functioning more as a quick-game, YAC option.
Kansas City (5-2) could also look to add along the offensive line, where there's been a lot of mixing and matching this year.
Potential adds: QB, RB, OL
The Vikings could hold the keys to how wild this trade deadline gets considering their quarterback situation: Minnesota will start Carson Wentz on "Monday Night Football" with Kyler Murray (hamstring) out. But even when healthy this year, Murray has struggled. The Vikings have leaned heavily on their defense en route to a 6-1 start this year, and they could look to really push their chips in by adding a new signal caller. Who is available and for what price, though, remains to be seen.
Another way to help the offense could be adding a running back. Minnesota has one of the league's worst ground attacks, with Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr. not especially productive.
Potential adds: RB, DL, DE
At 5-2-1, the Giants are the surprise NFC East leader despite having started three different quarterbacks. New York has been strongly connected on both sides of the ball, with running back and defensive line the top positional needs. The Giants have used a rotation of running backs throughout the year, but Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missed Week 9, and Tyrone Tracy Jr . (hamstring) is on IR. John Harbaugh came from Baltimore, where he had Derrick Henry , and has talked about the value of a bell-cow back.
New York could also look to add in the defensive trenches, where veterans D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris have played well, but depth could be a concern.
The Bills could use all the defensive help they can get in their quest to finally get over the Super Bowl hump. The secondary, in particular, is suspect. Safety has been a need for several years, and Buffalo should be pushing hard considering its 6-1 record and its terrific offense.
If not safety, the Bills could look to add at cornerback, where the options outside established starter Christian Benford have been up-and-down at best.
Potential adds: DT, OL, WR
Jacksonville continues to roll along, now 6-2 and winner of five of its last six. GM James Gladstone has never been afraid to be bold, having traded up for Travis Hunter in his first NFL draft and acquiring Jakobi Meyers at last year's deadline.
It's not very bold to predict Jacksonville will make another move this time around. It had been reported that the Jaguars were looking for defensive tackle help even before stout run defender DaVon Hamilton's season-ending injury, and now they are even more in the market for help on the interior . On the other side of the ball, tackle depth could be helpful after Anton Harrison's season-ending injury.
Kyle Shanahan was coy Sunday when talking about potential trades, but even after the Buckner add, San Francisco (7-1) could look to do more. The wide receiver room -- and really the entire roster -- has been ravaged by injury this season. That trend continued Sunday, when key rookie defensive lineman Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending broken ankle. Both of those positions could be places the NFC West leaders want to add to for a playoff push.
Potential players for sale: RB Jonathan Taylor , WR Josh Downs , DL Grover Stewart , WR Keenan Allen
Taylor is the name of this trade deadline, and he has already seemingly said goodbye to Indianapolis. The three-time Pro Bowler remains an elite rusher, though the Colts' abysmal offensive environment has limited his effectiveness this year. He is a certified home run hitter but also has a terrific nose for the end zone; he led the NFL with 18 rushing touchdowns last year. Downs has requested a trade, and Stewart, a pillar along the Indy defensive line for years, is in the final year of his deal.
Potential players for sale: EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu , EDGE Khalil Mack , CB Donte Jackson
Before you ask, the Chargers have reportedly made it clear they have no plans to trade quarterback Justin Herbert . But reports also say they have no plans to move anyone , including Mack, the 35-year-old former star on a one-year deal. Tuipulotu, in the final year of his rookie contract, would undoubtedly attract plenty of suitors. The Chargers are the NFL's only winless team, and amid a nightmare year, adding draft capital seems like an attractive option.
Potential players for sale: CB Riq Woolen, DL Moro Ojomo
Woolen, on a one-year deal, and Ojomo, in the final year of his rookie contract, seem to be the most notable names on the block. Pretty much everything has gone wrong for Philadelphia this year, from injuries to underperformance to an unexpected Lane Johnson retirement. The Eagles already traded away Cam Jurgens earlier this season, it should be noted, and GM Howie Roseman had already started accruing future draft capital with the A.J. Brown trade over the offseason.
Potential players for sale: S Budda Baker , EDGE Josh Sweat , DT Roy Lopez
Baker has seemingly spent countless trade deadlines in the rumor mill, but Arizona has more offerings than just the Pro Bowl safety. Sweat and Lopez could provide major value for buying teams, with Sweat at a premium position and Lopez at a position seemingly every contender wants to improve at ahead of the stretch run. Arizona has shown some nice signs early in their rebuild and already parted with Harrison, proving they're willing to move veterans for the right price.
Potential adds: Everywhere on defense Potential player for sale: WR George Pickens
The Cowboys are permanently in wild-card territory when it comes to potential personnel moves. Such is life under Jerry Jones. Dallas has already traded for Porter, but the defense continues to struggle, and Porter hasn't been healthy. Meanwhile, Pickens missed Sunday's game due to injury. Would Dallas really consider trading the talented but mercurial wide receiver who's on the franchise tag? Could Jones both buy and sell? It's hard to rule out anything with this team, which sits at 4-5 on the year but still within shouting distance in the NFC East.
Potential adds: RB, LB, DB
The wild card here is how willing the Bengals are to go all in ... again. Cincinnati loaded up on defense in free agency and traded the No. 10 overall pick for Dexter Lawrence shortly thereafter. Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , looking nearly unstoppable over the past few weeks, have done nothing but further heighten the Super Bowl aspirations. Would adding a running back truly take this offense over the top? Would a defensive stalwart help prevent so many big plays? The Bengals could have a huge say in this deadline ... or they could go quietly.
