title: Are the Broncos the NFL's luckiest Super Bowl contender? Their 7-2 start is unlike anything we've ever seen
summary: Denver keeps winning despite historically troubling numbers. Here's how they're pulling it off -- and what history says happens next.
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 7-2. They've won five straight, Bo Nix keeps engineering fourth-quarter comebacks, and they've somehow won an NFL-record 16 consecutive one-score games dating to last season.
Oh, and they've been outgained by 699 yards through nine games. It's the worst yardage differential in NFL history for a team with at least seven wins at this point in the season. The previous low was the 2010 Patriots at minus-469, and Denver blew past that mark with 230 yards to spare.
But here's what's even harder to wrap your head around: Denver was also 7-2 through nine games last season, when it had outgained opponents by 607 yards. That's a 1,306-yard swing in the wrong direction, the largest year-over-year decline among teams that started at least 7-2 in consecutive seasons going back to 2000.
Same record, completely different team. So: Are the Broncos actually good, or are they just remarkably good at winning games they probably shouldn't?
Start with this: Denver has been outgained in seven of nine games, including five victories. To put that in perspective, only two of the 126 teams that started 7-2 or better this century spent less time playing with a lead.
Against the Rams in Week 3, Denver was outgained by 225 yards, trailed for more than 39 minutes and led for exactly 118 seconds. They won anyway, 30-26.
They've also beaten the Jaguars and Chiefs despite leading for fewer than 10 minutes in each of those games. And six of their seven victories have come by eight points or fewer.
Here's how unusual that is.
The worst yardage differentials by teams starting 7-2 or better
The Broncos aren't just an outlier; they're making the other outliers look ordinary. They've scored just 12 more points than they've allowed all season, the third-smallest point differential among 126 teams that started 7-2 or better since 2000. Based on that plus-12 margin, Denver should be closer to 5-4 than 7-2.
No one told them that. And that difference between actual and expected wins? It's one of the 12 largest through nine games in the past 26 years.
Nix has already engineered five fourth-quarter comebacks, tied for the most through nine games since 1950 , according to CBS Sports Research. He's not consistently playing at the level of, say, draft classmate Caleb Williams, but when Denver needs a score, he's delivered.
The defense has done its part, coming up with sacks and turnovers when Denver needs them most. The Broncos have forced 12 turnovers while committing just seven, but here's the twist: Despite that advantage, they've actually been outscored 41-39 on points off turnovers. So it's not as simple as the defense creating easy points for the offense.
Special teams have helped, as well. The Broncos average 44.2 net yards per punt, although kicking half the time in Denver's thin air certainly helps. What's more impressive, though, is their ability to pin opponents deep: Nine punts have landed inside the 10-yard line, putting Denver in the top 4% of all NFL teams we looked at through their first nine games.
And here's something encouraging for Denver: The offense might finally be finding its rhythm. After struggling through the first six games, Bo Nix and Co. have played their best football over the past three weeks, with the passing game improving in five straight games. The timing couldn't be better, because the defense has taken a step back over the past two weeks.
Maybe Nix and Sean Payton are figuring things out. Or maybe it's a blip that won't last. Either way, the Broncos aren't winning exactly the same way they were a month ago.
Since 2000, 125 teams started 7-2 or better. A grand total of 18 were outgained over that stretch.
Those 18 teams won 56.6% of their remaining regular-season games. The other 107 won 68.6%. That's a meaningful difference, but it's hardly a guarantee that Denver is about to fall apart.
What happened next to teams starting 7-2 or better?
Win % rest of regular season
The 2010 Patriots offer some encouragement. They were outgained by 469 yards through nine games, then won their final seven regular-season games to finish 14-2.
The 2012 Ravens are an even better example. They were 7-2 despite a minus-325 yardage differential, finished 10-6 and won the Super Bowl when Joe Flacco got red hot in the playoffs. Of course, the 2022 Vikings went 13-4 despite being outgained for the entire season, then lost their first playoff game.
Put another way: teams can keep winning without dominating. Winning a championship that way is considerably harder, although Baltimore proved it's possible.
And that's the challenge for Denver. The good news is that they have seven wins through nine weeks, are now on their bye, and still have games against the Raiders (twice), Dolphins, Jets and Chargers.
The Broncos have found ways to win despite getting pushed around for much of the season. But counting on late-game heroics every week isn't a long-term solution, and it's why trading for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor could go from pipe dream to reality.
Would Jonathan Taylor be a great fit in Denver? 🤔 @advancereport says YES! #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/ehLiuZ5gR9
Maybe Nix's recent improvement is a sign the offense is turning a corner. Add a player like Taylor, and the Broncos would have a more reliable running game, taking pressure off the third-year quarterback and giving Payton more ways to manage games without depending on fourth-quarter comebacks.
History tells us teams can keep winning this way. How long they can keep it up is another question. For nine games, Denver has made winning ugly look easy. January will tell us whether that's a winning formula or a warning sign.
author: Ryan Wilson

title: NFL Week 9 grades for every team: Patriots among two teams with failing grades, Cowboys barely pass
summary: We're handing out grades for every team that played in Week 9
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 9 grades!

author: John Breech

title: Titans' Calvin Ridley involved in 'incident' at Nashville International Airport, per report
summary: Ridley has been the subject of trade rumors in recent weeks
full_text:
Tennessee Titans wideout Calvin Ridley was involved in an "incident" at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, according to WKRN . The Titans were on a bye this week. What took place is unclear, but the Titans organization did confirm to WKRN that an incident took place.
"We are aware of the incident and are in communication with Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority," the Titans said in a statement at the time of the incident. "We will not be able to comment any further at this time."
Titans head coach Robert Saleh also addressed the story during his Monday morning press conference .
"With regards to Calvin, we're aware of everything that's happening," Saleh said. "From my understanding, it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport. Unfortunately, the law enforcements have it, and that's as far as I can go on commenting."
This incident is notable given that Ridley has been the subject of trade speculation in recent weeks. He has not been a major part of the Titans' rotation at receiver, having played just 52.8% of offensive snaps this season. In seven games played, Ridley has caught just six passes for 91 yards. ESPN reported that he could be had for a late-round pick should an interested team come calling. Carnell Tate , Wan'Dale Robinson , Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike have been Cam Ward's top four receivers up to this point.
Ridley signed a four-year, $92 million deal with the Titans in 2024 after one season with the Jacksonville Jaguars . He caught 64 passes for 1,017 yards and four touchdowns in his first season with the Titans, then broke his fibula in November of last year. Ridley turns 32 next month, and has three 1,000-yard seasons to his name.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Drew Lock suffers oblique injury, Week 10 status up in the air: Seahawks could have to start Jalen Milroe
summary: Lock was already filling in for Sam Darnold, who missed Week 9 with quad and rib injuries
full_text:
Drew Lock sustained an oblique injury in the Seattle Seahawks ' Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals , and his status for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders is uncertain, Mike Macdonald said. The injury briefly sent Lock to the medical tent.
Lock entered the game dealing with elbow tendinitis and was only playing because Sam Darnold was out due to quad and ribs injuries. Darnold suffered the quad injury neat the end of Seattle's Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears and has been playing through a cracked rib.
Lock, making his second start in place of Darnold this season, went 19 for 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown in the 17-3 victory., though he was clearly not 100%.
Drew Lock and Seattle get it done vs the Cardinals. @MeganOlivi caught up with the @Seahawks QB after the win pic.twitter.com/e4xeJi2NCX
If neither Lock nor Darnold can play in Week 10, the Seahawks (5-4) would turn to third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe . They also have Adrian Martinez on their practice squad.
The Seahawks have little room for error. Entering "Sunday Night Football," the reigning champs were the No. 8 seed in the NFC, one spot out of the playoffs.
The Seahawks took Milroe, an Alabama product, in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft .
Milroe, now 23, had an up-and-down career with the Crimson Tide. In 2023 as a redshirt sophomore, he threw for 2,834 yards, 23 touchdowns and just six interceptions and added 531 yards and 12 touchdowns on the ground. He finished sixth in Heisman Trophy voting. That seemed to set the stage for a monster 2024, but instead, Milroe regressed as a passer and threw 11 interceptions. He still had 726 yards and 20 touchdowns on the ground, but it was not the follow-up he had been hoping for.
Should he be needed next week, Milroe would drastically alter the Seahawks' attack, making it likely more run-heavy. He has played three career NFL snaps and ran on all three for a total of 4 yards. Seattle did have one of its better ground performances Sunday with 120 yards, and the Raiders do struggle to defend the run.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Patrick Mahomes injury update: MRI reveals no significant damage to Chiefs QB's elbow
summary: An MRI revealed no significant injury after Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly
full_text:
Late in the first half of their blowout victory over the New York Jets , the Kansas City Chiefs got a significant scare. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass on a second-and-4 play coming out of the two-minute warning, and as he attempted to throw the ball downfield, his arm was hit by Jets edge rusher David Bailey . His elbow bent awkwardly backward, and he left the field with his right arm hanging by his side.
Mahomes already underwent an MRI after the game and it did not reveal a significant injury, according to ESPN . He will be monitored for pain and swelling throughout the week.
Patrick Mahomes was holding his elbow after this hit pic.twitter.com/jyzMdNfkwR
Mahomes ultimately didn't have to miss a snap because the Jets recovered the fumble on the play, and by the time the Chiefs got the ball back, Mahomes had gotten his arm warm while throwing on the sideline. He returned to play the rest of the game and finished the day 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, each on passes to Kenneth Walker III .
Mahomes, later in his postgame interview, said he didn't feel like himself at first when he came back into the game after the scare, but that things gradually improved as he settled into the second half.
"I felt like out of the half, I wasn't throwing the ball the way I wanted to," he said. "As the game went on — and we continued to work through it and it kind of got warmed back up — I thought I started throwing the ball better towards the end of the second half. That will be important this week is kind of getting the swelling and the fluid out of it so I can be ready to go from the first snap next week."
Mahomes further noted that he felt just fine after the game, but that he would have to go through the usual process to get himself ready for the Chiefs' Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons .
"I feel good now," he said. "Obviously, you get the win and the adrenaline's pumping. I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it. We'll get to work on it, and we'll get ourselves ready to go. It's great to get the win now, now it's about getting ourselves ready for next week."
author: Jared Dubin

title: Daniel Jones trade rumors: Colts tell QB he will not be dealt before NFL deadline, per report
summary: The 2-7 Colts have taken Daniel Jones off the market, even as Jonathan Taylor and several teammates remain names to watch
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts told quarterback Daniel Jones they will not trade him before Tuesday's deadline, according to Tom Pelissero.
Indianapolis (2-7) received calls for Jones with the trade deadline looming. The Colts, who already traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers , remain among the central characters on the trade market. Most eyes will be on star running back Jonathan Taylor , who said a goodbye of sorts to Indianapolis after Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys , but Josh Downs and Grover Stewart are potential names to watch, too.
Apparently, Jones will not be joining them. It's been a mess of a year in Indianapolis, which has already fired general manager Chris Ballard, and that has extended to Jones. This season, he has been among the league's worst quarterbacks.
Jones' surroundings have been far from ideal, with Alec Pierce -- signed to an extension this past offseason -- missing almost the entire season after aggravating the ankle injury he had surgery on this offseason. Currently, Keenan Allen leads the team in receptions (40), and Downs leads the team in receiving yards (354).
The Vikings seemed to be a potential tie to Jones, who spent time with Minnesota's practice squad two seasons ago. Minnesota has struggled offensively with Kyler Murray and is starting Carson Wentz on Monday as Murray deals with a hamstring injury. It's unknown, though, which teams had been in contact regarding Jones' availability.
Jones, who is a team captain, signed a two-year, $88 million extension this past offseason, though the Colts have a potential out after this season that would leave them with $35.2 million of dead cap. Indianapolis does not own its first-round pick due to last season's Sauce Gardner trade, so perhaps the Colts envision keeping Jones around as a placeholder next year. Regardless, he will be around at least for the rest of this season.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 9 overreactions: Joe Burrow or Jordan Love for MVP? Shedeur Sanders deserves to remain starter?
summary: Plus, speaking of MVPs, last year's is struggling
full_text:
There are lots of ways to break down an NFL game, but sometimes, it's as simple as "my guy is better than your guy." The Jimmys and the Joes matter more than the X's and the O's.
Or, rather, the Ja'Marrs and the Joes (and the Tees). The Bengals went to Spain and thumped the Falcons , 34-17, behind four total touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) by Joe Burrow . Ja'Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins had five catches for 47 yards and two scores.
Chase and Higgins are so, so good. CBS Sports NFL writer Jared Dubin had an excellent piece earlier this week about Higgins' breakout, but Sunday, Chase reminded everyone why he's either the best receiver or, at worst, one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. In the first half alone, Chase had eight catches for 142 yards and a score. He does it every which way: deep, intermediate, short. Over the middle or along the sideline. Open or contested catch. Yards after catch or before. Doesn't matter. This is receiving at its best.
Ja'Marr Chase's first half in Madrid... 142 yards, 8 catches, 47-yard touchdown 🔥 CINvsATL on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dqBRCHgTFJ
Chase and Higgins are the best wide receiver duo in the NFL -- it's not close --and, halfway through the year, they have us leading our overreactions and reality checks with ...
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
Here's Burrow's start to the season:
According to CBS Sports research, Burrow is the first player ever with a 70% completion percentage and four total touchdowns in four straight games. Not coincidentally, the Bengals have won four straight.
Burrow has great wide receivers, but that should not take away too much from his candidacy, especially when you consider how bad the running game is and how inconsistent the defense has been.
There are a few things holding me back from declaring Burrow the MVP winner -- in terms of odds, he's currently right next to Josh Allen as the favorite (+210 at DraftKings , but that could move around depending on when you're reading this). There's a long way to go; the weather will turn, and Burrow's checkered health history is worth noting. But if we had to name an MVP right now, it'd be Burrow, who has been truly excellent.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
Here's Jordan Love's so far this season:
Thank goodness "first-half MVP" isn't a real award, because I have no clue how I'd vote. Love has supported an even more anemic rushing attack this season: Green Bay gets under 20% of its yards on the ground, on pace for the worst mark since the 1970 merger. And also, he's been hurt by the league's highest drop rate.
Yes, Love has a better defense supporting him, but he has been stupendous, lifting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden into stardom alongside him. They became the first Green Bay wide receiver duo to both have 150+ yards and a touchdown in a single game as the Packers shredded the Patriots .
Love has the NFL's most completions 20+ yards downfield (23), and his deep ball is truly a thing of beauty.
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
Oh yeah, and Brock Purdy and Josh Allen have been pretty good, too. The MVP race will be a wild one.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
Many times, the box score lies. Not so for Shedeur Sanders . You just have to make sure to read all of it:
The 23-22 loss to the Saints will leave a bad taste in the mouth after what was otherwise a solid performance, especially given the circumstances. Cleveland's offensive line was abysmal, as has been the case much of the year, and the run game didn't help at all. There were also multiple drops.
But there were several things Sanders delivered that Deshaun Watson simply doesn't. How about three completions on throws 30+ yards downfield? Watson has one ... all year!
DENZEL BOSTON MOSSED HIM pic.twitter.com/ZZdzSZtnpj
SHEDEUR TO KC CONCEPCION 64-YARD TD FOR THE LEAD! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Zs6x4Ko8SO
Sanders also did excellently in several moments navigating the pressure. Was he great? No. The sacks are a major issue, and he invites some of the pressure on himself with how he holds onto the ball. But he also had an 11-yard scramble on a third-and-6 and, later, a 5-yard scramble on third-and-4.
Furthermore, let's remember this was his first start of the year in a new system. After a very poor start, Sanders threw for 259 yards after halftime .
Coaches rarely bench players due to injury, so I wouldn't be surprised if Watson returns to the lineup. Todd Monken refused to talk about it postgame . But in this writer's eyes, Sanders should keep the job.
Overreaction or reality check: Reality
The Rams are above .500 for the first time this year after outlasting the Commanders , 20-13. The Rams force-fed Puka Nacua (19 targets for 14 catches, 150 yards and a touchdown) and got just enough for the run game. Myles Garrett came back in full force with three sacks and a forced fumble. At 5-4 and winners of three straight -- and with the Cardinals up next -- Los Angeles should feel OK.
But Matthew Stafford just does not look good. Plain and simple. He threw an awful interception after locking in on Nacua, with no chance of completion.
Nick Cross picks off Stafford! LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/S8wex6qoAy
He's throwing an awful interception seemingly every week. He has nine picks through nine games. This was last week's.
Intercepted by Tarheeb Still ‼️ LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/N3Iqc8430g
Stafford missed a ton of throws he made routinely during his 2025 MVP campaign. Sunday alone, he missed an open Tyler Higbee on an out-breaking route; he missed Tutu Atwell twice -- once wide, once high -- and missed Nacua once, too, this time low.
Last year, Stafford completed 43% of his throws 20+ yards downfield and had a 10-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio on those throws. This year: 24% completion rate and a 1-to-3 touchdown-to-interception ratio.
The Rams can still be a good team. The defense looks excellent, and Garrett makes the pass rush truly terrifying. The Rams have found a physical run game during this winning streak, too. But at some point, they will need Stafford to play like his 2025 self, and it just doesn't look like he has that anymore.
Overreaction or reality check: Overreaction
The Eagles lost their seventh straight game Sunday, dropping an 19-11 eyesore to the Giants . It's Philadelphia's second-longest losing streak this century, and Nick Sirianni's bunch now sits at 2-7 on this dreadful year.
The Eagles used their third different starting quarterback (Joe Milton) of the season, and he looked like ... well ... a third-string quarterback who didn't even start the year with the team, which is exactly what he is. He completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards and ran for 64 yards, balancing out some fun moments with several frustrating ones. The defense had a much better day overall, especially considering the poor efforts it had put forth the previous few weeks.
Listen, everything has gone wrong for the Eagles. Jalen Hurts is done for the year. The offensive line has been in upheaval ever since Week 1. DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley have been hurt. And that's precisely why the Eagles shouldn't fire Nick Sirianni, now or at any point this season. Philadelphia has a first-year offensive coordinator, Sean Mannion, who would be best served by a stable environment. Same with Milton, who should continue to start all year. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio does not want to be a head coach again at this point in his career.
It's ok to have worst-case-scenario years and not make it worse, especially as you're just playing out the string. Maybe Sirianni gets fired after the year, but the team hasn't given up, and it needs what little stability it has.
Overreaction or reality check: Overreaction
The Giants' win puts…

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Seahawks Winners & Losers: Arizona has offensive issues in loss
summary: The Arizona Cardinals know that the maiden season of being under new head coach Mike LaFleur is over. It’s not. But it begins with a win on the road against division foe Seattle Seahawks, who beat Arizona 31-7 earlier on the schedule. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSE BACK TO BEING INEPT The Cardinals needed a win. They […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals know that the maiden season of being under new head coach Mike LaFleur is over. It’s not. But it begins with a win on the road against division foe Seattle Seahawks, who beat Arizona 31-7 earlier on the schedule. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSE BACK TO BEING INEPT The Cardinals needed a win. They may not make the playoffs, or vie for the division lead, but they can win 8-9 games which would become something positive to build on. Against Seattle, the Cardinals marched down the field on their first possession and scored a field goal to take a 3-0 lead. But that was the highlight, as the offense could not move the ball, and the punter was the game’s MVP. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS S Budda Baker – The dependable one just keeps racking up good tackling numbers. He had seven just in the first half alone. Ready for some AZ Cardinal football ‼️ pic.twitter.com/h3jNwpcaVp — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 8, 2026 In the second quarter, Baker read the run and was able to stop RB Jadarian Price for a short gain. In the third quarter, it was Baker who nailed RB Zach Charbonnet after a seven-yard gain on the third-and-15. Had the second most tackles with 11. P Blake Gillikin – In the first half, Gillikin was called on to kick four times and had 184 yards with a long of 55 yards. Half of those punts landed inside the 20. Finished with six punts for 269 yards and a 44.8 yards-per-punt average. What a weapon. S Andrew Wingard – This guy seemed to be everywhere in today’s game. Was able to tackle Price for a short gain as the first quarter was winding down. Combined with Baker, to stop TE A.J. Barner for just a one-yard gain on the first play of the second quarter. Tackled Charbonnet in the third quarter after a one-yard run. Led all Arizona defenders with 12 total tackles. K Chad Ryland – Oh look, another kicker doing his job. Made the 28-yarder on the Cardinals’ first drive. This habit of the field goal kicker scoring all of the points is getting old. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Third-down efficiency – Was a horrible 1-for-6 in the first half. Went 4-for-13 for the game. Ouch. SACKED BY D-LAW 😤 -6! @TankLawrence 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/d6U4zc1iEL — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 8, 2026 Offense – We realize the Cardinals are playing the Seahawks, which means playing their defense, but Arizona only had 110 total yards in the first half: 68 passing yards with just 42 on the ground. Nobody can win if the offense isn’t moving the chains. Only 13 first downs in four quarters is not a winning stat. Nine penalties for 97 yards are drive killers. Arizona could not buy a third down with an efficiency of 4 for 13 attempts. Could not run the ball whatsoever. Offensive drives for the game: FG, punt, punt, punt, punt, downs, punt, punt, downs. Sad. Very sad day for this group. Game recognize game. pic.twitter.com/0T4WTlT7np — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 9, 2026 Not using the tight end – Wait a sec, this can’t be correct. TE Trey McBride had just two targets in the first half? And caught both for seven yards? TE Elijah Higgins, one target/one catch for four yards? Finally got some action in the second half with McBride, but both Higgins and TE Teagan Quitoriano had few targets all game. McBride did have seven receptions for 54 yards, but he dropped the touchdown on the fourth-down play. These are weapons that need to be utilized. Lack of pass rush – Every week, it is the same thing: where is the pass rush? Seahawks backup QB Drew Lock had plenty of time to survey the field and find open guys. The Cardinals had zero sacks. None. Nada. Three QB hits. Josh Sweat: two tackles. Same for Andrew Billings and Dante Stills. Roy Lopez, Darius Robinson, and L.J. Fehoko had just a single tackle each. Was no wonder Seattle had 175 receiving yards. Lock was flushed several times, and it did look like he would be sacked, but he found ways to get around it and had five positive rushes. ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – When the candle factory burned down, everyone stood around and sang, ‘Happy Birthday’ QB Gardner Minshew – Very vanilla in the first half, connecting on 11 plays on 14 attempts for just 85 yards in the first half. The second half was better, but no explosiveness from the offense at any time. All these weapons, and every single player, had mediocre numbers. Finished 21 for 30 for 166 yards, a 5.5 average per pass completion, sacked three times, rushed once for 4 yards, and had an 83.5 QB rating. Meh. REGGIE VIRGIL + 25 😤 📺:FOX pic.twitter.com/N1eM79tDuO — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 8, 2026 WR Reggie Virgil – The rookie had one catch for 25 yards on the first drive. Spectacular catch and toe drag swag, and then that was it. Yawn.

(Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images You get three wins; you get three wins; EVERYBODY GETS THREE WINS! The NFC South operates within a liminal space; it is the Backrooms of divisions, where things don’t look quite right. Here’s the Week 9 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) Week 9 Result: Buccaneers 24 – Bears 27 Week 10 Opponent: Bye Week Caleb Williams threw four interceptions in this game, and he still wasn’t the worst quarterback on the field. Outside of 2-point conversions, Mayfield offered nothing for his offense. He was finally forced to throw the ball more than 20 times, resulting in two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and a 56% completion percentage. Despite their efforts, the Buccaneers can’t ask Bucky Irving to do everything, although I am sure he could have thrown at least one touchdown. It’s also become increasingly clear that Todd Bowles’ defense is not the problem. Should Jason Licht have stuck with his gut when he initially did not hand out an extension to Mayfield? Maybe the bye week can help the quarterback reset. BEARS DEFENSE ANSWERS BACK WITH A PICK-6 🐻 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HHVx9YtFDl — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 Carolina Panthers (3-5) Week 9 Result: Panthers 21 – Broncos 26 Week 10 Opponent: New Orleans Saints I have to be honest, I was expecting a blowout, but I underestimated how uninspiring Bo Nix can be and Bryce Young’s ability to overcome his bad offensive line. The Broncos jumped out to an early lead, but the Panthers took it in the 3rd quarter. Unfortunately for Charlotte, they couldn’t keep up with the Broncos , and the cracks in their roster became wider as the game dragged on. They also suffered an unlucky interception that Falcons fans can empathize with. Luckily, this is the NFC South, and despite firing their defensive coordinator and losing three games in a row, they’ll play the Saints for the division lead next week. Perfect place at the perfect time! Devon Key with an improbable INT for the @Broncos ! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AnjjfvlHFi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 New Orleans Saints (3-5) Week 9 Result: Saints 23 – Browns 22 Week 10 Opponent: Carolina Panthers The Saints won off their bye week and joined the ranks of their 3-win divisional opponents. It wasn’t pretty and required overtime against backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, but the Saints got the last laugh. Austin Estime provided much-needed ground support, which finally gave Shough some breathing room. After a last-place 2-5 start and the walls closing in, the Saints will host the Panthers this Sunday with the potential to walk out of the game as the division leaders. Game over in New Orleans. pic.twitter.com/e4pTvX7Ao4 — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Atlanta Falcons (3-6) Week 9 Result: Falcons 17 – Bengals 34 Week 10 Opponent: Kansas City Chiefs The Falcons were a penalty machine in Spain and got routed by Joe Burrow and his legion of dominant receivers. Penix and the offense’s performance were uninspiring and hampered by penalties. The Falcons defense was most notably shredded through the air, but they also gave up over 100 rushing yards to one of the NFL’s worst rushing offenses. Despite still being in the race for the NFC South title, this isn’t a good football team, and the new front office recognizes that. Jessie Bates has been traded , and we wish him nothing but the best, but this was the right call. The team gets a 2nd- and 5th-round pick for a soon-to-be 30-year-old on an expiring deal. Could anyone else be moved before the Falcons play the Chiefs? This is shaping up to be one of the nastiest NFC South seasons yet, but it is refreshing to see the Falcons realize that short-sighted moves to try and win the South aren’t as important as building a sustainable product for the future.

The team’s huge free agency splash in 2023 is gone after a fantastic run in Atlanta that spanned about three-and-a-half seasons, and the Falcons are loading up to try and remake their roster in 2027. The Jacksonville Jaguars are trading for Falcons S Jessie Bates III, sources tell @TheAthletic . The Jags are sending a 2027 2nd round pick and 2028 5th to Atlanta acquire Bates. A big move by one of the NFL’s top teams ahead of the deadline. — Jonathan Jones (@jjones9) November 9, 2026 Per Jonathan Jones, who I cited above, the Falcons will eat some of the contract to facilitate a move. That’s not surprising given that they’re going to be sitting on plenty of cap space next year and clearly want more early draft selections for next year and beyond. With Bates moving to Jacksonville, I’d have to expect that DeMarcco Hellams, Sydney Brown, or both will be taking on his snaps next to Xavier Watts, but we’ll get more clarity on that in the week ahead. For the moment, let’s appreciate what Bates gave the Falcons while he was here. Few safeties in franchise history were more impactful than Bates, who had 14 interceptions, three interceptions returned for touchdowns, 11 forced fumbles, and a fumble returned for a touchdown in his time in Atlanta. While he was typically solid-to-excellent in coverage and provided sure tackling throughout his tenure, the big plays were why the Falcons signed him and the big plays were worth every penny. He was a game changing player who lifted lousy defenses and headline great ones, and it goes without saying that this will be a greatly diminished Falcons defense in 2026 without him. I’ll miss watching him play for my favorite team, and I’m grateful we got to do so for the past four years. The Falcons looked at the writing on the wall for their 2026 and clearly felt their chances of making a real run were not worth as much as the long-term lift they could get from another second round pick next year; time will tell as always whether that calculus was the right one. It will be incumbent on a front office that has had some promising signings and trades to make sure that trading away a safety as good as Bates doesn’t come back to haunt them, but given that Bates will be a free agent in 2027, getting a second rounder and a future fifth for him is strong value despite how amazing he is. In the short term, as I said above, I’d expect run for Hellams and Brown. Getting Brown back at safety full-time would free up snaps at the nickel for Mike Hughes, Billy Bowman, and Avieon Terrell, who seem likely to split that role going forward on most Sundays. The fact that the team has a bit of a logjam at the position and that Bowman is an extremely physical player means we could see a lot more rotation back there the rest of the season. We wish Bates well in Jacksonville, thank him for the phenomenal plays and fond memories, and hope the Falcons can turn their new draft picks into players who can help to create the next great team in Atlanta.

title: Falcons – Bengals recap: Adios to hope
summary: Seasons start to slip away, and in any other division, they can come to a very swift end. The Falcons losing to the Ravens wasn’t a huge deal, but the Falcons losing to the Bears right after that was a big deal, because it put them at 2-4 and raised the specter that quality football […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Joe Burrow of Cincinnati Bengals throws the ball during the 2026 NFL Madrid Game match between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seasons start to slip away, and in any other division, they can come to a very swift end. The Falcons losing to the Ravens wasn’t a huge deal, but the Falcons losing to the Bears right after that was a big deal, because it put them at 2-4 and raised the specter that quality football teams were simply going to be too much for them. Atlanta tried to put that to bed by beating the 49ers, but after a 16-0 drubbing in the rain at the hands of the Buccaneers, it was beat the high-flying Bengals in Spain or sit at three games under .500 and in a weak position even in the ultra-weak NFC South. The Falcons did not beat the Bengals, and did not come particularly close to doing so. After a spirited first quarter things started to go sideways and then kept going sideways, with the Bengals outscoring the Falcons 27-7 the rest of the way. The defense had a disastrous day against a very good Cincinnati offense, as we feared, but the offense repeatedly turned promising drives into nothing much with penalties. Special teams struggled on returns heavily again and Nick Folk may have punched his ticket out of town with another miss, and now the Falcons have lost four of their last five games. You have to give a ton of credit to a Bengals team that is currently red hot, but it would be a mistake to overlook the major role Atlanta’s own repeated errors played in making this a rout. It’s difficult to see the rest of this season amounting to much based on the way Atlanta’s been playing, even though they’re absurdly right in the thick of a divisional race where not a single team has more than three wins. The Falcons are spiritually in deep trouble even if the math says they’re very much still alive, given that they’re 1-2 in the division thus far, have lost to every quality team they’ve faced save the 49ers and sleepwalking early season Packers, and putting lousy things on tape. The Falcons in their first year under Ian Cunningham and Kevin Stefanski have shown some good instincts with talent acquisition and have resisted the urge to give away resources chasing a dream they shouldn’t chase, which makes me cautiously optimistic about the foundation here. But with a thrifty offseason in the cards, it’s not exactly a surprise that the Falcons have weaknesses that have mounted as the season went on, and their one risky bet on an aging kicker in Nick Folk has utterly failed. A team that was supposed to be more competent and disciplined after last year’s frequent letdowns just committed 12 penalties in a single game, many of them back-breaking ones in the red zone. And so on. There is bountiful cap space and enough draft picks in 2027 to make the meaningful upgrades this team needs, and this regime will have to show this is about growing pains rather than a deeper dysfunction with team-building and how this team is coached. We’re not having a conversation about jettisoning anyone from the staff or front office a year after the most significant overhaul to this team’s power structure in years, but we are talking about the Falcons clearly not being good enough for the ninth straight season. The franchise can’t be too impatient—it has bit them in the ass over and over again during that stretch—but those of us who have been spending Sunday after Sunday after Sunday watching this cannot help but be weary of it. The urgency will be there for 2027, regardless of how Atlanta finishes this year; they are very clearly not talented enough top to bottom yet, and that won’t change even if they end up atop this ghastly division somehow. Shrinking this back down to the smaller screen of the weeks ahead, however, the Falcons have so much to fix it’s fair to go into the Chiefs game expecting the worst. If they can survive that effort and get a win, get right with the bye, and hit the ground running, perhaps they can still make something of this season and conquer the South. Me? I won’t be indulging in those hopes anytime soon, and will instead take the rest of the season one week at a time with a hope of seeing signs of a team building something worthwhile and surprising me along the way. A 3-6 team that keeps getting rocked the way this Falcons team has over the past month-plus can’t ask for more than that from its fans, who have invested hope in this team over and over again in a weakened division and gotten very little from it. On to the full recap. The Good The Falcons have enough weapons that defenses have to account for that you can sometimes sneak a depth option into the end zone with basically no one looking. The Falcons did that earlier this year with Nick Muse’s first career touchdown grab, and they did in Sunday with Charlie Woerner’s first career touchdown reception as Penix rolled out and found him streaking toward the end zone for Atlanta’s first touchdown. The Falcons can’t go to that well all the time, but there are opportunities for Muse, Woerner, and others to make their mark in the red zone when things tighten up. Michael Penix Jr. with the…wheels? The book on the Falcons offense is that Penix can’t and won’t move, which makes him easy to tee off on, but in this one he took off running repeatedly and wasn’t afraid to roll away from pressure, resulting in prolonged plays and some surprisingly great scrambles. Penix finished the first half with 51 yards on just three attempts and would’ve had more on a fourth if not for a Matthew Bergeron hold, and he looked decisive and fast. If this is something Penix can threaten defenses with a couple of times per week, it changes the complexion of this offense. Bijan Robinson is still a god, even when his usage is inconsistent. He had one bad, boneheaded play when he fumbled a tough catch out of bounds, but other than that he was patient, found holes, functioned as a useful receiving option, and generally did Bijan things all day long. He turned 25 touches into 147 yards and a touchdown, and should be more involved in the passing game in particular going forward, though ideally on fewer third and long screens. Drake London’s physicality is so fun to watch. He made a number of tough catches, as he so often does, but he also provided some key blocks and went into every yards after the catch opportunity looking to lower his shoulder into a defender. It was a quieter day in terms of yardage, but he was still the favored target for Penix and did a nice job with the balls sent his way. Brandon Dorlus was still a bully on Sunday, even if he didn’t get a ton of help, and he set up a nice LaCale London sack where Joe Burrow tried too long and too hard to keep the play alive. On a day where the pass rush was inconsistent at best, Dorlus, London, Gervon Dexter, and Zach Harrison came up with the plays of consequence. Unfortunately, the team was largely stonewalled off the edge. Jessie Bates was one of the few defenders who did anything consistent on Sunday. He flew all over the field making tackles, often serving as the last line of defense between a good Bengals play and a potential touchdown. Khalil Herbert is a solid returner who has been a useful runner and receiver in the limited opportunities he’s had. He should be RB3 when Brian Robinson Jr. is back, and right now I think you could get him a couple more touches a game and have that be a positive for the offense. Again, if you’re looking to not give up on the season and see some consequential football, the NFC South has obliged. The Falcons may not truly be out of this thing even if they lose to the Chiefs next week, and a win may put them in a strong position. This division is amazing, and I don’t mean that as a compliment. The Ugly Penix not seeing things well over the middle of the field and delivering…

title: Week 9 Snap Reactions: Falcons brought a paper sword to a shootout
summary: The Atlanta Falcons were no match for Joe Burrow and now have three straight losses this year. Take solace in knowing that they are still losing as a team, #brotherhood. Here are the Week 9 snap reactions. Death by Penalty Matthew Bergeron had two killer penalties in the red zone, Jawan Taylor had one as […]
full_text: Bengals' WR #1 Ja'Marr Chase (R) makes a touchdown reception during the 2026 NFL Madrid Game American football match between Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, on November 8, 2026. The National Football League return to Madrid with this 2026 NFL regular season game for the second time following 2025 first edition at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons were no match for Joe Burrow and now have three straight losses this year. Take solace in knowing that they are still losing as a team, #brotherhood. Here are the Week 9 snap reactions. Death by Penalty Matthew Bergeron had two killer penalties in the red zone, Jawan Taylor had one as well, and everyone else on the team joined in on the fun. It’s gonna be hard to win the game when you’re too busy setting a season high in penalties. There were no sloppy conditions to blame this week; the team was reckless on its own, and it cost them the game more than anything. If you are going to be a CEO head coach, execution errors like these can’t happen under your watch. A.J. Terrell Nightmare Game Chase has had Terrell’s number since college. He got whatever he wanted against the Falcons CB1, and he wasn’t alone. Tee Higgins also scored a touchdown against the corner, and fans need to accept that we are now on the downslope of Terrell’s peak. He’s still serviceable, but he is no longer a top-10 CB in the league, maybe not even top-15, and the position will need to be addressed again in the offseason. Ja'Marr Chase's first half in Madrid… 142 yards, 8 catches, 47-yard touchdown 🔥 CINvsATL on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dqBRCHgTFJ — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Cut Nick Folk Please cut Nick Folk. Please cut Nick Folk. Please cut Nick Folk. That was his miss inside the 40 since 2017. Please cut Nick Folk. Please cut Nick Folk. Please cut Nick Folk. Nick Folk misses left for the Falcons from 38 yards 😬 Bengals v Falcons is LIVE on Sky Sports, talkSport, VM Play and NFL Game Pass on DAZN 📺 pic.twitter.com/Mn2Fy0p70n — NFL UK & Ireland (@NFLUKIRE) November 8, 2026 Penix did not shake back After his best opening drive of the season, Penix and the offense faded fast. The quarterback struggled to see the field at times; he got away with a few would-be interceptions and tossed a bad one late in the fourth quarter. He also committed a killer delay-of-game penalty, but it’s fair to say his teammates had far more that spoiled some of his best plays. In a weird twist of fate, it was the best rushing game of his career; he looked healthier than ever. However, that wasn’t enough to get the win because the Falcons were in a shootout. They didn’t lose this game because of Penix, but he didn’t do enough to give them a chance late either. Questions about the quarterback’s future will only grow if he stays stuck in a rut. Michael Penix passing chart. He went 1 of 8 for -3 yards and an interception when pressured, the fewest yards when pressured by any quarterback in a game since 2018 (min. 7 pressured attempts). pic.twitter.com/XLqLlZV6CZ — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 8, 2026 The Tommy Rees conundrum Rees might have a better playbook than Zac Robinson, but he may be a worse play caller. We finally got an opening script worth celebrating, but when he had to adjust to the game in real time, he froze. Dialing up flea flickers for Chris Blair but nothing for Kyle Pitts, abandoning the run at the sight of a lead, and 3 & long screens. Is this really the OC you want developing a rookie if the team moves off Penix? Jeff Ulbrich isn’t going anywhere After the first four games of the season, fans were convinced Ulbrich might be gone in 2027; now many are hoping that happens. While the injuries have definitely taken their toll, Ulbrich has been his own worst enemy too often. For reasons I still can’t explain, a healthy Billy Bowman was scratched , and the Bengals immediately took advantage by targeting the slot. Divine Deablo was not a viable option in coverage or against the run, and the plan failed so spectacularly that when the Falcons needed to lean on other DBs, they inserted DeMarcco Hellams. The defense also gave up 100 yards on the ground to one of the worst rushing teams in history, so the talent excuses only go so far. Oh, and believe it or not, James Pearce Jr. played in today’s game, and Joe Burrow had the longest time to throw in his career (3.26 seconds). The trade deadline is about to come to a close, and while the Falcons are still in the thick of the NFC South race, is it even worth it? We’ll see how much Ian Cunningham likes draft picks this week.

title: Falcons – Bengals instant recap: Success in Spain proves elusive
summary: We knew that the Bengals passing game was going to be difficult for Atlanta to deal with, so the hope was that Atlanta could create a couple of turnovers, play disciplined football, and win in a shootout. Instead, they allowed Joe Burrow to play a clean game, got killed by Ja”Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Ja'Marr Chase of Cincinnati Bengals scores his team's first touchdown during the 2026 NFL Madrid Game match between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) | Getty Images We knew that the Bengals passing game was going to be difficult for Atlanta to deal with, so the hope was that Atlanta could create a couple of turnovers, play disciplined football, and win in a shootout. Instead, they allowed Joe Burrow to play a clean game, got killed by Ja”Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, piled up 11 penalties, and saw penalties and errors undermine the offense. The result was another lopsided loss for a team that we can emphatically say is not going to pull it all together in 2026 and make a real run at this thing. The Bengals were just the better team across the board, and given their mediocre run game got going and their good-but-not-great defense made a bunch of big plays, that was tough to watch. The passing game was probably even better than I would have expected, and paired with all the mistakes from Atlanta, it was enough to ensure another double digit loss. The Falcons have now lost four of their past five games, all of them by at least seven points, and are broken in all the ways you’d expect the Atlanta Falcons of the past nine years to be broken. The rest of this season will be about fixing what can be fixed, building some positive momentum, and getting ready to invest in all the places where this team has fallen down. We’ll hope we can have some fun along the way, but it’s probably wise not to expect it. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap from the day. 1st Quarter The Falcons fielded the opening kickoff, with Khalil Herbert taking it to the 32 yard line, but a holding call brought that back. Michael Penix Jr. hit Jahan Dotson over the middle for 13 yards and a first down. Bijan Robinson then turned on the jets outside and got another first down. Then Penix hit Bijan for six yards. Bijan then scooted ahead for three yards after taking contact around the line of scrimmage. Bijan then took it outside, got a nice block, and cut back inside for close to 20 yards. Penix then took off and scrambled for a first down, with a penalty on the Bengals giving Atlanta more yards. Penix then tried London in the end zone, but a pass interference call gave Atlanta the ball at the one yard line. Then Penix hit Charlie Woerner for the touchdown to cap off an impressive drive. 7-0 Falcons. The Bengals were planted by Mike Hughes on the return. Joe Burrow hit a reserve tight end for four yards on first down. A jet sweep to Dohnte Meyers went for 16 yards. Burrow rolled out away from pressure and was hit hard by Cameron Thomas at the end of it as he threw it away. Mike Gesicki reeled one in over the middle for eight yards. Burrow then hit Ja’Marr Chase deep for a 47 yard touchdown after Chase simply got by and outran A.J. Terrell. 7-7 tie. Herbert had a nice return back to the 41. Penix rolled away from pressure but couldn’t find an open man, throwing it away. Penix then got Drake London over the middle into a tight window. Bijan then got a yard on first down. Penix had pressure in his face immediately and rushed the throw to Kyle Pitts on a screen, and it fell incomplete. On third down the Bengals blitzed and forced an incompletion, but an offsides gave Atlanta five yards. Penix then scrambled for 20 plus yards again, with a nice block from Kyle Pitts. Bijan then picked six yards running outside and another four on the next play for a first down. Penix then scrambled to the one, but a hold on Matthew Bergeron backed the Falcons up. Penix then got Olamide Zaccheaus for five yards. A false start on Jawaan Taylor backed the Falcons up again. Penix then went to Dotson for about eight yards. Penix was under pressure from Dexter Lawrence and had to throw it away. Nick Folk’s short kick was good to make it 10-7 Falcons. Meyers got the Bengals to the 31 yard line. Chase Brown got caught from behind on a toss and maybe got a yard. A quick sideline ball to Tee Higgins for Burrow five yards. Higgins then pulled in a crazy leaping grab for a first down. Samaje Perine got four yards on first down. Chase then reeled in a one-handed grab, broke a tackle, and picked up a first down. A delayed screen to Brown got 10 yards and a first down. 2nd Quarter Chase Brown just got a huge hole and went for 16 yards. Burrow tried Chase in the end zone again, and Henderson did a great job in coverage to ensure it fell incomplete. Chase got it over the middle for a first down on the next play. Brown was then stonewalled after close to a yard. Burrow snuck it in on the next play for a touchdown to make it 14-10 Bengals. Herbert made it to the 32 yard line. A quick pass to the flat to Herbert picked up a yard or two. Then the Falcons were backed up five yards from a delay of game. Then Penix got Kyle Pitts for eight yards. Penix then had to throw it away with nobody open. The Bengals called for the fair catch at the 11 yard line. A quick slant to Ja’Marr Chase went for 31 yards as he took off and evaded multiple defenders. Then Chase Brown got eight yards. Perine was then stopped after a minimal gain by Gervon Dexter. Burrow just threw it up under pressure and Chase slid to make the grab, and Kevin Stefanski’s challenge failed. Burrow then hit Chase at the line of scrimmage, but Bates got him for just a yard. A false start on the Bengals backed Cincinnati up five yards. A quick hitter to Meyers went for five yards, but Meyers slipped before he could pick up anything else. Burrow got 14 yards and a first down on a toe tap sideline catch working against Terrell. Burrow tried to run away from the pressure, but Dexter sacked him. A defensive holding call on Terrell gave the Bengals five yards and a first down. Burrow then hit Chase over the middle for 12 more yards and another first down. Burrow hit Higgins in the end zone for the touchdown to make it 21-10 Bengals. Zaccheaus got it to the 29 yard line. They picked up four yards on first down and followed it up with three more from Bijan on second down. Penix then hit Kyle Pitts over the middle for a first down, but a holding call on Jawaan Taylor screwed the Falcons over again. A screen to Bijan got the first down after he got the blocks and turned on the jets. Bijan caught a short pass, fumbled it backwards, and it rolled out of bounds for a loss. A slant to London picked up eight yards. Penix tried to hit Zaccheaus but overthrew him a bit. Punt, and it bounced out around the 15 yard line. Burrow escaped pressure and hit Meyers for a big gain over the middle of the field. Then Burrow got Gesicki, and Mike Hughes flipped him up the air after five yards. Burrow then threw it in the dirt at Meyers’ feet. Evan McPherson’s kick was good from 57 yards out to make it 24-10 Bengals. The return didn’t get far. Penix had to throw it away on first down. Then he scrambled for a first down and got past the 40 yard line. Penix then fired one downfield and it was knocked down. 3rd Quarter Dohnte Meyers took it past the 30, but a holding call backed the Bengals up 10 yards. A quick gain of a yard and then a quick throw to Chase Brown went for maybe a yard. Burrow under pressure went too high to Chase. Punt, but Zaccheaus went a little bit backwards on the return and was injured on the play. A quick pass to London went for nine yards. Bijan then got a yard for a first down, and then followed that up with two yards. Bijan then went for two more yards on a delayed handoff. Penix then floated one down the sideline to Bijan for 28 yards. Herbert then picked up seven yards running to the left. Bijan then went right and picked up another seven or so yards and a first down. Bijan then was patient behind his blocks and got four more yards, and then five more falling forward. On third down, Dexter Lawrence came rumbling through the line on a…

title: Ravens news: Giants inquired about Justice Hill
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis of the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover trade rumors about the team’s running backs, the case for Eric DeCosta to sell at the deadline, and an assessment of first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Let’s dive in: Ravens RBs involved […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Justice Hill #43 of the Baltimore Ravens runs the ball for a 65 yard touchdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the fourth quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 05, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis of the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover trade rumors about the team’s running backs, the case for Eric DeCosta to sell at the deadline, and an assessment of first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Let’s dive in: Ravens RBs involved in trade rumors Let’s be honest: the Ravens were never going to engage in a fire sale, especially not with some hope about the potential return of Lamar Jackson. Trade talk about players like Derrick Henry is silly. But moving veterans on expiring contracts who may not be re-signed or net a valuable compensatory pick in the offseason could make sense. Baltimore’s No. 2 running back, Justice Hill, fits that bill. He has been an effective third-down back and could be worth retaining on a cheap extension, but investing in two veteran running backs is the kind of resource allocation mistake DeCosta has to avoid moving forward. Hill seems unlikely to net much, until you consider his rumored suitor: the Giants – John Harbaugh’s new team, aka Ravens North. He threw all sorts of money at his players in free agency and has demonstrated a hands-on approach to the deadline. Getting a friendly deal for a solid Day 3 pick from his longtime friend could have been a tidy piece of business for DeCosta, but the team’s win-now mindset will likely keep Hill in Baltimore. Ravens Will Not Trade Derrick Henry; Giants Called About RB Justice Hill – Adam La Rose (Pro Football Rumors) In the event a trade received consideration, the Giants and Patriots represented logical landing spots. Henry began his career under Mike Vrabel, who is now in New England. During the 2024 and ’25 campaigns, meanwhile, he played under John Harbaugh. Harbaugh’s Giants are known to be in the market for a running back addition, and Schefter reports the team called about Ravens backup Justice Hill. Hill has spent his entire eight-year career in Baltimore, making him a highly familiar face for Harbaugh. The former fourth-rounder has carved out a role as Baltimore’s top pass-catching back over time, and his work in pass protection and on special teams add to his value. Hill is attached to a salary of $2.75MM in 2026 and is a pending free agent. The case for Ravens selling at deadline NFL Trade Deadline: Biggest needs for all 32 teams – Gordon McGuinness (Pro Football Focus) The Ravens are trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals in an effort to save a season that has been derailed by injuries. That means they probably won’t be as active as sellers as they could have been before that trade. They could still look to move some players who won’t be around in 2027. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey has earned a 64.7 PFF coverage grade this season and is a candidate to be shipped out. His contract isn’t the most team-friendly for the acquiring team, but if the Ravens could get a late-round pick for him, this could make sense. Declan Doyle tabbed as NFL top first-year coordinator Drafting the first-year NFL coordinators: Who is making a real impact? – Jourdan Rodrigue and Ted Nguyen (The Athletic) Pick 1 Ted selects: Declan Doyle, Baltimore Ravens OC The 30-year-old fits the mold of the most in-demand coaches: a hot young play caller from a strong coaching tree. Doyle could be the first branch of the Ben Johnson tree, and you can see the shared DNA in his system with the Ravens. When Lamar Jackson was healthy, we saw a glimpse of how explosive this offense could be, as Doyle got Jackson to play under center more often. Production is hard when you’re down to your third-string QB — and the Ravens agreed to trade for Jacoby Brissett on Wednesday — but Doyle’s creativity and ability to put players in position to emphasize their obvious strengths, albeit in a short sample size. — Ted Nguyen
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens discussion: best-, worst-case with Jacoby Brissett under center
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are already fighting an uphill battle in a competitive division and conference. Their 4-5 record puts them in last place in the AFC North and outside of the AFC’s playoff picture. Now, they will have to weather a month without star quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. General manager Eric DeCosta […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the New York Giants during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are already fighting an uphill battle in a competitive division and conference. Their 4-5 record puts them in last place in the AFC North and outside of the AFC’s playoff picture. Now, they will have to weather a month without star quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. General manager Eric DeCosta swung a trade for Jacoby Brissett, who began the year as the Arizona Cardinals’ starter but was benched for Gardner Minshew in October. The 10-year veteran is expected to start in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Chargers and beyond with the goal of keeping Baltimore’s playoff hopes alive until and unless Jackson can return. The Ravens have a relatively easy slate of opponents coming up, starting with the winless Chargers and continuing with the Houston Texans, Carolina Panthers, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. All three are 3-5 and have looked exceedingly beatable this season; however, it is not hard to imagine any of the three winning comfortable against this current iteration of the Ravens. Nikhil’s take: Brissett can move, but he does not bring the same rushing upside as Jackson or Huntley that often serves as the offense’s ‘get out of jail free’ card. However, his gunslinging nature will open up the Ravens’ downfield passing game far more than Huntley did. He may also have a shot at running a fuller, more complex system than Huntley give his decade of experience in the NFL. Ultimately, the Ravens’ success comes down to two units who are not playing up to their salaries and/or draft slots: the offensive line and the secondary. The former finally has its best starting five in Week 9 and could gel in the coming weeks, though Thursday’s game against the Jaguars’ was not encouraging. Baltimore’s mini-bye could help Jesse Minter diagnose and address the problems in his pass defense that keep games close enough for Brissett to win. Best case, the Ravens manage to steal three wins out of their next four with Jackson returning to a 7-6 squad in Week 15 against the Steelers. Worst case, though, is the status quo. The offensive line continues to struggle, keeping Brissett from scoring enough points to compensate for a leaky defense that cannot sort things out on the back end. Unfortunately, I am not hopeful that enough will change for Jackson’s return to even matter. Zach’s take: The absolute best case scenario with Jacoby Brissett is he helps the Ravens three or four wins in the next five games, Lamar Jackson comes back, and the Ravens go on to win the Super Bowl. But that is not happening ,so the best-case scenario that’s realistic is that Ravens lose. A lot. Jacoby Brissett comes in as an NFL veteran and helps keep the offensive functioning. Guys like Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry get the stats they deserve because Brissett can operate and the young guys like Vega Ioane, Ja’Kobi Lane, Matt Hibner and Josh Cuevas can continue to develop in a competent offense. But the offense isn’t quite good enough with a journeyman backup and the defense doesn’t improve enough to win games. Lamar Jackson takes the time to fully recover instead of rushing back for a fool’s chance at a playoff run. Brissett starts the rest of the way and maybe gets one or two wins, setting the Ravens up to be in the top 10 of the draft. A functional product that isn’t as terrible to watch as Thursday’s fiasco but doesn’t stop the Ravens from landing a good pick. The worst case scenario is Jacoby Brissett does do enough on offense to win some close games, but Lamar Jackson’s hand injury doesn’t allow him to return. Somehow, the Ravens fall bass ackwards into the seventh seed of the playoff, ruining their chance at a top draft pick, all while not having Lamar Jackson for the playoffs. The Ravens hubris and pride refuses to let them embrace the suck and they fail to set themselves up with a better draft pick to improve the 2027 team.

title: Report: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson plans to return this season
summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return this season shortly after suffering a right thumb injury against the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, according to a report from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport. Jackson encouraged his team to keep their playoff hopes alive until he comes back. His IR placement will sideline him […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens takes the field for warmups prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return this season shortly after suffering a right thumb injury against the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, according to a report from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport . Jackson encouraged his team to keep their playoff hopes alive until he comes back. His IR placement will sideline him until after Baltimore’s Week 13 bye; however, surgery on his throwing hand will likely sideline him for longer. Rapoport adds that Jackson is specifically dealing with a fractured and dislocated thumb that typically has a six- to nine-week recovery timeline. If that is accurate, his earliest return would be in Week 15 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, a game that will likely have significant playoff implications. Nine weeks would keep Jackson out until Week 18, the Ravens’ second matchup against the Steelers, by which time taking the field may not make sense. Jackson’s potential return will only matter if recent trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett and Baltimore’s struggling defense can keep the team in the playoff race over the next month. They will face the winless Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10, who could be without starting quarterback Justin Herbert. After that are the Houston Texans and the Carolina Panthers, two of the NFL’s Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde teams this year, followed by the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers post-bye. The Ravens probably need to win three of those games, to get to 7-6, to keep their playoff hopes alive. They would then need at least two, if not three wins over the Steelers (twice), Cleveland Browns, and Cincinnati Bengals to close the season. It’s worth noting that Jackson recently called out Rapoport for an inaccurate report that he suffered a unique, neither high nor low ankle sprain. The two-time MVP said that head athletic trainer Adrian Dixon told him that it was, in fact, a high ankle sprain. As of Saturday, Jackson had yet to undergo surgery, per Bleacher Report’s James Palmer . No matter how much optimism and determination he may have regarding his return, he will not know anything about his ability to grip a football for weeks. That will be the ultimate test of the rest of the Ravens’ 2026 season.

title: Bills game-day food: A Buffalo spin on a classic Minnesota treat
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. What could be sweeter than your favorite team on Monday Night Football ? This Minnesota-inspired cereal treat gives it a run for its money. Making this a bit more “Buffalo” was pretty easy, too. Scotcheerios The Vikings are a fun team for this series because they’re not a frequent opponent for the Bills, which means there’s still plenty to explore. When diving into Minnesota culture I came across scotcheroos, which is a type of cereal treat bar where the binding ingredient starts with corn syrup rather than marshmallow. The base recipe uses crispy rice cereal and straight corn syrup for the liquid sugar. I swap out the rice cereal and use the more “Buffalo” cereal of Honey Nut Cheerios, and then augment that flavor profile with a partial substitution on the corn syrup. Aside from that, this recipe is basically the same as this one from the Karo Syrup website , and I like to give credit where it’s due when my recipe doesn’t deviate all that much from someone else’s work. Scotcheerios Makes: About 20 treats Active time: 20 min Total time: 30 min Ingredients 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips 1 cup butterscotch chips 3/4 cup light corn syrup (yes I used Karo and yes they should cut me an endorsement check) 1/4 cup honey 1 cup granulated sugar 1 cup creamy peanut butter 6 cups Honey Nut Cheerios (they also should cut me an endorsement check) Essentials: Greased 9×13 pan (use glass and thank me later), medium sauce pan, large glass bowl, high-sided sauté pan, large mixing bowl, measuring cups, rubber spatulas Partially fill the high-sided sauté pan with water; place the glass bowl in the pan (see below, and be careful of splashing). Add chocolate and butterscotch chips to the bowl; turn heat to MED (about 4 of 10 on my stove); continue with step 3 while allowing chips to melt. Add corn syrup, honey, and sugar to sauce pan on MED/HIGH (about 7 of 10 on my stove). Continuously stir syrup-sugar mixture until it begins to bubble; reduce heat to MED (4 of 10) and stir for another 2 min. Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter. Add cereal to large mixing bowl; quickly fold in syrup-peanut butter mixture. Carefully pour into greased pan and press to get even bars. Stir chocolate-butterscotch chips until smooth, then quickly spread on top of cereal mixture in pan. Cool for 45 min or longer; cut, and serve Wingin’ It tips If you’re not familiar with the melting technique I used, this is a cheap way to make a double boiler. The first picture shows how to set it up. Chocolate is a fan of scorching and just melting in a pan requires constant attention and/or very low temperature. This method has the water distribute the heat evenly and avoids the scorching. It’s not without peril though. If you’ve ever gotten so much as even a drop of water in melted chocolate you know what a nightmare that is. If you need to go higher heat to get a good melt, be careful of steam as it can collect on the bowl edges and screw things up. The next pictures are the initial and later stages of combining the syrup and sugar. It looks like it won’t work, but applying heat will lead to a smooth consistency. I was a little more precise with my stove settings this week, and that’s always a good plan with hot sugars. Like the chocolate, it’s easy to scorch. And while the corn syrup might be a bit forgiving, the honey will not be. That’s really it for tips though. These are super easy and when in doubt, it’s easy to start with lower temps and increase as needed. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! full_text: In the aftermath of the Jaguars monster trade to acquire Falcons safety Jessie Bates, a report has surfaced about the Buffalo Bills and their interest in that same position. Here’s what ESPN NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler tweet on the subject: Jaguars swung big at safety but aren't only ones in that market. Bills have scanned the safety pool of late. My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if AZ entertains talks (big if). Tennessee has calls on Amani Hooker but wants to keep him. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 9, 2026 While the Bills have plenty of bodies — and upside — at safety, after the release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson they certainly could use a veteran upgrade at the position. We did feature Baker in our trade-deadline candidate here at Rumblings, and it’s not exactly my favorite idea. Why? Because he’s a rather expensive, box defender – free safety hybrid who’s established his quality reputation mostly on tenacity as a tackler… not as a ball hawk. I’m of the belief they need better, more dynamic coverage players at the safety spot. And this is the second-consecutive season Baker has taken a clear step backward in coverage. Now, when Gardner-Johnson was let go, he was carrying the worst missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties in the NFL. Baker is much more reliable in that regard, Jim Leonhard made no mistake about his tackling emphasis this offseason. Let’s see if the Bills’ swing is for the 30-year-old Baker, who averages 90 tackles, six pass breakups, and one pick per season, or if Buffalo goes in a different direction at safety (or another position). *there are two coaching connections to Baker, as Bills WR coach Drew Terrell and special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers were both in Arizona with the safety for multiple seasons.

title: Buffalo Bills must show adaptability vs. Vikings on Monday Night Football
summary: The Vikings defense makes its opponents play a different game. Really. Minnesota blitzes like points are awarded when a quarterback is touched and tries everything in its power to force said quarterback to make an abrupt decision. When you watch the Vikings’ defensive film, you wonder to yourself — why isn’t every defensive scheme this […]
full_text: The Vikings defense makes its opponents play a different game. Really. Minnesota blitzes like points are awarded when a quarterback is touched and tries everything in its power to force said quarterback to make an abrupt decision. When you watch the Vikings’ defensive film, you wonder to yourself — why isn’t every defensive scheme this aggressive? Why do other defenses let the opposing quarterback stand in the pocket and scan the field? Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is calling a blitz on 74.2% of opponent dropbacks, almost 30 percentage points higher than… the team second in blitz rate, and more than 40 percentage points higher than the league average of 31.4%. That’s per Fantasy Points Data. According to PFF, the Vikings have blitzed on 80.7% of their opposition’s dropbacks, the highest rate in the NFL and around 30% higher than the second-place team currently. Regardless of which data-driven site you prefer, the point remains. The Vikings are blitzing fiends. There’s a strong likelihood the game tonight will be different. It’s an outlier, a one-off schematic and communication test for the Josh Allen, Joe Brady, Buffalo’s offensive line, and the club’s skill-position talent. And the Bills don’t have to be perfect to win. In fact, facing that many pressure packages, they probably won’t be. Brace yourself for that. But a week after I called for the Bills to piece together a convincing win over a quality, familiar opponent, I’m asking for the exact opposite tonight against a unique, unfamiliar foe. Grind out a gritty, scrappy, ugly victory. Wins of all varieties count the same in the standings. With that, I’d like to serve this reminder — tonight we’re unlikely to see the juggernaut Bills offense that moves the football with ease, a unit that shocks us when a drive doesn’t end with points. This game needs to be viewed through a different lens. But it absolutely is a “something’s gotta give” contest. That narrative is unavoidable. The Vikings defense is first in points per drive allowed at 1.20. It is first in points per game at 13.3, second in the NFL in yards per play allowed at 4.7, and first in success rate at 25.7% The Bills offense is first in points per drive at 3.13. It is first points per game 33.3, tied for first in yards per play at 6.3, and first in success rate at 56.6%. We probably shouldn’t expect the Bills to hum at a 3.13 points per drive pace against this Vikings defense. And we probably shouldn’t expect the Vikings defense to hold the Bills to 1.20 points per drive either. But on the road, in a majorly hyped prime time game, against a relatively obscure opponent Buffalo doesn’t play often — and Brady has never coordinated against as a member of the Bills staff — proving capable of winning differently is vital. Because in the NFL, not all games can be won on your terms, following your ideal script. Parity has become a central component of this league, to me, a secretly large driver of why ratings continue to soar. Through Week 8, 71 games were decided by one score , which tied 2022 for the most such contests through Week 8 in NFL history. Entering tonight’s end cap of Week 9, that one-score game count is up to 77. Sure, teams want to dictate to their opponents. The Bills have the offense to do that. And that’s an adage we’ve heard from Buffalo’s defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. But the best teams are those that somehow manage a small collection of strange victories throughout the season. It’s often the results of a few abnormal games in the regular season that separate the No. 1 seed from the No. 2, No. 3, and No. 4 in each conference. The Bills and their elite offense need to simply find a way to win against the Vikings and their elite defense to move to 7-1 for the first time since 1993, the last season they advanced to the Super Bowl.
