title: Todd Monken denies report Browns already make Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson starting decision for Week 10
summary: Among the conversations surrounding the Cleveland Browns after Week 9’s loss to the New Orleans Saints was whether Shedeur Sanders overtook Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback: There was also a comparison of the two quarterbacks: HC Todd Monken was non-committal after the game, but his answers were mostly based on the timing of […]
full_text: Among the conversations surrounding the Cleveland Browns after Week 9’s loss to the New Orleans Saints was whether Shedeur Sanders overtook Deshaun Watson as the team’s starting quarterback: There was also a comparison of the two quarterbacks: HC Todd Monken was non-committal after the game, but his answers were mostly based on the timing of the media session right after the game. Sanders’ performance was uneven , but Cleveland’s offense was explosive in the second half. Monken’s befuddling decision to share a conversation with Sanders about plays is just a footnote in a game that was lost by one point after the team went for two points at the end of overtime. Monday, the day before the NFL trade deadline, Monken and the Browns have already decided that Watson would return as the team’s starter, reportedly: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs the Texans, per source. Shedeur Sanders filled in Sunday in New Orleans, but returning to Watson was the expected move once he cleared concussion protocol. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 9, 2026 The two quarterbacks engaged in a long competition for the starting job throughout training camp, with the veteran winning out. Over the first eight games, Watson has led the Browns to five wins, of the come-from-behind fashion. During his time with the media Monday afternoon, Monken noted that the staff had reviewed the tape but had not gotten back together to discuss the starting quarterback decision. He also pushed back on the idea that he had to have a decision by Tuesday’s game planning session. title: Browns Week 9 loss: Shedeur’s progress, weapons galore, season in balance at trade deadline
summary: The NFL can be fun if your team is winning. However, if your team is losing, it can be stressful and cause friction within the fanbase. After a short winning streak, the Cleveland Browns are now on a short losing streak, falling to the New Orleans Saints in Week 9. For many, patience is running […]
full_text: The NFL can be fun if your team is winning. However, if your team is losing, it can be stressful and cause friction within the fanbase. After a short winning streak, the Cleveland Browns are now on a short losing streak, falling to the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 . For many, patience is running thin, but there is a lot to discuss : 1st Down: Uneven game from Shedeur Sanders It feels as if we’ve seen this movie play out before. Bad 1st or 2nd half from the quarterback, good 1st or 2nd half from the quarterback. With quarterback Deshaun Watson inactive, 2nd-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders got the start against the Saints. There was plenty of bad. Plenty of good. Sanders had some nice throws, including this one to wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, was one that many were impressed with: Shedeur Sanders takes a big hit but delivers a strike to Jerry Jeudy! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6ix7w5hhEp — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 As far as the negatives, Sanders had moments in which he held the ball longer than he should’ve; the 4th-and-goal miscue at the goal line was his fault as he went the wrong way and ran into guard Austin Barber, who was pulling. Overall, Sanders played okay. With that being said, Watson will likely start next week after clearing concussion protocol already. It doesn’t make sense for a QB change when the season isn’t over and the quarterback who you started the season with hasn’t given you a reason to bench him. 2nd Down: KC, Denzel, and Harold. Everyone knew how special tight end Harold Fannin was last year during his rookie season. This year? He might be even better. This clip shows why. HAROLD FANNIN GOES BEASTMODE! pic.twitter.com/wO5EDBSO8e — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 These are the types of plays that make you jump out of your seat and yell things that aren’t safe for work (in a positive manner). Rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion also showcased how good they can be. SHEDEUR TO KC CONCEPCION 64-YARD TD FOR THE LEAD! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Zs6x4Ko8SO — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 DENZEL BOSTON MOSSED HIM pic.twitter.com/ZZdzSZtnpj — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 It prompted ESPN analyst Mina Kimes to tweet this. Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr pic.twitter.com/IWP1uS1LNl — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) November 8, 2026 Now the team just needs a quarterback. 3rd Down: Defense played well until they didn’t For what it’s worth, the Browns defense played better than they did last week against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, it wasn’t enough. After watching Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett get three sacks in his first game back and watching defensive end Jared Verse not make an impact once again, have to wonder if the Browns were better off not trading Garrett at all. Yes, Cleveland had five sacks, but some of the sacks weren’t being finished that could have added to that number. The run defense was up and down. The tackling has to be better, but the reason for the tackling being poor has something to do with their aggressive style. The defensive tackles the Browns have aren’t bad, but they are small. The size doesn’t necessarily matter because smaller, compact tackles fit the scheme, but they need someone big who can help clog the running lanes. It was an average game from the unit, but it feels like the defense let the offense down. 4th Down: Season isn’t over. Yet. Let me put on my pessimistic outfit for a minute. The Cleveland Browns are 5-4. The team has somewhat exceeded expectations. However, going back home against the Houston Texans at 6-3 would be better than coming back at 5-4. If the team were to lose against the Texans, the season wouldn’t be technically over, but November is when the contenders start to emerge. The Browns aren’t contenders this year, and that’s fine. However, when you look at the landscape of the AFC, you start to wonder if the Browns missed their opportunity. People questioned whether or not this team would win a game after how bad opening week went but Cleveland has somewhat fixed that, leading to fan expectations. The team has talent that you can get excited for, but it’s hard to think about whether the Browns missed their opportunity with the Week 9 loss and the one to the New York Jets. Granted, it’s too early to tell, and Cleveland is still, technically, tied for the last AFC playoff spot . Extra Points The New Orleans Saints are not a good team. At all. They have some good players, but they could be in the market for a new head coach next season. Myles Garrett got three sacks in his first game back, but Jared Verse can’t get one in nine games. The running game is inconsistent; what else is new. If the Browns have to go tempo to avoid slow starts on offense, so be it. I wouldn’t pick up Jared Verse’s 5th-year option at this point. He has to earn it. Expect the Browns to be active at some point before the trade deadline on Tuesday. What are some of your thoughts the day after the Browns Week 9 loss to the Saints? title: Browns vs. Texans odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
summary: The Cleveland Browns opened as 4.5-point home underdogs against the Houston Texans ahead of their Week 10 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The over/under on the game is 39.5. The Browns (5-4) are coming off of a 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints. It was a one week start for Shedeur Sanders, and […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns opened as 4.5-point home underdogs against the Houston Texans ahead of their Week 10 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under on the game is 39.5. The Browns (5-4) are coming off of a 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . It was a one week start for Shedeur Sanders , and for three quarters, the offense looked quite ugly. Once he let loose and started airing the ball downfield, though, the offense came alive. Unfortunately, that also involved the Saints putting their first touchdowns on the board. In overtime, the Browns answered the Saints’ touchdown, but with a minute to go, they tried to go for the win (a two-point try) instead of settling for a tie or loss. They didn’t get it, and lost their second straight game. Deshaun Watson will return to start against the Texans. The Texans (3-5) are coming off of a 44-22 victory over the winless Chargers. C.J. Stroud had five touchdown passes and 384 passing yards in the win. Houston has been an odd team to get a pulse on. They are 0-4 at home, 3-1 on the road, and began the year with four straight losses before winning three of their last four. Statistically, they’ve been good at throwing the ball, but also bad at defending the passing game. Either way, it seems a little ‘off’ that the Browns are at home, yet one of the largest underdogs they’ve been all season. The over/under for the game is 39.5. What odds would you take if you were placing a bet?

title: Cleveland Browns news: An opportunity lost. A QB question answered.
summary: The Cleveland Browns had three goals on Sunday in New Orleans while playing a backup quarterback making his first start of the season and needing a win to stay in the AFC playoff picture. Stop with all the penalties. Limit the turnovers. Come home with a victory over a Saints team going nowhere. That was […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns had three goals on Sunday in New Orleans while playing a backup quarterback making his first start of the season and needing a win to stay in the AFC playoff picture. Stop with all the penalties. Limit the turnovers. Come home with a victory over a Saints team going nowhere. That was the assignment for the day against a two-win Saints team going nowhere. While the Browns made it through the game without a turnover, they failed miserably on penalties with 10, including a holding call on the final play of overtime, and couldn’t pick up that much-needed win. Even with a different quarterback running the show, it was a familiar story, as the Browns were bad for three quarters, came alive in the fourth, but, unlike previous weeks, could not pull out the victory. The loss overshadowed: A big catch from wide receiver Denzel Boston that would have been a walk-in touchdown, thus avoiding the whole overtime, if it had not been underthrown. The first touchdown of the season for wide receiver KC Concepcion on another ball that was underthrown, but the elusive Concepcion turned it into a 64-yard touchdown. A 39-yard touchdown in overtime when tight end Harold Fannin Jr. went all bull in the china shop to find the end zone. There will be far too much talk this week about the quarterback situation, which is a discussion no one wants, questions about head coach Todd Monken’s clock management, and more as the Browns deal with their first two-game losing streak of the season. For now, let’s get this Monday rolling with the latest edition of the Daily Dawg Chow. title: AFC playoff picture: Browns position unchanged despite Week 9 loss, out due to tiebreaker
summary: The Cleveland Browns loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 will be dissected for a few days, including HC Todd Monken’s refusal to “take the points” in a game decided by one point. Because it is the quarterback position and because Shedeur Sanders has such popularity, whether or not Deshaun Watson will take […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 will be dissected for a few days, including HC Todd Monken’s refusal to “take the points” in a game decided by one point. Because it is the quarterback position and because Shedeur Sanders has such popularity, whether or not Deshaun Watson will take back over as starter will be one of the talking points as well. What most Browns fans won’t be talking about is the AFC playoff picture . Two straight losses have most around Cleveland thinking negatively, for good reason, but the Browns’ position in both the AFC and AFC North is unchanged from last week, even if the chase for a playoff spot is now more difficult. Cleveland is still in third place in the division and in the eighth seed in the AFC coming out of Week 9. title: Browns playmakers did their part on offense vs. the Saints
summary: The Cleveland Browns lost what should have been a winnable game on Sunday to the New Orleans Saints. The defeat was the fourth on the road for the Browns, and similar to the Week 5 tilt against the New York Jets, it was a game the Browns should have won.  But it wasn’t to be, […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns lost what should have been a winnable game on Sunday to the New Orleans Saints. The defeat was the fourth on the road for the Browns , and similar to the Week 5 tilt against the New York Jets, it was a game the Browns should have won. But it wasn’t to be, because these are still the Browns until they prove otherwise , and Cleveland now sits at 5-4 on the season after losing their second consecutive game. It was not all doom and gloom on the afternoon, however, as a trio of Cleveland’s offensive playmakers made their mark on the game. Denzel Boston wins vertically, underthrown ball forces him to slow, win again and catch it off the CB's helmet. Big time. Boston is tied for the NFL-lead w/ 3 catches of 50+ yards pic.twitter.com/sa0s6EJDAE — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) November 8, 2026 Denzel Boston had a team-high 98 receiving yards, including a 60-yard reception in the third quarter that would have been a walk-in touchdown if the pass had not been underthrown by quarterback Shedeur Sanders. The Browns had to settle for a 30-yard field goal by Andre Szmyt, and those four points would prove crucial in a one-point loss. SHEDEUR TO KC CONCEPCION 64-YARD TD FOR THE LEAD! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Zs6x4Ko8SO — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 KC Concepcion finished with 85 receiving yards, which included a 64-yard catch-and-run touchdown on another underthrown pass as Concepcion darted through the New Orleans defense for the final 30 yards to the end zone. Harold Fannin Jr. only had two targets all day, which makes sense since he had 154 receiving yards just last week, but he made the most of them by bullying his way into the end zone for a 39-yard touchdown near the end of overtime. 39 YARD TD FOR THE YAC KING HAROLD FANNIN! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/EwW2lYo1UA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 After today, Concepcion and Fannin are tied for the team lead in receptions with 37 apiece, while Boston is right behind them at 32. And with a handful of games still to be played in Week 9, Boston (507 receiving yards) and Concepcion (437) are the top two rookie wide receivers in the NFL. On the Browns, Fannin sits between them with 453 receiving yards. The Browns still do not have a quarterback, but there is no denying that they have a nice trio of playmakers ready and waiting for when the new guy arrives in 2027. title: Browns winners, losers from Week 9 vs. Saints: CLE turns down 4 points, loses in overtime
summary: The Cleveland Browns were at a crossroads leading up to kickoff against the New Orleans Saints. They had built a record of 5-2-0, then were beaten badly last weekend and now stand at 5-3-0. A loss to the Saints would mean they would sink to a 5-4-0 record and would find themselves going in reverse. […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns were at a crossroads leading up to kickoff against the New Orleans Saints. They had built a record of 5-2-0, then were beaten badly last weekend and now stand at 5-3-0. A loss to the Saints would mean they would sink to a 5-4-0 record and would find themselves going in reverse. RELATED: SHEDEUR COMES CLOSE, CAN’T GET FINAL PLAY IN OT The New Orleans contest was the first start for backup QB Shedeur Sanders. The good part is that this was decided early in the week, so Sanders had plenty of time to get first-team reps during practices. The offensive line and receivers got a chance to re-familiarize themselves with the young signal-caller. Against the Saints, Cleveland refused to take four points in the contest and lost by one . You do the math. Now, it’s a 5-4-0 record and a two-game losing skid. The Saints are not a good team. Neither were the New York Jets. Good teams take care of business against the teams they should defeat. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES (DBN’s winners) LB Carson Schwesinger – One thing is certain: Cleveland’s defense will get everything out of Schwesinger every game. Injured or solid, he just balls out. A great punch on the ball on the one-yard line avoided a New Orleans scoring opportunity. Had seven total tackles in the first half alone, plus a sack of Saints’ QB Tyler Shough on their first drive of the game. He was able to tackle Shough on a third-and-six in the third quarter when the QB tried to leave the pocket and was short of the first down. Finished with 15 tackles, two sacks, two QB hits, and two tackles for loss. Andre drills it to tie the game!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/ipIeZmA08Y — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 K Andre Szmyt – Converted a 41-yarder in the second quarter, a 31- yard field goal in the third stanza, and then the game-tying FG from 51 yards with eight ticks left in regulation. Was also 1-for-1 on PATs and scored 10 of Cleveland’s 22 points. He does what he is asked to do. WR Denzel Boston – The rookie had a very quiet first half, but made up for it. With 11:15 left in the third quarter, he had a 60-yard gain to the Saints’ three-yard line as he beat CB Kool-Aid McKinstry. Then in the overtime period, he converted a second-and-14 for a 15-yard gain, followed by an eight-yard gain that got the Browns to midfield. Led all receivers with 98 yards on six catches with seven targets. Second-half QB Shedeur Sanders – Apparently, the cobwebs got dusted off at the intermission, because Sanders played well in the final three periods. He stopped leaving the pocket prematurely and found receivers open. The strike to Boston in the third quarter: Sanders faced a good rush and remained calm as the play went for 60 yards. His run on a third-and-four with 2:53 left in the game kept the drive going. Again, he was hit as he let the ball fly but found the waiting hands of TE Harold Fannin, who took it to the house. Earlier in the fourth quarter, the pass to WR KC Concepcion ended up as a 64-yard catch-and-run on former Browns CB M.J. Emerson. Sanders finished 19 of 31 for 297 yards, two TD passes, zero picks, and was sacked five times, with a QB rating of 114.6. CB Myles Harden – It was Harden guarding WR Chris Olave in the second quarter with that 36-yard completion, but the drive ended with a punt. Harden recovered from that play. He blitzed in the third quarter for a sack that destroyed the New Orleans drive. Then he had another sack with 6:58 left in the game. Good coverage of Olave in the third quarter, as Harden was able to stay with the quick receiver for an incomplete pass. Five total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss, one batted pass, and two QB hits. P Corey Bojorquez – The talented punter had a banner game. Kicked five punts for 267 yards, with a long of 59 yards, and finished the contest with a 53.4 average. Had punts of 48, 46, 57, 57, and 59. Incredible numbers. Shedeur 64-yd TD pass to KC Concepcion!! First TD for either team 💀 pic.twitter.com/GzyC5s2VeO — McNeil (@REFLOG18) November 8, 2026 WR KC Concepcion – Okay, four catches for 85 yards might not be considered exceptional, but that catch-and-run touchdown against former Browns cornerback M.J. Emerson was phenomenal. The mere fact that the rookie took it across the field was like a seasoned veteran. FROWNIES (DBN’s losers) Penalties, penalties, penalties – If players received game bonuses for every penalty they committed, it might make sense to explain why the Browns have so many in every game. Six were called in the first quarter alone for 33 yards. The holding call on LG Zion Johnson in the fourth quarter negated a good 15-yard run by RB Quinshon Judkins. S Tytus Campbell’s illegal contact penalty in the fourth quarter was a failed Saints third-down conversion. 10 penalties for 58, with two not accepted. Coming into this game, Cleveland was the most penalized offense and the most penalized offensive line group. Lack of offense : First half – In the first half, the Browns had a grand total of 81 yards on offense with just 38 through the air. The special teams unit got a fumble recovery at the Saints’ 19-yard line, yet it took 7 plays to go 18 yards, and then it got zero points. This offensive line is not moving the chains, and a backup QB isn’t helping matters. Certainly, penalties hurt, but these offensive weapons just aren’t being utilized. Refusing points – At the end of regulation, the Browns had to drive the field and get into field goal range down three points. But that kick would have been the game-winner (assuming nothing else changed). In the second quarter, Cleveland had a first-and-goal on the nine. Three plays later, they still hadn’t scored. Instead of accepting failure, head coach Todd Monken did not send out K Andre Szmyt. 4TH DOWN STOP 🛑 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/Rg13KrF0dM — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) November 8, 2026 What happened was the Browns were stuffed on the one-yard line and got zero points out of that drive. At the end of the game, they would have been tied and could have driven into field goal range for the winning kick (again, assuming nothing else changed). After the Browns scored the touchdown in overtime, instead of kicking for one and taking the lead, Monken once again refused points, as the two-point conversion had no chance, and the pass rush was once again in Sanders’ face, which collapsed the play. Having a tie right after the Saints had scored a touchdown, and then so did the Browns, would have been close to a Cleveland victory. It would have made the late Fannin TD catch heroic and continued the Browns’ late-game lore this season. Now, it’s a 5-4-0 record and a two-game losing skid. Shough spins his way to a first down 🙌 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/yeTz7NT57r — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) November 8, 2026 Red Zone – 0 for 2 (see refusing points). Missed tackles – Every week, this becomes an epidemic: Ronnie Hickman (3), Tyson Campbell (2), Mike Hall (2), Derek Barnett, and Winston Reid. Barnett missed badly in the third quarter when Saints QB Tyler Shough attempted to escape the pocket on a third-and-seven, and Barnett completely whiffed as Shough ran for 12 yards and kept the drive going and ended with a New Orleans field goal. ESTIME YOU ̶D̶A̶W̶G̶ SAINT!!! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/V9C1NTPnDb — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) November 8, 2026 Run defense – Again, poor execution. A player the Browns let go this week gashed them for 72, all up the gut. The Saints ended with 160 rushing yards. title: Browns vs. Saints: Takeaways from Week 9’s loss include lots of Todd Monken questions
summary: The NFL is always a wild ride; that is why it is so popular, but for Cleveland Browns fans, a calmer ride would be nice, as would more wins. A week after getting destroyed by the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Browns played a bad New Orleans Saints in Week 9, and another roller coaster ensued, with […]
full_text: The NFL is always a wild ride; that is why it is so popular, but for Cleveland Browns fans, a calmer ride would be nice, as would more wins. A week after getting destroyed by the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Browns played a bad New Orleans Saints in Week 9 , and another roller coaster ensued, with an outcome Cleveland fans were hoping to avoid . There will be a lot of conversation about the end-of-game decisions by HC Todd Monken and QB Shedeur Sanders, especially after the head coach’s befuddling decisions throughout the game (and what he shared with the announce crew this week about Sanders ). While the choice to go for two points, and failing to do so, will dominate the discussion, the coaching decisions were questionable throughout the game. On to a few key takeaways, written as the game went on, for the Browns loss to the Saints in Week 9: Tackling, particularly Ronnie Hickman, was poor on 1st drive, throughout the game Just too many times, plays were extended because Cleveland defenders failed to wrap up New Orleans players. While forcing turnovers is nice, only going for the football is just bad defense, and too many times Hickman and others were caught with their hands going for the ball instead of the ball carrier. Unacceptable in the middle of the season from season-long starters. Penalties and more penalties Six in the first quarter, including two against special teams; the second one gave New Orleans 30 more yards. The yardage wasn’t huge for the penalties but impactful, and sad compared to the offense’s yardage in the 1st quarter: 6 penalties, 33 yards Browns rushing yards: 8 Browns passing yards: 11 For the game, Cleveland ended up with 10 penalties for 58 yards, with a number of other flags declined, including one on the game-deciding two-point conversion attempt. For comparison, the Saints had just four penalties for 25 yards. Mike Hall’s sack, zone coverage, leads to NO missed FG A nice rush by the Browns defensive tackle forced the Saints out of field goal range. With Maliek Collins missing the game, it was good to see a big play by Hall late in the 1st quarter. HC Todd Monken yelling more Cleveland’s head coach was even more animated on the sidelines this week than he’s been much of the year. Whether it was just because of how the game was going, frustration boiling over from this week’s practice, or trying to jump-start the Browns, Monken was extra in Week 9. In the end, it didn’t work and the coach has to accept much of the blame. Carson Schwesinger with another punch-out, perfecting it, big sack Carson Schwesinger punches the ball loose for a Browns takeaway! CLEvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/t5eYGIrmOM — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Late in the 3rd quarter, Schwesinger was able to close on a scrambling Shough and got a two-yard sack to force a field goal. Saints are also not good DT Adin Huntington forced a big fumble on special teams, giving Cleveland great field position: ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Neither team has played well; Cleveland has just forced two turnovers in the first half. Quinshon Judkins hit and miss The Browns top running back will have a few plays, like his 12-yard gain, where he looks like he’s back to the quality back he was in 2025, but too often he is unable to make plays, leading to this stat line: 15 carries, 43 yards, 2.9 yards per attempt. Cleveland just needs more from the running game. Failed 4th-down takes points off the board Sanders and OL Austin Barber seemed to affect the timing of the pull play and running back, but a bold call by Monken failed. Looked like Sanders turned the wrong way after the snap; Monken was coaching him up after the play. Miscommunication on 4th and goal for the Browns. pic.twitter.com/EH9oKfvr6A — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) November 8, 2026 Offense’s halftime stats are laughable 80 total yards 55 rushing yards 25 passing yards 3 for 8 on 3rd down 0 for 1 on 4th down 2.7 yards per play Underthrown, but the big play to Boston was needed oh my GOODNESS Denzel!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/Cja2N3hYwr — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 More tackling issues as Tyler Shough starts to scramble late in the 3rd quarter A spin move by the Saints QB on third down led to a first down and New Orleans deep into the redzone. Cleveland defenders struggled to finish plays. 4-point play by Hickman in the 3rd quarter Shough had a touchdown throw, but Hickman continued to fight the tight end all the way to the ground, forcing the ball out and an incompletion instead of a touchdown. The Saints were forced to kick a field goal instead. Befuddling quote from Monken about Sanders I can’t believe Sanders suggested plays that were not in the Browns playbook, but even more, I can’t believe Monken shared that with the television crew , who repeated it during the game: Audio thanks to @JackMcCurry08 https://t.co/yN0f3vfnbD pic.twitter.com/hw8FDtQUi1 — Jared Mueller (@JaredKMueller) November 8, 2026 Another failed 4th-down play Just no chance with Sanders backing out of the pocket, but Monken deciding to go for it after the Saints penalty on the punt will be judged, for sure. Sanders seemed uncertain on the play; with double slants, he tried to extend the play before being forced to throw it out of bounds. More DB blitzes this week DC Mike Rutenberg brought a number of cornerback blitzes, including two sacks by Myles Harden, a little bit of a wrinkle this week. Deep ball bails out team again Former Browns CB Martin Emerson burnt by the rookie: KC FIRST TOUCHDOWN ON A 64 YARD PLAY #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/p4CPhjtQPA — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Snapping the ball late with time on the play clock is poor decision-making As the announcers noted, the Browns offense was in position to bleed the clock, but multiple times snapped the ball with time on the play clock. A little thing, but details matter so much in the NFL. Similarly, spiking the ball with 11 seconds left in the fourth quarter is a little detail that didn’t impact the result but matters. Saints walk the Browns defense down to take the lead with a minute left Six plays, 55 yards, 50 seconds, touchdown. New Orleans just walked the Cleveland defense right down the field. Concepción drop… too much time to think After a huge touchdown earlier in the quarter, Concepcion was wide open, and Sanders hit him right on time at the sideline, but the rookie dropped the ball trying to make sure he got his feet in bounds. Sanders to Jerry Jeudy A clutch throw, a big-time catch… Just an amazing throw by Sanders while getting blasted by DE Chase Young, and Jerry Jeudy holding on to the ball while being held by Martin Emerson was equally impressive: atta boy Jerry!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/Rwn09mqTZb — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Andre Szmyt hits huge once again Never assuming a kicker would continue to hit long field goals, but Szmyt did it once again, tying the game with eight seconds left with a 51 yarder. Deferring in OT was an interesting choice Saints drove the ball after Monken decided to defer, taking over half the time off the clock. New Orleans scored a touchdown and left the Browns with just over four minutes for a chance to tie the game. Ultimately, this decision did not impact the outcome of the game. Playing for the tie? Let 40 seconds run off the clock in OT An interesting decision by Monken, the Browns completed a pass with just under 2:40 left on the clock in overtime and let the clock run down to the two-minute warning. Again, an interesting decision that didn’t impact the outcome of the game because… Instead, Fannin dribbled defenders down the field for a score Just an amazing effort by TE Harold Fannin to score with one minute on the clock, with Cleveland looking for the victory: 39 YARD TD FOR THE YAC KING HAROLD FANNIN! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/EwW2lYo1UA —…
author: Jared Mueller

title: Cleveland Browns vs. New Orleans Saints recap: Shedeur Sanders comes close, but can’t get the final play in overtime
summary: I was hopeful to see QB Shedeur Sanders heading into this game, but it was very ugly for most of the game. Then, down 9-6 with a few minutes to go, he found WR KC Concepcion for a long touchdown pass to put Cleveland on top 13-9. The offense couldn’t quite close the game out […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns throws a pass against the New Orleans Saints during the first half of the NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images I was hopeful to see QB Shedeur Sanders heading into this game, but it was very ugly for most of the game. Then, down 9-6 with a few minutes to go, he found WR KC Concepcion for a long touchdown pass to put Cleveland on top 13-9. The offense couldn’t quite close the game out after that, and then the defense allowed their first touchdown of the day with a minute to go, being down 16-13. An incredible connection to WR Jerry Jeudy set up a 51-yard field goal by K Andre Szmyt to send the game to overtime, and he drilled it to make it 16-16. Unfortunately, the defense gave up a lengthy touchdown drive in overtime. Cleveland responded with a touchdown drive with a minute to go, and then faced the decision: a possible tie, let the Saints have a chance to win with a field goal, or go for the win with a two-point try. They went for the win, and it didn’t work out. Cleveland lost 23-22, and dropped to 5-4 on the season, with Deshaun Watson returning next week. Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Saints The Browns got the ball first, and it was a quick three-and-out for QB Shedeur Sanders on a drive that included a false start, no runs by RB Quinshon Judkins , and Sanders getting sacked on 3rd-and-long. Then punted to New Orleans, and despite all their run-game struggles, former Browns RB Audric Estime had three straight runs for 32 yards. Then, down by the goal line, after getting the Saints into a 2nd-and-13, DE Chris Williams and DE Jared Verse jumped into the neutral zone on back-to-back snaps to make it 2nd-and-3. On 2nd-and-3, the handoff to RB Alvin Kamara led to a muff and a loss of 5 yards. On 3rd-and-8, QB Tyler Shough tried to scramble after not finding anyone, but LB Carson Schwesinger darted in and sacked him for a loss of 2 yards to force a field goal. K Charlie Smyth hit from 30 yards out to give the Saints a 3-0 lead. The Browns began their second drive at their own 27 yard line. This time, they handed it off to Judkins for a pickup of 4 yards. A quick screen to WR KC Concepcion then moved the chains. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-9, a crossing route to WR Denzel Boston only got 7 yards, leading to a punt by the Browns. P Corey Bojorquez got his punt downed at the 7 yard line with about five Browns around it, but of course, the player who touched it (S Daniel Thomas ) was flagged for illegal touching (he went out of bounds and was first to touch it), leading to a re-kick. After the re-kick and a Saints return to the 37 yard line, it was a big difference in field position. After a first down pass to WR Chris Olave , Shough took off for 15 yards a couple plays later to avoid a sack, as individual mistakes were running rampant across the team. That included S Grant Delpit two plays later, as he was flagged for pass interference to put the ball at the Browns’ 29 yard line. Two runs by Estime set up 3rd-and-5. DT Mike Hall came up with the sack up the middle on Shough, pushing the Saints back to the 34 yard line. Smyth’s attempt was now from 52 yards out, and it was pushed to the right and no good. that's ✌️ on the year for Mike! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/xeQu8NHfBs — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 After the missed field goal, the Browns took over at their own 42 yard line with 8 seconds left in the quarter. Sanders ran a playfake from Shotgun, had plenty of time, but rolled to his left, and then had his pass tipped and incomplete. 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Saints A pitch play Judkins got 6 yards to set up 3rd-and-4, and Sanders got RB Dylan Sampson wide open in the flat to pick up a first down and get into Saints territory. Sanders avoided a free rusher on second down to throw the ball away, and then on third down, the Saints were finally called for a penalty via illegal contact to give Cleveland a fresh set of downs. Two runs by Sampson set up a 3rd-and-3, something looked off as Sanders quickly went up the middle and was stopped for 1 yard — it didn’t look like it should’ve been a quarterback draw, especially since Todd Monken looked animated on the sidelines as he sent the field goal unit out. K Andre Szmyt came on and connected from 41 yards out to tie the game at 3-3. Shough laid out a beautiful deep ball to WR Barion Brown for 52 yards, beating S Ronnie Hickman . BARION BROWN: 52 YARDS! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/cDAFRFMYil — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) November 8, 2026 Two plays later, WR Jaylon Tyson made the first catch of his NFL career, and lunged toward the end zone, but Schwesinger punched it out for a fumble, and CB Tyson Campbell recovered for Cleveland kept it at the 1-yard line. we'll take that thank you very much! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/MyEG67ze3b — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 To avoid a safety, Sanders did a quarterback sneak to gain 4 yards. Judkins got the next handoff for 5 yards, setting up 3rd-and-1. Another handoff to Judkins got the first down. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-6, Sanders tried to escape the pocket, but was chased down from behind after a 1 yard gain, forcing another punt. On the punt, Brown tried to reverse field to get more yards, but he ended up going backwards, and then DT Adin Huntington tackled him and forced a fumble, and S Donovan McMillian recovered at the Saints’ 19 yard line. ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Sampson carried for 1 yard, and on 2nd-and-9, the Saints jumped offsides to make it 2nd-and-4. The end around went to Concepcion, and he was able to squeeze three yards out with limited space to make it 3rd-and-1. Sanders handed to Judkins, and this time there was no miscommunication, as he got the yard to set up 1st-and-goal at the 9 yard line heading into the two-minute warning. Sanders ran a playaction fake, but the edge defender wasn’t fooled by the threat of a run, and got an easy sack on Sanders for a loss of 6 yards. On 2nd-and-goal from the 15 yard line, they handed to Judkins, and he found an opening for 11 yards to make it 3rd-and-goal at the 4 yard line. Sanders ran a quicker playaction fake, then took off up the middle for 3 yards to make it 4th-and-goal. Monken opted to go for it, and Sanders bumped into his lineman before handing it off, then gave to Judkins, and he was stopped a half yard short with 1:38 to go, keeping it a tie game at 3-3. 4TH DOWN STOP 🛑 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/Rg13KrF0dM — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) November 8, 2026 Now the Browns’ defense needed to seek out a safety opportunity. Shough tried to sneak it on first down, but got no gain, as Cleveland took their first timeout. On second down, Shough hit Olave on the outside for 7 yards, making it 3rd-and-3. Shough lofted it for Olave up the right side, and he made the catch with CB Myles Harden draped all over him for a gain of 35 yards. The defense came up with a stop after that, but only 27 seconds left. The Saints punted to Concepcion, and it was fair caught at the 9 yard line. Cleveland kneeled it out from there to send it to halftime. 3rd Quarter – Browns vs. Saints New Orleans got the ball to start the second half and began at the 36 yard line. Two runs to Estimate made it 3rd-and-5, and Shough tried to hit Olave again, but Harden tipped the pass away to force a punt. The punt went out of bounds at the 22 yard line, where Sanders would get his first crack at second half redemption. After two run plays by Judkins, it was 3rd-and-6. Sanders scrambled to his left and ran for 11 yards and a first down. On the next play, Sanders finally aired one out deep for Boston. Even though it was underthrown, Boston high-pointed the ball and got yards after the catch for 60 yards, down to the 3 yard line.…

title: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb refuse to lose as Cowboys top Colts
summary: Nothing comes easy for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, but they managed to get back in the win column on Sunday with a 27-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts. It is their first win scoring less than 30 points since last season’s miraculous comeback in Week 12 vs. the Eagles, which gave Brian Schottenheimer’s team their […]
full_text: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images Nothing comes easy for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, but they managed to get back in the win column on Sunday with a 27-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts. It is their first win scoring less than 30 points since last season’s miraculous comeback in Week 12 vs. the Eagles, which gave Brian Schottenheimer’s team their first winning streak of that 2025 season. At the end of another rollercoaster game, this fourth win of the season goes in the same bucket as the other narrow win the Cowboys have against another AFC South opponent – Dak Prescott refusing to lose with the ball in his hands, and making the plays when it mattered most to ensure this. The Texans win was defined by Prescott and CeeDee Lamb making all the plays when it mattered, and without George Pickens this time out, Lamb’s big day was even more crucial. There were plays by the defense in the first half that made this game feel like it wouldn’t come close to needing any late game heroics from the offense, but the offense didn’t capitalize early. Then, there were breakdowns on defense that helped the Colts storm back, but also more rallying by Christian Parker’s side of the ball to ultimately put this in the win column. Let’s get to some notes on the gut-it-out performance in Indy. Too Many 3rd Downs For the second straight week, the Cowboys faced 16 third-down attempts. The Cowboys have faced more third downs on offense than their opponents in every game since the Packers loss. Dak Prescott’s third-down fumble in the first quarter was the second straight week the Cowboys had a disastrous negative play in a formation that calls on Javonte Williams to stay in and block. This time around, the Cowboys also had Jake Ferguson in the game. Ferguson was the only pass option running a hot route against the pressure the Colts brought on this play, yet somehow the defense had an answer to bracket him with two defenders while also getting to Prescott. The strip sack set the Colts offense up on a short field they capitalized on to take a 7-3 lead. The Colts would not get points again until midway through the third quarter. While the Cowboys did get two touchdowns before this, they also punted on all four other possessions in this stretch. The touchdown drive that came in response to being down 10-7 got a rare Javonte Williams receiving play that went for positive yards on a 3rd-and-4, then overcame a 2nd-and-19 after a Brevyn Spann-Ford holding penalty, and was gifted an automatic first down after facing 2nd-and-15 on a Tyler Guyton penalty. Even after all this, it still took a 4th-and-2 attempt in the red zone to get points on the board with Jake Ferguson’s touchdown. The other touchdown the Cowboys got came a little bit easier, rewarding a drive that saw what felt like the first successful scramble drill in a long time. Lamb and Prescott made the play when the Cowboys decided to throw on 3rd-and-1, hooking up on the scramble drill for 22 yards. One play later, Lamb got behind Charvarius Ward for his 44-yard touchdown to go ahead 17-7. Yet again, the Cowboys felt in control of a game, but were left scrambling and fighting for their life to actually finish by the fourth quarter. The Cowboys had a perfect 34/34 run-pass split in this game, and Dak Prescott’s 9.9 yards per attempt was a season high, but it still felt like the offense majored in wanting to be in third downs, makings things hard on themselves yet again, and not putting the game away on their own terms early. Instead, they left it until late for more QB heroics that paint a clear picture of what this team is really all about. Defensive Resolve The number one thing the Cowboys defense needs to fix following these last two wild games is limiting the explosive plays for touchdowns. Two weeks in a row, a game has swung in the snap of a finger because any work the defense has done up to a point is wiped out by a long play for a touchdown. Ashton Dulin’s 55-yard touchdown on a screen pass evaporated the Cowboys hopes of taking a two-score lead to the fourth quarter, and led to another game that felt like it could see overtime by the fourth. Marist Liufau, DaRon Bland, and P.J. Locke were the defenders with the best chance to get Dulin on the ground, and none of them could. The Cowboys continued to do some interesting things with Shemar James in this game, as he was involved in the play where Caleb Downs had a sack, and Locke made a big stop on third down early in the game as well, but more consistent fundamentals is still something holding back the Dallas D as a unit. They need to tackle better. After the Cowboys offense squandered their chance by missing a FG with over three minutes remaining in the game, the Cowboys defense needed to come up with a stand. The Colts got into comfortable field goal range, but Josh Downs’ third-down drop stopped the clock and the defense had held Indy to a 23-20 lead after a field goal. The defense did not give up a touchdown, and they got the ball back to the offense with enough time to go win the game. The other defensive resolve point in this cardiac fourth quarter was of course Quinnen Williams forcing a fumble on Jonathan Taylor, recovered by James. We said coming into this matchup that just an arbitrary splash plays from Williams wouldn’t be good enough. So Williams stepped up and made multiple big plays, none bigger than this one, and helped the Cowboys overcome penalties on Bland and Dee Winters prior to the takeaway that made a difference in which team had just enough in the tank to win on Sunday. Kenny Clark even added his name to the splash play list from the defensive interior on the final drive, pressuring Jones into an intentional grounding throw that really wrecked the drive and led to Downs’ game-sealing interception. The highly-paid Cowboys defensive interior made the plays in crunch time. Play-Calling and What’s Next The goal for the Cowboys now resets back to exactly what it was after the Eagles game, don’t get too high after a win (against an arguably even worse team this time), and stay focused enough to get a win streak started in front of home fans next Sunday. To do so, the Cowboys will have to waste no time digesting not only the good things that happened to beat the Colts, but the bad as well. Fourteen penalties for 153 yards is one thing that should be unacceptable even in a win, but the bigger and more long-term concern is the poor play-calling that stamped this game as well. Even while getting Lamb ten catches on 16 targets for 10 catches and 195 yards, nothing outside of Lamb’s long touchdown felt like it came easy for the offense. The protection plans were not sound to give Prescott time to throw when needed. The early down aggressiveness to not face 16 third-down attempts was not there. Worst of all, the static routes, lack of motion, and number of pass plays where all of Prescott’s options were blanketed from start to finish, with receivers not even running hard on many of these plays, were abundant. As good as CeeDee Lamb’s day was – 10 catches, 195 yards, one TD – it could have been better. He had two catches wiped out because of offensive pass interference penalties (one was iffy, for sure) and missed out on another TD when he was unable to get his second foot down. “He… — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 9, 2026 This week will be telling when it comes to how Lamb’s leadership is received at large by this team, as even after his huge day he was more focused on what could have gone better and his costly fumble. This is the type of attitude the entire Cowboys team needs to take into the 49ers matchup, as significant improvements from how they played, mainly on offense, will be needed to pull that upset. Brian Schottenheimer’s responsibility for how the offense looks will come up as well, but his postgame locker room approach was quite different in mood than Lamb’s. keep playing & find a way 🗣️ #DALvsIND | @ATT…

title: Cowboys at Colts Stock Report: Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams excel
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. For real. The win was hardly the prettiest that the Cowboys have ever had, but it counts just the same as the ones that left us feeling happier than that one did. A win is a win, as they say. While the end result was the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. For real. The win was hardly the prettiest that the Cowboys have ever had, but it counts just the same as the ones that left us feeling happier than that one did. A win is a win, as they say. While the end result was the desired one, the path there was bumpy to say the least. There were players who rose to the occasion and others who left us wanting more in several types of ways. Let’s discuss in this week’s stock report. Stock Up: Caleb Downs It has felt like Caleb Downs was trending upward already, but Sunday was officially his announcement to the world. The game-sealing interception is what everybody will remember, but Downs was all over the place. He had a critical sack on an early third down. He was credited with two passes defensed and three tackles. Simply put, he was everywhere. It was needed in the worst way. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams Similarly, the Cowboys officially have a new war daddy. Like Downs, Williams had really been coming along as of late. The start to his season, his first full one with the Cowboys, was a little bit bumpy, but he singlehandedly disrupted so much of what the Colts wanted to do. We have dreamt of having a force of this nature along the interior. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy It was nerve-wracking when the Cowboys announced that George Pickens would be inactive for this game. Sure, Ryan Flournoy has been very good this season, but elevating to the WR2 role is a very different thing. Flournoy proved more than capable. He was hardly CeeDee Lamb, but he provided the necessary moments opposite of him. Dak Prescott targeted him when the team absolutely needed a spark at the end of the game. The future of George Pickens remains unknown, but the way that Flournoy is playing is going to make those conversations very interesting to say the least. Stock Up: Rashan Gary Obviously there was only up to go for Rashan Gary. But he is a stock up nonetheless. The Cowboys were able to really stifle the Colts’ offense (hardly something to be proud of, but you can only play who’s in front of you) and Rashan Gary even picked up his second sack of the season as the team kept the heat on Daniel Jones. He also contributed six tackles and two TFLs. There has been far and few in between to choose from regarding Cowboys pass rushers this season so we have to take what we can get. Stock Up: Tyler Goodson Caleb Downs is obviously the best new player on the Cowboys (as in players who weren’t on the team at all last season), but Tyler Goodson has a very strong argument for number two. Goodson runs so hard and everything he does is with every bit of his energy. Goodson averaged 6.4 yards per carry and finished with 77 yards. He has been such a breath of fresh air and is a really proper counterpunch to the attack that is Javonte Williams. Stock Up: Christian Parker This is also a “nowhere to go but up” situation, and the quality of the opponent is certainly worth keeping in mind. But let’s say that Christian Parker’s defense generated eight different stops on Sunday, including the one that sealed the game in Caleb Downs’ interception. Is this representative of a turning tide? That would be a huge leap to make. But it is definitely representative of a group that is getting better and that is awesome to see. Stock Up: Brevyn Spann-Ford Jake Ferguson deserves a lot of kudos for the touchdown that he had in this game, especially given that it came on fourth down. To call it clutch would be to not do it due justice. Noting that, Brevyn Spann-Ford is really making the most of his opportunities as of late. He is becoming someone who Dak Prescott clearly trusts and has assimilated well into his new role with the offense at large. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer We just mentioned it, but the Ferguson touchdown really was quite fortunate. In that respect it really bailed Brian Schottenheimer out. That touchdown came on fourth and short in the redzone, but the third down play that Brian Schottenheimer called right before it was so silly. While the Cowboys were gashing the Colts their play-caller decided to call a trick play for CeeDee Lamb that lost yardage. You can argue that the decision to go for it on fourth down, even though it worked out, was pressing a bit. This doesn’t even cover the fact that the Cowboys barely beat a really bad Colts team. Heck, they were losing to the team in question late in the game. They almost did lose. Schottenheimer’s squad pulled this one off with zero room to spare. He has to be better. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey Brandon Aubrey is still fine in an overall sense, but his trustworthiness from downtown certainly has to change . Rather the Cowboys’ trust in him has to change. Aubrey missed a 50-yard field goal that would have given the Cowboys a 23-20 lead in this game late down the stretch. Given that it was such a deep attempt the miss gave Indianapolis the ball at their own 40-yard line and they took advantage by netting a go-ahead field goal themselves. Stock Down: DeMarvion Overshown Drawing an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for being out in the middle of the field when you are not even active for the game is peak silliness. Overshown’s penalty put a drive that should have started at the Cowboys’ 30-yard line at their own 15. They wound up punting and surrendering points. Those 15 yards were consequential, even if the Cowboys wound up winning. The Cowboys have a clear lack of a lot of things and therefore cannot afford to make silly mistakes. This was a silly mistake in the silliest of ways.

title: Cowboys at Colts: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 9
summary: In a game that was looking very much like a repeat of last week, the Dallas Cowboys were able to avoid another second half collapse by winning 27-23 in close, nail-biting fashion against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s difficult to get too excited about the outcome of the game, however, winning feels much better than losing […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images In a game that was looking very much like a repeat of last week, the Dallas Cowboys were able to avoid another second half collapse by winning 27-23 in close, nail-biting fashion against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s difficult to get too excited about the outcome of the game, however, winning feels much better than losing no matter how they got there. It was a mixed bag Sunday afternoon for the Cowboys. Today we’ll take a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly from this Week 9 matchup before we start setting our sites on next week’s opponent, the San Francisco 49ers. THE GOOD – WR CeeDee Lamb With George Pickens sidelined, Dak Prescott repeatedly targeted CeeDee Lamb throughout the game Sunday afternoon. The two connected for 10 catches for 195 receiving yards and a touchdown. It ended up being a historic day for No. 88. He made NFL history by breaking the record for the most receptions before turning 28 years old. It would’ve been a near-perfect outing if not for a questionable fumble, but even that doesn’t lessen the impact he made. THE BAD – Penalties The Cowboys were once again nearly their own worst enemy Sunday afternoon against the Colts. They had a total of 14 penalties in this Week 9 matchup and quite a few of them helped Indianapolis hang around longer than they should have. The officials didn’t seem to help matters all that much either. There were several questionable calls that went against the Cowboys, more than a few of them involving WR CeeDee Lamb. Luckily it didn’t cost them the win. THE UGLY – Colts turnovers The Cowboys defense wasn’t dominant by any means, but they did what they needed to do in order to secure the victory in Indianapolis Sunday afternoon. They had two huge turnovers that ended up altering the game of the Cowboys favor. First, the fumble caused by DT Quinnen Williams that put a stop to a promising drive by the Colts, and second, the interception by Caleb Downs at the end of the game to seal the victory. It wasn’t pretty, but it was enough.
author: Brian Martin

title: 5 plays that helped Dallas escape Indy with a win
summary: The Dallas Cowboys needed playmakers to step up against the Indianapolis Colts. They were without George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. so others needed to step up to avoid another loss to a team they were favored to beat. They made the win a lot closer than it needed to be. Luckily, they were able […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys needed playmakers to step up against the Indianapolis Colts. They were without George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. so others needed to step up to avoid another loss to a team they were favored to beat. They made the win a lot closer than it needed to be. Luckily, they were able to get big plays from some of their best players and some from players that have endured a rough stretch as of late. The Cowboys still trail the New York Giants in the NFC East, who also won today, but it feels much better than if they had lost. It wasn’t always pretty. The Cowboys had to overcome difficult situations, largely ones that they created for themselves due to penalties. Still, as the old saying goes: “A win is a win”. Here are five pivotal moments that helped Dallas secure the victory over Indianapolis. 1. Jake Ferguson answers the call on 4th down 2nd Quarter | 14:13 remaining | 4th-and-2 at Indianapolis 10-yard line When you absolutely have to have it, your players need to deliver. Jake Ferguson made one of the better plays of the day and one of the more impressive catches of the afternoon. Trailing Indianapolis 7-3, Dallas faced fourth-and-2 at the Colts’ 10-yard line. Rather than settle for another Brandon Aubrey field goal, the Cowboys elected to keep their offense on the field. Dak Prescott looked toward Ferguson, who made a tremendous adjustment on the football with Colts safety Cam Bynum in coverage. Ferguson displayed strong hands and the ability to battle a very bright sun, while maintaining possession through the catch. The 10-yard touchdown gave Dallas a 10-7 lead and capped a 15-play drive that began late in the first quarter. Jake Ferguson fourth down touchdown! DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SQTPeUplgs — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 As for Ferguson, he has come under criticism lately and this was exactly the type of response he and the Cowboys needed. Ferguson didn’t just make a difficult catch. He delivered in a situation where failure would have meant leaving points on the field, that’s pressure and he came through. It also rewarded Dallas for its aggressive decision-making and gave the offense some much-needed confidence. Now we’ll see how severe his injury turns out to be. 2. CeeDee Lamb lets loose in the secondary 2nd Quarter | 0:28 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Indianapolis 44-yard line Sometimes all it takes is one busted coverage to change the tide. With less than a minute remaining in the first half, Dallas was protecting a narrow 10-7 lead. The Colts had an opportunity to drain the remaining clock, but a holding penalty pushed Indianapolis backward. Keenan Allen’s subsequent sideline reception stopped the clock, allowing Dallas to preserve a timeout. That was the opportunity Dallas needed. The Cowboys regained possession at their own 25-yard line with 49 seconds remaining. After a nine-yard Javonte Williams run, Prescott connected with Lamb for 22 yards on third-and-1, advancing the ball to the Indianapolis 44-yard line with 38 seconds remaining. Then came the explosive play of the first half. CeeDee TD! Dak Prescott connects with CeeDee Lamb to add on six for the @dallascowboys 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/S1SuT4BFDz — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 8, 2026 On first-and-10, Lamb ran free through the Colts’ secondary after a coverage breakdown, and Prescott found his star receiver for a 44-yard touchdown. Just like that, Dallas turned a three-point advantage into a 17-7 halftime lead. The significance of this sequence cannot be overstated. Dallas had struggled to create separation, but the combination of defensive pressure, clock management, Prescott’s execution, and Lamb’s explosive ability completely changed the momentum entering halftime. Granted, the Cowboy would eventually surrender the two-score lead later, but they mismanaged the end of half against the Arizona Cardinals last week. This was progress albeit incremental. It was also a reminder of why Lamb remains the most dangerous weapon in the Cowboys’ passing attack and why you take the very, very good with the occasional very bad as we saw today. 3. Quinnen Williams Forces a Game-Changing Turnover 4th Quarter | 9:55 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Dallas 18-yard line There are defensive plays that look good on the stat sheet, and then there are plays that completely alter the direction of a game. Quinnen Williams delivered the latter. With Dallas clinging to a 20-17 lead, Indianapolis was threatening deep inside Cowboys territory. The Colts had moved the football effectively, aided by Dallas penalties, and appeared positioned to take the lead. Jonathan Taylor took the handoff, but Williams penetrated the backfield and stopped the running back while forcing the football loose. Shemar James recovered the fumble and returned it 11 yards before an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty pushed Dallas backward. Cowboys come right back with a takeaway of their own! DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NVQtl0FpYU — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Williams had prevented Indianapolis from potentially taking control of the game. The play also illustrated why Williams’ presence along the defensive front matters so much. Earlier in the contest, his ability to disrupt the pocket helped create problems for Daniel Jones. Later, his pressure contributed to a holding penalty that stalled another Colts possession. Williams repeatedly made Indianapolis account for his presence. The Cowboys needed a defensive difference-maker, and Williams provided exactly that when the stakes were highest. 4. Oh Boy, Flournoy! Flournoy does his best Pickens impression 4th Quarter | 1:37 remaining | 1st-and-10 at Dallas 35-yard line Just when it appeared the Cowboys might let another winnable game slip away, Ryan Flournoy delivered the biggest reception of his afternoon. Indianapolis had taken a 23-20 lead following Spencer Shrader’s 50-yard field goal with 1:41 remaining. Dallas needed at least three points to force overtime, but with only 97 seconds remaining, the Cowboys couldn’t afford to waste opportunities. Prescott wasted no time. DAK TO FLOURNOY COWBOYS IN THE RED ZONE DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fDDObDvGPq — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 On the first offensive snap of the drive, the Cowboys quarterback connected with Flournoy down the right sideline for a huge 46-yard gain, immediately moving Dallas from its own 35-yard line to the Indianapolis 19. Against coverage from Sauce Gardner, Flournoy’s catch completely changed the situation for Dallas. Instead of trying to settle for a game-tying field goal, the Cowboys were now able to be aggressive and take the late lead. The Cowboys suddenly found themselves inside the red zone with plenty of time remaining. A Javonte Williams run and two Indianapolis penalties eventually positioned Dallas at the one-yard line, where Williams punched in the go-ahead touchdown with 1:10 remaining. The Cowboys had reclaimed a 27-23 lead. While Williams deserves credit for finishing the drive, it was Flournoy’s explosive reception that made the comeback possible. For a Dallas offense that often relies heavily on Lamb, Flournoy’s emergence as another reliable option could prove invaluable moving forward. 5. Kenny Clark applies the pressure, Caleb Downs seals the Brother Bowl 4th Quarter | 0:41 remaining | 3rd-and-22 at Indianapolis 14-yard line — Interception The Cowboys had regained the lead, but the game was far from over. With Indianapolis receiving the football and more than a minute remaining, Daniel Jones still had an opportunity to orchestrate a game-winning drive. Dallas’ defensive front made sure that opportunity disappeared quickly. On the opening play, Jones was penalized for intentional grounding, costing Indianapolis 12 yards and triggering a 10-second runoff. The Colts suddenly faced second-and-22 from their…

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys win over the Colts
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are back in the win column, and all it took was facing an Indianapolis Colts team in despair to pull it off. It wasn’t pretty, it was unnecessarily nerve-racking, and it was filled with zany ups and downs. Regardless, the win gives purpose to the rest of the Cowboys’ season, despite still […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are back in the win column, and all it took was facing an Indianapolis Colts team in despair to pull it off. It wasn’t pretty, it was unnecessarily nerve-racking, and it was filled with zany ups and downs. Regardless, the win gives purpose to the rest of the Cowboys’ season, despite still leaving a lot of things to worry about. Here are 10 thoughts on the Cowboys 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. 1. Ground attack Brian Schottenheimer wanted to show he meant business by committing to the run, using six offensive linemen right out of the gate. Broderick Jones was in on the first play from scrimmage and was used often. The Cowboys had a perfect balance between running and passing with 34 plays of each. Javonte Williams led the charge with 101 yards rushing, while complementary back Tyler Goodson finished with 77 yards rushing. Both averaged over five yards per carry. 2. The Lamb circus What a strange day for Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb. In a game without his pass-catching partner in crime, George Pickens, Lamb did all the heavy lifting in this one. He finished the game with 10 catches for 195 yards. Weirdly, he was also involved in some odd stuff as he got flagged for two separate offensive pass interference penalties, negating clutch first-down catches. It was a strange mix of good and bad, and sometimes it happened on the same play. In the fourth quarter, Lamb made a great catch on a crucial third-down play where he wisely got up and started running before being touched. It was great until he eventually fumbled the ball away after a shoestring tackle. 3. Laundry day Speaking of penalties, the Cowboys were flagged for just about every type of penalty possible in this game. Three different times they were flagged for offensive pass interference. It felt like every offensive lineman got caught for holding (they didn’t). Even players who weren’t playing were getting flagged for stuff, as DeMarvion Overshown was flagged for an unsportsmanlike penalty despite not even playing in the game. Some of the flag stuff was just touchy officiating, but for a team that struggles with discipline, it frustrating to continue to see some of this silliness. 4. Playbook problems While the offense came through with a nice game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, everything up until that felt underwhelming. The offense did some things, we’re not discounting that, but it just felt like they weren’t doing enough against the Colts, who are one of the worst defenses in the league. They continued to have issues near the goal line, as if their playbook starts to shrink. They got it done, but it just feels like Brian Schottenheimer chooses the worst plays possible to do it. Last week, Bryan Anger punted for a season-high four times. On Sunday, he set a new season-high with five punts. Don’t let the win fool you. The Cowboys’ offense is starting to show some signs of trouble. 5. Trouble finding the mark Dak Prescott was a bit off at times, as he was sometimes throwing behind receivers and into coverage. That’s not good. Even Prescott’s good throws weren’t great. If Lamb got tackled in bounds after having to come back on that underthrown ball late in the first half, the Cowboys likely would’ve had to settle for a field goal there. Prescott still made some big plays, but he hasn’t been as sharp as he usually is, and that will need to change if they are to have a chance against better teams. 6. Defense showing up In this game, it became more enjoyable to watch the Cowboys’ defense play than their offense. At least early on. How did that happen? The Cowboys’ defense played well early in the game, forcing four three-and-outs on the Colts’ first five possessions of the game, and Indy’s longest play during that span was just seven yards. The Colts only had 86 total yards in the first half. The Cowboys’ defense started to give way some in the second half, but fortunately they were able to come away with big stops in big moments, including two fourth-quarter turnovers. Well done, defense. 7. A new career high for Q Quinnen Williams is so good at football. The Cowboys’ stud defensive tackle continues to play incredibly well, as he was constantly living the Colts backfield. He added another three tackles for loss, including a forced fumble that killed an Indy drive in the fourth quarter. He now has a total of 14 tackles for loss this season, which is a new career-high eclipsing the 12 he had during his All-Pro season in 2022. 8. Too close for comfort While the Cowboys came away with the win, this was another game they tried really hard to give away. The penalties, the turnovers, and even botching a snap that may have caused Brandon Aubrey to miss a field goal he almost always makes. Again and again, they were doing things that losing teams do. And again, it was against a bad team. They had plenty of chances to pull away, but that is just not their style. They continuously play down to the level of their opponent, as if they just love to live for the drama. 9. Sauce’d Ryan Flournoy only had two catches on the day, but his second one was a big one. After the Colts went ahead 23-20 late in the fourth quarter, the Cowboys answered back thanks to a big catch by Flournoy. Prescott took a shot deep and found Flournoy who tracked the ball well even with All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner draped all over him. It immediately changed the mood of the game as the Cowboys were instantly in field goal range and now could play for the win. 10. Sibling rivalry It was fun to watch the Downs brothers, Caleb and Josh, go against each other, but it was nicer seeing little bro get the better of it. The Cowboys rookie safety had a sack early in the game and then a game-sealing interception late in the fourth quarter. Strangely, it was the Cowboys’ first interception of the season by a defensive back.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas avoids another late-game upset, winning late over the Colts
summary: If there is one thing that fans can rely on this season, it’s that Dallas will keep things interesting. Even with the win, the Cowboys and their front office still need to make a decision on what the goal for this season is and how much they trust the current staff to achieve that goal. […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images If there is one thing that fans can rely on this season, it’s that Dallas will keep things interesting. Even with the win, the Cowboys and their front office still need to make a decision on what the goal for this season is and how much they trust the current staff to achieve that goal. In a postgame interview, Dak Prescott acknowledged that this win was crucial. The Cowboys don’t need to run the table to make the playoffs this season; however, games like this are necessary today and going forward. Time will tell if Dallas is able to get the job done in those crucial games, but on Sunday, they got the job done. Cowboys 27 – Colts 23: How Tough is this Dallas Team?- Cody Warren, Inside The Star A chronological recap of the game. Dak’s throw to Jonathan Mingo on the opening drive was great. Third-and-3, George Pickens out, and Dak goes down the middle to Mingo for 23 yards. Imagine being the Colts and having to account for Mingo the rest of the game because you gave him that much room while CeeDee Lamb was on the field. A few uneventful plays to Javonte Williams and you just gave Brandon Aubrey a shorter field goal. 8 instant takeaways from Cowboys’ ugly win over the Colts in Week 9- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat Caleb Downs is starting to make a bigger impact. Downs does so many things well, and blitzing is one of them. Whether it’s due to injuries in the secondary or Christian Parker simply being overwhelmed as a first-time play-caller, he has not blitzed his star rookie nearly enough this season. Parker went back to that well on 3rd-and-8 early in the second quarter. Downs came flying off the edge and buried Daniel Jones for a 10-yard loss to force a punt . Jones never saw him coming. It was a free shot, so you almost wish Downs had managed to jar the ball loose, but that’s nitpicking what was an outstanding play by the rookie. Dak Prescott, Cowboys offense persevere vs. Colts: ‘We had to have it’- Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dak Prescott is well aware this team will have their backs up against the wall for the remainder of the season. With a Giants team ahead of them that keeps winning, Dallas will need to do the same. “You get a chance, you got to go win it, you got to go finish it,” Prescott said. “There’s going to be some ups and downs, we can’t ride them, we’ve got to stay focused and stay locked into whatever our job is individually and it’s important collectively. At the end of the game, when you’ve got an opportunity to win or to close them out, you’ve got to do it, you can’t let up.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Game Recap, Highlights: Cowboys beat Colts 27-23 thanks to Downs, Lamb- K.D. Drummond, Cowboys Wire The encouraging aspect of this game is the fact that Dallas was more dominant than the score indicates. However, that may be more of an indictment of the coaching and game plan than a sign of optimism. But Prescott, inaccurate in the first half, unloaded a deep bomb to Ryan Flournoy on the first play of their final possession. Subbing in for an injured George Pickens, Flournoy proved his value with a 46-yard reception. A few plays later Javonte Williams was running the ball in for a 27-23 lead. Cowboys’ Narrow Win Shouldn’t Quiet the Conversation Around Jerry Jones and Brian Schottenheimer- Conor Orr, Sports Illustrated Winning is always the best way to keep your job as a head coach in the NFL. But after the win on Sunday, the front office needs to ask if Dallas won because of the coaching staff or in spite of them. So, do we simply pass on that conversation because the Cowboys barely beat the fire-sale Colts? There’s some deserved nuance, of course. The Cowboys were without Joey Porter Jr. and George Pickens, and finally the defense looked close to adequate. Rookie first-round pick Caleb Downs sealed the game with a clutch interception and made a critical tackle earlier in the chaotic waning minutes. CeeDee Lamb sets NFL record in Cowboys win over Colts- Matthew Lenix, Blogging The Boys CeeDee Lamb had a great day, continuing a great season thus far, and has had a record-setting start to his career. The Cowboys will need Lamb to continue to produce if Dallas is going to make a bid at winning the NFC East. In addition to that, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb set an NFL record. With his 10 receptions on Sunday, he now has 641 for his career which passes DeAndre Hopkins (632) for the most by any player before the age of 28.
author: Aidan Davis

title: DeMarvion Overshown had a bad moment and didn’t even play
summary: Culture was a buzzword around Brian Schottenheimer. Over the summer and through training camp, many people noted the culture that the head coach was building for and through the Dallas Cowboys. That, obviously, has felt a bit hollow as losses have piled up this season, but on Sunday, during a win, it was on full […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Culture was a buzzword around Brian Schottenheimer. Over the summer and through training camp, many people noted the culture that the head coach was building for and through the Dallas Cowboys. That, obviously, has felt a bit hollow as losses have piled up this season, but on Sunday, during a win, it was on full display in the worst possible way. Never, ever, EVER seen this before pic.twitter.com/WYMVcSfIPQ — Shan Shariff (@1053SS) November 8, 2026 In case you have no idea what is happening here, allow me to explain: The Cowboys were holding on to a 20-17 lead against Indianapolis It looked like the Colts were about to score Quinnen Williams forced a fumble from Jonathan Taylor of all people Shemar James recovered it and took it to the Dallas 30-yard line The video in question is the Cowboys defense celebrating. Why would they not? They just took the football away at a critical moment. Their hard work was worthy of jubilation. But someone else enters the frame. You can see someone, as the official described to be in sweats while assessing the penalty, run into the celebration. That was DeMarvion Overshown and as he was not a part of the team for the game (he was inactive) he was assessed with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. This was the case because the celebration was not happening on the sideline where Cowboys players and staffers happened to be. You can see in the video that the action is quite literally in the middle of the field. Somehow, some way, Overshown ran out that far into the field and backed the team up 15 yards as a result. Quite simply, this cannot happen. Overshown has been around for a while and is regarded to be among the team’s leaders. His inability to stay healthy is an issue, but he has always been seen as someone who at the very least is great from a leadership standpoint. This certainly was not that. Consider that the Cowboys did wind up getting those 15 yards back right away, but they punted on the ensuing possession and the Colts went on to tie the game up before eventually taking the lead that Dallas took back once and for all. But maybe the lack of penalty yards could have helped Dallas put the game away sooner. The point isn’t to live in hypotheticals. The point is that Overshown directly impacted his team’s ability to win and he did so while not even a part of the game. Brian Schottenheimer has to take care of that kind of thing.
