title: Brandon Aubrey concern levels heightened after Colts win
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won on Sunday. They did so by the skin of their teeth. It took almost all four quarters for the Cowboys to declare victory against the Indianapolis Colts, and for a little while near the end it looked like they were going to lose. Dallas was trailing 23-20 but wound up scoring […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys won on Sunday. They did so by the skin of their teeth. It took almost all four quarters for the Cowboys to declare victory against the Indianapolis Colts, and for a little while near the end it looked like they were going to lose. Dallas was trailing 23-20 but wound up scoring a touchdown to give them their final lead, but it is important to note that they missed a field goal prior to their last drive that would have made matters simpler. It was a 50-yard attempt from Brandon Aubrey, his 24th from 50+ since the beginning of last season. The miss officially means that he now has double-digit misses of that variety. Brandon Aubrey is now 14/24 on 50+ yard field goals since the beginning of last season. 58% hit rate is the second-worst among all kickers with 15+ 50-yard attempts. Only Harrison Butker (44%) has been worse. — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) November 8, 2026 Aubrey’s miss gave the Colts the ball at the Dallas 40-yard line which meant that they did not have to travel all too far for the field goal that successfully gave them their 23-20 lead. That is the inherent risk with attempts from that far, and while it was once Aubrey’s specialty, it is now a higher-proposition risk than it used to be. It should be noted that eight of these field goals have been from 60+ which certainly changes the calculus and more importantly the evaluation. Half of the 60+ attempts are a part of the overall misses from Aubrey so there is still a legitimate value involved of misses between 50 and 59 yards which is pretty standard (relatively speaking) for today’s NFL kickers. The Cowboys gave Aubrey an extension this past offseason that officially made him the highest-paid kicker in the NFL. Without getting too interested in another person’s finances, the reality of that deal is that it means Aubrey has to be more reliable, especially at something that was regarded to be his forte.

title: The Broncos are riding high into their bye after comeback victory over Panthers
summary: The Denver Broncos, the comeback kings of the National Football League, pulled off another nailbiter on Sunday. Another impressive fourth quarter comeback was the big factor in their 26-21 win against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Broncos have set a new NFL record with sixteen-straight wins in one-score games. On top of that, they […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant (13) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos, the comeback kings of the National Football League, pulled off another nailbiter on Sunday. Another impressive fourth quarter comeback was the big factor in their 26-21 win against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Broncos have set a new NFL record with sixteen-straight wins in one-score games. On top of that, they have moved to 7-2 on the season and still hold the top spot in the AFC West. Another game, another mark in the win column. This year’s Broncos haven’t been at their best. Nevertheless, they’ve reeled off five victories in a row and enter the bye week with a lot of momentum in their favor. Now, Denver gets to enjoy their bye week and will have some much-needed time off to recuperate and recalibrate before their Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. After yesterday’s victory, Head Coach Sean Payton reflected on the team’s odds-defying streak of wins. The probability of the Broncos winning sixteen of those close affairs in a row? Presumably 150 million to one. While the wins are great, Payton isn’t content and knows the team still has a lot of work to do to get better in the second half of the season. “Well, part of it pisses me off because there’s been a few of them that you would say shouldn’t have been one-score games and then obviously there’s some that are. Look, they’ve been great. We knew coming in Thursday, we just knew the type of team we were playing,” stated Paton. “They’ve been doing some really explosive things on offense. They were banged up certainly on defense as we were. We’ll take this break, but we still have to be—and it’s not that you’re never satisfied—but we still have some work to do.” The Broncos struggled to find an answer to the Panthers’ offensive prowess late in the first half and at the beginning of the second half. Fourth-year quarterback Bryce Young was able to carve up Denver’s depleted secondary and march down the field numerous times to keep them in the game. At times, the Broncos were their own worst enemies. The penalties and miscues that happened late could have very well cost them the game. But when the stakes were at their highest, the defense was able to force several turnovers and the offense ignited in the fourth quarter to lead the team to their seventh win of the season. One issue that has plagued Denver all season long was third down conversions. Entering the game, they were one of the league’s worst converting less than 30-percent of those opportunities. Against the Panthers, the team was 6-of-10 and had a hot streak late in the game that was a huge difference maker. Quite impressive, considering they were down one of their top receiving targets for the entire second half. Quarterback Bo Nix took time after the game to highlight the other wide receivers who stepped up and were clutch when it mattered most. “We got plays for Jaylen that somebody else has to step in and take. That’s what, in my opinion, was the fun part of today. That was really cool to see Troy, Pat, and Marvin step up and make plays when their numbers were called,” stated Nix. “Even though they didn’t have reps at it all week, they studied and knew what they were supposed to do. To me, that’s fun football, when you’re in there and your back’s against the wall and you just have to figure out a way to go get a first down,” added Nix. Over the first nine weeks of the season, the Broncos have shown a lot of grit and guts. Their resilience is certainly one of their best qualities. No matter how tough things get, they don’t seem to flinch in the face of adversity. In fact, it almost seems like they relish it. Denver’s second half slate of opponents is much easier than the gauntlet they have faced to start the season. That may give them an inside track to have a shot at the AFC’s top playoff seed for a second consecutive season. However, they will need to play much better overall in order to make that happen. One question that looms large is whether or not the Broncos’ brass feels confident that the current group of players are good enough to accomplish that. Coach Payton noted he likes this year’s squad, but will certainly be leaving no stone unturned when it comes to potentially making additions before tomorrow’s trade deadline. “That’s impossible to predict. We’ll discuss what’s out there, and I think we’ll see what happens. But I like this team. There’s room for us to get better, but I like this team a lot. We just got to take advantage of the position we’re sitting in right now.” At 7-2 and atop the AFC West, Denver is in a great spot. Will they make a big move that can help solidify their status as a true Super Bowl contender? We will know that answer to that in the next thirty hours.

They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? title: Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 10 vs. Panthers
summary: The Broncos did it again! After yet another 4th-quarter comeback, the Broncos won their 5th straight game with their victory over the Carolina Panthers and improved to 7-2 on the season. Like every Broncos game, this game was a rollercoaster from the start. They took an early 10-0 lead, but the Panthers came charging back […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos scores a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Broncos did it again! After yet another 4th-quarter comeback, the Broncos won their 5th straight game with their victory over the Carolina Panthers and improved to 7-2 on the season. Like every Broncos game, this game was a rollercoaster from the start. They took an early 10-0 lead, but the Panthers came charging back and were on the verge of going up 21-13. Then it happened. Devon Key’s incredible interception flipped this game upside down and gave the momentum back to the Broncos, and they never looked back. Things did get tight there at the end, but Nik Bonitto called game with a clutch strip-sack, and the Broncos went on to celebrate another remarkable win. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell you which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After yet another 4th-quarter comeback and one-score victory, we have plenty of stocks trending in the right direction, with a few notable stocks going in the wrong direction. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up slightly: I thought Bo Nix played well overall on Sunday. He made some good throws and was leading the Broncos up and down the field against this Panthers secondary full of backups. However, he did have the interception and the off-target pitch late in the game. This was Nix’s first interception since the one he threw vs. the Rams, where his arm was hit mid-throw, so I am not going to knock him too much for it. I am going with stock slightly up. He threw for 237 yards and 2 touchdowns, which is a stat line I will take each and every week from Nix. He is beginning to look more and more like the quarterback we saw last season and I believe that will continue as the team emerges from their bye week. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos veteran backup. Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ third-string emergency quarterback. Running Back Jonah Coleman – Stock up: The takeover has happened. Jonah Coleman played 58 of the 75 snaps on Sunday (77%) and was the unquestioned starter of the Broncos’ backfield. He did not disappoint either. He had 17 carries for 57 yards, which is more of an offensive line problem than a running back problem (more on that later), but did score another touchdown and had an additional 4 receptions for 31 yards. Altogether, he had 21 touches for 88 yards and a touchdown. A pretty solid showing for the Broncos rookie running back, but we’ll have to see if they add to this running back room prior to the trade deadline this week. JK Dobbins – Stock down: 4 carries for 18 yards and a 15% snap share. That right there says it all. Dobbins has clearly fallen out of favor in the Broncos’ backfield, and his time with the team could be coming to an end if they add another back at the deadline. We’ll see what happens, but his role has significantly decreased since Jonah Coleman returned from injury. Cody Schrader – Unchanged: Schrader was elevated from the practice squad but did not have a major role in Sunday’s game. Adam Prentice – Unchanged: Played 15 snaps on offense while also being a main contributor on special teams. He has his role on this team and he does it well. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Unchanged: This was going to be a big Jaylen Waddle game, but unfortunately, the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver was knocked out of the game early after he suffered a concussion from a dirty hit by a Panthers defender. Before he left the game, he had 1 catch for 22 yards and was destined for more. Courtland Sutton – Stock up: I thought Sutton played solid on Sunday. It wasn’t a huge game for the Broncos veteran wide receiver, but he led the wide receivers with 85% of the snaps and had 5 catches for 45 yards and a touchdown. He caught everything thrown his way and made multiple big catches on third down for the Broncos. A solid overall showing. Pat Bryant – Stock up: Welcome back, Pat Bryant! The Broncos’ second-year wide receiver returned from IR before the game and made an immediate impact on the offense. He led the Broncos in receiving yards with 56 and had what ended up being the game-winning 26-yard touchdown late in the 4th quarter. I think we will continue seeing Bryant make more and more impact plays as the season progresses. Troy Franklin – Stock up: Like Sutton, I thought Troy played a solid overall game that nearly ended up being a big game. He finished with 3 catches for 31 yards, but had multiple clutch catches on third down late in the game. However, he nearly had a touchdown right before halftime, but a Panthers defender was able to knock the ball away. It was an incredible pass by Nix to Franklin who was open down the seam. Close, but not cigar. Marvin Mims – Unchanged: Mims did not do a whole lot on Sunday, but played his role. He saw limited snaps on offense but wasn’t able to do much with them and continued being a kick return specialist for them. Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He was inactive. Tight End Adam Trautman – Stock up: He continues to lead the Broncos tight ends in snaps and has seen his role in the passing game increase a little bit in back-to-back games. He had a 20+ yard reception vs. the Chiefs and vs. the Panthers, he had 2 receptions for 15 yards. Nothing to write home about, but the bar is low. Evan Engram – Stock down: The stock down has little to do with his performance on Sunday, but more to do with the reports that the Broncos are looking to trade for a tight end. If they acquire a tight end, it will be a pass-catcher in all likelihood, which would negatively impact Engram’s role and potentially even his roster spot. Now, nothing has happened, but the fact that they are looking isn’t great for Engram. On Sunday, Engram did have 4 catches for 33 yards, which is one of his better performances this season, so we’ll see if anything changes here in the coming days. Nate Adkins – Unchanged: Played 24% of the snaps on offense, but primarily played special teams and made a nice tackle on a return late in the game. He has his role, and he fills it well. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Remained inactive. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: Continues to be one of the better blindside protectors in the NFL. Ben Powers – Stock down: The middle of the Broncos’ line struggled on Sunday, and Powers was 50% of the problem. It’s hard to get a run game going when you’re allowing immediate pressure. Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: Here is the other 50% of the problem. Wattenberg is praised for his intelligence, but he was knocked back a bit on Sunday and allowed immediate interior pressure. Both need to play better or it doesn’t matter who our running back is. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: Stud. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: Can’t say I really noticed him positively or negatively on Sunday, which usually is a good thing. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played 5% of the snaps on Sunday, but maybe should see some time at left guard moving forward. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Kage Casey – Unchanged: The rookie remained inactive, but maybe should see time at left guard? Defensive Line Zach Allen – Unchanged: I expected the defensive line to dominate a struggling Panthers offensive line, and that did not happen. DJ Jones – Unchanged: Has been solid for the Broncos this season, but the Panthers had success on the ground vs. them. Malcolm Roach – Unchanged: Has been a very underrated part of the Broncos’ defensive line this season, but the unit struggled throughout most of the game. Sai’vion Jones – Unchanged: Played 35% of the snaps and saw a minor boost in snaps with Uwazurike now on the IR. Jordan Jackson – Unchanged:…

title: Game balls for the Broncos’ win over Panthers in Week 9
summary: The Denver Broncos set the NFL record for most consecutive one score wins in NFL history with their 26-21 road win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Bo Nix also added yet another fourth quarter comeback to his belt. He is setting a pace so far above historical norms that most assume he’ll come crashing […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Nik Bonitto #15 of the Denver Broncos blocks pass by Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos set the NFL record for most consecutive one score wins in NFL history with their 26-21 road win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Bo Nix also added yet another fourth quarter comeback to his belt. He is setting a pace so far above historical norms that most assume he’ll come crashing back to earth at some point. But not today… Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . It looked early on like the Broncos were going to steamroll the Panthers, but momentum is a very real thing in the NFL and this game had two massive momentum swings that determined the outcome. The first came when Nix and the Broncos were rolling. In the red zone, on the verge of extending their 10-0 lead, a defender made a great play on the ball to intercept the pass. Nix never saw him. That sparked the Panthers on a run of their own that had them up 14-13. Then, Devon Key made a heads up play on a ball that was tipped up in the end zone and snatched the ball just before it would have hit the ground. That really was the game-saving turnover and swung momentum back Denver’s way. The were up 26-14 in very short order. Carolina made a game of it anyway late, but as usual, the defense made a play when it needed it the most. This team just has that clutch factor in all phases. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to from the Broncos win over the Panthers: Nik Bonitto When the Broncos needed a game-changing play, Casa Bonitto was open for business. The Broncos edge rusher delivered a strip-sack of Bryce Young on first-and-10 with 1:24 remaining in the game. Bonitto also recovered the fumble for Denver to help secure the big road victory. For the game, Bonitto finished with two tackles (two solo), two tackles for loss, one sack, and one quarterback hit. And as a fan who was surrounded by crying and whining Panthers fans the whole game, they got really quiet after Bonitto pulled his best Von Miller impression. #KeepPouting – Ian St. Clair NIK BONITTO STRIP SACK!!! pic.twitter.com/J1S1WXz4LK — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 Pay Bryant Pat Bryant get my gameball. In a game where the Broncos lost Jaylen Waddle to injury, Pat Bryant needed to step up, and step up he did. He led the team with 56 receiving yards and caught 4 of his 5 targets. It also seemed like every one of his catches was a first down (or a TD). Coming back from injury, he showed that the Bronco offense is so much more effective with him in the game then with injured. – Joe Mahoney PAT BRYANT TOUCHDOWN!! pic.twitter.com/B7yLaSF3zx — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 Jonah Coleman Jonah Coleman has worked his way into being the Broncos starting running back. The numbers don’t explode off the page, but his day against the Panthers earned him a gameball. With 57 rushing yards, 31 receiving yards, and one rushing touchdown, he helped the Broncos get a road win to stay atop the division. He also recovered the fumbled pitch from Bo Nix, which could have lead to disaster. When it was time to work the clock, it was Coleman that carried the load. Big game for the rookie. – Adam Malnati JONAH COLEMAN TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/cUV3F2sMA2 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 Courtland Sutton I feel like this was Courtland Sutton’s best game of the year. He dominated his 1v1 and drew multiple fouls on the Panthers’ defense that extended drives. He finished with just 5 catches for 45 yards and a touchdown, but his impact was felt at key moments that won’t show up in that final stat line. We need more of that from Sutton down the stretch and it will open things up across the board. – Tim Lynch TOUCHDOWN COURTLAND SUTTON pic.twitter.com/ET4XZEMPEm — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 Sean Payton Sean Payton gets my game ball for getting the challenge flag on the interception in the end zone that swung the momentum for this game. He barely beat the snap, and it changed everything. Not only that, but Payton has this team dialed in on how to play football in tight ball games. He’s changed this culture in his time with this team from a team full of players just playing to a team full of players playing with belief in each other every play, no matter what the situation. – Sadaraine DEVON KEY WITH AN UNBELIEVABLE INT!! pic.twitter.com/Cz0tX58Htb — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Panthers game? title: Broncos’ offense continues to improve
summary: The Denver Broncos are on a five-game win streak and head into the bye with a 7-2 record and temporarily atop the AFC West. The Kansas City Chiefs could retake it through tiebreaker with a win next week. After the game, head coach Sean Payton was asked about the offensive turnaround over the last three […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 08: Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant (13) celebrates scoring a touchdown during an NFL football game between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers on November 8, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos are on a five-game win streak and head into the bye with a 7-2 record and temporarily atop the AFC West. The Kansas City Chiefs could retake it through tiebreaker with a win next week. After the game, head coach Sean Payton was asked about the offensive turnaround over the last three games and he was cautiously optimistic. He said the offense is improving and that matches what we’ve seen on the field. “Hopefully, we’re improving,” Payton said after the game. “We talked a little bit going into this game, remember at the start of the week with a new defensive coordinator. I would say the difference clearly was a lot more Buffalo nickel, not Okie. If you said what was the change? Prior, we had a good portion of the plan devoted to the out front, and I think you almost had to have gotten in your really heavy groups to get it, so a lot of Buffalo nickel and a lot of nickel. That was what was maybe a little bit different, and we felt that early on.” I would say the turnaround began in the first half of the Thursday Night Football game against the Seattle Seahawks. That defense is elite and there was a moment when we saw the full version of the offense come alive in the second quarter with 16 play, 74 yard and 9 play, 79 yard touchdown drives. Of course, they looked pretty awful the rest of the game, but we caught a glimpse of what their offensive identity could be. From there, the inconsistency reared up at times but less often as the team racked up 30, 28, and 26 points in those last three games. Two of those required comeback wins again and that is something many say is unsustainable, but there is also a mantra to the comeback mentality that this team thrives under. “There’s always a look in the huddle that, like, hey guys, we don’t have a choice right here,” Bo Nix said of the comeback mentality. “We got to go make something out of it. Today, those second-half touchdowns were really, really important.” The streak will end as all streaks do, but the end of the streak doesn’t necessarily mean a violent return to the mean for this team. They have battled-tested experience in close games and that should give them confidence in any situation and against any opponent to go out there and make the plays needed to pull a rabbit out of the hat. I love how they do it. How they continue to do it. No one can explain how Denver is 7-2 and no one outside of Denver thinks they are good. However, they own the best record in the NFL since the start of the 2025 season. At some point, you just have to accept that this team is as good as their record. Horse Tracks

full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers with Bo Nix #10 during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. However, the New England Patriots were blown out and fell to 5-4 on the year and have several teams on their heels looking to get into the postseason. Another loss for the Cleveland Browns has them free-falling; the Las Vegas Raiders lost again, but continue to be a scrappy team, while the Baltimore Ravens will look to stay in the conversation with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. The 3-win Houston Texans are looking and could make a run for a wild-card spot in the second half of the year. AFC West Standings Denver Broncos (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) AFC playoff standings after Sunday of Week 9 Buffalo Bills (6-1) – Monday Night Football Denver Broncos (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, win over CIN, 3-2 AFC) Kansas City Chiefs (6-2, 6-1 AFC) Cincinnati Bengals (6-2, loss to PIT, 4-2 AFC) New England Patriots (5-4, 5-1 AFC) In the hunt Cleveland Browns (5-4, 3-3 AFC) Las Vegas Raiders (4-5, 3-3 AFC) Baltimore Ravens (4-5, 2-4 AFC) Houston Texans (3-5) New York Jets (2-7, 2-4 AFC) Indianapolis Colts (2-7, 1-5 AFC) Miami Dolphins (1-7, 1-4 AFC) Tennessee Titans (1-7, 1-5 AFC) Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) Division Leader s 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) The Bills entered the week as the one seed in the AFC but face a tough Vikings defense on Monday Night Football. A win would keep them as the one seed, but a loss would push the Denver Broncos to the one seed. Both teams will play each other on Christmas, which could decide who comes away with the number one seed in the AFC. They are led by MVP candidate Josh Allen and this strong Buffalo Bills run game and will be a difficult matchup for whoever plays them this season. Looking ahead: @ Vikings, @ Jets, vs. Dolphins, vs. Chiefs, @ Patriots, @ Packers, vs. Bears, @ Broncos, @ Dolphins, vs. Jets 2. Denver Broncos (7-2) The Denver Broncos improved to 7-2 on the year after their win over the Panthers and head into their BYE with a shot to take over as the number one seed in the AFC if the Bills lose on Monday Night. This is a much-needed week off for the Broncos, who are a bit banged up right now and can use this extra week to heal up and get ready for the strong second-half push. They had a brutal schedule to start the year, but on paper, the schedule gets much easier in the second half. If they can take care of business, they control their own destiny when it comes to the AFC West and the number one seed in the AFC. Looking ahead: BYE, vs. Raiders, @ Steelers, vs. Dolphins, @ Jets, @ Raiders, vs. Bills, @ Patriots, and vs. Chargers 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) The Jaguars are one of the hottest teams in the NFL (the Broncos beat them, though) and entered the week as the number 3 seed in the AFC. With a win on Thursday Night vs. the Ravens, the Jags improved to 6-2 and look like one of the top contenders in the AFC. They’re led by head coach Liam Coen, quarterback Trevor Lawrence, and one of the more explosive offenses in the NFL. They have a strong passing game, run it well, and have a defense that will keep them close in each and every game. Looking ahead: @ Titans, @ Giants, vs. Titans, @ Bears, vs. Steelers, @ Texans, @ Cowboys, vs. Commanders, and @ Colts 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) The Steelers remain the kings of the AFC North, led by future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers, a strong run game, and a dominant defense. However, they have the Bengals right on their heels in what figures to be a tight race for the division moving forward. We saw the Bengals win early this morning in Madrid, Spain, while the Steelers enjoyed their bye week. The Ravens, who lost Lamar Jackson but traded for Jacoby Brissett, are lurking as well. Looking ahead: @Bengals, @ Eagles, vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, @Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, @ Titans, and @ Ravens Wild Card teams 5. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) The Chiefs ended their two-game losing streak at home vs. the Jets. However, their season flashed before their eyes after quarterback Patrick Mahomes looked to hurt his throwing elbow. While it did not look good, Mahomes returned to the game and finished it without any issues. They still trail the Broncos in the division but will look to keep it close for the remainder of the season. On paper, they have a tough second-half schedule, so they will need to beat some good teams if they want to reclaim the AFC West. Looking ahead: @ Falcons, vs. Cardinals, @ Bills, @Rams, @ Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, @ Chargers, vs. Raiders 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) The Bengals stayed hot in Madrid this morning and defeated the Atlanta Falcons due to their explosive offense led by Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. They currently trail the Steelers in the division but face them in a key game next week. Despite a poor run game and a leaky defense, the Bengals are one of the hottest teams in the NFL and currently have the best passing offense in the NFL. Can the arm of Joe Burrow lead them to an AFC North crown? Looking ahead: vs. Steelers, @ Commanders, vs. Saints, @ Browns, vs. Chiefs, @ Panthers, @ Colts, vs. Ravens, and vs. Browns 7. New England Patriots (5-4) After a tough blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers, the Patriots fell to 5-4, but remain in the playoffs as of now due to the struggles of the rest of the AFC teams. However, they have a few hungry teams behind them ready to pounce. The Patriots had a tough start to the season, but seemed to turn things around recently, but have dropped two of their last three games, and needed a comeback to beat the Dolphins last week. They cannot afford many more losses if they want to make the playoffs or even consider winning the AFC East. Looking ahead: vs. Lions, BYE, @ Chargers, vs. Bills, vs. Vikings, @ Chiefs, @ Jets, vs. Broncos, and vs. Dolphins In The Hunt 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) 11. Houston Texans (3-5)

title: Winners and Losers from the Broncos’ 26-21 victory over the Panthers
summary: That wasn’t the prettiest of games, but the Broncos have perfected winning ugly and sloppy games, and did it again today on the road vs. the Panthers. After an up-and-down 4th quarter, the Broncos, with the help of a timely strip-sack by Nik Bonitto, came away with the win and improved to 7-2 on the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images That wasn’t the prettiest of games, but the Broncos have perfected winning ugly and sloppy games, and did it again today on the road vs. the Panthers. After an up-and-down 4th quarter, the Broncos, with the help of a timely strip-sack by Nik Bonitto, came away with the win and improved to 7-2 on the year. The offense played well at times, but left points on the field due to some sloppy play. Key defensive plays by Devon Key and Nik Bonitto were game-changers and a big reason why the Broncos won this game. Again, this was a sloppy game, but we have multiple big winners from this game with some losers mixed in. So, with all that said, here are my winners and losers from the Denver Broncos’ 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers. WINNER – Nik Bonitto, clutch strip-sack The defense and pass rush were not great for most of the game, more on that later, but once again, the Broncos’ defense and their pass rush came up big when it mattered most. After a near fumble on a pitch play set the Broncos’ offense back, they punted the ball to the Panthers with plenty of time to lead a game-winning drive. After a 21-yard pass on the first play, things looked dire for the Broncos, but Bonitto called game with what ended up being the game-ending strip-sack. Clutch. NIK BONITTO STRIP SACK!!! pic.twitter.com/J1S1WXz4LK — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 This is the second week in a row where the Broncos defense needed some late-game magic to win the game, and the defense came through. They had their struggles throughout (again, more on that later), but came up big in the biggest moment and won this game for the Broncos. WINNER – Devon Key’s wild INT in the end zone The Panthers were driving with a one-point lead and were on the verge of making it an 8-point lead after driving down the field against the Broncos’ helpless defense. Instead of running it in on 1st down, Bryce Young threw a pass into the end zone that fell incomplete. They would run another play, or so we thought, that ended with the Broncos stuffing the run. However, the refs deemed that Broncos head coach Sean Payton threw the challenge flag prior to the snap because it appeared that reserve safety Devon Key made an incredible INT off the deflection. It looked like he caught it, and they ruled he made the interception. Wow. A game-changing and momentum-shifting INT by Key. DEVON KEY WITH AN UNBELIEVABLE INT!! pic.twitter.com/Cz0tX58Htb — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 This took points off the board for the Panthers and completely changed the outcome of this game. It looked like they were about to go up by 8 points and continue their dominance of the Broncos’ defense. Not so fast, my friend! The Broncos would take a 19-14 lead on a Jonah Coleman touchdown and then a 26-14 lead after a Pat Bryant touchdown. The Panthers made it close late, but this play completely changed the outcome for the Broncos. LOSER – Sloppy play This was not a well-played game by the Broncos. Sure, they made some big plays throughout, but they left points on the field on offense, and the defense made errors throughout and allowed the Panthers to drive up and down the field multiple times. Nix’s INT in the red zone while up 10-0 ignited the Panthers’ comeback, and later his iffy pitch to Jonah Coleman led to a fumble, which they recovered, but completely derailed the drive and allowed the Panthers to get the ball back. On defense, they had missed tackles, no pass rush for most of the game, and allowed multiple third/fourth long plays to go for a first down. Back-breaking conversions that kept the Panthers in this game. In the end, they won the game, and that is all that matters, but they kept the Panthers in this game and nearly gave them a good shot at winning this game. LOSER – Broncos defense (outside of the two turnovers) For a second straight week, the Broncos defense played poorly for most of the game. The pass rush was non-existent; the Panthers were able to run the ball consistently, they had no answer for Darren Waller, and allowed conversions on 3rd and 17 and 4th and 18, which is unacceptable. Again, they made the clutch plays to win this game, but the Panthers’ offense had their number for most of the game. Bryce Young had a good game with 276 yards and 3 touchdowns; Hubbard had 4.9 yards per carry; Waller had 90 yards and a touchdown, and they had missed tackles throughout. Injuries to Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufange who were inactive and cornerback Riley Moss who left with a concussion likely contributed to the woes in the secondary, but still, not a great showing. Joseph calling soft zone coverage on those 3rd-and-4th and long plays led to two wide-open receivers. In the end, they won the game, but I had hoped for a better performance from the defense. WINNER – Welcome back, Pat Bryant Pat Bryant was activated off the injured reserve this weekend and made a huge impact in this game. His 26-yard touchdown catch ended up being the difference in this game and he showcased how he can be a difference-maker for this team in the second half of the season. PAT BRYANT TOUCHDOWN!! pic.twitter.com/B7yLaSF3zx — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 He finished the game with 4 catches for 56 yards and a touchdown, which led the team. With Waddle leaving the game with an injury, they needed him to step up, and he did. LOSER – Broncos interior OL The interior of the Broncos’ offensive line, specifically Ben Powers and Luke Wattenberg, struggled at times today. Multiple times, they allowed an unblocked defender in the backfield to blow up a run. The run game was not great today, but that’s more on the offensive line than the runners in my opinion. WINNER – 4th quarter Bo Nix I thought Bo played a good game today. Probably his best as a passer all season. However, the mistakes clouded what looked to be a good game by Nix. The interception, which he doesn’t throw many, wasn’t great. He was fooled by the defender, whom he thought was going to take RB JK Dobbins, but instead drifted infront of Courtland Sutton and led to the easy pick. They were on their way to making it a 17-0 game, or at least 13-0, but this turnover sparked the Panthers’ comeback. Then, late in the 4th quarter, Nix had a poor pitch to RB Jonah Coleman, which led to them losing 10+ yards on the play. It wasn’t a turnover, and I am not sure who gets the blame there (I didn’t get a good look at it), but still, you can’t have that in that big of a moment. Still, Nix led the Broncos to 13 4th quarter points, including the touchdown pass to Pat Bryant to give him yet another 4th quarter comeback. I saw some encouraging stuff, but the sloppy play clouds what was a good game by Nix. LOSER – Injuries suck Thank god for the bye week because the Denver Broncos are banged up. Talanoa Hufanga – Inactive Brandon Jones – Inactive Jaylen Waddle – Left the game with a concussion Riley Moss – Left the game with a concussion Eyioma Uwazurike – Placed on the short-term IR Tyler Badie – On the IR RJ Harvey – On the IR Now, the BYE will not impact the IR players since it doesn’t count towards the 4 games, but it does give everyone an extra week to heal and rest up. Thankfully, Waddle and Moss will get two weeks to recover from the concussions they suffered, and hopefully, Jones and Hufanga will be back after the Bye week. Other notable Winners and Losers WINNER – Courtland Sutton: Had 5 catches for 45 yards and made some clutch catches for the Broncos. WINNER – Troy Franklin: Made some big plays on 3rd down in the second half of the game. WINNER – Jonathon Cooper: Had a big sack and multiple pressures. WINNER – Jonah Coleman: Played alright…

title: Instant reaction: Broncos rally in fourth quarter to defeat Panthers in another nailbiter
summary: The Denver Broncos battled the Carolina Panthers this afternoon in their Week 9 matchup. It was a back-and-forth game between the two teams that came down to the final of quarter of play to find a winner. In the end, the Broncos came out on top registering another comeback victory to move to 7-2 on […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos battled the Carolina Panthers this afternoon in their Week 9 matchup. It was a back-and-forth game between the two teams that came down to the final of quarter of play to find a winner. In the end, the Broncos came out on top registering another comeback victory to move to 7-2 on the season. Here are some instant reactions from today’s game. Broncos’ offense ignites in fourth quarter to seal the deal For the entire first half of the season struggling on offense, the Broncos had an opportunity to shine against the Panthers. Carolina entered today’s matchup sporting a bottom 5 run defense, a bad third down defense, and the second-worst red zone defense in the NFL. After scoring 10 first quarter points against the Panthers, things looked up for Denver’s offense. They dominated first half time of possession and notched 15 first downs and 159 yards of total offense. Unfortunately, a Bo Nix interception in enemy territory proved to be a big momentum change in the game. In addition to that, Denver’s interior offensive line was manhandled in the first two quarters. Ben Powers and Luke Wattenberg struggled with Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown and Denver gained just 34 yards on the ground in the first half. The Broncos’ offense wasn’t on the field much in the third quarter. But as usual, four quarter heroics once again came into focus. Denver was able to carve out two scoring drives. The first was a 17-play drive that went 80 yards and was capped off with a Jonah Coleman touchdown run. On their next possession, Nix was able to hit Pat Bryant on a beautiful 26-yard touchdown throw. The touchdowns were great, but it was awesome to see Nix and the offense perform well on third down. They had a lot of big drive-sustaining conversions that made the final touchdowns possible. But that pitch to Coleman late in the game that could have cost Denver the win? Oof. That certainly raised the collective blood pressure of Broncos Country. I was hoping for more effectiveness in the ground game, but I’m happy to see Denver’s offense come together in the fourth quarter and ignite to lead the Broncos to victory. Their success was a big part of why they were able to get their fifth-straight victory of the season. Well done, offense! Beat up Broncos’ defense struggles, but does enough to hold off Panthers’ offense The Broncos entered today’s matchup with several key starters out on defense. The starting safety tandem of Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga were out, making Devon Key and J.L. Skinner the next men up. Defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike was also inactive after being placed on injured reserve. To make things worse, Riley Moss exited the game in the second quarter after suffering a concussion. Down four starters, Bryce Young and the Panthers’ offense was able to gain some steam and have success. Carolina reeled off back-to-back touchdown drives at the end of the first half and the start of the second half to take a 14 to 13 lead in the third quarter. Whether it was the pass or the run, Vance Joseph’s defense couldn’t find a way to get them off the field. Young had an impressive streak of fifteen-straight completed passes. A big issue all game long was the absence of a formidable pass rush which was quite a bit of a surprise. The Panthers entered today’s matchup allowing 23 sacks. Denver wasn’t able to take down Young until halfway through the four quarter when Jonathon Cooper came up big on third down and finally brought the fourth-year signal caller down. The defense had two big plays that saved their poor play throughout the contest. The first was when Key was able to intercept a pass in the endzone that bounced off Tommy Tremble’s right arm. To end the game, Nik Bonitto was able to strip sack Young in the final minutes of play to seal the deal for the Broncos. I’ll say this though, Denver giving up so many third-and-long plays, even with the injuries, was extremely concerning. I thought Joseph’s conservative playcalling late in the game was perplexing. The defense will have a lot of reflection to do over the bye week to rectify some of the issues we have seen recently, but I’m happy they were able to close the game out with a big turnover. Broncos enter bye week with momentum and a 7-2 record It’s incredibly hard to get a read on who this year’s Broncos are. However, they just keep finding ways to win. Today’s victory over the Panthers is their fifth in a row. They still maintain the AFC West lead with their victory today and hold their place as the second seed in the AFC’s tough playoff race. All things considered, the bye week couldn’t have come at a better time. It’s time for Denver to recalibrate, regroup, and find a way to fix their issues in the second half of the season.

PAT BRYANT TOUCHDOWN!! pic.twitter.com/B7yLaSF3zx — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 8, 2026 The Panthers had no quit in this game either. They had to convert on a fourth and 18 on their next drive to keep their hopes alive with three minutes left in the game. He was able to recover, but the damage was done and the Broncos would be punting it back to Carolina with plenty of time on the clock for them to execute their own comeback. The Panthers looked like they would mount a comeback of their own on a 21-yard completion on the first play, but on the second Nik Bonitto batted the ball out of Byrce Young’s hand where Denver recovered to ice the game. title: Detroit Lions trade for veteran safety from Jets
summary: The Detroit Lions are on the board for the 2026 NFL trade deadline. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Lions are trading for New York Jets safety Andre Cisco. In return, the Lions are sending the Jets a 2028 sixth-round pick. Cisco was drafted in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft and spent […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Andre Cisco #8 of the New York Jets talks to teammates in a huddle prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions are on the board for the 2026 NFL trade deadline. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Lions are trading for New York Jets safety Andre Cisco. In return, the Lions are sending the Jets a 2028 sixth-round pick. Cisco was drafted in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft and spent the first four years of his career with the Jacksonville Jaguars. He played in 63 games for the Jaguars, starting 47 games for them over that time. After his rookie deal was up, he signed a one-year, $8.5 million deal with the Jets in 2025 and re-signed with the team on a one-year, $2.5 million deal this offseason. This season, Cisco has seen his role diminished in New York after starting eight games for them last year. After starting the first three games for the Jets in 2026, Cisco has played a total of just 23 snaps with New York over the past five games. In Detroit, Cisco should give the Lions some much-needed depth at the safety position. Brian Branch recent returned from his Achilles injury and Kerby Joseph could be on the path to returning now that his practice window has been opened up. However, the Lions have been struggling with their depth at the position. Veteran Chuck Clark has been the primary reserve and has played okay, tallying his second interception of the season on Sunday. But Christian Izien has been benched, Thomas Harper remains on injured reserve, and the Lions have scaled back the work of rookie Keith Abney, who moved to safety midseason. This move could open up the opportunity to move Abney back to nickel cornerback. As for Cisco, he’s a versatile safety capable of playing both in the box and as a deep, coverage safety. He’ll be appealing to the Lions, because he’s an aggressive run defender. But he also has pretty good ball skills. In college, he tallied 13 interceptions for Syracuse, including seven in his freshman season. At the NFL level, Cisco has eight interceptions, 26 passes defended, four forced fumbles, and 2.5 sacks.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 08: Detroit Lions guard Miles Frazier (71) run blocks during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, November 8, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Mami, FL (Photo by Icon Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions walked away victorious against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon, but it didn’t come without some struggles and controversy. At the top of the list of stories was Christian Mahogany’s surprise benching. While we don’t have a ton of details around the decision to bench him, Lions coach Dan Campbell did reveal that it was for breaking one of the team’s rules . “That was team rules (for) Mahogany. It was really that simple,” Campbell said. “Miles deserved his opportunity, so he got it. Doesn’t mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today.” On this week’s PODcast, we recap the Lions’ 19-9 win over the Dolphins, and also debate Campbell’s decision to punish Mahogany. While it’s impossible to know whether the punishment fit the crime without knowing the crime, did Campbell owe it to the team to put them in the best position to win after it was clear that Miles Frazier was struggling in his first career start? Or is it more important to stay strict and consistent with their message to maintain the culture and standard within the building? We also discuss the heroic and impressive performance from the defense in the wake of Jack Campbell’s serious injury last week. Credit is due for the coaching staff and players for making it through a difficulte week. We close out this week’s show talking about some of the recent offensive struggles, the ridiculous NFC playoff picture, and some closing thoughts on Tuesdays’ NFL trade deadline with some wishes and predictions. As always, catch the PODcast on your favorite podcasting platform, or you can use the Spotify embedded player below: We had some technical difficulties on the video side of the PODcast, but you can still catch most of the show in separate segments. And on this week’s podcast, we did three spins on the Wheel of Pain. So enjoy watching that!

title: Lions owner Sheila Hamp speaks up in emotional post-game video
summary: We haven’t seen a lot of Detroit Lions owner Sheila Hamp since she took over the team in 2020, but after the team’s emotional win over the Miami Dolphins, she wanted to speak to the team. It’s been an indescribable week for the Lions. The first half was spent processing their emotions after watching team […]
full_text: We haven’t seen a lot of Detroit Lions owner Sheila Hamp since she took over the team in 2020, but after the team’s emotional win over the Miami Dolphins, she wanted to speak to the team. It’s been an indescribable week for the Lions. The first half was spent processing their emotions after watching team captain Jack Campbell lie motionless on the Ford Field turf. As the team continued to receive more and more positive updates on Campbell’s condition, the focus shifted back to football and preparing for a gritty Miami Dolphins team. The rallying cry for the week was to prepare and play as Jack Campbell would—with ruthless devotion and an unstoppable work ethic. After Detroit’s 19-9 victory over the Dolphins, Lions management wanted to commend the players for persevering through the arduous week. “I’m so proud of you guys. I am unbelievably proud,” coach Dan Campbell said. “For the week that we had, to be able to come in here and finish the way that we finished against a hungry, young team. I’m very proud of you. I really am, man. I love this team. It was built for a reason. The guys that are in this room, you’re in here for a reason—and of course, football players. But it’s what you’re freakin’ made of, men. It’s important.” Campbell then gave the game ball to Jack Campbell. Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard also offered some thoughts. “Nothing about this year has been easy, but leaning on y’all, man? It’s why I wake up every day,” Sheppard said. “It’s why I enjoy that drive to work every day, man. Serving y’all. And offensive guys? Listen, I’d be remiss not to mention y’all, man. How many times y’all [expletive] tapped me during that trial and told me you got me? Well, it was my turn to have y’all. ” Then Hamp stepped up to deliver a similar message. “I just want to say how incredibly proud I am of everyone in this room, ” Hamp said. “All you players and the coaches. This has been a hugely emotional week. You all hung together, stuck together, leaned on each other. And look what we did. We won. It was great. I’m so proud of you all. “I saw Jack a couple days ago, and he was worried about all of you. Well, I know he’s not now. I know he’s as proud of you as I am. So, awesome job. Congratulations. We’re all proud of you and with you.” Watch the entire post-game locker room video below: Game ball's going to freakin' Jack Campbell pic.twitter.com/VGHOBpWrww — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 9, 2026

title: Detroit Lions grades: Defensive dominance overshadows offensive line struggles
summary: In the standings, style points do not count. The Detroit Lions’ 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins counts the same as if the Lions had blown the Dolphins out 38-3. But in our weekly report cards, we only talk style points. We examine the good and the bad, because life isn’t really just a binary […]
full_text: Detroit Lions linebackers coach Shaun Dion Hamilton talks to linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) after a play Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In the standings, style points do not count. The Detroit Lions’ 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins counts the same as if the Lions had blown the Dolphins out 38-3. But in our weekly report cards, we only talk style points. We examine the good and the bad, because life isn’t really just a binary of wins and losses. So let’s hand out some mediocre grades in the Lions’ Week 9 victory. Quarterback: D+ Jared Goff wasn’t exceptionally bad in this game, but there was probably more bad than good. He was put into some tough positions early with pressure coming from seemingly every angle. It’s hard to fault him for the interception when his arm was hit while throwing, but Goff also didn’t handle the pressure particularly well in this game. There are two plays in which I think illustrate Goff’s self-made struggles in this game. The first was Detroit’s run-back of the CFL-like play with Amon-Ra St. Brown 15 yards behind the line of scrimmage. The play successfully distracted the Dolphins defense from aptly covering Jahmyr Gibbs’ wheel route of the backfield, but Goff, under mild pressure, didn’t make that throw and checked it down instead. Then, late in the game, the Lions faced a third-and-7 from the Dolphins 25-yard line. With a defender in his face, Goff tried to hit St. Brown on an out route. When at his best, Goff steps into that throw knowing he’s going to get hit and delivers a perfect ball. On Sunday, feeling the effects of the pressure, Goff faded away and delivered a ball several feet beyond St. Brown’s reach. Again, not a horrible day from Goff, but below average certainly. Running backs: C- I thought the running backs did a decent job in pass protection, but there weren’t any standout plays in which it felt like they created any yardage on their own. The Lions managed just 1.55 yards after contract on Sunday, the second-lowest mark of any team in Week 9. This unit certainly wasn’t helped by the offensive line for much of this game, but I still left the game wanting more from Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki. Tight ends: C- Last week’s “sidecar” formation—with two tight ends in the backfield—was so successful vs. the Vikings. On Sunday, it didn’t seem to have the same effectiveness. There were several times it felt like the tight ends weren’t getting the push they got last week, and I think that impacted both the run and pass game. That said, Sam LaPorta was an effective receiver that I wish Detroit had targeted more. He caught four of his five targets for 32 yards—though he also had a false start penalty. Wide receivers: C Jameson Williams’ drop would’ve been costly had the Lions not followed it up with a successful fake punt. And he made up for it with a 31-yard grab and a 9-yard run. But it was really Amon-Ra St. Brown’s afternoon. He was the team’s best offensive player on Sunday, constantly finding room in the Dolphins’ zone coverage. He finished with eight catches on 10 targets for 86 yards. Offensive line: D Christian Mahogany’s violation of team rules proved to be costly, as Miles Frazier struggled in his first NFL start. But he was far from alone in his troubles along the front five. The Lions gave up a 35.5% pressure rate (11th highest of Week 9), but they did at least improve as the game went on: Q1 pressure rate: 55.6% Q2: 37.5% Q3: 14.3% Q4: 28.6% This has been an odd trend all year, as pointed out by our own Al Karsten: Detroit Lions Pass Protection Entering Week 9: 1st Half • Sack Rate: 9.0% (29th) • Pressure Rate: 41.7% (24th) 2nd Half • Sack Rate: 2.5% (3rd) • Pressure Rate: 29.2% (2nd) The Dolphins defense entered Week 9 ranked 28th in sack rate (4.1%) and is somehow making life hell… — Al Karsten (@FootballGuy_Al) November 8, 2026 Frazier and rookie right tackle Blake Miller were the worst offenders on Sunday. Miller allowed three pressures, according to PFF, and Frazier finished with the worst overall grade on the offense (44.1). But they finished strong, and the Lions were again able to run the clock out on offense on the backs of their offensive line. Defensive line: A The Lions absolutely stalled the Dolphins’ rushing attack, holding the Dolphins to just 77 yards and 3.7 yards per carry. Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon had his worst game since September by both rushing yards (55) and yards per carry (3.4). And as a team, the Dolphins had just a 23.8% success rate, ranking 27 out of 28 teams this week, and their 28.6% stuffed rate was third-highest. While pressure was a little inconsistent with the front four (35.5%, 11th best this week), they came up in big moments. All of Detroit’s three sacks happened in the second half, helping secure their lead. But the biggest impact of all from this unit cannot be seen easily on the box score. The Lions defensive line helped produce five holding penalties that absolutely killed several Dolphins drives. And if we’re being honest, they probably should have been called for at least a handful more. Aidan Hutchinson was quietly dominant. Derrick Moore looked extremely promising in his first major action. And Alim McNeill continues to be an absolute force in the middle of the defense. Linebackers: B+ Without Jack Campbell, it was tough to know how this unit would respond. Consider me very pleasantly surprised. I think Malcolm Rodriguez has been quietly having a very solid year, and he built on that performance in this game. He led the team with eight tackles, was a force in the run game, and had an impressive punchout on a third-down pass, preventing a conversion. Trevor Nowaske may be the most trustworthy coverage linebacker on the team right now. On 15 coverage snaps, he wasn’t even targeted. Derrick Barnes continues to be more up and down than the rest of the room. There are still some coverage lapses that are concerning, but this was one of his best games as a run defender, and he tallied a QB hit, as well. Defensive backs: B The Lions are still clearly trying to figure some things out in the cornerback room, especially without D.J. Reed in this game. I think Rock Ya-Sin is slowly coming back into form, and he put up a strong performance against the Dolphins. But against this young Dolphins receiving corps, I was hoping for more out of the likes of Roger McCreary and Ennis Rakestraw. McCreary probably got the worst of it, credited by PFF as allowing four catches on seven targets for 49 yards—and he also allowed a deep completion that was luckily negated by a holding penalty. That said, this is the best game the Lions have gotten from their safety duo. Brian Branch was quiet, but steady working near the line of scrimmage. And Chuck Clark was essentially flawless as the deep defender. His interception was an impressively athletic play, and his return put Detroit immediately into field goal range. Chuck Clark picked it off! pic.twitter.com/I98vZOuzbq — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 8, 2026 Special teams: C A lot going on in special teams this week. The good: Jake Bates was a perfect 5-for-5 on his kicks, Jack Fox dropped his one punt inside the 15-yard line, Fox converted a fake punt with a great throw to Tay Martin, and the coverage teams were fine. However, Bates kicked one kickoff short of the landing zone and placed another kickoff in the end zone for a 35-yard touchback. Christian Izien committed a holding penalty that erased some good field position on punt return. And worst of all, the Lions allowed a massive 46-yard pass on a fake punt from Miami. In the end, I think it all evens out for an average grade. Coaching: A- I think the coaching staff deserves a ton of credit for navigating an extremely difficult week. The emotions from Jack Campbell’s traumatic injury could not be easy to process and get the team ready to go, but clearly the Lions found a…

title: NFC playoff picture: Detroit Lions get no help again
summary: The Detroit Lions are on a four-game winning streak. They’re 6-2 for the third time in last four seasons. They’re 2-0 in divisional play, and are tied in the conference for the best record against NFC opponents (4-1). Yet, they are still stuck at third in the division and sitting with the six seed in […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions celebrates after an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on November 8, 2026 in (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions are on a four-game winning streak. They’re 6-2 for the third time in last four seasons. They’re 2-0 in divisional play, and are tied in the conference for the best record against NFC opponents (4-1). Yet, they are still stuck at third in the division and sitting with the six seed in the NFL playoff picture through Week 9 (with “Monday Night Football” still pending). It’s a frustrating spot to be in, but the good news is that if the Lions can just continue to take care of business, everything is still in front of them. Let’s take a closer look at the NFC playoff picture and what it means for the Lions. NFC North standings Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (2-1 in division) Chicago Bears: 7-2 (0-2) Detroit Lions: 6-2 (2-0) Green Bay Packers: 6-3 (1-2) The Bears and Packers didn’t just win on Sunday, they looked darn good. The Packers blew out a Patriots team that was starting to look like an AFC Super Bowl contender. They had their first explosive offensive game of the season (45 points, 478 yards), and their defense was opportunistic with three interceptions and four sacks. Meanwhile, the Bears jumped all over the Buccaneers early on Sunday night. And while a four-interception game from Caleb Williams kept the Bucs in it late, his two-minute drill was all Chicago needed to put the game away. The good news is that the Minnesota Vikings will have their hands full on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. If they lose that game, the Vikes will drop to third place in the division, technically tied with Detroit, but the Lions have the head-to-head tiebreaker. NFC playoff picture Division leaders: 49ers: 7-1 Vikings: 6-1 Giants: 5-2-1 Panthers: 3-5 Wild Card leaders (top three advance) 5. Bears: 7-2 6. Lions: 6-2 7. Packers: 6-3 8. Seahawks: 5-4 9. Rams: 5-4 10. Cowboys: 4-5 11. Saints: 3-5 12. Buccaneers: 3-6 13. Falcons: 3-6 14. Cardinals: 3-6 15. Commanders: 2-5-1 16. Eagles: 2-7 Miraculously, every NFC team seeded from 1-11 won this week, with the exception of the Carolina Panthers (lost to Broncos) and the Minnesota Vikings (haven’t played yet). So not only did the Lions fail to climb any spots in the playoff race, but they didn’t create any space between them and most of the teams behind them. They still remain 1.5 games ahead of the Seahawks and Rams—and neither of those teams were very convincing in their wins—but it’s still annoying to have such a good record and not feel completely safe in their playoff standing. That said, it’s not all that uncommon. The Cincinnati Bengals are in a pretty similar situation in the AFC, holding an identical 6-2 record and the six seed. Now, if the Vikings lose on Monday night, the Lions will slide up to the five seed, while the Bears would overtake to two seed and Minnesota would drop to the six seed. Let’s hope the football gods can offer at least one sacrifice this week.

title: Lions vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
summary: Seid ihr bereit für etwas Football? The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It’s been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. […]
full_text: Nov 10, 2024; Munich, Germany; A large helmet with the 2024 NFL Munich Game logo at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Seid ihr bereit für etwas Football? The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It’s been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL’s Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it’ll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots’ 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers’ worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: “Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven’t turned the ball over, they haven’t exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it’s just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven’t quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error.” The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

title: Discussion: Are you concerned about the Detroit Lions’ offense?
summary: The Detroit Lions are winning, but one thought has lingered in my mind: should these games be this close? The Lions are up to 6-2 on the season and have now won four games in a row, yet there has been a tonal shift with this team. To start the season, the Lions’ offense was […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) scrambles for yards during the first half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions are winning, but one thought has lingered in my mind: should these games be this close? The Lions are up to 6-2 on the season and have now won four games in a row, yet there has been a tonal shift with this team. To start the season, the Lions’ offense was on a tear, scoring 164 points across their first five games (32.8 points scored per game). However, that was offset by a defense that was giving up just as many points (33.8 points allowed per game), leading to a disappointing record of just 3-2 at the bye. Things have picked of a late for the defense, but the same cannot be said about the offense. Across their past three games, the Lions have scored just 20 points versus the Green Bay Packers, 19 points versus the Minnesota Vikings, and 19 points against the Miami Dolphins. Early in the season, this would have meant three-straight losses, but some stout defensive showings (allowing just 17, 15, and 9 points across those games) have kept Detroit on a win streak. Head coach Dan Campbell has often preached the importance of complementary football. The defense has stepped up in recent weeks, but the offense is suddenly and surprisingly lagging behind. After a torrid start to the season, what is up with the offense? Today’s Question of the Day is: Are you concerned about the Detroit Lions’ offense? My answer: No. The Lions offense has had some lackluster moments against the Packers, Vikings, and Dolphins, without question. However, I think that the ceiling of this offense shines through enough to ease my worries—the offense is in a lull, not a fall. There are two drives in particular that I want to highlight that show how good this offense can be. Firstly, I want to address the Lions’ second drive of the fourth quarter versus the Vikings. Minnesota had just scored a touchdown to put themselves up 15-12. With just under eight minutes left in the game, the Lions not only had to mount a scoring drive, but also eat up enough time to make things uncomfortable for the Vikings when they got the ball back. The Lions wound up going on a seven-play, 69-yard touchdown drive to eat up four minutes of clock. What truly stood out about that drive was the presence that Detroit brought. Throughout most of the game, Detroit had struggled to run the ball. Jahmyr Gibbs had scored on a 30-yard scamper earlier in the third quarter, but aside from that, we had not seen the dominant run game that Detroit was known for. That changed on this drive. Detroit started churned out yards with ease—carries of 17 yards, 12 yards, 10 yards, and two 9-yarders made up the bulk of the drive. Detroit enacted their will against the Vikings defense and ran the ball down their throat. That was vintage Lions football under Dan Campbell. Secondly, the lone touchdown drive versus the Dolphins this week: it was a thing of beauty. Most of us would agree that the Lions had left plenty of points off the board on Sunday. They settled for a lot of field goals, particularly due to some ill-timed negative plays on third downs—Detroit would have had to take a significant risk forego a kick. Miami had not been threatening, but time was running out for Detroit to net themselves a more comfortable lead. Whereas the drive versus the Vikings was them dominating in the trenches, this drive versus the Dolphins showed how explosive the offense can be. Right off the bat, Jared Goff hits Jameson Williams deep for 31 yards. The very next play, he hits Amon-Ra St. Brown for 17 yards. The following plays gained 5 and 4 yards. Suddenly in the blink of an eye, Detroit has marched down the field to score. Thankfully on this drive, they finished it, as Gibbs sprinted around linebacker Jordyn Brooks for the touchdown. That ended as a six-play, 65-yard drive in just two minutes and 40 seconds. It looked easy . That is the genuinely scary thing about this offense: when they are on point, nobody can stop them. The Lions have a plethora of weapons, a reliable and tough-as-nails quarterback, and a creative play caller—this is a combination few teams can stop. When it works. Whenever I look at this offense, I do not see a team devoid of talent (like the Dolphins). I do not see a team suffering from horrendous decision-making (like the Los Angeles Chargers). More often than not, the only team capable of stopping the offense is the offense itself. Look back to that game against the Cardinals. Even the best offenses in the league rarely look as dominant as Detroit did in that game. Scoring 45 points is certainly an outlier, but the offense genuinely has the mettle to make that a weekly threat. I would love to see the Lions score earlier in games to cement more comfortable leads, but I think the offense nonetheless passes the eye test. I think Petzing is an adaptive play caller and knows how to get the best out of his players. As an example, a week after running the creative 15-yard-deep screen, they lined up St. Brown in that same look but instead threw the ball elsewhere—the team knows how to zig one week then zag the next. Part of what makes Petzing a good coordinator is that he takes what does not work during a game and adapts in the moment. I trust him to get the offense out of a hole. Is the Lions’ offense perfect? Certainly not. However, I think their recent low-scoring affairs do not tell the whole story. I still feel confident in the team’s talent and creativity, and they have shown enough flashes on a weekly basis to instill plenty of faith. Do you agree with me? Let us know in the comments below. title: The NFL’s Other Credibility Problem: Replays
summary: It’s been a rough year for NFL officiating, as penalties are way up in frequency and, as a result, calls are still having a major impact on games. This has been discussed to death; however, I wanted to raise the additional issue of the NFL’s broadcast partners’ complicity. Yesterday, late in the Packers-Patriots game, when […]
full_text: (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough year for NFL officiating, as penalties are way up in frequency and, as a result, calls are still having a major impact on games. This has been discussed to death ; however, I wanted to raise the additional issue of the NFL’s broadcast partners’ complicity. Yesterday, late in the Packers-Patriots game, when the Packers had victory well in hand, and backup quarterback Tommy DeVito had replaced Drake Maye, the officials made a call that, in the grand scheme of things, didn’t matter. Patriots right tackle Caleb Lomu completely blew a block on Packers edge rusher Dani Dennis-Sutton, who capitalized by forcing a rushed throw from DeVito. Dennis-Sutton made some light contact with DeVito just after the throw, best described as “maybe a light push” or perhaps “brushing by.” Here, take a look. Dennis-Sutton was flagged for a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty on this play for the love tap, which is ridiculous, but if you were watching the game, you probably didn’t know how ridiculous it actually was. You see, Fox never showed a replay, which would have almost certainly led to yet another discussion of how the league is protecting quarterbacks to an absurd extent, or worse. Let’s talk about the “or worse” because while this play did not have an impact on the outcome of the game, it absolutely did have an enormous impact on the outcome of the drive . The result of this play would have been a third and goal from the Green Bay eight-yard line, and a good chance that they Packer defense holds the Patriots to either three or zero points, depending on how aggressive they wanted to be. Instead, the call gifted the Pats a first down at the Packer four-yard line, and on second down, backup running back Corey Kiner punched it in from the four, cutting the Packer lead to 45-27. The Pats would fail on the two-point try after a false start penalty. Major League Baseball has suffered several pitch-rigging scandals in the last year , where bettors conspired with pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz to throw specific pitches for balls in order to win hundreds of thousands of dollars. With live-action betting now ubiquitous, it is now possible to bet on individual events that don’t matter (much) to the overall outcome of a game, and with it comes extra temptation. One of the best ways to defend against such things (other than reversing course on the ubiquity of gambling) is to cover your games as transparently as possible, so that at the very least, anything suspicious is out in the open. The NFL, along with its broadcast partners, too often opts for the alternative, where they elect not to show replays of controversial or poor calls if they can avoid it. Sometimes this is impossible, but every football fan has experienced a play where they are screaming at their TV about not getting a replay. That strategy may have worked in 1996, but here in 2026 all it did was send me and several of my colleagues looking for the clip the following day because we were all wondering what we missed. It turned out what we missed was an extremely bad call that gifted the Patriots an extra three-ish (or six-ish) points. I have no issues assuming that a random poor call is just a mistake; however, once people start trying to hide things from me, they lose the benefit of the doubt. The league has an officiating problem this year. If they’re not going to show it and talk about it, I’m going to assume they are in on it. I am quite sure I am not alone.
