To try to cut through the fat and keep everything contained, we’re going to launch a tracker to give you all the news from the trade deadline. Follow along and voice your opinion on these moves in the comments section, if you have the chance. Jets EDGE Will McDonald IV demands a trade McDonald wants out of New York after being displaced by Kingsley Enagbare and first-round rookie Joseph Ossai. McDonald was picked right after Lukas Van Ness in the 2023 draft, when the Packers and Jets flipped first-round picks as part of the Aaron Rodgers trade. Colts QB Daniel Jones isn’t being traded Multiple reports are claiming that Jones won’t be moved, even though the Indianapolis Colts’ season is functionally over. Minnesota is a team that would have made sense if Jones were made available. Falcons trade S Jessie Bates to Jaguars Jacksonville sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta for the 29-year-old All-Pro safety. In the deal, the Falcons agreed to eat most of Bates’ salary for 2026. He’ll be a free agent in 2027, so the Jaguars will be able to collect a 2028 compensatory pick to backfill for their losses if they don’t spend on outside additions next offseason. Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars This one is interesting, from a Packers perspective, because Godchaux was a pre-draft visitor for Green Bay — players that the Packers usually attempt to target when available. Jacksonville needed more depth at the position after some injuries, which is why Green Bay is in the same market. For what it’s worth, I’ve heard buzz about the Packers being interested in the running back and defensive line market. Other teams looking around at defensive tackles are the New York Giants and the Minnesota Vikings (Jacksonville seemingly called everyone for a lineman). Moro Ojomo is probably the biggest name that’s out there right now, but I’m not sure there’s an offer out there that Howie Roseman likes. Jets trade S Andre Cisco to Lions The Lions’ secondary needs help, and they’re getting it in the form of safety Andre Cisco. He’s being moved for a 2028 sixth-round pick, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter .

title: Kevin Zeitler looked like Kevin Zeitler on Sunday
summary: I’ve watched so much bad interior offensive line film this season, and this was such a nice breath of fresh air. The signing folks spent all summer clamoring for finally got his first material snaps this Sunday, and boy did the royal we look correct. The Green Bay Packers’ Kevin Zeitler only had four pass-pro […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve watched so much bad interior offensive line film this season, and this was such a nice breath of fresh air. The signing folks spent all summer clamoring for finally got his first material snaps this Sunday, and boy did the royal we look correct. The Green Bay Packers’ Kevin Zeitler only had four pass-pro snaps, but didn’t allow a pressure and even handled a stunt better than just about any interior lineman has in what feels like literal years at this point. Given that most of his snaps came in near-or-actual garbage time, most of those snaps involved running the ball, which the Packers actually did pretty well in his snaps. The important caveat is a lot of this came in garbage-ish time, when the Patriots were not going full bore. The counterpoint is that everyone in the building knew Green Bay was running. The Packers had a yards-per-carry of 4.93 in Zeitler’s 15 run snaps, and a success rate of 53%. If you don’t include the final drive, which was just to burn out the final bit of clock, the yards-per-carry number jumps up to 6.25 and the success rate all the way to 67%. In the non-Zeitler snaps, the run game was atrocious, with a yards-per-carry of 3.18 and a success rate of a truly abysmal 17.2%. Now, is Zeitler responsible for all of that difference? No. No offensive lineman is that important. But it’s not nothing. And how does the film look? Zeitler does fine here (more vertical displacement than anyone else). Morgan just gets beat across his face really badly and it blows the play up. pic.twitter.com/8eIT36DbmG — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 The Pacekrs don’t convert here because Morgan can’t successfully pull off a pretty difficult reach block, but Zeitler does his job. wins the initial rep and then Belton whiffs so badly he runs into Zeitler's guy and throws Zeitler off balance. pic.twitter.com/imhjbfgP9y — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Belton, who had his worst game in over a month, ends up running into Zeitler’s man here, but there’s nothing wrong at all with this rep. don't get beat inside. Didn't get beat inside. pic.twitter.com/W43RShacfh — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Designed quarterback draw where the entire objective is to not let the man beat you across your face, and Zeitler makes sure he has to take the long way around. split zone look here, kinda think Johnson shouldn't have hard cut this and just followed the hole right behind Zeitler. Solid gain either way. Good job by the OL. pic.twitter.com/3YFqtEiUKc — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 This is well-blocked across the board. Williams and Zeitler displace the nose, and Zeitler gets his butt into the hole and seals out the nose. I don’t think Johnson should have cut this back against the grain, but rather have taken this right off of Zeitler’s butt, but it ends up being a solid gain either way. this ends up turning into kind of a mess and Williams gets beat back across his face to plug up what had become a decent hole pic.twitter.com/vXBYBUa3gk — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 If Williams doesn’t get beat back inside, this play might have picked up a few more yards. Zeitler and Williams get plenty of vertical displacement here. Everyone else? Not so much. pic.twitter.com/386ylQ9pVb — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Exhibit A of why Jager Burton was seen as a center prospect. He gets isolated with the three-tech here and gets stonewalled, which wastes the displacement Zeitler and Williams get on the nose. Belton has to make a pretty tough reach here given the front alignment, and can’t pull it off. Zeitler doesn't let the man across his face. John Williams just doesn't take the backer for some reason. Redman completely whiffs the edge man. pic.twitter.com/93kAvTMH02 — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Zeitler does his job on outside zone, as he successfully reaches the 1-tech. Redman whiffs hard, and it blows the whole thing up, only worsened by no one (John Williams) accounting for the play-side linebacker. nothing life changing. Just not losing. pic.twitter.com/tUm0kHDYct — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 just doing the job pic.twitter.com/CBWKIi9fKh — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 A couple snaps of just doing your job. Not moving bodies, just winning the body shape battle. Zeitler does his job. Tough beat for John Williams. NE runs a run blitz into his gap and the nose is clearly holding him. Should have been a penalty, but the refs understandably just want this game to end. pic.twitter.com/6IXGqRp4Pd — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Watching live, I thought John Williams just whiffed this, but it’s a tough beat for him here. New England calls a run blitz into his gap (always rough on combo blocks), and he gets held by the nose tackle, so he can’t even reach the linebacker. OZ here. Jonnu and Belton lose the end man here and blows up the angle. OL got enough shift to create a crease and it's still a four yard gain. pic.twitter.com/sw1RTYdtWi — rcon14 (@rcon14) November 9, 2026 Another successful reach by Zeitler, but the front side of the play blows it up here. Jonnu Smith and Anthony Belton combine to not block the end man, forcing a sharp cutback that still ends up being a workable run. How much of the improvement in the run game is the game being mostly over? How much of it is not having Aaron Banks, who has been abysmal in both the run and pass game in his two games, and Travis Glover, who has not played well even if he’s been modestly better than the apocalyptic play of Jacob Monk, Donovan Jennings, and Jager Burton? Hopefully we find out. Based on his snaps this week, and the play of Aaron Banks, there’s no reason the Packers shouldn’t start Laken Tomlinson at left guard against Minnesota and Kevin Zeitler at right guard. Especially with the exotic pressure looks Brian Flores brings, the veteran’s experience and the more successful run game are going to be very important in a game that will more or less determine if Green Bay can make a run at the division this season.

title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 9 win over the Patriots
summary: As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Week 9. Offense Let’s start with personnel usage. For the game, the Packers leaned primarily into 11 personnel […]
full_text: (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports . Today we’re looking at the 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Week 9. Offense Let’s start with personnel usage. For the game, the Packers leaned primarily into 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR), but not overly so. If you look at the full game numbers, they weren’t a huge 11 team: A lot of that is driven by the full-game nature. This game was well in hand by the 4th quarter, so it’s pretty safe to throw those numbers out. Through 3 quarters, here is what that breakdown looks like: 11 personnel: 65.4% (+0.387 EPA/play) 12 personnel: 30.8% (+0.454 EPA/Play) 13 personnel: 3.8% (-0.604 EPA/Play) As we’ve seen over the last few weeks, this seems to be their preferred way to operate. The 13 personnel EPA/play is lower than we’ve been seeing, but Whyle’s injury likely factors into that. Either way, an 11 personnel that features Tucker Kraft and a 12 personnel that features Tucker Kraft & Mark Redman seems like the best way to operate. Let’s talk about the passing game, because that’s what we really need to be talking about. Before the game, I went on Patriots on CLNS and said that Love was “ chucking chucking”, and he proved me correct. The protection was fine, but not elite, with Love being pressured on 42.4 of his dropbacks. That’s been par for the course, so got rid of the ball pretty quickly. For the game, Love’s average time to throw was 2.5 seconds, but his ADOT (Average Depth Of Target) was 13.0 yards. For reference, the highest ADOT for a QB who has taken more than 60 snaps this year is JJ McCarthy at 11.5 yards (for the season, Love is at 9.7 ADOT). Will those pressure numbers look better if we see a guard tandem of Tomlinson (LG) and Zeitler (RG) going forward? That’s certainly something I’ll be keeping an eye on. Love was tremendous no matter how you looked at it. When pressured? When blitzed? By coverage? One of the big things was Love in play action. The Patriots’ defense came into the game as a subpar play-action defense, and the Packers dialed up their usage a bit this week. They came into this week with a play action rate of 18.9%. This week they used play action on 31% of their passes, with an EPA per play of +1.16 on those dropbacks. Love’s success is certainly tied to the receivers, and they did their part. Matthew Golden was a monster. He caught all 10 of his targets (no drops!) for 164 yards and a TD. He had an EPA per target of +1.28 and an ADOT of 12 yards. MATTHEW GOLDEN IS TAKING OVER GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GRgg5MOShA — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Golden’s best route was a Go route (2/2, 92 yards, +2.98 EPA per Reception). He was targeted most on Out routes (4/4, 39 yards, +0.82 EPA per Reception). Matthew Golden caught 10 passes for 164 yards and 1 TD and was still eclipsed in terms of yardage by Christian Watson. Watson 7 of his 8 targets for 171 yards and a TD (+2.07 EPA per Reception). Golden’s ADOT of 12 yards was high enough, but Watson’s ADOT of 23.75 is insane. He averaged 6.1 yards per route run and 2.4 yards after catch. He also had a remarkably casual one-handed catch that I’ll be thinking about for a while. Christian Watson just casually snagged it with one hand 😳 GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rrMHQlpP7t — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 In The New Thinking Man’s Guide to Pro Football , the late, great Paul Zimmerman (aka, Dr. Z), relayed an anecdote about about a catch from Don Hutson. As Dr. Z tells it: Edmond F. Rovner, a lawyer from Bethesda, MD, says that he will take a lie detector test that he once saw Hutson catch a low pass, one-handed, in full stride, with the palm of his hand facing downward. Dr. Z goes on to say that he does not believe this story. Until this week, it always seemed like an insane catch. After seeing this catch from Watson, I’m starting to believe. (That’s one of the all-time great football books, by the way. If you haven’t read it, you should fix that.) Defense The Patriots were primarily in 11 personnel (65.6%), but, even then, the Packers leaned more heavily into Nickel than the Patriots leaned into 11 (Packers played Nickel on 77% of snaps). That’s essentially been the trend since Edgerrin Cooper went down, but I like that it’s continuing. Less Nickel means less Javon Bullard, and I’m not really a fan of a defensive group that doesn’t have Bullard in the mix. It’s a fairly common sense thing, but it’s something not every DC would do: find a way to keep your best players on the field. The Packers dialed up their blitz this week, blitzing on 41.3% of their plays and getting pressure on 47.8% of Drake Maye’s dropbacks. The blitz worked, too. We’re 9 weeks into the Jonathan Gannon experience and I’ve been extremely impressed. He does a great job of changing his approach every week, depending on the opponent. More than anything, he does such a great job at putting his players in their best position to succeed. It’s been a remarkably fun unit to watch every week…and Micah Parson should be added to the mix in the next couple weeks. Albums listened to: Lydia Loveless – Accolades EP ; Spanish Love Songs – Future Nausea

title: Packers Film Room: The snaps behind Trey Smack’s perfect day
summary: In this space, we look at the snap-to-hold operation on field goals and extra points. We’ve got a heavy week (7 kicks), so let’s get to it. Last week was rough. There was a missed kick, but more than that, Matt Orzech had his least accurate game of the season. How did he do this […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this space, we look at the snap-to-hold operation on field goals and extra points. We’ve got a heavy week (7 kicks), so let’s get to it. Last week was rough. There was a missed kick, but more than that, Matt Orzech had his least accurate game of the season. How did he do this week? One week after his worst performance, Orzech turned in his best. Even the snaps to the body were splitting the difference between body and hold point. Kick 1: Extra Point (Make) Nice snap, if a bit slow. Slightly to the body of Whelan, with the spin of the ball allowing him to catch it by the laces and get it down for a nice, easy hold. Ball is leaning slightly forward and away from Smack. Karl Brooks [94] is on the right side of the screen. He gets his arm wide, but it doesn’t do much to divert the path of the rusher. This was closer than it should have been. This was also the slowest snap-to-kick time of the day (1.32 seconds), which led to this being closer than it should have been. That’s on Orzech: his snap-to-holder time was 0.36 seconds, his slowest time of the day. Kick 2: Extra Point (Make) Nice snap. More or less the same as the last one. Slightly to the body, with the spin allowing Whelan to catch it by the laces. Good hold. Good kick. Brooks is slightly slow out of his stance on the right side and only barely gets a hand on the nameplate as the rusher flies past him. Snap-to-holder: 0.32 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.27 seconds Kick 3: 41-yard Field Goal (Make) Same as the last two. Great snap, great hold, kick is a no-doubter. Once again, Brooks barely gets a hand on the rusher. With this kick set up on the right hash (as opposed to the dead-center positioning of the first two), the ball has to travel slightly back to the left, towards the rusher. This one was close. Snap-to-holder: 0.28 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.24 seconds Kick 4: Extra Point (Make) Great snap, great hold, great kick. Brooks does a good job on the outside this time, but a rusher is able to split Aaron Banks [65] and Anthony Belton [71] and gets real close to blocking this one. This was Orzech’s second-slowest snap-to-holder time, which contributed to this close call. Snap-to-holder: 0.34 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.31 seconds Kick 5: Extra Point (Make) Good snap, slightly to the body. Good hold. Good kick. Brooks gets a hand on the nameplate of the rusher as he dips past. It’s worth saying that, if the choice is a wide rusher or an interior rusher on these block attempts, you’ll take the man off the edge every time. Unless it’s a slow snap-to-kick time, it’s really hard to get a block off the edge. Still, it’d be nice to give up at least a little resistance. Snap-to-kick time here was 1.26 seconds, which won’t really give the edge a chance to block this. Snap-to-holder: 0.30 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.26 seconds Kick 6: 51-yard Field Goal (Make) Good snap, to the body of Whelan. Orzech does a great job with his spin consistency: I can’t remember a kick this year where Whelan caught the ball by anything other than the laces in the same spot. Brooks gets a little bit more of the rusher this time as he tries to dip pass, so this is not particularly close to being blocked. Snap-to-holder: 0.28 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.23 seconds Kick 7: 38 yard Field Goal (Make) Perfect snap, right over the hold point. Good hold. Good kick. There is no rush. The Patriots have given up at this point. Snap-to-holder: 0.32 seconds Snap-to-kick: 1.28 seconds For the first time this season, I tracked the snap-to-holder time and snap-to-kick time for every kick this week. I messaged briefly with Chris Kluwe over the past week and the range he gave me for snap-to-kick is between 1.2-1.28. Average time this week: 1.27 seconds. title: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup
summary: The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel’s numbers. That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel’s numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers’ offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they’ve already had their bye week and 2) they’re playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they’ll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We’ll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it’ll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they’ve been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the “good” teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic’s playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there’s whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

title: NFL Trade Deadline: Which picks can the Packers trade?
summary: No matter who you want at the NFL trade deadline, which is on Tuesday, getting that player — be it a running back, offensive lineman or defensive lineman — likely involves trading a draft pick in the 2027 class. Which of the Green Bay Packers’ draft picks are tradable? Let’s break it down for you. […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images No matter who you want at the NFL trade deadline, which is on Tuesday, getting that player — be it a running back, offensive lineman or defensive lineman — likely involves trading a draft pick in the 2027 class. Which of the Green Bay Packers’ draft picks are tradable? Let’s break it down for you. Packers’ tradable 2027 picks 2nd-round pick 3rd-round pick 4th-round pick (Dallas Cowboys) 4th-round pick 5th-round pick 6th-round pick 7th-round pick The Packers’ original draft choices are available to trade, which include their second- through seventh-round picks for 2027. Their first-round pick is gone, part of the Micah Parsons trade. Either the Dallas Cowboys or New York Jets will own it, depending on whichever pick is higher (the highest goes to the Jets). Packers expected comp picks 3rd-round (Malik Willis) 5th-round (Quay Walker) 5th-round (Romeo Doubs) 6th-round (Kingsley Enagbare) These are the Packers’ expected compensatory draft picks, based on Over the Cap’s current projections . You can toss out the idea of Romeo Doubs’ comp pick rising to the level of a fourth-round pick, as he’s been placed on the injured reserve with a shoulder injury. Playing time does have a factor in these picks graduating, depending on whether a player is on the bubble of two rounds. Please stay healthy, Malik Willis! — So in total, the Packers are expected to have 11 draft picks in 2027, but they’re only able to trade 7 of them currently, as 4 of them are comp picks — which won’t be awarded until the start of the new league year. How many picks do the Packers use? 2018: 11 2019: 8 2020: 9 2021: 9 2022: 11 2023: 13 2024: 11 2025: 8 2026: 6 The counts above are the number of picks that general manager Brian Gutekunst has turned in while he’s sat in the big chair. On average, he’s using 9.6 picks per draft — which holds even when you exclude the highest and lowest pick-count drafts on his resume. On paper, you could think of Green Bay holding an extra pick and a half right now than a “normal” Gutekunst season. One thing that could influence decisions, though, is both the Packers’ future cap situation (it’s not looking good, folks — they need cheap deals) and the fact that the team already is down to six draft picks for the 2028 class, because the team traded away two late-round selections for running back Kaleb Johnson and tight end Mark Redman while also adding a late-round pick for quarterback Kyle McCord. The 2027 draft vs. the 2028 draft An interesting X factor for the upcoming draft class is going to be “early” declarations. In the past, Gutekunst has stated that players receiving an extra year of eligibility for the 2020 COVID year have made for deeper draft classes than in the past. That is not in play for this year’s crop of players, as a 2021 high school recruit is now a redshirt senior at the college level, if he’s still even playing. So, no more sixth-year players, right? That should help the strength of this class. Wrong! The end of the COVID year also came with the NCAA instituting five-for-five, allowing all players to benefit from what would have been a “redshirt” year, even if they played all five of their seasons of college eligibility. Because of that (and NIL), 39 of the top 40 players in the 2027 class (and 83 of the top 100) would have to declare early for the NFL to be eligible for selection. In the past, a true senior would have exhausted his eligibility. Now, that player has another year of college football, if he wants it. Based on my discussions with NFL scouts, more players are expected to return than in the past. (Side note: We really need to figure out what to call these fifth-year players, because you can’t assume a senior is going to be out of college eligibility as it stands right now — only redshirt seniors.) Last season alone, 29 underclassmen (juniors or redshirt sophomores) who were projected to be top-150 selections returned to school , and now we have a class of true seniors with remaining eligibility who can go back to school on top of the underclassmen. With colleges spending double on high-end rosters over the last two years , it’s going to be harder to get players to declare if they’re not projected to be first- or second-round picks. 2027 will be a buffer class, where the pool of fifth-year seniors will begin to fill at the college level before the draft talent starts to normalize in 2028.

title: Packers Snap Counts, Week 9: Green Bay shakes up the offensive line
summary: The Green Bay Packers broke the 100-yard rushing mark on Sunday against the New England Patriots, in part because they changed up both their backfield and their offensive line. Will those changes stick moving forward? That hasn’t been determined yet. Let’s get into how this Packers team looked different than in the past in our […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers broke the 100-yard rushing mark on Sunday against the New England Patriots , in part because they changed up both their backfield and their offensive line. Will those changes stick moving forward? That hasn’t been determined yet. Let’s get into how this Packers team looked different than in the past in our week’s snap count breakdown. As a reminder, these only include offensive and defensive snaps, not special teams. Quarterback Jordan Love: 56 snaps Tyrod Taylor: 8 Backup quarterback Tyrod Taylor got in for the second time this season, his first since he kneeled down twice against the Chicago Bears. Taylor operated the offense on the last few drives of the game, when the Packers had already put away the game. No quarterback controversy here. Running Back Pierre Strong: 29 Kaleb Johnson: 26 Josh Jacobs: 9 The leading rusher on the night was Kaleb Johnson, who has been a healthy scratch as of lately. Johnson was pushed into action because of MarShawn Lloyd’s knee injury, and he split time on the field about 50-50 once starter Josh Jacobs left the game with a fractured finger . Between Lloyd, Jacobs and Chris Brooks, who only has two weeks left in his practice window , the Packers will need to make some tough decisions soon at the running back position. They’re dealing with three injuries, have five roster-caliber players, can only carry four on the 53-man roster (at most) and can only carry three on the game-day 48-man roster. At some point, something is going to have to give here. Receiver Christian Watson: 49 Matthew Golden: 48 Savion Williams: 30 J. Michael Sturdivant: 15 Bo Melton: 14 Coleman Owen: 8 Former practice squadder and current punt returner Coleman Owen got his first looks on offense in garbage time. He had not played on offense up to this point in the season. Owen was also pulled off the kickoff return unit, allowing Bo Melton to be the top returner with J. Michael Sturdivant as the “off-returner.” Belton had a 48-yard return that highlighted the night in the kicking game, while Owen had a 13-yard punt return. Oh, yeah. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden went off . Tight End Tucker Kraft: 52 Mark Redman: 24 Jonnu Smith: 16 There’s nothing special about the tight end rotation this week, other than Josh Whyle being out with an injury. Last week, the Packers decided to roster only three tight ends on game day for the first time all season, and they don’t seem to want to do that again. Instead, they brought up Drake Dabney from the practice squad to help replace Whyle’s snaps on special teams. While Dabney didn’t play on offense, he did play six snaps in the kicking game. Offensive Line 64: Anthony Belton 64: John Williams 56: Jordan Morgan 56: Laken Tomlinson 45: Aaron Banks 19: Kevin Zeitler 8: Mekhi Becton 8: Jager Burton The Packers played all eight of their offensive linemen today, with their last two — Mekhi Becton and Jager Burton — only getting in when Tyrod Taylor hit the field. For what it’s worth, Becton played left tackle in his reps. In total, 13 offensive linemen have now played for Green Bay’s offense this season. The big story here, though, is that the Packers are back to a guard rotation, which they have been famous for in previous years. This time, though, they’re moving around three guards for two spots, not just splitting reps at one spot between two guards. Before garbage time, Green Bay played two drives where Laken Tomlinson played left guard and Kevin Zeitler played right guard. Aaron Banks was on the bench for those looks. Otherwise, the team played Banks at left guard, pushed Tomlinson at right guard and Zeitler was on the bench. So the Banks vs. Zeitler rotation also comes with Tomlinson flip-flopping sides to get them on the field, too. For a staff that tried to sell us on continuity on the line early in the year when the guards were at their worst under Jacob Monk and Donovan Jennings, they seem to have thrown that playbook out entirely. A guard musical chairs is going on, and we’ve already seen six players suit up at those two spots this season. Who even knows which eight players are going to be up on game days when Sean Rhyan and Travis Glover are finally back healthy? I’m done guessing about who the line will be. We’ll find out on Sundays. Defensive Line 32: Karl Brooks 31: Chris McClellan 29: Devonte Wyatt 23: Anthony Campbell 19: Jordon Riley Again, nothing too shocking here. Campbell and Riley are going to be the lower defensive linemen on the team’s depth chart until the likes of Warren Brinson and/or Jonathan Ford can return from the injured reserve. Edge Defender 32: Lukas Van Ness 32: Brenton Cox Jr. 30: Barryn Sorrell 30: Dani-Dennis Sutton It remains close to an even split for all four of the Packers’ top edge defenders, something we’ve seen throughout the year. Can this keep up whenever Micah Parsons returns to the lineup? I doubt it. Off-Ball Linebacker 59: Isaiah McDuffie 57: Nick Niemann 2: Kristian Welch 2: Ty’Ron Hopper After just two defensive snaps, injury replacement starter Ty’Ron Hopper left the game with a chest injury, which head coach Matt LaFleur was not asked about in the post-game press conference. Officially, the Packers ruled him out of action, and he never returned to the game. At the end of the game, Isaiah McDuffie, the team’s replacement starter at the Mike position, left with an undisclosed injury, too. Forcing Kristian Welch, the team’s sixth linebacker option, into the game. Keep an eye on the injury report this week, as the Packers cannot afford to be out Zaire Franklin, Edgerrin Cooper, McDuffie and Hopper. If those four can’t go, they might need to call up practice squad linebacker Jack Dingle and sign a player off the street. Cornerback 51: Keisean Nixon 51: Brandon Cisse 11: Carrington Valentine 10: Benjamin St-Juste 4: Kamal Hadden Carrington Valentine got one rep as a dime defender (a second slot) in the first half, but otherwise his snaps and Benjamin St-Juste’s snaps came in garbage time, when Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse were pulled out of the game. Kamal Hadden’s snaps all game as a slot defender, when safety Javon Bullard was getting worked on. Safety 59: Evan Williams 51: Xavier McKinney 44: Javon Bullard 12: Kitan Oladapo Kitan Oladapo played some safety in garbage time and when Evan Williams was out. Williams had the air knocked out of him at one point, but he returned to action. At the end of the game, it was Hadden in the slot with Williams and Oladapo playing the high safety looks, due to their lack of bodies at the position. Ultimately, the team allowed Xavier McKinney and Javon Bullard, who was in and out of the game twice, to rest.

title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 9 vs. the Patriots
summary: The Green Bay Packers traveled to face off against the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon, and they were in control the entire time. With a commanding 45-27 win over the reigning AFC champions, the Packers find themselves 6-3 after 9 weeks of play. Let’s dive in and take a look at what worked this […]
full_text: (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers traveled to face off against the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon, and they were in control the entire time. With a commanding 45-27 win over the reigning AFC champions, the Packers find themselves 6-3 after 9 weeks of play. Let’s dive in and take a look at what worked this week. Winner: Xavier McKinney S Xavier McKinney logged his second multi-interception game of the season, and that’s about enough to name him a winner this week. McKinney is up to 5 picks on the season, his most since 2024 (8). McHIMMEY 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/W1s8MmngSr — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 8, 2026 Winner: Matthew Golden WR Matthew Golden had 6 catches for 126 yards…by the end of the first quarter. Not only is this a career high in a game for Golden, but it’s also the most receiving yards by any player in one quarter so far this season. He was wide open, pretty much at all times, which led to big gain after big gain. MATTHEW GOLDEN IS TAKING OVER GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GRgg5MOShA — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 We saw firsthand on Sunday exactly why the Packers selected Golden in the first round of the draft last year. As a result of his growing chemistry with his quarterback, he had the honor of becoming the answer to the trivia question “Who caught Jordan Love’s 100th career TD pass?” 💯 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/lCspSQ9m6q — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 8, 2026 Golden finished the day catching all 10 targets for 164 yards and 1 TD. And the WR success didn’t stop with him. Winner: Christian Watson Death. Taxes. WR Christian Watson was wide open. Watson showed us some gorgeous stuff on Sunday, including this one-handed catch which he made look absolutely effortless. Christian Watson just casually snagged it with one hand 😳 GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rrMHQlpP7t — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 He had another incredible catch later in the game to get the Packers close to the endzone (I think this should’ve been ruled a TD, but IT’S FINE, I’M FINE). Love to Watson near the end zone! GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8wmu1tmGgG — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Watson finished the day catching 7 of 8 targets for 171 yards and 1 TD. Who needs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins when you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden? Winner: Evan Williams If S Evan Williams isn’t First Team All-Pro by the end of this season, something has gone very, very wrong. He was all over the field on Sunday: getting after Patriots QB Drake Maye and forcing quick throws, making big tackles at the point of catch, and coming down with one of the most impressive interceptions I’ve seen all year. I mean, look at this! Damn, Evan 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/OWHe5FIN7K — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 8, 2026 We all held our breath as he was slow to get up after a scary play in the second half, but he came back into the game and continued right where he left off: haunting Drake Maye. Williams finished the day with 5 tackles, 1 INT, and 1 PD. It all started to make sense when Tom Brady announced during the broadcast that Williams’ mom, Dani, babysat Brady when he was a child. Brady clearly got his power from Dani Williams, and so did Evan. Winner: Kaleb Johnson For the first time this season, we finally get to say THE PACKERS RUN GAME HELPED THEM OUT TODAY, kind of. The offense had 129 yards on the ground today, and Kaleb Johnson accounted for 68 of them on 14 carries. He had the team’s biggest run of the day with a 34 yarder to open the 4th quarter. Also, Baby’s First Touchdown! Kaleb Johnson powers in! What a first half for the @Packers GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dmNuSX6KwF — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Redeemed: Trey Smack SMACK IS BACK (for now). After a rough couple of weeks which caused me to make an emergency visit to my hair colorist to get rid of some grays, the Packers rookie K was perfect against the Patriots. He made all 4 XPs, and made 3 more FGs, with a long of 51. Let’s do this again next week. Winner: Jordan Love Do you hear that? The MVP chants…they’re getting louder. QB Jordan Love was absolutely incredible on Sunday. He used his legs to escape a collapsing pocket, and scored the team’s first TD of the game. From there, it was nothing but the Air Show. The unfortunate victim this week was the NFL’s highest paid DB, Christian Gonzalez. Love picked a good time to be a walking highlight reel. Here you go: SILLY BODY DOING SILLY THINGS 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/oDoSrcbGLK — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 8, 2026 There’s more. Packers' offense picking up where they left off! GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LKu32y46Mh — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Please remain seated; we’re not finished. Love to Savion Williams! @Packers add on 🧀 GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZEQiTsd3aY — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Almost done! JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 You’re welcome. Love finished the day 23 of 29 (79%) for 372 yards and 3 passing TDs, with another 13 yards and 1 TD on the ground, for a 153.2 rating. Loser: Josh Jacobs The RB finished the day with 4 carries for 5 yards before exiting with a hand injury. He also pled no contest to battery in September after a May 2026 incident involving his former girlfriend. Despite being 6-3, the Packers are sitting at the bottom of the toughest division in football, leaving little room for error as they head into the second half of the season. Next week is a big one, as they head back home to face off against the Minnesota Vikings, who are 6-1 at the time of publication. After an embarrassing Week 1 loss to Minnesota, can the Packers redeem themselves and flip the NFC North on its head in the process?

title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs fractured his finger
summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his finger against the New England Patriots, according to head coach Matt LaFleur. In his post-game press conference, LaFleur stated, “Hopefully, we can do something to allow him to go out there.” Notably, Jacobs was ruled questionable with a hand injury mid-game, but he was never officially […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his finger against the New England Patriots, according to head coach Matt LaFleur. In his post-game press conference, LaFleur stated, “Hopefully, we can do something to allow him to go out there.” Notably, Jacobs was ruled questionable with a hand injury mid-game, but he was never officially ruled out of action. At the moment, the Packers carry four running backs on their active roster: Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson. Lloyd missed Sunday’s game with a knee injury, opening up the door for Johnson, who ended up leading the backfield in rushing yards against the Patriots. Another factor here is that running back Chris Brooks has his practice window open. At some point, the team will need to make a decision on whether to bring Brooks up for game action or shut him down for the year. It seems highly unlikely that the Packers will ever carry more than three backs on their game-day 48-man roster this season, so there will need to be some level of trimming at the position. Jacobs’ injury coming at the same time as Brooks’ recovery makes the situation more complicated. LaFleur was not asked about linebackers Isaiah McDuffie (undisclosed) or Ty’Ron Hopper (chest), who were also injured against the Patriots. They were the replacement starters in for Zaire Franklin (ruled out) and Edgerrin Cooper (injured reserve). Currently, the only healthy off-ball linebackers for the Packers are Nick Niemann and Kristian Welch, who had only played a combined two defensive snaps in the season prior to today’s game. — Update: Jacobs claims it’s a fracture to his right ring finger, according to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman. Josh Jacobs said he fractured his right ring finger. They’ll try and figure out a way for him to play through it. He just couldn’t grip the ball. — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) November 9, 2026 Jacobs said he actually popped his finger back in right away after it got caught on a facemask. https://t.co/AdqmbrUKdo — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 9, 2026 Josh Jacobs suffered a broken finger in today's game, per Matt LaFleur. pic.twitter.com/EiiJm8hj9p — Easton Butler (@Easton__Butler) November 9, 2026

title: Value of Things: In the rearview mirror
summary: These things seem to happen once a year. Last year it was an undermanned Baltimore Ravens team winding up on the business end of a 44-10 drubbing at the hands of the Texans. The final score will say 44-22 in this one, but it really wasn’t that close. The Texans were up 38-9 at one […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Nico Collins #12 of the Houston Texans reacts after a play during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images) | Getty Images These things seem to happen once a year. Last year it was an undermanned Baltimore Ravens team winding up on the business end of a 44-10 drubbing at the hands of the Texans. The final score will say 44-22 in this one, but it really wasn’t that close. The Texans were up 38-9 at one point, but allowed two fourth quarter touchdowns in garbage time to make the score look a lot more respectable than it otherwise would have. As blowouts go, this one was as complete a blowout as you can have. This puts your Houston Texans in the unenviable positions of scoring more points than their opponents this season, but winding up with a 3-5 record. I suppose that’s what happens when two of your three wins come by blow out. It also means that the final numbers may not completely reflect what went on in the game today. However, we look at things in the aggregate and with each passing game the aggregate seems to be more and more accurate. So, the numbers for this game may not be completely indicative of what went on for the better part of three quarters, but when we look at the whole season in the same prism we suddenly see some definite trends on both sides of the ball. Since this one was a blowout win we get the great, good, and bad in addition to a special look at C.J. Stroud. Key Numbers Total Yards: Texans 66/485, Chargers 68/315 Rushing Yards: Texans 28/104, Chargers 30/138 Passing Yards: Texans 38/381, Chargers 38/177 Third Downs: Texans 8/14, Chargers 5/17 Fourth Downs: Texans 0/0, Chargers 2/4 Sacks: Texans 8, Chargers 1 Turnovers: Texans 1, Chargers 2 Time of Possession: Texans 28:33, Chargers 31:27 We will get into the nitty gritty on some of these numbers when we look at the great, good, and bad, but I think these numbers show the value of looking at some numbers with a grain of salt. Yes, the Chargers scored some points and gained some yards in the fourth quarter but they are what some people would call empty calories. This game looked more like what we might expect from the Texans and we will just leave it at that. The Great This one was an offensive win and that has been the case for most of the season when the Texans have won. It will be a game that Nick Caley puts on his resume when he is undoubtedly looking for work in the offseason. I say that partially with tongue firmly planted in cheek, but also out frustration. There are moments when he seems to get it and this was one of those moments. He clearly put the game in Stroud’s hands and he was rewarded handsomely. In particular, game balls go to Keshaon Boutte and Tank Dell after both eclipsed 100 yards as Texans and scored three of the five offensive touchdowns. Boutte in particular has largely been a disappointment after coming over shortly before the season in a trade, but he made good on his presence with this effort. Like with the Caley offense as a whole, his totals on the season will suddenly look respectable and will make statheads like me wonder why everyone wants him gone. We know the NFL is a week to week league and that is particularly true with Caley and the offense. He might choose to go jumbo again and gain two yards and a cloud of dust. However, this feels like something they should build on and we can only hope that he does that next week when they play Cleveland. The Good The Texans do three things well on defense and they are all interrelated. Unfortunately, for much of the season two of those seemed to take a hiatus. They have been able to get after the quarterback consistently and as we are waiting for Monday night to be completed, they are poised to take over the league lead in sacks. Having eight sacks in a football game has a way of vaulting you into the top spot. The other two have been more elusive. They have been great at making opposing quarterbacks miserable. That tends to come hand in hand with the pressure, but the Texans have gotten their sacks this year without making their opponents miserable. Herbert was miserable today and that brought us the third part of the triangle. They turned the Chargers over two times. When you throw in the failed fourth down plays and it ends up being what felt like four turnovers on the day. The two touchdowns given up came on explosives and that seems to be the achilles heel of the Texans. However, if you are able to have as many negative plays as the Texans had and create the turnovers they did then you can live with the occasional explosive. It is when they have played bend but don’t break that those explosives have seemed that much more glaring. The Bad The rushing output included 20 yards on two carries from Stroud. That’s 26 carried and 84 yards for the remainder of the carriers. My math skills are a little shaky, but that looks like just over three yards a carry. Earlier in the week, a reporter asked Caley about his tendencies to run it to to the right side of the line. On brand, Caley said he wasn’t aware of that because he didn’t have the numbers. Another reporter looked it up and spouted out the 73 percent count within minutes of the original question. Does it matter that they run it that often to the right side? I suppose one could argue that their better blockers are on that side so it makes perfect sense. Still, this is a larger issue than that simple question and the response to it. This team seems blissfully unaware of their own tendencies. Opponents can look up that information in the blink of an eye. Why are you unaware of it? It’s hard to crticize a coordinator after his team scores 44 points. It’s hard to criticize him when they are close to top ten in points per game. Yet, it is things like this that make you wonder if he is in over his head. Focus on Stroud Each week in the NFL is a data point and we should always remember that whether a quarterback looks great or terrible. He was officially 21 for 35 (60.0) for 384 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception. That is good for a passer rating of 125.5. It’s not a perfect rating. If he hadn’t thrown the pick it likely would have been a statistically perfect performance from him. Even though it is a single data point, it is another data point showing that Stroud is indeed a franchise quarterback. The look at the running game above is simple proof that this team is going as far as Stroud can take them. Can he take them to the playoffs without the defense being good? I suppose we are about to find out. The fear is that Caley and Ryans will turtle again and try to become that smash mouth football team that no one has seen in Houston since Arian Foster roamed the plains. Those keeping up at home, that means that Stroud has thrown for 2251 yards, 16 touchdowns, and 2 interceptions. This is effectively the halfway point of the season, so he is on pace to eclipse 4000 yards and 30 touchdown passes. Will he do it? That remains to be seen. It depends on whether he can stay healthy and whether Caley will commit to letting Stroud cook. I still have my doubts because every time it feels like they have turned a corner they revert back to the same crap they did before. Here is hoping it’s different this time.

title: Buccaneer at Bears Sunday Night Football Discussion Thread
summary: Hi y’all. It’s me again. If you’re reading this, you may have just noticed the Houston Texans have defeated the Los Angeles Chargers of San Diego 44-22 through a supreme force of effort by C.J. Stroud and his merry band of wideouts. This win included the first touchdown for one Tankthaniel “Nate” Dell, but he […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 08: Chicago Bears place kicker Cairo Santos (8) warms up before a regular season game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Chicago Bears on November 08, 2026, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hi y’all. It’s me again. If you’re reading this, you may have just noticed the Houston Texans have defeated the Los Angeles Chargers of San Diego 44-22 through a supreme force of effort by C.J. Stroud and his merry band of wideouts. This win included the first touchdown for one Tankthaniel “Nate” Dell, but he goes by Tank, in 648 days. Think about that for a moment. Think about the injury he had in Kansas City where his knee basically exploded. In any other era of football, his career would be unquestionably over. It would be beyond their capacity in medical science to bring him back. Yet, here we are, and not only do we have the scientific capacity to repair his knee, and not just be able to repair his knee to the point where he can return to his career as a professional athlete, but repair it in such a way that he hasn’t even missed a step in his speed. It’s nothing short of a wonder and a testament to medical science (to say nothing of Tank Dell’s determination to return) that such a thing is possible. What does any of this have to do with either the Bears or Bucs, you might ask? Must everything be connected to other things? Can’t I just ramble from one thing to another? Here’s what you need to know about tonight’s matchup: Who: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) at Chicago Bears (6-2) What: Sunday Night Football Where: Soldier Field, Chicago, IL When: Sunday, November 8, 7:15 p.m. CST Why: Because soon the Chicago Bears will be playing in Indiana. Figure that one out. TV: NBC Radio: Westwood One Streaming: DirecTV*, Fubo*, Hulu+Live Sports*, NFL+*, Peacock*, SlingTV*, YouTubeTV* (*subscription required) Enjoy the game, y’all. Go Texans

title: Texans blow out the Chargers
summary: There are days when everything comes together. Sometimes it is just because all of your plans came to fruition. Sometimes it is because the team on the other sideline is beleaguered with injuries and ineffectiveness. Sometimes it is a glorious combination of those things. That all came together on Sunday as the Texans dominated the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Xavier Hutchinson #19 of the Houston Texans scores a touchdown against Genesis Smith #22 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the first half at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sirius Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are days when everything comes together. Sometimes it is just because all of your plans came to fruition. Sometimes it is because the team on the other sideline is beleaguered with injuries and ineffectiveness. Sometimes it is a glorious combination of those things. That all came together on Sunday as the Texans dominated the Chargers for most of the game as the Texans would come out on top 44-22. It could have been worse, but the Texans obviously called off the dogs in the fourth quarter when the issue was no longer in doubt. The first three quarters saw the Texans dominate the Chargers on both sides of the ball as the defensive line registered a season high eight sacks and the defense also turned the Chargers over two times. The Chargers did snap their touchdown drought streak, but that didn’t happen until the fourth quarter when the Texans were already up 38-9. They added a second touchdown in garbage time with their backup quarterback. The final score obviously doesn’t indicate how much the Texans dominated this game. On the offensive side of the ball, the Texans finally jettisoned their running game until the second half when the game had already been decided. Stroud responded with arguably his best game as a Texan. He came an eyelash away from six touchdown passes, but settled for JUST five and one interception. Tank Dell and Keshon Boutte had over 100 yards receiving on the day as both had 60+ yard touchdowns. Nico Collins added a circus catch for another touchdown. It was the most complete domination the Texans had since they beat the Baltimore Ravens 44-10 in October of 2025. Ironically, that result was said to have kickstarted the Texans comeback last season. Perhaps this result does something similar for this Texans team this year. Only time will tell whether this result means anything over the long-term. What do you think? Is this the start of something special or is this a blip on the radar?

title: The Colts aren’t trading Jones, but that doesn’t mean he should start
summary: The Indianapolis Colts entered Sunday with a chance to make the season interesting. The string of subpar opponents kicked off with the Dallas Cowboys. A win could have seen the Colts go on a little run. That didn’t happen, and for all intents and purposes, 2026 seems to be a wrap. Don’t tell that to […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts against the Dallas Cowboys after the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts entered Sunday with a chance to make the season interesting. The string of subpar opponents kicked off with the Dallas Cowboys. A win could have seen the Colts go on a little run. That didn’t happen, and for all intents and purposes, 2026 seems to be a wrap. Don’t tell that to Shane Steichen or others in the Colts organization, though, as the team is planning on keeping Daniel Jones on the roster. That may not be breaking news, but this isn’t either: that doesn’t mean he has to start. All of this begins with the premise that the Colts could actually trade Jones. They need a willing partner, and he hasn’t been impressing lately. In nine games, Jones has failed to pass for more than 200 yards in five of them. Throwing for 108 at Minnesota was a season low, and a paltry 180 against a less-than-stellar Dallas D is the latest example of the struggles. When you can’t pass, you don’t score. Six touchdowns thrown is a quarterback stat one doesn’t want to see nine weeks into a season. Throw ten interceptions on top of that and things go from bad to worse. If this is the type of play the Colts are going to get, why play him at all? What Jones was paid is a sunk cost. It’s done. Let’s move on. Anthony Richardson is still a wild card. Is he the future? Most likely not, but that doesn’t mean he can’t show you how much he has grown. What’s the risk? He plays poorly? What’s the difference between that and Jones? Richardson would be playing with a depleted arsenal, but at least he would get another real shot. If the Colts move away from both players, at least they will 100% know that neither man is suited for the job. Regardless of Richardson’s abilities, Jones isn’t the answer. “Experiment time” in Week 10 of the NFL season means things have gone off the rails. Daniel Jones hasn’t earned that big offseason payday. It was a misguided decision (one of many by Chris Ballard). The season is spiraling, so let’s have some fun as it goes down in flames. The Colts need to let loose and hand the keys to Anthony Richardson. Literally, does it get any worse?

title: Cowboys spoil comeback bid with TDs at end of each half in Colts’ 5th straight loss
summary: INDIANAPOLIS – The Indianapolis Colts fought their way back from down 10 in the second half and took control late in the fourth quarter, but the thrill of stealing a comeback win was short-lived as Dak Prescott led the Dallas Cowboys on a game-winning touchdown drive inside the final minute to escape with a 27-23 […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 8: Caden Curry #55 of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – The Indianapolis Colts fought their way back from down 10 in the second half and took control late in the fourth quarter, but the thrill of stealing a comeback win was short-lived as Dak Prescott led the Dallas Cowboys on a game-winning touchdown drive inside the final minute to escape with a 27-23 win. The fifth-straight loss spoiled a furious rally and wasted another heroic performance from Spencer Shrader, who outdueled All-Pro kicker Brandon Aubrey with the roof open and the wind breezing through Lucas Oil Stadium. Aubrey broke the ice with a 45-yard field goal on Dallas’ opening drive, but finished 2-for-3 on Sunday. Shrader connected on field goals from 47, 59 and 50-yards out, but his go-ahead kick to give the Colts a late lead would not be sustained. Colts edge rusher Laiatu Latu raced around the edge of left tackle Tyler Guyton, got a firm grasp of Prescott twice from behind, and knocked the ball loose for a strip-sack. Rookie edge rusher Caden Curry recovered the fumble and returned it inside the red zone to give Indianapolis an early takeaway. Curry, a Greenwood, Ind. native, had a breakout performance and later secured his first sack in his first NFL start. First NFL career sack for Caden Curry 💥 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/SNK9wDvFfk — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 8, 2026 The Colts leaned on their ground game as rookie running back Seth McGowan finished the six-play drive with a 2-yard touchdown to take an early 7-3 lead. McGowan provided a spark for the rushing attack, finishing with 45 rushing yards on just six carries and scoring his first NFL TD. Dallas answered with a methodical, 18-play scoring drive. Toward the end of the first quarter, an unnecessary roughness penalty from rookie linebacker C.J. Allen gifted Dallas a first down. Faced with fourth-and-2 from inside the 10, Prescott laid a perfect pass on a corner route near the back pylon to tight end Jake Ferguson, who rose above the defender to haul in a touchdown and put the Cowboys back ahead 10-7. Indianapolis struggled to generate any offense during the first half as quarterback Daniel Jones was held to just 50 passing yards, while Dallas’ pass rush found a way to wreak havoc in the pocket. Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs blitzed untouched for a blindside sack to force another punt and had a breakout performance in his first matchup against his older brother, Josh. Four consecutive possessions for Indy in the second quarter resulted in a punt, gaining a total of 40 net yards and controlling just six minutes on the game clock. The Cowboys closed the first half with a pair of deep shots to receiver CeeDee Lamb, with the latter striking for a 44-yard touchdown to increase the lead to 17-7. Prescott recognized the cloud zone, saw Lamb with his hand raised and fired a missile to burn safety Hunter Wohler for the explosive score. Lamb was virtually unstoppable, hauling in 10 catches for a season-high 195 receiving yards and a touchdown. Jones’ stats were inflated late in the third after he hit receiver Ashton Dulin on a screen, then the speedster broke through the initial tackle before racing 55 yards into the end zone. The most explosive offensive play of the game brought the score to within 20-17 and injected life into a restless crowd that had watched its offense struggle through nearly three quarters. DUUUUUUUULIN 📺 Fox pic.twitter.com/ekPvzWUjFp — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 8, 2026 Perhaps the most momentum-shifting play happened early in the fourth. Faced with 3rd-and-12, Prescott stayed in the pocket and took a big hit, but found a wide open Lamb diving to secure the catch inside of Colts territory. The All-Pro receiver was never touched or down by contact, so he got up and tried to race for the end zone, but lost the football as the turf knocked the ball out of his grasp, allowing rookie Kenneth Harris to recover and seize the momentum. Lamb was initially ruled down by contact, but Colts head coach Shane Steichen challenged the play to reverse the ruling. CeeDee Lamb makes a diving catch He doesn't get touched Gets up and picks up several yards Fumbles while getting tackled Colts recover it after the play is reviewed FOOTBALL DALvsIND on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ApA5vJgMM4 — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The Colts chance to capitalize unraveled after a 40-yard defensive pass interference penalty against Bland moved Indianapolis into scoring position. Running back Jonathan Taylor was stuffed behind the line of scrimmage by defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and coughed up the football, wasting another scoring opportunity as linebacker Shemar James recovered the lost fumble. Midway through the fourth, McGowan broke free on a left zone run for a 36-yard burst to breach Cowboys territory. Shrader delivered on a 59-yard field goal to level the score at 20, then later added a 50-yarder to take a late 23-20 lead with just 1:37 left to play. On the very first play of Dallas’ final true drive, Prescott launched another missile downfield and receiver Ryan Flournoy hauled in the 46-yard catch over cornerback Sauce Gardner to instantly set the Cowboys inside the red zone. After consecutive penalties set Dallas up at the 1-yard-line, running back Javante Williams plunged into the end zone from 1-yard out to score the go-ahead touchdown with just 1:08 remaining. Despite Dallas’ offense piling up 508 total yards, Indy still had a chance to get one final stop with the lead. Instead, the Colts allowed the Cowboys to reclaim the lead in less than 30 seconds. The Colts final drive lasted just three plays, featuring intentional grounding and another incompletion before Jones’ lofted an awful pass over the middle of the field, which Caleb Downs picked off to terminate the last chance to steal a victory. Caleb Downs faced his older brother Josh for the first time in the NFL and delivered his best performance yet. 3 TKL, 1 SACK, 1 INT, 2 PD, 1 TFL vs Colts. The rookie was making plays everywhere and is looking like a future star for Dallas. pic.twitter.com/DhpDtwsSdl — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 8, 2026 Taylor was held to just 46 yards on 13 carries. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 passing yards, with one touchdown and one interception. For Indianapolis, the comeback demonstrated the ability to fight back when the game appeared out of reach, but multiple defensive lapses, along with a pair of costly turnovers ultimately overshadowed the effort. The stampede once again left the stadium to boos, listening to “Here we go” cadences, and “How ‘bout them Cowboys” chants. The Colts host the 1-7 Miami Dolphins next Sunday inside Lucas Oil Stadium, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m.

title: Colts inform Daniel Jones he will not be traded ahead of NFL deadline
summary: The Indianapolis Colts have informed quarterback Daniel Jones that he will not be traded ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, according to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. The decision comes despite reported interest from multiple teams, with Indianapolis fielding calls about its starting quarterback over the past several days. According to Pelissero, the Colts were willing […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts against the Dallas Cowboys after the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have informed quarterback Daniel Jones that he will not be traded ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, according to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. The Colts informed QB Daniel Jones on Saturday they’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Teams called and the Colts listened. But they never had any intention of moving him. Despite speculation, Jones is staying in Indy. pic.twitter.com/Ew0cVkmEuW — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 9, 2026 The decision comes despite reported interest from multiple teams, with Indianapolis fielding calls about its starting quarterback over the past several days. According to Pelissero, the Colts were willing to listen to inquiries but never seriously intended to move Jones, even as the organization began trading established veterans in preparation for a potential rebuild. Jones, 29, signed a two-year, $88 million extension with Indianapolis during the offseason following his impressive 2025 campaign. However, his performance has declined considerably this season, with the Colts falling to 2-6 and their offense struggling to find consistency. The organization has already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, leading to speculation that Jones could be another player moved before the November 10 deadline. There had been particular interest surrounding a potential reunion with the Minnesota Vikings, where Jones briefly spent time during the 2024 season. Minnesota has dealt with quarterback injuries and could benefit from an experienced veteran with previous ties to the organization, although Indianapolis has now made it clear that a deal is not expected. Interestingly, keeping Jones for the remainder of 2026 does not necessarily mean he will be part of the franchise’s long-term plans. According to Pelissero, Jones is scheduled to earn $38 million in 2027, but only approximately $10.5 million is currently guaranteed for injury, with additional guarantees becoming relevant in March. That structure could give whoever takes over as general manager considerable flexibility when evaluating the quarterback position during the offseason. For now, however, Indianapolis appears committed to keeping Jones under center despite its increasingly uncertain future. With the Colts potentially entering another rebuilding period and still searching for long-term stability at quarterback, his role beyond this season remains far from guaranteed.

title: Jaguars double down on defense, trade for Davon Godchaux
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars aren’t messing around. Just hours after agreeing a blockbuster trade for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars have returned to the negotiating table, acquiring New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in a second significant defensive addition ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. According to reports, Jacksonville will send a […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: Davon Godchaux #92 of the New Orleans Saints looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Cesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars aren’t messing around. Just hours after agreeing a blockbuster trade for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars have returned to the negotiating table, acquiring New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in a second significant defensive addition ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. According to reports, Jacksonville will send a 2028 sixth-round pick to New Orleans in exchange for the veteran defensive tackle. The selection could be upgraded to a 2027 sixth-round pick if the Jaguars acquire one through the compensatory selection process, or via another trade. It’s another relatively modest price for an experienced NFL starter, but the bigger picture is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: Jacksonville are going all-in. What does Davon Godchaux bring to Jacksonville? TRADE: Saints trading DT Davon Godchaux to the Jaguars. (via @CameronWolfe ) pic.twitter.com/RstMWuJrZy — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 At 6-foot-3 and 330 pounds, Godchaux brings some considerable bulk to the Jaguars’ defensive interior. The 31-year-old was originally selected by the Miami Dolphins in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft, spending four seasons in South Florida before moving to New England in 2021. He subsequently spent four seasons with the Patriots before returning to his home state of Louisiana with the Saints in 2025. Godchaux has built a reputation as a run-stuffing defensive tackle, providing a sizeable presence in the middle of the defensive line. He isn’t somebody Jacksonville should expect to transform their pass rush, however. Across 144 career appearances, including 128 starts, he has recorded 486 tackles and 5.5 sacks. His value comes primarily from his ability to occupy blockers, hold his ground against the run and make life more difficult for opposing offenses between the tackles. There is an obvious need for that in Jacksonville. The Jaguars have lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton to a season-ending quadriceps injury, leaving a gaping hole in the middle of their defensive front. Godchaux provides an experienced replacement who can contribute immediately, rather than asking the coaching staff to rely exclusively on younger, less experienced options. His 2026 production hasn’t been particularly impressive, with 14 tackles in seven appearances for New Orleans and no sacks. There are legitimate questions about how much he has left to offer at this stage of his career. Nevertheless, Jacksonville isn’t acquiring Godchaux to be a superstar. They’re acquiring him to provide some much-needed depth and physicality at a position where they have been hit by injury. A familiar face for Anthony Campanile Godchaux's not much of a pass rusher, but you'll be hard pressed to find many better gap controllers in run defense. Very good combination of instincts, play strength, awareness, and competitive toughness. Should be instant impact run defender up the middle. https://t.co/sT8UNeAeu9 — AJ Schulte (@AJSchulteFB) November 9, 2026 There is another interesting aspect to this acquisition: Godchaux has previous experience working within a coaching staff led by Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile. Campanile spent four seasons as the Miami Dolphins’ linebackers coach between 2020 and 2023. Godchaux was also in Miami from 2017 through 2020, meaning the pair overlapped during the 2020 season. That familiarity could prove useful as Godchaux makes the transition to Jacksonville. Campanile knows the type of player he is getting, while Godchaux should have some understanding of the defensive philosophy and coaching expectations that Jacksonville are trying to establish. It’s worth remembering that Campanile was coaching the linebackers rather than the defensive line in Miami, and their shared time was relatively brief. Godchaux was placed on injured reserve in October 2020 after appearing in five games. Still, there is a connection there, and the familiarity certainly won’t hurt when it comes to integrating a midseason acquisition. Campanile has already demonstrated his ability to build a formidable defensive unit in Jacksonville. Godchaux gives him another experienced body to work with as the Jaguars attempt to maintain that standard through the second half of the season. Jaguars trade grade: B This is a sensible piece of business from Jacksonville. A sixth-round selection for a veteran defensive tackle with 128 career starts is a relatively small investment, particularly when the team has an immediate need at the position. Godchaux isn’t going to solve every problem on the defensive line, and his declining production this season means there is some risk attached to the acquisition. There’s also the faint sting of reality after star names like Jalen Carter and Christian Barmore were bandied around as potential options. However, Jacksonville isn’t paying a premium for a player who needs to develop. They’re bringing in somebody who has spent almost a decade in the NFL and understands the demands of playing defensive tackle at the highest level. The injury to Hamilton makes this move particularly understandable. It’s not a spectacular acquisition, but it addresses a genuine weakness without costing the Jaguars significant draft capital. The Jaguars are ALL IN Jags 2027 draft picks after acquiring Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux today: Round 1 Round 3 Round 4 Round 5 Round 5 (projected comp pick) Round 6 (projected comp pick) Round 6 (projected comp pick) Round 7 — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) November 9, 2026 Perhaps the most significant part of this trade isn’t actually the player Jacksonville has acquired. It’s what the move represents. The Jaguars had already made a substantial statement with the Jessie Bates trade; a genuine difference-maker at safety who brings elite experience, ball skills and leadership to the back end of Campanile’s defense. Now, they’ve followed that up by addressing another defensive weakness with the acquisition of Godchaux. That’s two defensive reinforcements in a single day, with the Jaguars surrendering considerable future draft capital to improve their chances of competing right now. Jacksonville entered the deadline at 6-2, leading the AFC South and looking increasingly like a legitimate contender in the AFC. There is little point pretending these moves come without risk. Bates is in the final year of his contract, and Godchaux is a veteran whose best football may already be behind him. The Jaguars are also reducing their collection of future draft picks, limiting some of the flexibility they would otherwise have had. But this is what competing for a Super Bowl looks like. The Jaguars have a talented roster, an explosive offense under Liam Coen and a defense that has already demonstrated its ability to compete with the best in the league. They have identified weaknesses, recognised an opportunity and acted decisively to address them. The Bates acquisition was the headline move. Godchaux is the reinforcement that helps make the first deal even more meaningful. Jacksonville isn’t sitting back and hoping their current roster is good enough – they’re making sure of it. And with time still left on the trade deadline clock, don’t be surprised if the Jaguars aren’t finished just yet.
