title: Jaguars Add Safety Jessie Bates in Trade with Falcons
summary: With the Jacksonville Jaguars recently rumored to be in the 2026 trade market for a big fish, the team made its first big splash, completing another deal with the Atlanta Falcons. This one brings in a legitimate difference-maker in the secondary. According to NFL Insider Adam Schefter, Jacksonville is acquiring safety Jessie Bates from the […]
full_text: Oct 13, 2024; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) walks off the field after the game at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con With the Jacksonville Jaguars recently rumored to be in the 2026 trade market for a big fish , the team made its first big splash, completing another deal with the Atlanta Falcons. This one brings in a legitimate difference-maker in the secondary. According to NFL Insider Adam Schefter, Jacksonville is acquiring safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Jessie Bates signed with Atlanta in 2023 and has started all 60 possible games, totaling 14 INTs, 11 forced fumbles and 392 tackles. Jacksonville recently lost S Eric Murray to a season-ending injury, prompting them to explore the safety market. They now land Bates. https://t.co/xKhiIbKP1v — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 It’s the latest move in a trade pipeline that has been building between the two franchises since James Gladstone became general manager. A Name We Flagged Weeks Ago Bates is a player we initially put on the radar about three weeks ago in our defensive trade targets piece. We projected his trade value at a conditional 2027 third-round pick that could rise to a second, so the final price landed right around where we expected. Bates is in the final year of his contract and is expected to want, and likely get, a new deal. Atlanta evidently wasn’t eager to pay it, which opened the door for Jacksonville. Gladstone mentioned on the Jags HQ show couple weeks back when discussing trades, that there were times when they had to essentially pay a tax in form of a higher Draft pick in order to get a team to eat cap money in return- looks like they did that here. https://t.co/8qqdHe9cgB — Couch (@BCBCouch) November 9, 2026 Per Jonathan Jones and Ian Rapoport , Atlanta will pay most of Bates’ 2026 $6.5M salary to complete the deal. What Jacksonville Is Getting Bates arrives with a résumé built on production and takeaways: 3× Second-team All-Pro (2020, 2023, 2025) 2023 Pro Bowler 28 career interceptions 14 interceptions coming over the last three and a half seasons in Atlanta 11 career forced fumbles 2026 PFF overall grade of 84.1 (fourth best) 2026 PFF coverage grade of 87.9 (second best) Most importantly, against the backdrop of the Eric Murray injury that took the Jacksonville safety for the season , durability matters. Bates hasn’t missed a game since signing with Atlanta, starting 60 of 60 games. The Missing Piece in Camp’s Defense? With Jacksonville recently losing Murray for the year, that left the safety room needing a boost. While Ray Lane has played well during Murray’s absence, rather than patching the spot, the front office went after one of the better playmakers at the position. This move still allows Lane to play the third safety looks that Campanile loves, while pairing Bates with chess piece Antonio Johnson on base downs. For me, the biggest takeaway is what Bates does for the scheme. He’s the first true rangy, sideline-to-sideline safety the Jaguars have had under defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile. Over the past two seasons, Jacksonville has leaned heavily on two-high safety looks. Bates gives them a ballhawk who can play over the top, which opens up more Cover 1 and Cover 3 looks, with Bates playing as the security blanket over top. Campanile’s defense already thrives on takeaways, disguise, and variety. With Bates in the mix, it should be even more unpredictable and even more dangerous to opposing quarterbacks. Through week 8, Bates has Pro Football Focus’s third-highest safety grade when playing man coverage, coupled with the 11th-highest grade in zone coverage. What are your initial thoughts on the trade, Duval? Is that a big enough fish for your appetite? Or is the cost too high? Drop your thoughts in the comments!

title: Andy Reid on trade deadline: Brett Veach ‘always keeps his eyes open’
summary: The NFL trade deadline is tomorrow, Tuesday, November 10th, at 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time. Plenty of smoke has surrounded the Kansas City Chiefs’ potential activity before the cut-off, especially at wide receiver. On Monday, during a video press conference, head coach Andy Reid was asked about a potential move at the position. He began with […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is tomorrow, Tuesday, November 10th, at 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time. Plenty of smoke has surrounded the Kansas City Chiefs ’ potential activity before the cut-off, especially at wide receiver. On Monday, during a video press conference, head coach Andy Reid was asked about a potential move at the position. He began with two thoughts on the young receivers already in the Chiefs’ rotation. “[Jalen] Royals did a nice job,” Reid reflected on the Week 9 win over the New York Jets . “[Cyrus Allen], we’re kind of working in; we feel pretty good about him on some things there and his improvement, although he didn’t have much production yesterday. “But, as you know, Brett always keeps his eyes open,” Reid continued. “He’s always looking and trying to improve the roster. That part hasn’t changed; he’s out there searching and doing his due diligence with his guys.” Reid’s words reflect reports from sources like CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson, who has covered a Chiefs game each of the last two weeks. She has heavily implied that Veach is searching far and wide on the receiver market, especially with how the win over the Jets ended: wide receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring) came up limp while reaching for his hamstring. The thought of adding more firepower to Kansas City’s offense comes after a game in which the team scored 35 points despite fumbling away two possessions. The Chiefs rank second in total yards per game (384) so far this season. Reid pointed to what the offense looks like when it avoids shooting itself in the foot. “I think when you eliminate some of the penalties that we’ve had that have set us back, you’re playing pretty good football,” Reid said. “You can see, when you get rid of those negative plays, good things can happen. It’s hard to stop a run game, it’s hard to stop a pass game and a blend of that with the screens, it can be tough to stop at times, you just can’t go backwards.” Injury update Reid shared that Worthy is considered “day-to-day.” He shared the same update on quarterback Patrick Mahomes (elbow) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle). “All three of those guys are kind of day-to-day,” Reid shared. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick; it looks like just a matter of some rehab in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We’ll just see where it goes from there, but he’s in good spirits today.” When pressed on whether Mahomes would miss time in practice this week, Reid wasn’t ready to answer. “Give me a couple of days, just until we have to get out there and do it, and we’ll see where he’s at,” Reid answered. “He’s feeling pretty good today, but we’ll see where it goes. He’s sore; I’m glad we’re not practicing today.” No kicking change (yet) During his opening statement in the call, Reid shared that he has not made a decision about kicker Harrison Butker and potentially replacing him with practice-squad member Justin Tucker. It was the same answer he gave at the podium on Sunday. “With Butker, I haven’t made any decisions yet,” Reid said. “I’m just sitting and going to evaluate everything and go forward from there. I haven’t decided on reps during practice; I haven’t done any of that right now, so just going through and evaluating, and we’ll go from there.” Creed Humphrey snaps When asked about center Creed Humphrey and the bad snaps that have popped up often times this season, Reid acknowledged there needs to be improvement. He was asked if the problem was technique, mental or physical. “Yes. All of the above,” Reid responded. “He’s working on that, and that’s not like him, so he’s cleaning all that up; we’ll get that straight.” This season, Mahomes leads the NFL in fumbles recovered (8) primarily because of Humphrey’s low snaps that seem to pop up once a week.

title: Chiefs Week 9 snap count analysis: Kristian Fulton steps up again
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ snap counts in the 35-12 win over the New York Jets in Week 9. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 35-12 win over the New York Jets in Week 9. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Jaylon Moore, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, WR Cyrus Allen, RB Kenneth Walker and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, NT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, CB Kristian Fulton, CB Nohl Williams, S Chris Roland-Wallace, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: N/A Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder), FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, DT Peter Woods (neck) and OT Diego Pounds The big takeaway: Kristian Fulton continues playing well in relief With Delane out again, veteran cornerback Kristian Fulton stepped into a starting role for the second consecutive week. His role as a reliable outside cornerback was further solidified over 62 snaps and 39 snaps in coverage. He was targeted three times and allowed just one catch for five yards. He had a clean sheet on the penalty front after drawing a flag for over-aggressive coverage against the Denver Broncos . It’s the fourth game this season that Fulton has had to fill in for an injured Delane, and he has stepped up in a big way seemingly every time. When you look at his entire season, Fulton has been faulted for just 50 receiving yards on 8 catches (15 targets) against him in coverage; quarterbacks are registering a 32.6 passer rating when targeting the veteran cornerback. Kansas City has a strong trio of outside cornerbacks as it tries to figure out how best to cover the slot. The Offensive takeaway: Chiefs have a WR3 by committee The Chiefs’ wide receiver position continues to be led by Xavier Worthy (74% offensive-snap rate) and Rashee Rice (58%). After that, there hasn’t been a clear WR3 like there was when the group was completely healthy. Here’s how the rest of the group’s snaps broke down: Andrew Armstrong (22 snaps) — 0 targets Jalen Royals (21 snaps ) — 2 catches for 18 yards (1 first down) Cyrus Allen (19 snaps) — 1 target Allen took a step back in playing time after 30 snaps in Denver; he did fumble a kick return this week. Royals made a strong catch on a pass thrown over the middle in traffic, slightly behind him, to move the chains in the red zone. Armstrong seems to have a defined role as the strongest blocker of the trio, so the coaching staff is trying to use each player to their strengths while general manager Brett Veach potentially adds a proven player to the mix before tomorrow’s trade deadline. The Defensive takeaway: Chris Roland-Wallace has become one of defense’s key players Since veteran slot cornerback L’Jarius Sneed was placed on the Reserve/Injured list before Week 8, the Chiefs have trusted safety Chris Roland-Wallace as the Nickel and primary slot defender. With 45 snaps against New York, he out-snapped teammates in the secondary like safety Alohi Gilman (44 snaps) and safety Jaden Hicks (19 snaps). He has mainly been a staple in defending teams’ quick passes, but he was also used on blitzes a season-high five times in Week 9; he registered two hurries. While I believe rookie Jadon Canady could eventually prove he has the coverage chops to be trusted more in the slot, Roland-Wallace is proving defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo right in trusting him to this extent, even after an undisciplined post-snap play that got him ejected in Week 6. title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ get-right game against the Jets
summary: For the first part of this game, it felt like the Kansas City Chiefs might be heading for another disappointing outing — only this time, it wasn’t against one of the better teams in the NFL; it was against the cellar-dwelling, lame-duck New York Jets. Early on, a sinking fear set in that if the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first part of this game, it felt like the Kansas City Chiefs might be heading for another disappointing outing — only this time, it wasn’t against one of the better teams in the NFL; it was against the cellar-dwelling, lame-duck New York Jets . Early on, a sinking fear set in that if the Chiefs couldn’t take care of business against the Jets, this team’s flaws ran deeper than we thought. Thankfully, Kansas City woke up in the second half and, in the words of the GOAT Mitch Holthus, laid the hammer down. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs’ 35-12 victory over the Jets. 1. The Chiefs are a good team Good teams look great against bad teams, and bad teams look bad against great teams. Will the Chiefs make the playoffs? Probably. Will they catch the Denver Broncos and win the AFC West? Who knows. Can they win a playoff game? Sure, why not? Will they make the Super Bowl? Probably not. But that’s okay. After going 6-11 last year, you want to see a return to competitiveness from this team, especially if the franchise keeps heading in the right direction. But if we look in the mirror honestly, this is probably a Wild Card team. A Wild Card team that could go on a run and surprise some people, but their margin for error against good teams isn’t slim; they are starting at a deficit in enough areas that the Chiefs need to play perfect football to win against the cream of the crop in this league. It didn’t used to be this way, and maybe it won’t be again someday. But for now, that’s who this team is. 2. Andy is fed up with Butker Just before the half, up by two points, the Chiefs had a chance to take the lead 17-12. They trotted out their much-maligned placekicker, Harrison Butker, for a 56-yard field goal attempt. He, of course, missed it, because Harrison Butker is in his missing 50+ yard field goals era. Thankfully for the Chiefs, a flag was thrown on the play—a member of the Jets lined up in the neutral zone. The refs moved the ball five yards closer, and Butker got a second crack at it, only this time, it was just barely in his trouble zone of 50+ yards. But if Butker is one thing, it’s that he’s consistent. As before, he booted the ball just wide of the goalpost, and the Chiefs went into halftime clinging to a narrow lead. As he left the field, reporters asked head coach Andy Reid what he needed to see from Butker in the second half, and his response was simple. “I need to see them go in.” Now, that’s about as close as you will ever get to the old ball coach throwing one of his players under the bus. The fans booed Butker as he left the field. After the game, Butker said that he understood the fans’ frustration and that he is booing himself for missing these kicks. Harrison Butker on the miss today and his ongoing kicking issues. #Chiefskingdom pic.twitter.com/wmyB2vvgtd — 96.5 The Fan (@TheFan965) November 8, 2026 Andy is fed up. The fans are fed up. Butker is fed up. We are at the point where the leash is too long, especially when you are trying to keep pace in a division race with Denver. 3. Eyes are on the front office The Chiefs narrowly dodged a possible season-derailing injury to quarterback Patrick Mahomes when rookie standout edge rusher David Bailey Jr. blew past right tackle Jaylon Moore nearly untouched and hit Mahomes’ arm as he threw the ball. All of Chiefs Kingdom’s hearts sank when they saw Mahomes get up off the turf clutching his arm in pain. Thankfully, early reports say the injury is mild. The issue is that this is not the first time Mahomes has been hung out to dry by his linemen. It’s not the second or third. It’s been a continuous process for the last few years — the Chiefs haven’t been able to find the right guys to protect the greatest player in franchise history. Kansas City also can’t field a fully capable receiving unit. General manager Brett Veach’s biggest priority has to be to protect Patrick Mahomes. His second priority should be to give Mahomes the weapons he needs. Players haven’t panned out as we hoped. But guess what, that’s the job. Brett Veach is paid to get it right, and when I see Mahomes lying on the ground in pain like we did today, I can’t say that he did. #Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes underwent an MRI following today’s win and sources say the tests did not reveal a major injury. Mahomes’ elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling. But so far, so good. Mahomes did go back in the game. pic.twitter.com/uWPbBY3Gaa — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 9, 2026 4. The Chiefs should not abandon the tush push On the Chiefs’ first drive of the game, they faced third and one from their own 34-yard line, and to everyone’s amazement, the Chiefs did something fans have been clamoring for. They lined up with backup quarterback Justin Fields under center to take the snap and hopefully run for a first down. Unfortunately, Fields was stopped short of the one yard he needed for a first down, and to make matters worse, he fumbled the ball away to the other team. I could easily see Andy Reid pointing to this turnover in the future as a reason why they don’t run QB sneaks, but here is the thing: even though the Chiefs fumbled the ball, it was still the right call to make. Failure to execute should not be the reason you remove a play from your call sheet. The Chiefs FINALLY attempt a QB sneak, subbing in Justin Fields… – stopped short – ruled to have lost a fumble after Jets challenge😳 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/QvtjSWmjDz — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 8, 2026 5. The Chiefs need two WR’s The Chiefs needed help at wide receiver before Xavier Worthy went down with a hamstring injury. Soft-tissue injuries like this can linger for the rest of the season, especially at wide receiver. Reports say Brett Veach is trying to add a guy before this week’s trade deadline. But one might not be enough. The Chiefs probably need at least two new wide receivers Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Xavier Worthy suffered a hamstring injury and Jaylon Moore hurt his ankle. — Pete Sweeney (@pgsween) November 8, 2026

title: Chiefs News: Chiefs have the NFL’s all-time QB-TE receiving yards duo

full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Among the many polarizing storylines the Kansas City Chiefs produce every week, a record-breaking performance by quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce got overshadowed after the 35-12 win over the New York Jets in Week 9. According to the CBS broadcast, the duo took over the No. 1 spot in NFL history for receiving yards produced by one quarterback-to-tight end connection (9,360 yards). The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce make NFL history in Chiefs win | Touchdown Wire Kelce hauled in three receptions for 67 yards on Sunday for the Chiefs during their victory, and on a 38-yard connection between Mahomes and his tight end, the duo set the all-time NFL record for the most combined passing and receiving yards by a quarterback and tight end, surpassing Philip Rivers and Antonio Gates for the top spot on the list. The pair has now combined for 9,360 passing and receiving yards. What’s remarkable is the short amount of time that it has taken the pair to accomplish this feat – Rivers and Gates played together for 14 years. The pair in third place, Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski, played together for 11 years. But Mahomes and Kelce have outdone them in just eight and a half seasons. Jets was fueled by something special from Patrick Mahomes | The Kansas City Star None of that, though, was the real takeaway from his game. It was the fact that Mahomes was back on the field before the half even ended, completing a 12-yard pass to Kelce and running 7 yards himself — and appearing to land on the elbow — to put the Chiefs in field-goal range. “We see him toughing it out,” center Creed Humphrey told The Star in the locker room, “and it makes us want to step our game up.” NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN Most surprising performance: Before this week, the Chiefs had only nine sacks, tied for the fewest in the league. But the Chiefs recorded more than half their previous season total on Sunday, sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times. The last sack was significant one for defensive tackle Chris Jones, who now has the second-most sacks in franchise history (90.5). — Nate Taylor Latest updates as Kansas City Chiefs GM Brett Veach continues to pursue wide receiver help ahead of NFL’s trade deadline | A to Z Sports “As we’ve been talking about the lack of deep threats for the Chiefs, and I spoke with GM Brett Veach before the game,” Wolfson said. “He told me that as the trade deadline approaches, the focus continues to be at that wide receiver position. There has been increased dialogue this week, and he found that some of the major franchise players they looked at are off the market, but they will continue to have conversations over the next 24 hours to see if they can get something done by the trade deadline.” Wolfson told viewers during the broadcast: “There will be increased dialogue as week 9 comes to a close. And perhaps some of those conversations over those major franchise players might change.” Around the NF L John Harbaugh: Giants did pull offer for Jonathan Taylor but ‘things do change’ | ESPN Fox Sports reported Sunday morning that the Giants offered the Colts a second- and a fifth-round pick for Taylor. Harbaugh was asked about that offer after the Giants’ win over the Eagles later Sunday. “I’m not saying that report’s not true. Those conversations are taking place,” he said following the 19-11 victory. “If something happens for any player, can’t talk about any [specific] player because they’re with other teams right now, but we’re not ruling anything out.” Lamar Jackson reportedly expected to miss 6-9 weeks, is telling teammates he’ll return this season | Yahoo! Sports Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is determined to return before the end of the 2026 NFL season. Jackson, who is expected to miss between six and nine weeks, reportedly told teammates to “just stay alive” ahead of his return, according to ESPN. Daniel Jones trade rumors: Colts tell QB he will not be dealt before NFL deadline, per report | CBS Sports The Indianapolis Colts told quarterback Daniel Jones they will not trade him before Tuesday’s deadline, according to Tom Pelissero. Indianapolis (2-7) received calls for Jones with the trade deadline looming. The Colts, who already traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, remain among the central characters on the trade market. Most eyes will be on star running back Jonathan Taylor, who said a goodbye of sorts to Indianapolis after Sunday’s 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, but Josh Downs and Grover Stewart are potential names to watch, too. title: The Winners and Losers from Chiefs’ big win over the Jets
summary: Your Kansas City Chiefs finally got back in the win column after taking care of the New York Jets 35-12 at Arrowhead on Sunday. The beginning was as ugly as it gets, and there were some ball security issues and short-yardage challenges. But the home team eventually remembered how to put together a complete game. […]
full_text: Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Your Kansas City Chiefs finally got back in the win column after taking care of the New York Jets 35-12 at Arrowhead on Sunday. The beginning was as ugly as it gets, and there were some ball security issues and short-yardage challenges. But the home team eventually remembered how to put together a complete game. They ran the ball, played great defense, limited penalties, and Mahomes got the ball into the hands of playmakers to rack up the YAC. That’s been the formula for each of the team’s six wins. Here are a few who stood out on Sunday, for better or worse. 7 Winners Running back Kenneth Walker III: Ken had three touchdowns and 143 yards from scrimmage; the Chiefs scored 35 points. It’s that simple: get Walker going, win football games. Running back Emmett Johnson: Number 10 continues his hot streak, breaking tackles on every play and scoring his second career touchdown. The Chiefs appear to have a complementary back who can help carry the load without sacrificing explosiveness. Left guard Kingsley Suamataia: Correlation may not be causation, but the fact is that Kingsley was back as a starter on the same day both running backs made the winners list. He put some highlights on film against the Jets in the run game and on screens— especially the Kenneth Walker touchdown. Maybe having the starting left guard in the game is a good idea. Defensive end George Karlaftis: George stayed Furious on Sunday— he was everywhere, with two sacks, six tackles and a pass defended. Three of those tackles were for a loss, forcing the Jets offense to (literally) go backward in the third quarter. Honorable mention to Ashton Gillotte, who also had a solid game and a quarterback sack. Defensive lineman Chris Jones: The CEO is back in the office— it wasn’t just the two sacks, but there was a different level of pocket-crushing and explosion this week than we’ve seen. Chris Jones got to the quarterback from the inside and the outside, had a tackle for loss, and a batted pass. This defense works so much better when he’s using offensive guards for sleds. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: It was a solid day for Mahomes — 23-of-31 for 242 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. But it’s the toughness that people will remember from this game. Somehow, after getting his throwing arm mangled on a strip sack, he didn’t miss a play. He went on to lead multiple touchdown drives and take multiple big hits without concern for his body. Tight end Travis Kelce: With question marks all over the wide receiver room and a disastrous start to this game, Mahomes went back to old reliable. Kelce delivered on four catches for 72 yards and a touchdown, including a 38-yard catch-and-run. 8 Losers The QB sneak: One attempt, one fumble, zero first downs, one snarky Head Coach in the postgame— it’s a 90% or better chance of converting for most teams. Why is this so difficult for the Chiefs? Quarterback Justin Fields, Center Creed Humphrey, Kick returner Cyrus Allen: Each of these guys was responsible for a fumble this week. Along with the two strip sacks of Mahomes, that makes five times the Chiefs put the ball on the ground. Luckily, they recovered four — but the sloppy play started on the opening kickoff and could have cost them the game. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: Another injury on an otherwise decent day. Worthy finished with six catches for 48 yards before leaving with a hamstring injury. It wasn’t a great sign that the Chiefs were reportedly desperate for a wide receiver before— they may want to add more than one now. Kicker Harrison Butker: The Chiefs didn’t need field goals to win this one, but Butker missed his only attempt — twice. He was predictably wide right from 56, then from 51 after a Jets penalty. The team would actually lose some available cap space if they were to cut their highly compensated kicker, but perhaps it would be worth the investment. Note: Applying the labels “losers” is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.

title: Chargers Week 9 PFF Grades: Backups come out better than starters in lopsided loss
summary: Even though the Chargers scored 22 points against the Texans, it somehow seemed like one of their worst outings of the year. Well, it sort’ve was before Quentin Johnston broke a short slant for a big 58-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter and the backups somehow found the end zone on their first drive of […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - November 08: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Derius Davis (12) catches a touchdown pass against Houston Texans safety Calen Bullock (2) during the second half of an NFL football game at Sofi Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026 in Inglewood, CA. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Even though the Chargers scored 22 points against the Texans, it somehow seemed like one of their worst outings of the year. Well, it sort’ve was before Quentin Johnston broke a short slant for a big 58-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter and the backups somehow found the end zone on their first drive of the game once they replaced the starting group. Defensively, this was not a good game for Chris O’Leary’s unit but how can you blame a group looking a bit deflated after balling out for seven weeks just to see their offense make zero improvements two months into the year. I don’t blame them for flopping finally. It was bound to happen. The Texans receivers were also making crazy play after crazy play. Sometimes that happens! But alas, 0-8 is still 0-8. Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Sunday. Offense Best WR Derius Davis – 90.1 TE Charlie Kolar – 67.0 QB D.J. Uiagalelei – 65.2 OT Joe Alt – 63.8 RB Keaton Mitchell – 63.5 Davis posted his first elite game grade of his career on offense. He caught the second touchdown of the game from D.J. Uiagalelei, which was also the latter’s first career touchdown scored in the NFL. After the starting offense, including Justin Herbert, went 37 drives between touchdown drives, it took DJU and the backups just one! That’s pretty ugly! Alt continues to be the team’s best offensive lineman. He allowed no sacks and two pressures. Mitchell was an efficient player in his stats with some good chunk runs and a trio of passes caught which tied for the team lead on Sunday with Kolar. Worst FB Scott Matlock – 31.1 QB Justin Herbert – 46.3 RB Kimani Vidal – 48.0 C Jake Slaughter – 49.9 OT/G Alex Harkey – 51.6 Herbert threw his 11th interception of the season which also made it eight consecutive games with a pick thrown to begin this season. He did throw his sixth touchdown of the year, but even that was quite the lucky break when Johnston breaks one tackle on a five-yard slant and takes it 58 yards to the house. Slaughter looked rough in this one in all phases. Specifically, there was a screen play to wideout Tre’ Harris who caught the pass in stride to then run behind Slaughter and Cole Strange out in front of him. Both linemen missed the first defender in pursuit and Harris was tackled before he could even get started. Harkey was dealt a bad hand as he was forced to play right guard in place of the benched Strange who was initially replaced by Branson Taylor. Taylor was rolled up on after just nine plays and Harkey had to transition inside after spending most of this year at right tackle. Defense Best LB Marlowe Wax – 91.3 DT Jamaree Caldwell – 79.3 EDGE Akkheem Mesidor – 77.7 DT Justin Eboigbe – 77.7 LB Daiyan Henley – 69.7 Wax made one of the best plays of the game for the defense when he made a diving pass deflection that ended up in the arms of Daiyan Henley. Caldwell recorded the team’s best pass rush grade at 77.5. Mesidor had a top five grade in both run defense and pass rush. With the aforementioned pick, Henley had one of his best games this year with every single one of his individual grades finishing at 60.0 or above. Worst CD Donte Jackson – 28.6 S Genesis Smith – 33.9 CB Tarheeb Still – 34.9 CB Rodney Shelley – 37.4 LB Troy Dye – 40.6 Jackson returned to the lineup for the first time since Week Four and he wound up being the worst-graded player on the Chargers against the Texans. His 29.0 coverage grade was his worst mark this year as he allowed four-of-six targets his way to be completed for 58 yards. He was also called for the penalty. Smith posted a 19.0 tackling grade, by far his worst of the season. He had five previous tackling game grades above 75.0. Still also posted his worst game of the season vs. the Texans. His 29.5 was by far his worst this year as he allowed seven completions on eight targets for 79 yards (also a season high) and a touchdown. The cornerback room continued to look like chopped liver with Shelley also among the bottom five. That’s three cornerbacks in the red in a single week. However, Shelley did post great marks in tackling (79.3) and run defense (72.8).

title: Chargers-Texans Game Recap: Bolts pummeled at home during night honoring team legends
summary: Former Chargers kicker John Carney and wide receiver Anthony Miller were honored on Sunday at SoFi Stadium as they were inducted into the Chargers Hall of Fame. Whatever nostalgia and warm fuzzies that ceremony gave to the Chargers fans in attendance was about all they got out of their trip to Inglewood on Sunday. The […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 08: Houston Texans wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson (19) scores a touchdown with Los Angeles Chargers safety Genesis Smith (22) defending during an NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Los Angeles Chargers on November 8, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Karl Anderson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former Chargers kicker John Carney and wide receiver Anthony Miller were honored on Sunday at SoFi Stadium as they were inducted into the Chargers Hall of Fame. Whatever nostalgia and warm fuzzies that ceremony gave to the Chargers fans in attendance was about all they got out of their trip to Inglewood on Sunday. The Chargers were battered by the Texans 41-22 at home in Week Nine behind C.J. Stroud’s 384 passing yards and five touchdowns. Not only did Stroud make a number of impressive throws, but his receivers were also equally as impressive with the amount of tough and contested catches they managed to come down with. Until the fourth quarter, the Chargers offense was the antithesis of the Texans. While it took long drives for Justin Herbert and the Bolts to end up with only three points, Houston only needed two or three plays on multiple drives to find the end zone in a flash. By the time Quentin Johnston took a short slant from Herbert for a long 58-yard touchdonwn, the Chargers had gone 37 consecutive drives without finding the end zone. They entered Sunday’s game with 27 consecutive drives, which was the second most since 2024 when the Mike McDaniel-led Dolphins went 30 drives without a touchdown. Herbert ended the night 13-of-23 for 193 yards and one touchdown with one intereception. His 11th pick of the season was on a deep pass to Johnston on a skinny post out of the slot that cornerback Derek Stingley snagged with one hand over his shoulder. The interception was not a pretty choice, but otherwise Herbert played fine enough while his receivers dropped several passes in the first half. The run game was mostly held in check until Omarion Hampton broke loose for 32 yards in the fourth. He ended up leading the team with 60 yards on 13 carries. Johnston’s lone reception of the night was his 58-yard score which also left him as the team leader in receiving yards. KeAndre Lambert-Smith also snagged a singular pass for 50 yards while Keaton Mitchell and and Charlie Kolar caught a trio of passes for 34 and 31 yards, respectively. It was a step back for the Chargers defense that had been playing very well given the circumstances of this season. Even when you take out the multiple drives against the Texans offense tha started in their own territory, the Bolts secondary was getting diced up for most of the night. Whether it was deep ball completions or huge gains via catch-and-runs, the Houston wideouts were legitimately balling out for their quarterback. At 0-8, the Chargers sit in the same place they’ve been all season long. They have no wins. They have no answers. And at this point, it’s incredibly hard to say if anyone has a future with the franchise outside of an elite few. Getting trounced in your own home is embarrassing. Getting trounced at home on a night honoring a pair of team legends is even worse. As much as this dire situation normally calls for some level of change, this team has been immensely stubborn in enacting that presumed path forward. Will that dreaded call from the very top finally come in? Was losing by three touchdowns at home the final straw? The short history of this season tells us there’s likely nothing of substance coming out of the team over the next 24 hours, but this is the NFL. Crazy things happen just about every week. The Chargers’ time for things to finally hit the fan has been waiting around the corner for weeks and weeks. Camels can only carry so much straw. For a complete recap of today’s game, continue on below! First Quarter The Texans began the game on offense after the Chargers won the coin toss and chose to defer. Stroud came out throwing, hooking up with receive Nico Collins for a gain of 19 on the first play from scrimmage. Two plays later, the Chargers defense looked to have gotten a stop by forcing an incompletion on third-and-two, but cornerback Tarheeb Still was flagged for a facemask penalty and the Texans were given 15 free yards and an automatic first. On third-and-six from the Chargers 17-yard line, Stroud found wide receiver Xavier Hutchison to put Houston up early 7-0 roughly five minutes into the game. Justin Herbert and the Chargers responded with a nine-play, 34-yard drive that ended in a 52-yard field goal by Cameron Dicker. On third-and-nine from the Houston 40-yard line, Mike McDaniel chose to run the football over passing for the first down, which resulted in a gain of six but well short of the sticks. The Chargers defense did a better job of getting off the field on their second outing, but Houston still go close enough to convert a long 56-yard field goal. On the other side, Herbert and the offense could not bring themselves back into field goal range to match Houston and were forced to punt for the first time. Second Quarter Los Angeles’ defense finally forced their first punt of the game after a three-and-out by the Texans to begin the quarter. The Bolts turned that momentum into their second field goal of the day after a nine-play, 36-yard drive that looked like a touchdown was finally in the forecast when Herbert and Co. faced a first-and-goal from the nine-yard line. However, they ended up going backwards six yards over the next three plays before settling for three. The Chargers defense struck with their first turnover of the game when a Stroud pass over the middle was deflected into the air by linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips. Fellow linebacker Daiyan Henley was luckily in the area and managed to haul in the takeaway before returning it 18 yards the other way. Despite the momentum shift, the Chargers offense managed just 14 yards in six plays. Dicker came on and converted from 43 yards out to make it 10-9 with a little over five minutes remaining in the first half. That one-point deficit unfortunately lasted no time at all for the Bolts. On the second play of the ensuing drive for the Texans, wide receiver Tank Dell ran an out-and-up against Donte Jackson along the right sideline. Jackson left his feet to bat the pass but the ball sailed over his hand and Dell caught it in stride before coasting untouched into the end zone. It took just 43 seconds and the Bolts were now facing their biggest deficit of the game. Needing points in the worst way, the Chargers offense got things started by allowing a sack on Herbert for a loss of five yards. All-Pro Will Anderson was lined up to Herbert’s left and he only had to beat tight end Charlie Kolar one-on-one to get home. Mitchell hauled in a 13-yard pass on second-and-24 and the third-down pass attempt was incomplete, leading to another punt after only going backwards. After another forced punt by the Texans, the Chargers offense once again only went backwards, this time four yards the wrong direction, before sending the ball back to Houston. Dell, who scored the Texans’ second touchdown of the game, actually botched the punt but somehow the ball ended up back in his hands despite multiple Chargers getting hands on during the play. That unfortunate luck only went on to bite Los Angeles even more. The Texans turned in a seven-play, 76-yard drive that took only 34 seconds and was capped with Stroud’s third touchdown pass of the game. This time, a 12-yard strike to receiver Kayshon Boutte. Third Quarter Instead of coming out of the halftime break rejuvenated and reenergized, the Chargers offense turned in a quick five-play, seven-yard drive that was cut short by Herbert’s 11th-interception of the season. Herbert was looking for Quentin Johnston who ran a skinny post up the left seam but cornerback Derek Stingley closed on the pass and made an incredible…

title: Is Sean McVay blind to the Rams need for another wide receiver?
summary: Sean McVay continues to talk about getting his offensive weapons more involved, but his actions tell a different story. Week after week, Sean McVay’s offense runs through Puka Nacua, leaving Matthew Stafford with limited dependable options when Puka Nacua isn’t the target or if he is not on the field. Nacua is undoubtedly one of […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay continues to talk about getting his offensive weapons more involved, but his actions tell a different story. Week after week, Sean McVay’s offense runs through Puka Nacua, leaving Matthew Stafford with limited dependable options when Puka Nacua isn’t the target or if he is not on the field. Nacua is undoubtedly one of the NFL’s best receivers, but the Rams cannot continue relying on him to carry such a significant portion of the passing game. Despite McVay’s intentions to distribute opportunities, the offense repeatedly gravitates toward Nacua when it needs a play. That raises a legitimate question: Is Sean McVay naive to the playmakers around Matthew Stafford? Puka had 150 receiving yards yesterday. The Rams' next-closest player had 20 (!!!) yards. The gap between Puka and their WR2 right now is absurd. And unsustainable. https://t.co/QPCJ50FRbR — Cameron DaSilva (@camdasilva) November 9, 2026 NFL commentators have repeatedly pointed out the limitations of the Rams’ supporting cast. Other wide receivers and tight ends have struggled to consistently create separation, particularly when working through their routes and getting out of their breaks. When receivers cannot generate meaningful separation, Stafford is forced to make tighter-window throws or move on to another option. #Rams WR route win rate is 30th in the league. But sure you don’t need anyone 🤷‍♂️ https://t.co/cnBx7Pu6Wk — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) November 7, 2026 Drops have only compounded the problem. Stafford has consistently put the ball in positions where his receivers can make plays, but too many opportunities have ended with incomplete passes. For a quarterback playing at a high level, that has to be frustrating. If the problem with the Rams offense is not skill, then it's scheme. What is the disconnect between what Scheelhaase/McVay are running that isn't translating in front of Stafford? Nobody outside a select few analysts even mentioned the potential setbacks losing LaFleur… — Big Tuna 🏈 (@1standtuna) November 8, 2026 The Rams have an elite quarterback and a superstar receiver, but that combination needs more support. McVay cannot keep expecting Nacua to be the answer to every offensive problem. Whether through a trade or another personnel move , Los Angeles needs another legitimate playmaker who can separate, create after the catch and consistently secure the football. The Rams were not hesitant in 2021 to add Odell Beckham Jr to the WR room when they already had Cooper Kupp and Robert Woods. Robert Woods went down with a torn ACL and showed just how important it was to have WR depth for the stretch run. Had Odell Beckham Jr stayed healthy in the Super Bowl, the Rams might have blown out the Cincinnati Bengals because they could not account for Odell Beckham Jr and Cooper Kupp. The longer the Rams wait, the more predictable their offense becomes.

title: Rams’ Braden Fiske might be trade asset before deadline
summary: The Los Angeles Rams might have to part ways with an important piece of their defensive line to acquire the wide receiver help they desperately need before the NFL trade deadline. Braden Fiske could become the trade asset that makes a potential deal possible, particularly if the Jacksonville Jaguars are willing to discuss Brian Thomas […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Braden Fiske #55 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the first half of a game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams might have to part ways with an important piece of their defensive line to acquire the wide receiver help they desperately need before the NFL trade deadline. Braden Fiske could become the trade asset that makes a potential deal possible, particularly if the Jacksonville Jaguars are willing to discuss Brian Thomas Jr. A Fiske-for-Thomas swap could make sense for both organizations. Jacksonville recently lost defensive tackle Davon Hamilton for the season after he tore his quadriceps, creating an immediate need for additional help along the interior defensive line. Fiske could provide the Jaguars with a young, disruptive defensive lineman who still has plenty of upside and multiple years of team control. James Gladstone, the Jaguars GM, was a big proponent of the Braden Fiske pick in 2024. Could he want to reunite with the 2nd rounder with shipping away Brian Thomas Jr to the Rams? Gladstone here gushing about Braden Fiske before the #Rams traded up to get him 👀 #Jaguars https://t.co/bgrflySjRY — @UCjags (@UCJags) November 9, 2026 Meanwhile, the Rams have a different problem to solve. Their offense continues to funnel opportunities through Puka Nacua, while the supporting cast has struggled to consistently separate and make plays. Adding Thomas would give Matthew Stafford another legitimate outside receiving threat and provide Sean McVay with a much-needed offensive weapon. There is also a potential roster squeeze in Los Angeles. Kobie Turner is working his way back from a groin injury, and his return figures to eat into Fiske’s playing time along the defensive front. That doesn’t necessarily make Fiske expendable, but it could make him a more attractive trade chip. Sacrificing a promising defensive lineman is never an easy decision. However, if the Rams can turn Fiske into a young receiver like Thomas, it might be a worthwhile investment in their championship aspirations.

title: Rams game-by-game predictions for second half of 2026
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have positioned themselves to make a serious push in the second half of the 2026 season, but the road ahead will determine just how far and how high they can go. full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates after his team's touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have positioned themselves to make a serious push in the second half of the 2026 season, but the road ahead will determine just how far and how high they can go. With several important matchups remaining, including a tough stretch from Weeks 12-14, Sean McVay’s team will need to find consistency on both sides of the football while navigating injuries and the challenges of a competitive NFC playoff race. Matthew Stafford and the offense will be expected to elevate their play, while the defense must maintain its ability to make game-changing plays when it matters most. From divisional battles to potential playoff previews, the Rams have plenty of opportunities to strengthen their postseason position. Here’s a game-by-game prediction at what lies ahead and how Los Angeles could finish the regular season. Week 10: @ Arizona Cardinals Since Los Angeles’s embarrassing loss to Arizona at home in Week 6, the Rams have rattled off three consecutive wins, albeit against the Raiders, Chargers, and Commanders. The Rams will want revenge against a divisional foe and they need the win to keep pace with other NFC teams. Prediction: Rams 30-17 (Record: 6-4) Week 11: BYE Much needed to get bodies back for stretch run. Week 12: vs. Green Bay Packers Because the Packers are red hot right now, I think the Rams see their four game winning streak ending to a team that has more working for them right now. The Rams best chance will be to cap the explosives that Green Bay loves to dial up with Jordan Love. Trent McDuffie should be able to silence either Christian Watson or Matthew Golden. But LaFleur has had McVay’s number… Prediction: Packers 27-24 (Record: 6-5) Week 13: vs. Kansas City Chiefs If the Rams lose to the Packers, they really do not have much more room for error. Patrick Mahomes is special but running away from Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald may not be his preferred option. Prediction: Rams 29-21 (Record: 7-5) Week 14: @ San Francisco 49ers Sometimes desperation is a good thing. San Francisco might be able to lock up the division with a win but even then the Rams desperation to stay in the hunt is enough to get LA a win on the road against their rivals. Prediction: Rams 23-20 (Record: 8-5) Week 15: vs. Dallas Cowboys The Cowboys offense is strong but the defense is not. Luckily that may play in favor of the Rams as their defense should be able to contain Dallas if McDuffie locks on Cee Dee Lamb. Prediction: Rams 33-24 (Record 9-5) Week 16: @ Seattle Seahawks Ever since the Thursday Night Football nightmare ending in 2025 and the NFC Championship Game, LA has probably been long awaiting this game. With the game being on Christmas Day, it will be entertaining watch. With the chance to bounce Seattle from the playoff picture, the Rams get a HUGE win for their playoff percentge odds. Prediction: Rams 23-17 (Record: 10-5) Week 17: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Needing a road win to guarantee a spot in the playoffs, Sean McVay clinches a playoff berth before Week 18; allowing them to rest starters in Week 18. Prediction: Rams 27-20 (Record: 11-5) Week 18: vs. Seattle Seahawks Maybe this matchup is playoffs or bust. Call me an optimist for thinking the Rams will have locked up either the 6 seed or 7 seed by this point. Prediction: Seahawks 20-10 (Record: 11-6) There you have it. PLAYOFFS. 11-6. The Rams can only afford 2 more losses. It should make for an interesting final 8 regular season games in 2026!

title: Rams 2026 mid-season report card
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have officially hit the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season with plenty of reasons to feel encouraged, but also several areas that need improvement if they intend to make a legitimate Super Bowl run. With 9 games under their belt, there is plenty of data and eye test to evaluate the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the second quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have officially hit the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season with plenty of reasons to feel encouraged, but also several areas that need improvement if they intend to make a legitimate Super Bowl run. With 9 games under their belt, there is plenty of data and eye test to evaluate the current roster. Sean McVay’s team has demonstrated the ability to compete with the league’s best, fueled by a strong running game, Puka Nacua’s yearly dominance, and a defense capable of shutting offenses down. However, inconsistency, injuries, and questions surrounding the supporting cast have prevented this team from reaching its full potential. With the second half of the season approaching, it’s time to evaluate how the Rams have performed across the board. From quarterback play and offensive production to defensive consistency, special teams, and coaching, here’s a midseason report card for Los Angeles. 2026 Mid-season Grades Matthew Stafford: B- Stafford’s 2026 season has been much different than his 2025 MVP campaign. This time last year, he was on an absolute heater. The story has been quite different in 2026 as he at one point had four consecutive 300+ yard passing games but as followed that up with four consecutive games of less than 250 yards passing. The reckless version of Stafford has been more prevalent as seen by his 9 interceptions which exceeds his 8 total interceptions in 2025. Stafford has been better as of late (last 5 games), throwing 10 touchdowns to 3 interceptions. Lastly, there is concern for Stafford’s elbow. Reports have suggested that he is nursing an elbow injury which is likely causing is air yards/attempt to be significantly less this year. Stafford is still having a “good” year but its a far cry from last season’s pace. He is projected to finish with 4484 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 17 interceptions. Kyren Williams & Blake Corum: A+ The Rams offense has been saved by the strong run game of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The two running backs have combined for 1040 rushing yards, 10 rushing touchdowns, 357 receiving yards, and 2 receiving touchdowns. They are producing when the team has needed it most. At minimum, Blake Corum is clearly a more efficient rusher than Kyren Williams You can even make a statistical argument that he is the most efficient rusher in the NFL Despite this, he is only getting 39% of the Rams' rush attempts this year pic.twitter.com/UJmzMc2auo — Box Score Scout (@boxscorescout) November 5, 2026 Expect Sean McVay to lean into both running backs in these next eight games with the passing game still trying to find its way. Puka Nacua: A+ Year in, year out, Puka Nacua does his thing. In seven games active, Puka Nacua has produced 715 receiving yards (102.1 yards/game). The only other wide receiver in the NFL averaging more receiving yards per game is Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Other WRs: D+ Apart from Davante Adams in Weeks 2 & 3, the Rams other wide receivers have been non-existant. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington have combined for 273 yards and 1 touchdown. That’s 30 receiving yards/game amongst 3 players. It’s simply not good enough. Here’s the worst part – this group has only accounted for 12 of the team’s 122 first downs. With Davante Adams having missed the last 3 games and Puka Nacua nursing a knee injury, the Rams NEED more from this group. Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury. Davante Adams is already on IR. The Rams' other wide receivers have 170 yards this season. Combined. Great week to find out if it's the system. pic.twitter.com/xml1mpuSjC — bunchu (@BunchuBets) October 22, 2026 Tight ends: C+ This is a tough group to grade because Terrance Ferguson has missed 5 games. Colby Parkinson has missed 2 games. This group provides so much value in the run game which is excelling. In the passing game, it’s been lukewarm at best. Tyler Higbee had a solid three game stretch from Weeks 3-5 but has been largely quiet since then. Davis Allen had a two touchdown game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Offensive Line: A- The Rams have been very fortunate in 2026 with their offensive line health through 9 games but now await the news of Steve Avila who reaggravated his hamstring . Coleman Shelton has been a rock at center and easily the Rams best offensive lineman. Alaric Jackson has been great aside from his Week 5 postgame antics which resulted in him missing Week 6 which turned out to be a loss to Arizona. Defensive Line: B The Rams were able to “coerce” Aaron Donald out of retirement. AD99 did miss the Week 1 loss vs San Francisco and the Week 4 win at Philadelphia but has become more of his usual self in recent weeks. Donald is blowing up run plays and causing offensive lines a headache with his interior pressure which frees up Garrett and Co. opportunities on the outside. The disappointment for the defensive line has been the original starters as Kobie Turner (IR, 0 sacks in 6 games), Braden Fiske (1.5 sacks in 9 games), Poona Ford (out for season) have not been more effective with the return of Aaron Donald. Tyler Davis, Larrell Murchison, and Ty Hamilton have done an admirable job of holding down the fort. Edge Rushers: B Myles Garrett was traded to be the upgrade over Jared Verse but he’s only played in 2 of the team’s 9 games. Finally, against Washington we saw why the Rams made the blockbuster deal for the reigning defensive player of the year . Via Next Gen Stats: With both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field (23 plays), the Rams’ defense allowed 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. On all other plays (19), the defense allowed 8.1 yards per play and a touchdown with no sacks. — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) November 9, 2026 Despite not having Garrett’s presence, I have been encouraged by the ascension of undrafted free agent Wesley Bailey . Bailey has 2 sacks, 2 tackles for loss, and 2 forced fumbles in his rookie season. Byron Young leads the team in sacks with 4.5 while he tries to put up a strong season in a contract year. The return of Myles Garrett should free him up significantly to win 1 on 1s. Linebackers: B Nate Landman is good, not great. He will occasionally show up with one of his peanut punches. The pleasant surprise has been Omar Speights who has 2 sacks, 2 pass deflections, 1 forced fumble, and 1 fumble recovery. He has been more aggressive in his tackling pursuit, something he struggled down the stretch with in 2025. Shaun Dolac continues to be a solid rotational piece for LA. Defensive Backs: A- When Trent McDuffie plays, the secondary is on a different level. Problem is that McDuffie has missed 3 games in 2026 due to multiple injuries. The Rams might have the BEST cornerback room in football. 👀 FOUR CBs ranked inside PFF’s Top 10 defensive grades Is this the deepest secondary in the NFL? pic.twitter.com/Uj73tlRrhb — LAFB Network (@LAFBNetwork) November 3, 2026 The addition of Jimmy Lake in the secondary has provided immediate benefit as we have seen Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace, Quentin Lake, and Kam Kinchens improve on the field. Jaylen Watson’s season-ending shoulder injury is Special Teams: F 3 kickers (technically 4 with the addition of Joshua Karty for kickoffs) in 9 games is not normal or recommended. Harrison Mevis lost the job due to carelessness. Blake Grupe lasted half of a game due to a torn ACL. Now the team is relying on Brandon McManus. However, Sean McVay does not seem inclined to kick a field goal beyond 45 yards and rightfully so. The team is also on their third punt returner. Xavier Smith was released after 4 games. Then Alex Bachman got a turn and the coaching staff realized (very late) that he was pretty much a non-factor. The job now belongs to Kyren Williams.…

title: When will Terrance Ferguson return for Rams?
summary: Terrance Ferguson had a setback in practice last week and the details coming out are that Ferguson is expected to miss a few weeks. Will Ferguson be able to stay healthy enough to play again for the Los Angeles Rams in 2026? The expectation is, yes, but he was expected to play in Week 9 […]
full_text: Terrance Ferguson had a setback in practice last week and the details coming out are that Ferguson is expected to miss a few weeks . Will Ferguson be able to stay healthy enough to play again for the Los Angeles Rams in 2026? The expectation is, yes, but he was expected to play in Week 9 and that didn’t happen. That’s concerning. Add in that Puka Nacua could miss Week 10 , and if there is no Ferguson, the Rams may not have a reliable pass catcher. Will the Rams make a trade before Tuesday’s deadline? If so, is there a receiver who can join and truly help the Rams less than a week later against the Arizona Cardinals? The Rams may have to roll with who they have, and after Nacua, the Rams passing game is a question mark, and that’s not a great look halfway into the NFL season. Sean McVay shares disappointing update on Terrance Ferguson’s latest injury (ramswire) ““Pulled his hamstring. You can’t make it up, can you?” McVay said, visibly disappointed. “He was running just a standard out-cut, felt his hamstring pull and probably be another couple weeks for him.” The Rams play the Cardinals next week, a game that Ferguson is almost certain to miss. After that, they have a bye in Week 11 before returning to face the Packers in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Eve. The Rams are going to take it a week at a time with Ferguson, as McVay wants to avoid any scenario where he isn’t activated before the 21-day window closes.“ Puka Nacua, Myles Garrett lead Rams to 20-13 win over Commanders (espn.com) ““I thought our guys did a great job of being able to find a way,” coach Sean McVay said. “There was a lot of opportunities that we missed offensively to make plays, extend drives, but they did enough. I love the way that Matthew responded after the turnover where he leads us down the field — had a bunch of gutsy conversions.” Stafford threw for 219 yards with an interception on 26-of-43 passing. Nacua, seemingly open all afternoon, was the target on 19 of those attempts. “He was awesome,” McVay said. “That’s one of the things that we want to be able to show as coaches, is show confidence to come right back to you. He made a bunch of plays. We needed all 14 of those catches.” Fans knew Rams needed another WR before Puka Nacua’s late injury vs. Commanders (ramblinfan) “Stafford’s first-half interception captured it perfectly. With no one to throw to and passes being dropped like hot coals, he forced the ball into double coverage targeting Nacua on the sideline for an easy pick. It was a poor decision to let that one go, but his frustration is understandable. The offense is predictable. It’s not going to work in the long term. In the trade market, names within a realistic price range for the Rams may not be among the most enticing available. Armed with only four draft picks next season, and without a first-rounder until 2028, can they afford to meet the asking price for the Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr. or the Colts’ Michael Downs?“ Rams WR Puka Nacua injured his knee on final play, will get MRI (ramswire) “ Washington Commanders , but about 90 minutes after the game ended, some concerning news was shared regarding the Los Angeles Rams receiver’s health. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported after the game that Nacua injured his knee on the Rams’ final offensive snap and will get an MRI to determine the severity. The play was a jet sweep handoff to Nacua that picked up 5 yards. Schefter added that the Rams don’t believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the MRI will give them more information. In the Rams’ 20-13 win , Nacua caught 14 of his 19 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown. He also had two carries for 20 yards.“ Rams Week 9 Stock Report: Myles Garrett and 4 Others Surge, but 2 Rams Slip in Washington (athlonsports) “Garrett finished with three sacks, a forced fumble, three tackles for loss and three quarterback hits in his first game since Week 1. His 93.7 grade led the Rams, and he had eight pressures on 37 snaps, according to PFF. He’s the first Ram with three or more sacks and a forced fumble in a game since Donald in 2020, according to the team . “Just getting back to who I am,” Garrett said.“ Aaron Donald’s interview after his first game with Myles Garrett was hilarious (ramswire) “Donald’s postgame interview in the locker room was hilarious, as the three-time Defensive Player of the Year was cracking jokes and laughing like crazy. “I did, man!” Donald said excitedly when asked if he got some one-on-ones Sunday. “I got close. Every time I got close, they got the ball out. I’m like, ‘Damn, they don’t want me to have a damn sack.’ But it’s all good. As long as we win, I’m good, man. But my ops were there. I had some good rushes, some clean wins but every time I got close, he got the ball out. But it’s all good. We got a good win, though.” Rams should trade for not one, but two Colts receivers (ramswire) “Allen is on a one-year contract, and considering his many years with the Los Angeles Chargers, moving back to Southern California shouldn’t be much of an issue. Despite his veteran age, Allen remains highly useful, especially as he’s able to find space against a variety of coverages. He’s excellent at reading the blitz and turning into a hot read. Plus, he’s a critical, reliable target on third down. The Rams are struggling to pass the ball in general, and Allen could help fix execution issues immediately. The other pass catcher is Downs. The Rams need a playmaker who can naturally stretch the field, while serving in a role that has ups and downs in usage. Also in the final year of his rookie deal – he’s Nacua’s 2023 draft classmate – the Rams wouldn’t have to be attached to a big contract for long. Plus, Downs could be a natural successor to Davante Adams, as long as the team is willing to switch up their offense while writing two massive checks. One to Downs, the other to Nacua.“ Browns 2027 NFL draft positioning: Flip spots with Rams after Week 9 results (sports.yahoo) “ The Cleveland Browns loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 9 has a chance to define the team’s season, as “the same ol’ Browns” is now back in play , unfortunately. Strangely enough, Cleveland did not see their AFC playoff position change at all , remaining in a tie for the final playoff spot, despite a level of despondency among the fanbase after two straight defeats. With the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, it will be interesting if the Browns’ strategy changes now that they sit 5-4. Cleveland fans may have also changed their focus to the upcoming 2027 NFL draft order and what could be added, especially with an extra first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams . The Rams got Myles Garrett back in Week 9 , and he put on a show. As noted in DBN’s Feed, he wasn’t the only Myles to do so this week:“ 2026 NFL season, Week 9: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Around The NFL breaks down what you need to know from Sunday’s action in Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season. Catch up on each game’s biggest takeaways using the links below: Madrid Cincinnati Bengals 34, Atlanta Falcons 17 Early Window Denver Broncos 26, Carolina Panthers 21 Dallas Cowboys 27, Indianapolis Colts 23 Kansas City Chiefs 35, New York Jets 12 Detroit Lions 19, Miami Dolphins 9 New Orleans Saints 23, Cleveland Browns 22 (OT) New York Giants 19, Philadelphia Eagles 11 Los Angeles Rams 20, Washington Commanders 13 Late Window Houston Texans 44, Los Angeles Chargers 22 San Francisco 49ers 38, Las Vegas Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers 45, New England Patriots 27 Seattle Seahawks 17, Arizona Cardinals 3 Sunday Night Chicago Bears 27, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 24 ” Report: Jaguars acquiring safety Jessie Bates III from Falcons for two draft picks (nfl.com) “The Jacksonville Jaguars are acquiring safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for a 2027 second-pick and 2028 fifth-round selection, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Monday. Atlanta is paying most of Bates’ $6.5 million salary to complete the deal, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported.…

However, those plans changed after Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury during Friday’s practice. You can’t make it up, can you? “He was running just a standard out-cut, felt his hamstring pull and probably be another couple weeks for him.” The extended absence is unfortunate for a Rams offense that could use more production and consistency from its supporting pass catchers. Ferguson has the athleticism and receiving ability to provide Matthew Stafford with another option at tight end, particularly as Los Angeles continues searching for ways to distribute targets beyond Puka Nacua. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson suffered his hamstring injury on an out route late in practice and imaging revealed it was a “pulled hamstring.” Likely a grade-one hamstring strain. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) November 9, 2026 While Ferguson’s ankle injury appeared to be nearing its conclusion, the hamstring issue has created another hurdle. full_text: FanDuel has the Los Angeles Rams as 7.5 favorites over the Arizona Cardinals entering Week 10. Considering the Cardinals are the home team, that is a fairly massive spread in favor of L.A. Throw in AZ beat the Rams earlier this season, though the Rams won in Week 9, their offense struggled once again throughout the game. Week 10 is not a lock for the Rams. L.A.’s defense has been the star of the show for the Rams in 2026 more so than the offense. Throw in the possibility that Puka Nacua could miss week 10 , and that 7.5 point spread seems even less likely for the Rams to cover. It should be interesting and worth monitoring to see if Gardnew Minshew get another start for Arizona as they could want to see rookie Carson Beck at some point, but that may not be against Myles Garrett and the Rams. Garrett had three sacks in Week 9, does he get another in Week 10? Will Aaron Donald get his first sack of the year in Arizona? Will Matthew Stafford throw more than one touchdown pass? Will Blake Corum out carry Kyren Williams? Does Trent McDuffie make his return for the Rams? There’s plenty of variables to consider, so pay attention as that 7.5 line could move between now and Sunday. Will this particular matchup be another low scoring affair like their earlier season game? Neither the Rams or Cardinals broke 20 points in their first contest, does that change the second time around? The Cardinals just lost to the Seattle Seahawks, and they’ll likely need to win against the Rams to keep their season alive from a playoff perspective. For the Rams, they are 5-4, but their margin for error is likely too small to drop Week 10’s game and still expect to make a real postseason push. There’s a lot on the line at this point in the season, and you can check out FanDuel to bet on the Cardinals or Rams and more NFL games. Bet responsibly.

title: The Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald combo was as-advertised
summary: It took two months longer than we thought it would, but we finally saw Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald wreck a game. Garrett sacked Jayden Daniels three times including a forced fumble. Donald did not record a sack, but he was productive in both the run and pass games despite what the box score indicates. […]
full_text: It took two months longer than we thought it would, but we finally saw Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald wreck a game. Garrett sacked Jayden Daniels three times including a forced fumble. Donald did not record a sack, but he was productive in both the run and pass games despite what the box score indicates. As a result, the Los Angeles Rams held the Washington Commanders to just 13 points as the team moves to 5-4 . According to SumerSports, Donald tied with Puka Nacua for a team-leading nine impact plays. Garrett came in third place with four. Donald: Average time to pressure: 2.15 seconds (0.45 faster than NFL average) 12.9% pressure rate (0.95% above NFL average) Two total pressures Garrett: Average time to pressure: 2.38 seconds (0.05 faster than NFL average) 21.4% pressure rate (7.18% above NFL average) Five total pressures Myles Garrett strip sack! LARvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5RBIONmDIR — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The Rams were creative in how they deployed Garrett and Donald. Donald stunted on 28.6% of his pass rushes, which ranks roughly 15% above his counterparts at the position. Garrett often lined up over the offensive interior in order to take advantage of a lineup change after the Commanders since they were without their starting center. While these numbers are unofficial and pending review, Pro Football Focus (PFF) also confirms stellar performances by both players. Garrett finished with an unofficial, team-leading defensive grade of 94.5 and Donald was third at 81.6. PFF had Garrett with nine pressures and Donald with five. LA finished with 21 pressures overall, which suggests the duo was also creating opportunities and favorable matchups for other defenders. Daniels was under pressure on 35% of his drop backs. It’s extremely difficult to play quarterback effectively in that environment, even if the Rams were without Trent McDuffie on the backend. Myles Garrett has 3 sacks today in his first game back. His return changes everything. pic.twitter.com/TQTJ6VO5jQ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 8, 2026 But another way to read that is to say the defense should get even better once McDuffie returns from the back injury he suffered last week. The Rams will be tough to face on defense. With Garrett back in the fold, it’s not a bold take to say they are now a defensive team. Opposing offenses should be shaking in their boots. Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald were exactly as advertised. They just put the rest of the NFL on notice.

title: Steve Avila injured, reaggravates hamstring

Avila appeared to be trending in the right direction throughout the week, initially participating in a limited practice Wednesday before upgrading to full participation Thursday and Friday. His […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Steve Avila #73 of the Los Angeles Rams gets set during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams suffered another potential setback along the offensive line as Steve Avila entered Sunday’s matchup against the Washington Commanders dealing with a hamstring injury. Avila appeared to be trending in the right direction throughout the week, initially participating in a limited practice Wednesday before upgrading to full participation Thursday and Friday. His progress allowed him to avoid a game designation on the final injury report, giving the Rams optimism that their starting left guard would be available without limitations. However, those concerns resurfaced Sunday. Avila exited during the second quarter after appearing to aggravate his hamstring while blocking on a Kyren Williams rushing attempt. He was escorted to the locker room by trainers and subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the game. Beaux Limmer replaced Avila at left guard, leaving Los Angeles without one of its most important interior offensive linemen. 🚨 BREAKING: Steve Avila (Rams LG) — hamstring; downgraded to OUT during today's game at Washington, per the Rams. A mid-game loss on the #Rams interior line. Updates to follow. pic.twitter.com/eTLHej1twA — The Blue Tent (@TheBlueTentnfl) November 8, 2026 Beaux Limmer was serviceable in his two plus quarters of action. However Los Angeles will hope that Avila’s absence is not a lengthy one as injuries have been a reoccurring for the team each week. The Rams play the Arizona Cardinals before their Week 11 bye, so it would not surprise me if Avila misses Week 10 to avoid any significant damage to the hamstring.
