title: Pay Puka Nacua already
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have made Puka Nacua the engine of their offense. That kind of responsibility can make a star receiver invaluable, but it also leaves the team exposed when the workload becomes unsustainable. Now Nacua is dealing with a knee injury, and the risk of building so much around one player is suddenly […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have made Puka Nacua the engine of their offense. That kind of responsibility can make a star receiver invaluable, but it also leaves the team exposed when the workload becomes unsustainable. Now Nacua is dealing with a knee injury , and the risk of building so much around one player is suddenly hard to ignore. Puka Nacua after the Rams victory. He talked about going into the medical tent after being flagged for concussion protocol, but mentioned nothing about the knee injury and seemed okay to me. pic.twitter.com/jdxNjr0cyD — Michael J. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) November 8, 2026 No one wants to see what the Rams’ offense looks like without him. The supporting cast has not shown it can reliably carry the load. Matthew Stafford could soon be leaning on Konata Mumpfield and Terrance Ferguson as his top targets, a tough situation for any quarterback and one that could make even a matchup with the Arizona Cardinals a challenge. The Rams have seen enough to know what Nacua means to the team. He has earned a new contract. Pay him. There are legitimate off-field concerns, and the situation created an unnecessary distraction and public relations headache for the organization. But the NFL did not determine that the matter warranted a suspension. Teams across the league have navigated serious controversies, too. Whatever the Rams decide about those concerns, they should not lose sight of Nacua’s value on the field. His usage tells the story. 21 plays went Nacua’s way against the Washington Commanders, and he drew 12 targets against the Los Angeles Chargers. His season-high workload came against the Buffalo Bills, when he saw 24 targets and added two rushing attempts. That is an enormous share of the offense for a receiver to shoulder week after week. Again, in this must recent outing, he comprised nearly two-thirds of LA’s passing production. All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 The Rams have put nearly all their eggs into Nacua’s basket. They have not developed another skill player who can offer the same combination of production and reliability. Receivers may be easier to find than players at some other positions, but finding one who can replace Nacua is another matter. He has established himself as one of the best players in professional football, and a replacement is unlikely to match his impact. The injury may be temporary, but the warning is clear: the Rams cannot keep asking Nacua to continue carrying this burden. Whatever the diagnosis, he has earned a new contract. The team should pay him, then build a better support system around him before this dependence costs them even more. Pay Puka Nacua already. Then step two: find him some help.
author: JB Scott

title: Rob Leonard’s clock ticking after Week 9 San Francisco 49ers loss with historically bad Las Vegas Raiders’ defense
summary: We’ve officially reached the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders are technically in the AFC Wild Card hunt. However, the Week 9 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers means the Raiders still haven’t beaten a playoff-caliber opponent, and a defense that hasn’t given up fewer than 27 […]
full_text: We’ve officially reached the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season, and the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders are technically in the AFC Wild Card hunt . However, the Week 9 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers means the Raiders still haven’t beaten a playoff-caliber opponent, and a defense that hasn’t given up fewer than 27 points since Week 2 is a big reason for that. Hence, defensive coordinator Rob Leonard leads off this week’s winners and losers column. LOSER: Rob Leonard To be fair, the offense had a pick-six in San Francisco, so the Raiders’ defense “only” gave up 31 points. However, they also became the first team since 2020 (fifth in the modern era) to give up at least 30 points in six consecutive games (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). The Detroit Lions and the Jacksonville Jaguars were the clubs to do it six years ago, and that was Matt Patricia’s last season as the Lions’ head coach and Doug Marrone’s final run in Jacksonville. While Klint Kubiak isn’t going anywhere in Las Vegas, Kubiak can’t continue to watch the defense struggle and not make a significant change. Leonard may not get fired this week, but he should at least be on the hot seat moving forward. After the game, the head coach was asked about making changes defensively and replied: “We’ll look at the film and make our decisions when we have cooler heads,” per Warren . So, Leonard might be safe for now, but that quote isn’t exactly a vote of confidence. If Kubiak wants to salvage the rest of the season, something has to change defensively, and it might start at the top. LOSER: John Spytek It’s fair to say that Spytek wasn’t going to fix all of the Raiders’ problems this past offseason, but he shoulders at least some of the blame for the defense’s struggles. Between Kwity Paye ($48 million), Quay Walker ($40.5 million), Nakobe Dean ($36.03 million), Eric Stokes ($30 million) and Malcolm Koonce ($11 million), the general manager spent over $165 million in total contract value on defensive players in the offseason. Other than Dean, none of those signings have been consistent and legitimate difference makers so far this season. On top of that, everyone knew that defensive tackle was one of the defense’s biggest needs heading into the offseason. However, Spytek essentially ignored the position. Now, the unit can’t stop the run and has little to no interior pass-rush. His job may not be in danger just yet, but Spytek should be feeling a lot of pressure right now. WINNER: Treydan Stukes Granted, what the GM might point to is the fact that Stukes is showing signs of becoming an impactful defensive back. It feels like he’s been getting better just about every week, and he had a strong performance in San Francisco, nabing his second interception of the season. The second-round pick was also targeted five times and allowed four catches for 19 yards while recording a pair of stops in coverage, per Pro Football Focus . That helped Stukes earn a career/season-high 84.4 grade that ranks fourth among safeties for the week (pre-Monday Night Football) . LOSER: Kirk Cousins A week after temporarily silencing Fernando Mendoza talks , Cousins played his worst game of the season to reignite the conversation. He completed 22 of 32 passes (68.8%) for just 216 yards and one touchdown to a season-high three interceptions. While the veteran quarterback is far from the Raiders’ biggest problem, the only thing keeping him in the starting lineup is that the Raiders are still in the playoff mix. However, as the losses mount and the team continues to show it isn’t a legitimate postseason contender, the more the organization’s focus shifts to the future. LOSER: Spencer Burford The coaching staff is clearly higher on Burford than outsiders are, but it’s getting hard to ignore that his PFF grade has bounced back and forth between good and well below-average every game since Week 4. This past Sunday’s game came in with a 43.6 mark , and Sumer Sports credited him with just one “impact block”. Additionally, Burford had a 48.7 run-blocking grade against the 49ers and is at 58.5 for the entire season while the offense can’t run the ball. At some point, the change up front can’t just be at right guard. Someone else needs to get a shot to replace Burford, especially since he’s only on a one-year contract. WINNER: Jermod McCoy It’s been a tough rookie season for McCoy, who looked rough in his limited playing time before this past weekend. While his production came in garbage time, it was good to see him record a couple of pass breakups on two targets in San Francisco. In a way, it felt like an NBA jump shooter going through a cold streak hitting a pair of free throws just to see the ball go through the hoop. Hopefully, that helps the fourth-round pick build some confidence moving forward, because the defense needs someone to step up at cornerback. LOSER: Adam Butler To be clear, Vegas’ defensive tackle issue extends far beyond just one player. However, Butler isn’t helping matters, and Sunday was a pretty rough afternoon for him. The veteran defensive lineman registered a start and 46 snaps (26 against the run, 18 as a pass-rusher and two in coverage) but posted a season-low 48.3 PFF run defense grade and failed to record a pressure. LOSER: Tim Keenan III On a similar note, Keenan made his first NFL start but failed to seize the opportunity. The practice squad call-up was the Raiders’ lowest-graded defender ( 39.4 ) and didn’t do what he was elevated for: stop the run. San Francisco’s wide zone rushing attack — which it leaned on more than any concept or for 32.6% of the offense’s carries, per Sumer — gave Keenan trouble as he was constantly washed out of his gap. That’s the rookie’s third call-up of the year, meaning he has to be added to the 53-man roster to be active for another game. If the coaching staff was using Sunday as a deciding factor in that decision, then it seems like Keenan will spend the rest of the year on the practice squad unless an injury or full-on youth movement happens down the stretch.
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders make plays but cough up ball too much in 38-17 thumping to 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders just couldn’t get out of their own way Sunday afternoon. Five awful second-half turnovers in a disconcerting 38-17 defeat were a testament to that. Facing a well-oiled machine that the San Francisco 49ers are, the Silver & Black fell quickly behind 21-10 after generating just 48 yards through the air and […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders just couldn’t get out of their own way Sunday afternoon. Five awful second-half turnovers in a disconcerting 38-17 defeat were a testament to that. Facing a well-oiled machine that the San Francisco 49ers are, the Silver & Black fell quickly behind 21-10 after generating just 48 yards through the air and 27 yards on the ground while yielding 123 passing and 125 rushing yards on defense. And on its first offensive play of the second half, Las Vegas gifted San Francisco seven more points off quarterback Kirk Cousin’s pick six and just like that, 28-10 Niners, and turnover No. 1. The Raiders didn’t go away, however, and put together a solid nine-play, 69-yard scoring drive that culminated in tight end Brock Bowers climbing the ladder for a 21-yard touchdown dart from Cousins to trim the deficit to 28-17. The Silver & Black gained even more momentum with rookie safety Treydan Stukes’ leaping interception of Brock Purdy. But just two plays later, linebacker Fred Warner punched the ball out of Bowers’ hands and the Red & Gold recovered, for Raiders turnover No. 2. A 10-minute sequence that we'll never be able to unsee. pic.twitter.com/DzxMlxsVK6 — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 8, 2026 Again, Las Vegas refused to lay down and Rob Leonard’s much-maligned Raiders defense rose to the occasion stuffing Purdy on a QB sneak to get the ball back to Klint Kubiak’s offense. And it appeared the visitors from the desert were poised to get within four points of their former Bay Area rival when tight end Michael Mayer hauled in a sharp 24-yard pass from Cousins. But as the big pass catcher dove towards the goal line, he lost control of the ball fumbling it into the end zone with Warner recovering for the touchback. No points, and pivotal turnover No. 3. Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers offense responded with a seven-play, 80-yard touchdown drive capped by Purdy’s 37-yard laser of a throw to Jordan Watkins for a pretty 37-yard touchdown catch in which the 49ers wide receiver boxed out rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses. Trailing 35-17, Kubiak’s offense once again got within striking distance on Raheem Morris’ stingy 49ers defense after Bowers’ 33-yard catch and run to the one-yard line. But the Nines read the QB sneak to perfection to stonewall that, an iffy offensive pass interference by Mayer cost the Raiders six points, and Cousins’ throw to Tre Tucker in the end zone was intercepted on 2nd-and-goal from the 13-yard line to thwart Kubiak’s offense once more — turnover No. 4. After allowing a 49ers field goal, the Raiders ended the day offensively with another Cousins interception — a deep throw intended for Tucker that was picked off, turnover No. 5. Michael Mayer almost had two touchdowns, one was called back due to a penalty and the other, Mayer fumbled the ball at the one yard line and it was recovered by San Francisco. Mayer spoke with the media after the Raiders loss to SF pic.twitter.com/GJ7N8ky2Rf — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) November 9, 2026 Las Vegas made it fair share of plays, but San Francisco simply made more and the defeat showcases just how far the Raiders are from competing with and beating good teams in the NFL. At 4-5 overall, Kubiak has done well to win four games in his rookie year as a head coach but those victories came against struggling teams. When faced with upper-echelon opposition, the Raiders have come close and no cigar or been boat raced. Sunday afternoon in Santa Clara was a mix of both. Kubiak’s Raiders were in a dogfight and allowing just 10 second-half points against the 49ers is a plus. It’s just too bad Leonard’s defense couldn’t have that kind of performance in the opening half. As I noted when I previewed the Raiders-49ers Week 9 matchup, the team that Kubiak wants in Las Vegas what Shanahan currently has in Santa Clara . The foundational model of a complementary football team that’s disciplined, efficient, and explosive in all three phases (offense, defense, and special teams) is what Kubiak eventually wants in the desert. And today’s loss highlights fleeting moments of that but also the hideous warts of the complete opposite. Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as both teams turned the ball to one another in a topsy turvy third quarter: —The Niners’ 31 points on offense marks the sixth-straight time the Raiders defense has allowed 30 or more points this season — tying a modern era NFL record. Heading into Week 9 play, Las Vegas allowed 230 points total and only the Arizona Cardinals (238) and Baltimore Ravens (236) allowed more. —A week after jumping too early in pass coverage (and not snagging two potential interceptions) , Stukes displayed perfect timing and baiting Purdy on his interception of a pass intended for 49ers tight end George Kittle. The second-round pick is progressing well in his rookie year. Treydan Stukes in the right place at the right time 👏 LVvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ybBp5MdnTi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 —Cousins finished 22 of 32 passing for 216 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions . Sunday’s performance was the worst the veteran quarterback put forth this season and it was a game where the 38-year-old’s arm strength waned as the game progressed. —Even facing top-flight defenses, Bowers continues to be a productive Raider and un-guardable at times. The tight end hauled in seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown (long of 33) to pace Las Vegas’ offense. Tucker finished behind Bowers with four receptions for 54 yards and Mayer had three catches for 37 yards. —Las Vegas’ run game continues its abysmal performances finishing with 27 yards on 15 carries — three yards less than the first half sum of 27. Ashton Jeanty paced the group with six carries for 25 yards (long of nine) while Bowers added one carry for two yards, Cousins had two carries or no yards (but a touchdown) and Mike Washington Jr. finished with six totes for negative three yards. —Raiders kick return man Dylan Laube continues to be a electric special teamer with seven returns for 197 yards (28.1 average per return) with a long of 57 yards. The Raiders first kick return was hauled in by Laube but he pitched it to wide receiver Dareke Young on a reverse for an additional 25 yards. Quote of Note “We’ll look at the film, and we’ll make our decisions when we have cool heads.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on whether changes are needed to be made on defense after allowing 30 points for the sixth-straight week “At this time of year, we’re focused on winning games. I really like our team. I don’t like losing games like this. You’ve got to have a lot more resilience to you when you’re playing a really good team that we played today. And when you start that slow, you don’t put yourself in good position. But I’m proud to coach the guys that we’re coaching.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on the current state of his Raiders roster Up Next The 4-5 Raiders return to the confines of Allegiant Stadium in Week 10 to take on the visiting Seattle Seahawks. The home cooking hasn’t been too good for the Silver & Black as the team is just 1-3 inside Allegiant. Coming off a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9, the 5-4 Seahawks bring a team that Kubiak is all too familiar with. How that familiarity benefits his Raiders remains to be seen, however. A better showing and a win would lift Las Vegas back to .500 with a Week 11 AFC West showdown with the Denver Broncos on the horizon.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: It’s time for the Raiders to trade Kirk Cousins
summary: Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders had a bad game against the San Francisco 49ers, but to be clear, that isn’t the reason why he should be traded. Cousins, is 38 years old and playing some of if not the best ball of his career. After getting beaten the way they did on top […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders had a bad game against the San Francisco 49ers, but to be clear, that isn’t the reason why he should be traded. Cousins, is 38 years old and playing some of if not the best ball of his career. After getting beaten the way they did on top of suffering the implosion they did, it should be clear to everyone that head coach Klint Kubiak has the team trending in the right direction. What should also be clear is that as is, the 2026 Raiders have an extremely diminutive chance of making the playoffs. As of this weekend, the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him, per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is… pic.twitter.com/g9aU9OGyHl — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 Raiders ahead of schedule but not that far With a 4-5 record and the defending Super Bowl champions coming into Allegiant Stadium next week, the Raiders’ playoff chances are dwindling down to a mathematical permutation. The solution to that equation is a variable resting between slim and none. Cousins has had a good run, exceeded expectations and been a good bridge for both Kubiak and quarterback of the future, Fernando Mendoza, to come in and get situated. The Raiders are not in a position for Cousins to lead them into the playoffs. Despite lining up in power formations a majority of the time, the Raiders rushing attack is non-existent. In fact, they have as many games above 100 yards (2) as they do under 50 yards as a team. Taking that a step further, after his second successful quarterback sneak for a touchdown against the 49ers, Cousins is leading the team in rushing touchdowns. Defensively, despite a strong start, the Raiders defense stands on the precipice of being historically bad. For six straight weeks, the defense has allowed 30+ points to playoff and non-playoff teams alike. They have been the game on the schedule struggling offenses see on the calendar and circle, because they know a get-right game when they see it. Seven straight games of 30+ points against a defense has never been done in the modern era. A statistic no one should ever want to be associated with and one would be remiss if one declined to state that the Raiders likelihood of setting that record was high. Yes, the 49ers may have had two weeks to prepare for the Raiders on both sides of the ball. But the Raiders had their opportunities to make it a game and blew chunks all over their cleats. All that to say, Cousins needs help and it’s obvious that he’s not going to get it here in 2026. Trading Cousins Cousins has been the dutiful soldier and if possible, should be granted the opportunity to go back where he last had meaningful success in Minnesota with head coach Kevin O’Connell. Currently, the Vikings have an extra third-round draft pick and two additional fifth-round draft picks as well. Trading carries no dead cap hit for the Raiders and the $1.6M salary fits within the remaining $6.17M of remaining cap space the Vikings have. The way Schefter is talking here intimates something massive for the Vikings at QB lol pic.twitter.com/hPHVBkY8s9 — Sayre Bedinger (@SayreBedinger) November 6, 2026 The Vikings have a defense, better wide receivers and a better running game. Everything Cousins needs to take the pressure off himself and contend. Although word on the street is that the Raiders may have missed their window to move him. According to Adam Schefter, there haven’t been any offers made for Cousins, and the Raiders have had no intention of moving him. Ever the optimist, Kubiak is looking at the schedule and still sees the team as being in it, despite not having any answers for better defensive play or balance on offense. The trade deadline is Tuesday 4pm EST/1 pm PST and the Raiders only have six draft picks in the 2027 draft, with lots of holes to fill. It would behoove the Raiders’ front office to take a long, hard look at what they could get for Cousins and weigh it against the near future. Unpopular as it may be.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders expected to face Drew Lock on Sunday
summary: Sunday night, it appeared the Las Vegas Raiders would be facing a No. 3 quarterback Sunday when they host the Seattle Seahawks. Now, though, it seems as if they will be playing a backup. Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald told a local radio station Monday morning that starting quarterback Sam Darnold will miss his second […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday night, it appeared the Las Vegas Raiders would be facing a No. 3 quarterback Sunday when they host the Seattle Seahawks. Now, though, it seems as if they will be playing a backup. Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald told a local radio station Monday morning that starting quarterback Sam Darnold will miss his second straight game because of quad and ribs injuries. However, Macdonald said backup Drew Lock is expected to play after he had positive news on an oblique injury. Sunday night, Macdonald indicated No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe could face the Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald told @BrockHuard and @TheMikeSalk on Seattle Sports 710 ESPN that he is ruling out Sam Darnold for this week’s game vs the Raiders. But tests on Drew Lock’s oblique injury were “good”, and they believe he can start vs. the Raiders. pic.twitter.com/mba3rSJrZt — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 Still, playing against backup is a good advantage and the Raiders, who are 4-5 and who have lost five of the past six games, could use an advantage for their defense. Las Vegas has allowed 30 or more points in six straight games. It has tied an NFL record. Lock is 2-0 as a starter this season, with both wins coming against the Arizona Cardinals. Sunday, he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown pass with no interceptions.

title: Raiders News: Las Vegas’ AFC West slide continues with Broncos’, Chiefs’ wins
summary: Week 9 was brutal for the Las Vegas Raiders. Not only did they suffer a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but the Raiders also pretty much fell out of contention for the AFC West Championship. Not that Las Vegas had good odds of winning the division heading into the weekend, but the loss […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 9 was brutal for the Las Vegas Raiders. Not only did they suffer a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but the Raiders also pretty much fell out of contention for the AFC West Championship. Not that Las Vegas had good odds of winning the division heading into the weekend, but the loss combined with the Denver Broncos’ and Kansas City Chiefs’ wins virtually puts an end to any slim hopes. On that note, let’s check in on the rest of the division, including the Los Angeles Chargers. Broncos vs. Panthers Score: 26-21 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 25/37 (67.6%), 237 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT RB Jonah Coleman: 17 carries, 57 yards (3.4 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 31 yards WR Pat Bryant: 4 catches, 56 yards, 1 TD EDGE Nik Bonitto 2 tackles, 1 sack, 1 FF, 1 FR S Devon Key: 4 tackles, 1 INT This was a solid road win for the Broncos, as they scored on the game’s opening possession and led for three out of four quarters. Granted, Denver did get a scare in the third quarter, falling behind by a point. However, Key’s interception flipped the momentum back in the Broncos’ favor, leading to a two-score lead with about six minutes left. A late fumble by Coleman gave Denver a late scare, but the team had control of the game for the majority of the contest. Next week: Bye Chiefs vs. Jets Score: 35-12 Chiefs win Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 23/31 (74.2%), 242 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs RB Kenneth Walker III: 18 carries, 102 yards (5.7 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 41 yards, 2 receiving TDs TE Travis Kelce: 4 catches, 72 yards, 1 rush, 1 yard, 1 rushing TD LB Nick Bolton: 12 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 FF EDGE George Karlaftis: 6 tackles, 2 sacks, 3 TFLs, 1 PD, 3 QB hits This was a pretty dominant performance where Kansas City outgained New York by more than 160 total yards. The Chiefs’ defense didn’t give up a touchdown in the first half and pitched a shutout in the second, while Walker turned in a three-touchdown performance while flirting with 150 yards from scrimmage. The only worry coming out of Kansas City was an injury to Mahomes’ throwing arm/elbow, but the quarterback came back into the game and isn’t believed to have a significant issue. He will undergo more testing on Monday, though. Next week: @ Falcons Pat Mahomes is on the sidelines after injuring his right arm on this play pic.twitter.com/rdOEkmr5uq — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 8, 2026 Chargers vs. Texans Score: 44-22 Chargers lose Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 13/23 (56.5%), 193 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT RB Omarion Hampton: 13 carries, 60 yards (4.6 ypc) WR Quentin Johnston: 1 catch, 58 yards, 1 TD LB Daiyan Henley: 10 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 INT S Tony Jefferson: 5 tackles, 0.5 sack This game was so bad that Herbert got benched. That might have been an effort to spare the quarterback, because Houston’s pass rush feasted on Los Angeles’ weak offensive line with eight sacks. Meanwhile, the Chargers defense wasn’t any better, giving up 485 yards and 7.3 yards per play to C.J. Stroud and Co. At the end of the day, the Bolts look every bit like the worst team in the NFL. title: Las Vegas Raiders’ Wild Card hopes still alive in AFC Playoff Standings despite Week 9 loss to San Francisco 49ers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a brutal 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 9. However, the Raiders got some help with the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots and Cleveland Browns also losing over the weekend, keeping Las Vegas in the AFC Wild Card hunt as we take a look at the playoff […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a brutal 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 9. However, the Raiders got some help with the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots and Cleveland Browns also losing over the weekend, keeping Las Vegas in the AFC Wild Card hunt as we take a look at the playoff picture/standings below. [Editor’s note: The standings below are before the Buffalo Bills-Minnesota Vikings game on Monday night. Silver and Black Pride will update this article when that game goes final.] AFC Playoff Standings 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) – Monday Night Football 2. Denver Broncos (7-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2 in AFC for tiebreaker over PIT) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, win over CIN, 3-2 in AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2, 6-1 AFC for tiebreaker over CIN) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2, loss to PIT, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-4, 5-1 AFC for tiebreaker over CLE) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5, 3-3 AFC for tiebreaker over BAL) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5, 2-4 AFC) 11. Houston Texans (3-5) 12. New York Jets (2-7, 2-4 AFC for tiebreaker over IND) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-7, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-7, 1-4 AFC for tiebreaker over TEN) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7, 1-5 AFC) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) Explaining the 6-2 logjam: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals are both 6-2, so they first have to settle the AFC North leader. Pittsburgh’s win over the Bengals slots the Steelers into fourth place. In the Wild Card, the Chiefs and Bengals are tied. The Chiefs have the best AFC record at 6-1, so they fill in at fifth. The Bengals are sixth. As mentioned last week, the Ravens’ playoff hopes are dwindling now that starting quarterback Lamar Jackson is likely out for the season and backup Tyler Huntley is on injured reserve. Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett last week to give the offense another option, though. Meanwhile, the Patriots got blown out by the Green Bay Packers to lose two of their last three games, and the Browns fell a point short after going for two in overtime against the New Orleans Saints. So, the Raiders are only a game back of the third Wild Card spot. However, it’s technically a game-and-a-half since the Patriots have the tiebreaker with the head-to-head win. Additionally, Las Vegas heads to Cleveland at the end of the month, giving the Silver and Black another opportunity to gain some ground in the seventh-seed race. Next week, New England has the Detroit Lions in Germany, the Browns host the Texans, and the Ravens host the Chargers on Monday Night Football (yuck!), while the Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks.

title: Raiders-49ers: 16 things we learned
summary: After ending a four-game losing streak with an impressive second half comeback win last week, the Las Vegas Raiders faced another quality opponent in Week 9 and, well, the results were familiar. The Raiders were blown out in their first game in Bay Area since 2019 as the San Francisco 49ers clubbed the 38-17 on […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images After ending a four-game losing streak with an impressive second half comeback win last week, the Las Vegas Raiders faced another quality opponent in Week 9 and, well, the results were familiar. The Raiders were blown out in their first game in Bay Area since 2019 as the San Francisco 49ers clubbed the 38-17 on Sunday. The Raiders are now 4-5 and fell to under .500 for the second time this season after starting 3-0. There has been a clear theme under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak so far this season. They beat bad teams and lose to good teams. The four teams the Raiders had a collective 5-24 record going into this week’s slate. The Raiders are 0-5 against teams with a .500 record or better. Games against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos loom in the next two weeks. They both have winning records. However, The Seahawks may be down to third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe next with both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock dealing with injuries. This was their third blowout loss. With the trade deadline looming Tuesday, the Raiders have a chance to become sellers if they wish. The Raiders’ problems Sunday were easy to spot. They were sloppy on offense and leaky as usual on defense. The Raiders committed turnovers on five of their six possessions in the second half with two turnovers in the end end and a Pick Six. Kirk Cousins had his worst game as a Raider with three interceptions. The Raiders allowed 30 points on defense for the sixth straight game. It tied an NFL record. Here is a look at the key aspects of this game: Rob Leonard needs to figure it out: The Raiders’ defense is getting gutted every week and first-year defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has to be feeling the pressure. He is likely not in jeopardy of losing his job. But he has to find a way to get improved results. The same thing is happening every week. Cousins struggles: Cousins made some awful decision Sunday. The Pick Six was a disaster than he should have thrown away and his interception in the end zone was rough as well. The team will probably stick with Cousins until they re out of the playoff race. but games like this will not quiet the Fernando Mendoza chatter. Run game isn’t there again: The Raiders fell behind early, so that hurt the run attack. But when the did run the ball, like as usual, the Raiders didn’t get much going. The Raiders had just 24 yards rushing. Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington each ran the ball six times. Jeanty had 25 yards and Washington had minus-3. Last week, Washington ran the ball 25 times and Jeanty ran it twice. 49ers ran all over the Raiders: The Raiders’ trouble stopping the run continued as the 49ers had 190 yards on the ground. Quarterback Brock Purdy had 32 yards rushing on one drive. Trade candidates: Kubiak didn’t say the Raiders won’t trade any payaers by Tuesday’s deadline, at 1 p.m. PT. It would be a shock if the Raiders made a big trade such as dealing Maxx Crosby (who said again after the game he wants to stay in Las Vegas) or Cousins. But a smaller deal could happen. Maybe they can get something for wide receiver Tre Tucker or safety Jeremy Chinn, who are a free agents after the season or the benched Jackson Powers-Johnson. Las Vegas general manager John Spytek has some decisions to make. Third quarter insanity: Wild, just wild. The quarter started with Kirk Cousins throwing a pick six to give the 49ers a three-possession lead. Then, the Raiders answered with a touchdown. Then, Treydan Stukes picked off Brock Purdy and returned it deep into 49ers’ territory with the Raiders down 11. Then, Brock Bowers fumbled it brought back to the 49ers. Then, they were stopped on their own 40 on fourth and inches. Then, Michael Mayer fumbled into the end while trying to score and make it a one-score game. Wow, just wow. A 10-minute sequence that we'll never be able to unsee. pic.twitter.com/DzxMlxsVK6 — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) November 8, 2026 Bowers’ big plays: Bowers had three receptions of 20 plus yards Sunday and e leads all NFL tight ends with 11. Remember, he missed two games this season. Bowers had seven catches for 111 yards and a score. Yes, he’s a monster playmaker. Crosby gets home: Crosby sacked Purdy in the second quarter. It was the second straight game Crosby had a sack and he has four on the season. Tackle machine : Raiders’ free-agent pickup, linebacker Nakobe Dean had his fifth straight game with, at least, 12 tackles. He joins Denzel Perryman (2021) as a Raider to do that since 1994. Laube strikes again: Dylan Laube is a weapon. The kick returner had a 54-yard return to 49ers’ territory in the second quarter. This came a week after he had a 95-yard kick return for a score in a five-point Raiders’ win. It was the first kick return for a touchdown in the NFL this season and the Raiders’ first in 15 years. Laube enter Week 4, leading the NFL with a 34.1 kick return average, nearly three yards more than any other returner. He’s fun. Zuhn starts again, then hurt: Rookie, third-round pick, Trey Zuhn, started at right guard for the seconds tight week. He is the Raiders’ third starter at the position this season as fellow recent high-draft picks, Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, have both been benched. But Zuhn left the game in the third quarter with a concussion and was replaced by Rogers. CB rotation continues: Darien Porter was back in the starting lineup, but rookie Jermod McCoy did play some in the second quarter. Rookie Zeke Masses played in the third quarter. This will likely continue. Keenan starts: Rookie defensive tackle Tim Keenan started as the Raiders began the game with three defensive tackles, Keenan, Adam Butler and Foley Fatukasi. Keenan has been elevated from the practice squad the past three games. Thus, the next time he plays this season. He must be on the 53-man roster. So, he could be promoted soon. Wide receivers sit again: Las Vegas wide receivers Dont’e Thornton and Malik Benson are both healthy scratches for the second straight week. They both may need an injury to occur to see the field in the foreseeable future. The fact they cut Cody White last week before bringing him back the next day, shows they feel like Thornton and Benson could get claimed on waivers if they cut them, so their roster spots may be relatively safe even though they’re not playing. Deferred again: The Raiders won the coin toss and deferred to get the ball in the second half. That is their normal practice when they win the coin toss. But two weeks ago. They won and they took the ball first. Good crowd: Many Raiders’ fans were in the stands at Santa Clara on Sunday. This was the Raiders’ first game in the Bay Area since their last game in Oakland in 2019. Bay Area fans missed the Silver and Black.

Here is everything to need to know about the contest: c First quarter : The Raiders won the coin toss and deffered to the secodn half. The 49ers walzted down the field taking a 7-0 lead on a 12-play, 69-yard rive. The Raiders went three-and-out on their first drive. The 49ers have run all over Las Vegas. They have 94 yards on the ground and quarterback Brock Purdy had 32 of his own on the 49ers’ second drive, including converting a first down on third and 15. The 14-0 lead with 1:52 to go after an 89-yard drive and the Raiders have run just three offensive plays. Second quarter: . The Raiders answered with a solid, touchdown drive of their own, capped by a one-yard sneak by Kirk Cousins. The 49ers lead 14-7 with 12:41 to go in the quarter. The 49ers answered with their third touchdown in as many drives as Purdy hit Christian McCaffrey for an easy score. San Francisco leads 21-7 with 5:15 to go. After a 54-yard kick return by Dylan Laube (yes, he’s on fire), the Raiders converted a Matt gay field goal to make it a 21-10 game with 1:12 to go. Halftime, 49ers 21, Raiders 10. Las Vegas gets the ball to start third quarter. Third quarter: Oh, dear, to open the second half, Kirk Cousins bobbled the snap and then panicked and threw a Pick Six. 49ers 28, Raiders 10. What an awful start to the half. The Raiders answered with Cousins hitting Brock Bowers for a 21-yard score to cut the 49ers’ lead to 28-17 with 9:29 to go. Now, Las Vegas rookie safety Treydan Stukes picked off Purdy and ran it well into San Francisco territory. New ball game. Oh no, Bowers fumbles. San Francisco ball. Blown opportunity. Now, the 49ers were stopped on fourth down on their own 40. Raiders back in business. What a wild quarter. Oh wow, Michael Mayer fumbles into the end zone while trying to score. 49ers ball. Insanity. 49ers settle the madness and connected on 37-yard pass play to make it a 35-17 game with 36 seconds to go. It’s not over, but the Raiders have work to do. Fourth quarter: Cousins threw an interception in the end zone. That’s four turnovers for Las Vegas this half. 49ers hit a field goal, up 38-17 with 5:21 to go. The Raiders commit their fifth turnover of the second half, a third interception by Cousins. Final score: 49ers 38, Raiders 17 Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 4-5. The San Francisco 49ers are 7-1. What the loss means for the Raiders: The Raiders are under .500 for the time this season after starting the year 3-0. Their defense gave up 30 points or more for the sixth straight game, which ties an NFL record. They still have not beat a team with a .500 or better record. Turning point of the game: The 49ers were in control from the start. It was never really a contest. Injury report: Right guard Trey Zuhn suffered a concussion in the third quarter and was replaced by Caleb Rogers. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders are hosting the Seattle Seahawks next Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:05 p.m. PT. Raiders Week 9: Meet the 49ers

title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week nine defeat
summary: The Miami Dolphins played one of the best football teams in the National Football League on Sunday — the Detroit Lions — and while the defense was able to ground their opponents’ typically high-flying offense, it was their own ineptitude while possessing the football that dug the Dolphins’ grave this past weekend. Miami lost 19-9, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Zane Gonzalez #31 of the Miami Dolphins kicks a field goal against the Detroit Lions during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins played one of the best football teams in the National Football League on Sunday — the Detroit Lions — and while the defense was able to ground their opponents’ typically high-flying offense, it was their own ineptitude while possessing the football that dug the Dolphins’ grave this past weekend. Miami lost 19-9, mostly due to ugly offensive line play and a litany of penalties. The latter is understandable when you consider the youth movement the Dolphins are currently swearing by. They are seeing the most playing time by rookies out of all teams in the NFL. Still, at the midway point of the 2026 campaign, you’d hope to employ a more disciplined roster at this stage. FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is pass rusher Josh Uche. Uche ended the day with one sack of quarterback Jared Goff, two quarterback hits, one of which affected the trajectory of Goff’s pass and allowed rookie cornerback Chris Johnson to intercept his first pass as a professional. Uche — 28 years old — signed a one-year deal with Miami that totals just a hair over $1.4 million. His quality season will allow the soon-to-be free agent to ink a more lucrative contract in the offseason — either with Miami or another team looking for pass rush help. Uche has already surpassed his season high best mark in tackles — he currently has 34 combined takedowns this year. He’s also contributed three sacks, five tackles for loss and a fumble recovery, giving Miami a veteran presence on defense that has been sorely needed on this difficult year. FINS DOWN Our Fins Down player is kicker Zane Gonzalez. Against the Lions, Gonzalez missed a 38-yard field goal try by doinking it off of the upright. It is his second consecutive game with a missed field goal — as he also shanked a kick against the Patriots in last week’s narrow defeat. Gonzalez hasn’t shown enough in his three games with Miami to give general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan a reason to promote him full-time to an active roster spot — and with all three of his practice squad call-ups in the rearview mirror, don’t be surprised if the Dolphins are going shopping for a new place-kicker ahead of their clash with the Indianapolis Colts this weekend.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions
summary: The Miami Dolphins entered Week 9 looking to get back on track after their loss to the New England Patriots last week. Instead, they walked away from Hard Rock Stadium with another frustrating loss — falling 19-9 to the visiting Detroit Lions. There were certainly some positives to take away from Sunday’s performance, particularly on […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Derrick Moore #8 of the Detroit Lions pressures Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins during the fourth quarter of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins entered Week 9 looking to get back on track after their loss to the New England Patriots last week. Instead, they walked away from Hard Rock Stadium with another frustrating loss — falling 19-9 to the visiting Detroit Lions. There were certainly some positives to take away from Sunday’s performance, particularly on the defensive side of the football. Unfortunately, the offense once again struggled to find its footing, and a seemingly endless parade of yellow laundry made an already daunting task feel even harder. Let’s take a look at the good, bad, and ugly from Miami’s Week 9 loss to Detroit. GOOD Miami’s defense gives high-flying Lions offense fits If there was one reason for Dolphins fans to feel good about Sunday’s performance, it was the team’s defensive effort against one of the NFL’s most dangerous offenses. Detroit came into this matchup with an offense capable of putting a lot of points on the board in a hurry. With Jared Goff under center and weapons like Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, and Jahmyr Gibbs at their disposal, the Lions have enough firepower to make even good defenses look silly. The Dolphins held the Lions to just 19 points — tied for Detroit’s lowest point total in a single game this season —limiting Goff to 170 passing yards, and keeping the Lions out of the end zone for nearly three quarters. Goff finished 17 of 25 with no touchdown passes and an interception. Detroit’s only touchdown came on an eight-yard Jahmyr Gibbs run late in the third quarter. Outside of that, the Lions were forced to rely on Jake Bates, who connected on four field goals. Miami’s pass rush was on point against the Lions. They managed to sack Goff three times, with Joshua Uche, Zeek Biggers, and Jacob Rodriguez contributing to the damage. The secondary deserves some recognition too. Rookie cornerback Chris Johnson came up with an interception in the first quarter, returning it 21 yards and giving Miami an opportunity to take control of the game. It was his first interception as a professional. Holding an offense with this much talent to just one touchdown is no small accomplishment. Unfortunately, the Dolphins’ offense decided that playing complementary football wasn’t on the docket for the day. BAD Miami’s offense doesn’t take advantage of juicy matchup The Dolphins managed just nine points against a poor Lions defense on Sunday. Malik Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards, threw an interception, and finished with a disappointing 50.1 passer rating against a team allowing 276.6 passing yards per game heading into Sunday — worst in the NFL. Miami also failed to move the ball well on the ground — finishing with just 77 rushing yards on 21 carries. Miami went 4 for 12 on third downs and failed to score a touchdown on all three of their trips to the red zone. When you can’t convert third downs, can’t consistently run the football, and can’t finish drives inside the 20, you’re going to have a difficult time winning football games. Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas provided one of the few bright spots on offense, hauling in six receptions for 70 yards — but even he had a key drop on a late game fourth down play. However, the Dolphins’ best offensive highlight might have actually come from punter Bradley Pinion, who completed a 46-yard pass to rookie Kaytron Allen on a fake punt in the fourth quarter. Perhaps offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik should consider giving Pinion a few more snaps. I kid. I think… UGLY Penalties piled up for Dolphins against Lions Eleven penalties for 87 yards. That’s what Miami had against Detroit on Sunday. That’s an entire afternoon of self-inflicted wounds, and several of them came at particularly costly moments. Miami’s offensive penalties were especially frustrating because they repeatedly erased positive plays and put the offense behind the chains. One of the more damaging examples came immediately after Chris Johnson intercepted Goff in the first quarter. Miami had just received a gift from its defense and had an opportunity to turn that takeaway into points. Instead, the offense was immediately pushed backward by a holding call. Another holding penalty wiped out a long bomb from Willis to rookie Kevin Coleman Jr., taking away a much-needed explosive play and forcing Miami to move backwards. By halftime, Miami had already been penalized seven times! The Dolphins’ 11 penalties included five holding calls. When your offense is already struggling to generate yards and sustain drives, repeatedly moving backward because of penalties is a recipe for disaster. It’s difficult enough to beat a team like Detroit when everything is going right. Asking an offense that can’t consistently move the football to overcome penalty after penalty is an entirely different challenge. The Dolphins didn’t need any additional help making life difficult for themselves. Unfortunately, they provided plenty. ___ The Dolphins played tough on defense, but fell flat on offense against Detroit. The loss drops the team’s record to 1-7 on the year. Do you think they can get back on the right side of the scoreboard with a victory against the struggling Indianapolis Colts next week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .

title: Miami Dolphins news: Rebuild working, Lions game review, trade deadline updates
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost their seventh game of the 2026 season, having won just once this year. It has been a rough season according to the record, and we all know you are what your record says you are, but in the Dolphins case this year, they may be a little more than that 1-7 […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins cornerback Chris Johnson (3) runs with the ball after an interception as Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki (33) pursues during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Miami Dolphins lost their seventh game of the 2026 season, having won just once this year. It has been a rough season according to the record, and we all know you are what your record says you are, but in the Dolphins case this year, they may be a little more than that 1-7 record. The Dolphins are a rebuilding team, and this year’s losses are understandable for a team that completely tore down its roster and is relying heavily on rookies and other younger players to build a foundation for the future. The 2026 season is not the goal for the Dolphins’ front office and coaching staff. They are more concerned about making Miami a consistent threat year after year in the AFC playoffs, rather than making a one-year splash. The Dolphins are playing a physical style of football this season. They have matched up with some of the league’s top teams. They are also seeing flashes of potential from younger players who may promise a brighter future. The rebuild seems to be working. The Palm Beach Post’s Joe Schad agrees that, despite a 1-7 record, the Dolphins are proving on the field that the rebuild is working: “A lot of stuff that we started off the year doing, we’re not doing anymore,” [quarterback Malik] Willis said [after Sunday’s game]. Miami has the youngest team in the NFL and at times, it shows. But on this day, first-round cornerback Chris Johnson had his first career interception and second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez had his first career sack… The Dolphins have not quit and that’s way more important than their record. Miami is 1-7 and yet the Dolphins are optimistic. Fans should be, too. The Splash Zone returns this morning to collect all the latest news, updates, and rumors in one place for you. title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Miami Dolphins rumors, updates, and moves
summary: The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. Eastern. While the NFL has lagged behind some other major sports leagues in moves made ahead of the trade deadline, we have seen an increase in deals in recent years. This year, we could see the trend continue, with many rumors already swirling and several teams […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks (20) looks on after the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. Eastern. While the NFL has lagged behind some other major sports leagues in moves made ahead of the trade deadline, we have seen an increase in deals in recent years. This year, we could see the trend continue, with many rumors already swirling and several teams expected to be sellers over the next couple of days. The Miami Dolphins may be one of those teams that sell this year. After a Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Miami fell to 1-7 as it works through the first season of a complete roster rebuild. The Miami front office will be tempted to add draft picks, but who could they trade to create additional selections? We will track all of the rumors, updates, and moves Miami makes over the next few days right here. Will the Dolphins be sellers? Miami could be sellers for many reasons this week, especially given their 1-7 record. The Dolphins tore their roster down to the studs this past offseason, taking on a record $188.8 million in dead money to set themselves up for future success. Continuing to move on from veterans, who might be able to help a team in “win-now” mode while providing Miami with additional draft picks makes sense for both sides. But Miami may be in a position where they aren’t interested in most trade offers. The roster teardown has left the team with few proven veterans who can serve as leaders and role models for younger players. The Dolphins may be content with the players they have, keeping them through the rest of the season and into 2027. No trade can ever be ruled out, but if the Dolphins plan to keep their veterans, they may be in a position to ask for huge draft packages in return for any trades. They can tell other teams that they either meet Miami’s asking price, or the Dolphins will be happy to keep their players. It seems like a good situation for a rebuilding franchise. Possible Dolphins trade bait Miami does have some veterans who might draw interest heading into the deadline: Jordyn Brooks, linebacker Brooks might be the biggest name among the Dolphins rumors swirling around. The veteran linebacker has averaged 163 tackles over his two seasons in Miami and he already has 63 tackles this season. He was selected as a First-Team All-Pro last year and can immediately come in and provide stabilization to a defense if he were to move. The Dolphins, however, identified Brooks as one of the pillars around which the team would be built. They signed him to a contract extension over the summer and seem to like the combination of Brooks and rookie middle linebacker Jacob Rodriguez as the defense’s foundation. Sunday’s opponent, the Detroit Lions, have to be interested in Brooks as a replacement for the injured Jack Campbell. Would they be willing to pay a high premium for the linebacker? Teams that might be interested: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Pittsburgh Steelers Zach Sieler, defensive tackle Sieler has become such a fixture in the middle of the Dolphins’ defensive line that it is hard to imagine him somewhere else. Miami has multiple younger defensive tackles who could fill in if a trade happens, with 2025 draft picks Kenneth Grant, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers all making an impact when they are on the field. It could make Sieler someone the front office would consider moving for the right price. They still have to weigh the costs and benefits of any offer, though. Sieler is a defensive captain who always seems to make a play when the defense needs it; he brings strong leadership to the team. He has also publicly said he wants to stay in Miami, which could be a consideration if the front office wants to prove they are taking care of their own players – if Sieler wanted to make a move to a contender, it could be understandable, but that he wants to stay and work through the rebuild in Miami could be a good example for the team. Teams that might be interested: Jacksonville Jaguars, Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers Austin Jackson, tackle Jackson might be the most likely player to be traded this year if Miami makes any deal. The right tackle has struggled to stay healthy throughout his career and, after a solid start in the NFL, injuries seem to have caught up with him. He has struggled this year, especially when left on an island, and the team may have already decided he is not part of their 2027 plans. He is in the final year of his contract and will be a free agent after the season. The Dolphins could look to the draft or free agency to add a right tackle, or move rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor to right tackle next year. Proctor has played really well inside, so leaving him there for his career might be a great option, but Miami’s options are the key part of that discussion. Moving Jackson could land the Dolphins an additional draft pick from a player they expect to leave in free agency anyway. Teams that might be interested: Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers Josh Uche, edge Uche could be a factor in the trade talks, especially after his performance against the Lions on Sunday. The 2026 free agent addition signed a one-year deal, and Miami might see the opportunity to turn that signing into a 2027 draft pick. Like Sieler, Uche has said he wants to stay in Miami and be a part of the rebuild, with his belief in head coach Jeff Hafley factoring into that desire. Teams that might be interested: New England Patriots, Philadelphia Eagles, Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys Dolphins trade rumors We will update with the latest rumors starting Sunday evening. Dolphins trades We will update with any confirmed trades the Dolphins make. Does Zach Sieler want to be traded away from Miami Dolphins? title: Lions vs. Dolphins final score, immediate winners, losers, reactions
summary: The Miami Dolphins’ Week 9 schedule brought the NFL’s top-ranked offense to Hard Rock Stadium as the Detroit Lions came to South Florida. It was a tough matchup for a 1-6 team still trying to grow and develop with a roster full of rookies, but the Dolphins stood up and fought for all 60 minutes. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions scrambles with the ball against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ Week 9 schedule brought the NFL’s top-ranked offense to Hard Rock Stadium as the Detroit Lions came to South Florida. It was a tough matchup for a 1-6 team still trying to grow and develop with a roster full of rookies, but the Dolphins stood up and fought for all 60 minutes. Detroit put the game away late, but with the over/under set at 50.5 points for the day, a combined 28-point total reflects strong defensive play from both teams. Final Score Lions 19 – 9 Dolphins Immediate Reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Jeff Hafley, head coach The Dolphins defense showed up to play in this game. Hafley, the former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator, clearly brought that experience to Miami and used it against the Lions today. The defense was ready to face the number one offense in the league and they did well for much of the game. They allowed one touchdown drive in the second half with a couple of big plays, but for the most part, Hafley’s defense was ready and executed well. Chop Robinson, edge Early in the season, frustration over Robinson’s lack of production was growing. Over the past few weeks, he put that behind him, and on Sunday, he was a force throughout the game. Josh Uche, edge Continuing with the defensive theme, Uche was disruptive throughout the game as well. Uche set the tone early, disrupting the run, setting the edge, deflecting the pass that led to a Chris Johnson interception. and getting a sack. He was a factor in the game, even if things fell off a little in the second half. Caleb Douglas, wide receiver Douglas dropped a late fourth-down attempt that would have given Miami a first down as they tried to come back, but aside from that, the rookie receiver had a day. He finished the game with six receptions for 70 yards. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred Bradley Pinion, punter The Dolphins’ punter has struggled this year, especially in terms of consistency. Also serving as the kickoff specialist, Pinion was flagged on the opening kickoff for failing to get the ball into the landing zone. In the second quarter, he shanked a punt for just 25 yards. It was not a banner day for the Dolphins’ punter. Pinion did have a 46-yard pass to running back Kaytron Allen on a fake punt, which nearly pushed him off this list, but the season-long inconsistency keeps him here. Penalties So many flags were thrown against the Dolphins this week, especially against the offensive line. Counting declined penalties, Miami was flagged 12 times in the game. It feels more like a rookies trying too hard more than an issue of players not paying attention. Chris Bell, wide receiver Rookie receiver Chris Bell was just non-existent on Sunday. He was targeted one time and recorded no receptions. While Douglas continues to break out, Bell is struggling to produce. The potential is still there, and he will break out at some point, but right now, he is a complete afterthought for the offense. Other thoughts Dan Campbell comes home and brings others with him Lions head coach Dan Campbell’s first coaching job was with the Dolphins, starting as an intern, then as the tight ends coach, and ending as the team’s interim head coach after Joe Philbin was fired. Campbell showed flashes of what he would become as a head coach, but he was not yet ready to get the job full time. There was definitely temptation there. Campbell instead went to the New Orleans Saints as their tight ends and assistant head coach. Campbell moved to the Lions in 2021 and has worked therm through a rebuild into a team that should be a contender for a deep run in the NFC playoffs. After Campbell’s interim stint, Miami hired Adam Gase, then Brian Flores, then Mike McDaniel, and now Jeff Hafley. The Lions coaching staff also includes defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers, and outside linebackers coach David Carrao – all of whom were Dolphins players or coaches. Just a quick look at the Lions coaching staff including HC Dan Campbell, DC Kelvin Sheppard, d-line coach Kacy Rodgers, and OLB coach David Carrao. pic.twitter.com/T2jsF5VMoY — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) November 8, 2026 Malik Willis’s groin injury a factor Willis is clearly bothered by the groin injury that has been on the injury report for the last couple of weeks. He just doesn’t have the same mobility we have seen from him before. He tried a couple of times to run away from pressure, but he just didn’t have the speed to get going. He showed solid understanding of the situation and threw the ball away at times, but the lack of scrambling ability was very noticeable in the game. Teams continue to forget to be special Pinion’s struggles (and the fake punt) were mentioned above, but overall, the Dolphins’ special teams still aren’t special. They gave up a fake punt, Zane Gonzalez blasted the upright on a field goal attempt to end the half, and overall, it feels like Miami cannot trust their special teams this year.

title: Lions vs. Dolphins preview: 5 questions with Pride of Detroit
summary: The Miami Dolphins are about to kick off against the Detroit Lions, but I wanted to make sure I got this preview for the game posted. I also wanted to thank Ryan Matthews from Pride of Detroit for taking the time to answer my questions about the Lions. 1. The Lions have the league’s top […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 16: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions looks on while playing the Miami Dolphins during a NFL Preseason game at Ford Field on August 16, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are about to kick off against the Detroit Lions, but I wanted to make sure I got this preview for the game posted. I also wanted to thank Ryan Matthews from Pride of Detroit for taking the time to answer my questions about the Lions. 1. The Lions have the league’s top offense (395+ yards/game) and third-ranked scoring attack (29 points per game) under new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. What has Petzing introduced compared to past years, and when opposing defenses have gotten Detroit off schedule this season, what worked? Through seven games, a few unique things have stood out about Petzing as an offensive coordinator, but the biggest takeaway is how he’s going back to what made this offense so efficient and productive in 2023 and 2024. One of those callbacks is offensive personnel. Ben Johnson relied heavily on 12 personnel–two tight end sets–utilizing it on 30% of snaps across ’23 and ’24. Under John Morton and Dan Campbell in 2025, the Lions lined up in 12 personnel just 25% of the time, but that was likely influenced by not having enough healthy, NFL-capable tight ends to line up. Without Sam LaPorta or Brock Wright for a good chunk of the season, the offense as a whole suffered. This season, Petzing has that number up to 35.2%, the third-highest rate in the NFL. As a result, the Lions have one of the best run games in the NFL: fifth in success rate (45.0%) and fourth in rush DVOA (9.0%). Elsewhere, Petzing has Jared Goff lining up under center 53.4% of the time (second in NFL) and utilizing play-action passes 34.6% of the time (third in NFL). Goff is at his best when he can use deception to create more time to deliver throws across the middle of the field, and Petzing is accommodating. However, when Detroit’s offense gets off schedule, it’s been tough sledding. No matter if it was Johnson or Petzing, that’s usually been the case. Goff doesn’t bring that ability to extend plays with his athleticism, so if Detroit is facing a third-and-10+, there’s usually a screen play, or a delayed handoff to try and catch the defense napping. If so, they have Dan Campbell ready to go for it on fourth down. 2. On the other side of the ball, the Lions rank 29th in total defense, allowing over 373 yards per game, but they are stuffing the run as a top-ten unit, giving up just 96.6 yards per game. What is making this front seven so stout against the run, and are there specific rushing schemes or alignments where opponents have found creases? It all starts up front with Detroit’s defensive line. Even though the individual statistics don’t paint players like Tyleik Williams and Alim McNeill as difference makers in the middle of their defensive front, they’re doing the dirty work: taking on multiple blockers, holding their ground in gaps to disrupt run plays and provide opportunities for the guys behind them to do their jobs. Unfortunately, Jack Campbell, one of their ultra-reliable linebackers, remains hospitalized after a serious neck injury suffered last week against Minnesota. He leads the team in run defense stops (10) per Pro Football Focus, but there’s just no way to quantify how much Detroit will miss his presence as a leader and communicator in the middle of their defense. Derrick Barnes–the team’s SAM linebacker–and Malcolm Rodriguez–often lining up as the WILL–could be next in line to take over the green dot duties for Campbell as the MIKE linebacker. Both are solid in run defense, but can be inconsistent in coverage, so there might be some opportunities for the Dolphins to work the middle immediate areas of the field in the passing game. 3. The Lions’ secondary has given up plenty of yards this year, ranking 32nd by allowing 276.6 yards per game. They are currently dealing with major injuries, including star safety Brian Branch entering concussion protocol. However, Miami’s passing attack looks entirely different now, relying on Malik Willis and a young, revamped receiving corps led by rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. How do you see defensive coordinator (and former Dolphins linebacker) Kelvin Sheppard game-planning for this specific matchup—will he test Miami’s inexperienced wideouts with aggressive coverage, or play conservatively to limit big plays? Detroit often sticks in base personnel (43.7%, fifth in NFL) and plays with a heavy box (28.9%, eighth in NFL), and with some of the question marks in regards to player availability in the secondary, it’s going to be very interesting to see how Kelvin Sheppard adjusts. Not only is Brian Branch working his way through concussion protocol, but D.J. Reed, the team’s top cornerback, is dealing with a hip injury that’s kept him out of practice so far this week. From the sound of things, Reed is going to miss this game, so Sheppard will have to rely heavily on their depth at outside corner, a position that’s been in flux basically all season long. Realistically, he could turn to any number of players. Could be veteran Rock Ya-Sin, could be Ennis Rakestraw, could be Khalil Dorsey–someone who primarily plays special teams. Roger McCreary has settled into the slot cornerback role for the Lions, but they’ve also pushed him outside when injuries have necessitated shuffling. It wouldn’t surprise me to see Sheppard stick to his game plan and expect the reserves to carry it out. His approach to sending extra defenders has varied week to week– Week 2’s game against Buffalo saw Detroit blitz on 47.4% of snaps–but since then, he’s dialed back his aggressiveness, blitzing on just 16.2% of snaps, the lowest blitz rate in NFL over the last six weeks. The Lions have worked through some of their early-season missed assignments and breakdowns in coverage, opting to play more man (33.3% in Weeks 5-8, fourth in the NFL over that span) to pair with their ability to get after the quarterback effectively by sending just four pass rushers. Given Malik Willis’ ability to use his legs, there’s a good chance Sheppard stays in that base defense and has his defensive front maintain gap integrity to limit Willis’ escapability. 4. Dolphins fans do not see the Lions very often; Sunday’s game is just the 14th meeting between the two teams. Several familiar faces from the 2022 game remain in Detroit, but the roster also includes many new players. Who is an offensive player Dolphins fans may not know but should watch on Sunday? A defensive player? On offense, one name to keep an eye on is backup running back Sione Vaki. Drafted in 2024, Vaki was primarily a safety for the Utah Utes, but Detroit saw enough in his limited opportunities as a runner to transition him to a full-time running back. Vaki’s defensive chops earned him an early opportunity to contribute on special teams where he became a four-core special teamer. Reps at running back were in short supply when you consider the backfied consisted of David Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs his first two seasons. A freak injury in training camp, where Vaki broke his nose, prevented him from getting valuable experience as the team’s RB2, but against Minnesota last week, Vaki earned the trust of the coaching staff. His role on third down as a pass-protector, combined with his hard-nosed, north-and-south running style–11 carries for 65 yards, both career highs–will surely have him taking his fair share of snaps on offense this Sunday. For defense, keep an eye on fifth-round rookie cornerback turned safety Keith Abney. Detroit has primarily used him at deep safety after the rocky start to the year for the safety group, but they could end up returning him to cornerback for this game considering how shorthanded the team is due to injuries. He could spell McCreary in the slot, or he could be pushed into the team’s CB2 role…

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Camryn Bynum #24 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates as Patrick Peterson #7 of the Minnesota Vikings slides after getting a game winning interception in overtime against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills enter the game leading the NFL in both total offense and scoring. They surprisingly have the 2nd best run game in the league. The Bills are 2nd only to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with 148.4 yards per game on the ground. However, James Cook has had some fumble problems and the Bills are a -2 in the turnover margin for the year. The Vikings will need to take advantage if the Bills put the ball in harm’s way. Series Record: 9-6 Home Record: 4-2 Streak: W1 Largest Victory: 38-14, December 5, 2010 Largest Defeat: 27-6, September 23, 2018 Adrian Peterson will be inducted in the Vikings’ Ring of Honor during halftime. This is the first time since 2013 that a team averaging 33+ points a game has faced a team allowing less than 14 points this late in the season. Josh Allen’s first NFL victory was also the largets Buffalo Bills victory against the Vikings in September 2018, a 27-6 drubbing. Josh Allen is 2nd in the NFL with 9 rushing TDs, trailing only D’Andrea Swift, who has played two more games. There seems to be some belief out there that the Vikings will be able to keep this game close. The only way I see that happening is if they force turnovers. The Bills have put the ball on the ground this season, and the Vikings will need to capitalize if they get those opportunities. The Vikings will need more than a few tonight against the Bills. They will also need to provide short fields for this struggling offense. I am not a believer in Wentz (or Murray) at this point. If the team can pull it off, I expect the chants for Wentz to echo loudly through the night. I’m not expecting that to happen. Bills 20 – Vikings 12

title: Ben Brown injury forces Patriots to once again adjust their O-line
summary: While wide receiver A.J. Brown might be making the trip to Germany this week alongside the rest of the New England Patriots, another member of the team’s starting lineup will not be available for the upcoming game against the Detroit Lions. Guard Ben Brown, who exited Sunday’s loss to the Green Bay Packers with a […]
full_text: While wide receiver A.J. Brown might be making the trip to Germany this week alongside the rest of the New England Patriots, another member of the team’s starting lineup will not be available for the upcoming game against the Detroit Lions. Guard Ben Brown, who exited Sunday’s loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury, will be out this week. Head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed his status during a press conference on Monday. “He won’t make it this week,” Vrabel told reporters from the Gillette Stadium podium. Starting the Packers game at left guard, Brown remained down after suffering a knee injury late in the second quarter. He departed for the blue medial tent on the sideline and later the locker room, and was initially announced as questionable to return. However, he never made his back onto the field. In Brown’s place, Walter Rouse finished the game at left guard. Based on the personnel available, Rouse is also likely to draw the start against the Lions. That said, Vrabel did not rule out the possibility of his team activating fellow interior lineman Greg Van Roten from injured reserve in the coming days. “That’s something that we’ll look at,” Vrabel said. “He’s eligible and has been working hard to get back. So, we’ll take a look at that and see where he is tomorrow or Wednesday when we practice.” The Patriots entered the 2026 regular season with Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu as their starting guard. However, Onwenu was lost to an achilles fracture in Week 2, followed by his backup Van Roten going down with a thigh injury just one week later. Brown was the next man up at that point, but he himself was hurt in Week 6 against the New York Jets — the same game that saw Vera-Tucker go down as well. Unless Van Roten is indeed activated and reinserted into the lineup, the Patriots are looking at Rouse and Matt Pryor starting at left and right guard, respectively, against the Lions in Week 10.
