title: A.J. Brown could travel with Patriots to Germany ahead of Week 10
summary: The New England Patriots are leaving the door open for wide receiver A.J. Brown to return in Week 10. Head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday morning that while no final decision has been made on Brown’s availability, the current plan is for the veteran receiver to travel with the team to Germany on Wednesday. “I […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots are leaving the door open for wide receiver A.J. Brown to return in Week 10. Head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday morning that while no final decision has been made on Brown’s availability, the current plan is for the veteran receiver to travel with the team to Germany on Wednesday. “I mean I think that that’s the plan,” Vrabel said. “I mean, certainly we want to — we haven’t — there’s no decision on that, but I would imagine that that’s the plan and try to work to continue to get guys back that can get back and be healthy and help the football team. That’s the goal. So, to be able to answer that right now, today, I can’t do that with a few guys, but I know that that’s the plan is to try to get everybody that can help us to get on the plane on Wednesday and go over there and help us win.” The Patriots will practice in Foxboro on Wednesday before departing for Germany that evening. Once in Munich, New England is scheduled to hold a walkthrough Thursday before ramping up to a full practice Friday. Brown’s potential return would provide a significant boost to a Patriots offense that has struggled to keep its receiving corps healthy. Acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles in June in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round selection, Brown has appeared in just three of New England’s nine games this season. The 29-year old suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 before returning for Weeks 6 and 7. However, a previous knee injury flared up ahead of Week 8, forcing him to miss the Patriots’ last two games. Through three appearances, Brown has recorded just nine receptions on 20 targets for 101 yards and no touchdowns. Without Brown, the Patriots wide receiver room features just DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Kyle Williams, and Mack Hollins, who returned from injured reserve himself this past week. The Patriots are set to take on the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday with kickoff at 9:30 a.m. ET. New England will then be off on their bye week.

title: Patriots vs. Packers: Fan observations from Week 9
summary: Brady and Gronk were back in the building, capping off what was supposed to be an awesome weekend of celebrating all-time great Patriots players… and then this happened. This was the kind of loss that has you heading for the exits before Gillette Stadium stops selling booze. Just a complete disaster from start to finish […]
full_text: Brady and Gronk were back in the building, capping off what was supposed to be an awesome weekend of celebrating all-time great Patriots players… and then this happened. This was the kind of loss that has you heading for the exits before Gillette Stadium stops selling booze. Just a complete disaster from start to finish that has you wanting to put the game behind you as quickly as possible. At the end of the day, there are two ways you can look at this loss. I suppose you could dip into the old glass half empty vs. half full adage, but I think more than anything it’s more what your relationship to this team is. The first way to see this game is that the Patriots just kind of laid an egg. They weren’t prepared, they got thoroughly outplayed and outcoached, and made zero adjustments. Guys looked lost out there, and there wasn’t any fire to this team. Drake Maye didn’t play well and the defense had its worst outing of the season. That happens sometimes, and when it happens against a good team as opposed to a mediocre-to-bad one, the result is a complete blowout. The other way to see this game is that it’s indicative of where the 2026 Patriots are in the NFL as a whole, which is a decent team very far behind the real contenders. In a season in which the NFC is running circles around the AFC in terms of talent and team strength, the Pats just aren’t in the category of serious contenders. They can only go as far as Drake Maye will take them, and when Maye isn’t at his best, everything falls apart. They can still go 10-7 and make the playoffs, but not having to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl this year might be a blessing. I know that this team is all kinds of banged up. I know that they have very little top-tier talent on the field for the offense right now. But injuries alone aren’t responsible for what we all had to see yesterday. On the plus side, most of us missed the only parts of the game where the Patriots were still in it courtesy of some amazing bonus coverage of Colts vs. Cowboys. If there’s one thing Boston sports fans would rather see than their favorite team, it’s a Colts-Cowboys game. I’d make some comment about how paying an obscene amount of money for NFL Sunday Ticket should mean that you’d have the chance to watch whatever game you wanted in case a game went to OT and there was some kind of contractual obligation to keep showing it, but that would also mean that the NFL would have to show even the slightest bit of common sense or concern about the happiness of the fans. And since that isn’t ever going to happen, I’ll just move on. The plus side of this game being pretty much over before most fans at the game made their way through the beer line is that it doesn’t sit with you very long. I reached the acceptance part of the grieving process by halftime and got right on with my day. And yes, I know that the Patriots were only down 10 at the half, through some combination of miracles. But anyone who thought that Green Bay wasn’t going to march right down the field and score on the first possession of the third quarter represents the smart folks who weren’t really paying attention. You have to give the Packers credit, as they found a great way to exploit New England’s defensive weakness. They opted to target an all-pro shutdown corner currently playing on one of the largest contracts in the NFL. Sheer genius. Christian Gonzalez not only had his worst game as a pro yesterday, but he is the first DB in almost 10 years to give up 80-plus yards to two different receivers. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson netted a combined 10 receptions for 187 yards yesterday. That would have represented a pretty decent day for Year 2 Mac Jones during his tenure here. And Gonzalez also had trouble tackling. And staying upright. And looking even remotely interested in being there. As soon as I got into college, I didn’t do a single lick of work for the second semester of my senior year of high school. Didn’t see much point in it, as I already had what I wanted. So I have a unique perspective on people who have what they need and are just kind of playing out the string going forward. And while I won’t go so far as to say that Gonzo has checked out on the game of football now that he has his bag, I certainly don’t see him playing with the same intensity as he had last year. As a man who will never pass up the opportunity to slack off on the job, I highly respect the move… but as a fan of a team that wants to see players try their hardest, I’m not overly happy. Again, I don’t think Gonzalez is a bust or anything like that. He had a bad game, and he’s allowed. But I have sensed a marked lack of urgency in his coverages across several games now and it’s worth noting. At the same time, outside of Elijah Ponder, pretty much nobody on the defense showed up yesterday. And this unit is more or less healthy. 129 yards on the ground, 372 yards through the air. Surrendered four scoring drives of 70 yards or more. Forced two three-and-outs. Just a dud all around. Should I even bother talking about the offense? I mean there were some moments. There were some nice throws. And the game was within 10 at one point, even though I never once thought that the Patriots were going to dig themselves out of the early hole. So I don’t know if I should even bother breaking down any individual plays. People seem to be either very down on Drake Maye today or looking to absolve him of all blame, when (as with most things) the truth lies somewhere in the middle. I’ve already said that this team will go as far as he can take them. And the only entity working so hard to hold it all together right now is my belt. But he’s still making completely horrendous decisions and trying to do too much with too little. We all know that not all interceptions are created equal, and the ones he has been committing can be picked up at any Dollar Store. He’s still a young kid. He’s still growing into the game. And I still have faith in him. I just wish there wasn’t so many massive swings in both directions. 2026 Drake Maye is the city of New Haven, CT; you walk past some of the most beautiful architecture you’ll ever see as you admire the ivy-clad walls of one of the world’s finest universities, but then you make a left at the next block and the odds of you getting out alive just dropped by 75%. Do I think that the Patriots are going to be OK? Honestly, yes I do. I think they can get over this loss and bounce back. I don’t know if it’s going to be some kind of 2014 Kansas City moment for them or not, but we’ll find out very soon. They need to put this nonsense behind them and get ready for Detroit. There’s a massive difference between 6-4 and 5-5, particularly with the bye week looming. You don’t want to go into a week off on back-to-back losses. This is still a playoff team. I’d take them over a lot of teams in the AFC. The Bills look strong, but the Patriots beat the Bills in Buffalo. Kansas City might be in a ton of trouble depending on the severity of Mahomes’s injury. The Ravens are done and the Bengals are inconsistent. Denver seems like a team that needs every second of every game to squeak out wins regardless of who they’re playing. So who the hell knows what the second half of the season will bring. Good for the Packers. Better players, better gameplan, better coaching. I know we’re not used to our coaches getting mind-melted by the guy across the sidelines around these parts, but it has happened on a few occasions now. Mike Vrabel is a good coach. He’s not the best coach in the league. Goor coaches with good quarterbacks seem to know how to put one over on him and he doesn’t adjust as well as others. I’ll still take him over most of the other coaches in the league. I told my friends that the Patriots had to win one of these two games with the Packers and Lions in order to really make a strong push into December. I honestly thought that win would come yesterday. Oops. That means they need to…

summary: Even coming out of a blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers and dropping to 5-4 on the year, the New England Patriots are not necessarily in “seller” territory heading toward Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. full_text: Even coming out of a blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers and dropping to 5-4 on the year, the New England Patriots are not necessarily in “seller” territory heading toward Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. That being said, one player has still been mentioned as a potential candidate to be moved over the past few weeks: defensive tackle Christian Barmore. Whether or not a trade will materialize remains to be seen, but Sunday’s game did little to clear the smoke emanating from that particular fire. Barmore, after all, played a season-low 26 of 61 defensive snaps for a playing time share of 39%. While the margin is not significant — he averaged 31 snaps and a 50% share over his first seven games — it, at the very least, creates more data points to fuel speculation over the next 24-plus hours. The other top-level DTs, after all, did not see such a drastic change relative to their normal usage. Milton Williams had a slightly lower playing time share than his season average up to that point, while Cory Durden was on the field a bit more. Does that mean a trade is imminent? No, it doesn’t. Playing time fluctuates based on a variety of factors including opponent, game script and physical fitness. In Barmore’s case, he did have some positive contributions by registering a sack and a stop on a 3rd-and-1 run. Of course, that probably still won’t stop the rumor mill from turning until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 45-27 loss . Offense Total snaps: 63 | Time on the field: 23:11 | * denotes starter C Jared Wilson* (63; 100%), RG Matt Pryor* (63; 100%), QB Drake Maye* (51; 81%), RT Morgan Moses* (51; 81%), WR Kyle Williams* (49; 78%), LT Will Campbell* (45; 71%), WR Mack Hollins* (43; 68%), WR DeMario Douglas (43; 68%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (38; 60%), TE Eli Raridon (36; 57%), WR Efton Chism III (32; 51%), LG Walter Rouse (32; 51%), TE Hunter Henry (31; 49%), LG Ben Brown* (31; 49%), LT/TE Caleb Lomu* (22; 35%), RB Lan Larison (14; 22%), TE Tanner Arkin* (14; 22%), QB Tommy DeVito (12; 19%), RT Marcus Bryant (12; 19%), RB Corey Kiner (11; 17%) The Patriots offense suffered even more injury losses against the Packers, with the most prominent being running back Rhamondre Stevenson departing in the fourth quarter — in what was effectively garbage time already — with a knee injury. With RB2 TreVeyon Henderson already out due to an illness, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are next on the depth chart and likely to see increased opportunities should Stevenson show any signs of limitations heading into Week 10. Injuries also hit the offensive line once again. Left guard Ben Brown hurt his knee late in the second quarter and was unable to continue, with Walter Rouse entering the game in his place. Early in fourth quarter, left tackle Will Campbell also exited with a knee issue, even though he could have reentered the contest, per himself. Campbell’s departure also gave insight into the Patriots’ backup offensive line hierarchy with Marcus Bryant activated off of injured reserve. Caleb Lomu is the next man up at left tackle, and likely also on the right side; Bryant, meanwhile, is the No. 4 who only entered late when RT Morgan Moses was pulled alongside Drake Maye. Speaking of players coming off of injured reserve, Mack Hollins started and played 68% of snaps in his first game back since Week 4. He was part of a four-receiver rotation that also heavily involved second-year man Kyle Williams, who played 78% as a de facto replacement for top perimeter option A.J. Brown. Williams was targeted two times, with one of those targets a dropped could-be touchdown and the other an interception. At tight end, Hunter Henry played a limited role after participating in only one practice this week. Rookie Eli Raridon out-snapped him 36 to 31, with Tanner Arkin also playing 14 snaps. title: Will Campbell injury update: Patriots OT shares positive news after Packers game
summary: Injuries have been one of the defining stories of the New England Patriots’ season so far, and Sunday’s loss to the Green Bay Packers was no exception. Multiple players were unable to finish the contest, including offensive tackle Will Campbell. The Patriots’ starting left tackle departed in the early fourth quarter for the blue medical […]
full_text: Injuries have been one of the defining stories of the New England Patriots’ season so far, and Sunday’s loss to the Green Bay Packers was no exception. Multiple players were unable to finish the contest, including offensive tackle Will Campbell. The Patriots’ starting left tackle departed in the early fourth quarter for the blue medical tent, and was later announced as questionable to return with a knee injury. He never actually reentered the 45-27 defeat. Afterwards, however, he gave the all-clear. “I’m good,” he told reporters at his locker. Campbell added that he had his leg whipped but actually would have went back in had the Patriots not been down by 24 points with around 10 minutes left in the game. For a New England team that also lost left guard Ben Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson to knee injuries during the game, Campbell’s announcement is a positive. That is especially true given that he had to deal with medical issues since his arrival as a first-round draft pick in 2025, including spraining his knee in a Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this year. In Campbell’s absence, the Patriots inserted first-round rookie Caleb Lomu into the lineup. Lomu ended up playing the final 18 snaps against the Packers at left tackle, with fellow backup Marcus Bryant eventually relieving right-side starter Morgan Moses later in the game. The Patriots will play the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, this Sunday. They will hold their first practice of the week inside Gillette Stadium on Wednesday, before taking the flight across the Atlantic.

title: Drake Maye reverts to early-season self in loss to Packers
summary: Drake Maye was announced as AFC Offensive Player of October last Wednesday, an honor reflective of his impressive turnaround. After struggling mightily over the first three weeks of the season, the New England Patriots quarterback rebounded nicely to take home the accolade. Four days later, the very same early-season Drake Maye made his return. He […]
full_text: Drake Maye was announced as AFC Offensive Player of October last Wednesday, an honor reflective of his impressive turnaround. After struggling mightily over the first three weeks of the season, the New England Patriots quarterback rebounded nicely to take home the accolade. Four days later, the very same early-season Drake Maye made his return. He helped set the stage for the Patriots getting blown out at the hands of the Green Bay Packers. Maye turned the ball over three times during the 45-27 defeat , tossing a trio of interceptions in the first half that contributed to his team finding itself in an early hole it failed to get out of. And while the second-year passer did have some promising moments as well, those were once again overshadowed by his ball-security concerns. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s starting with me,” Maye said during his post-game presser at Gillette Stadium. “It’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games. I put our defense in a bad spot on the first drive, just gave them the football, had some other chances down the field, and have to see in front.” Sunday’s loss to the Packers was Maye’s second three-interception game of the season, making him the only player in the league with multiple such games on his record. On the year, Maye has now thrown 11 picks — tied with the Chargers’ Justin Herbert for most in the NFL. The first of his picks versus Green Bay already set the tone for the rest of the day. On his first pass attempt, Maye maneuvered a muddy pocket and lifted a floater across the body intended for wide receiver Mack Hollins. Instead of hitting his target, however, the ball landed in the waiting arms of safety Xavier McKinney. McKinney returned the interception 36 yards to set his offense up at the New England 9. Two players later the Packers took a 7-0 lead that continued to grow with the offense unable to find its rhythm. Even when it did, Maye’s interceptions quickly halted any progress. He threw a second pick early in the second period, on a play reminiscent of his first interception of the year. Just like in Week 1, when he was targeting Romeo Doubs deep down the left sideline, he attempted to connect with Kyle Williams only to see the pass broken up and intercepted on the deflection. Two possessions later, after the Patriots had decreased their deficit to 17-7 with a 30-yard touchdown pass from Maye to Rhamondre Stevenson, McKinney registered another pick when he undercut a throw intended for Eli Raridon. “Just throwing the football in spots that I don’t think I should have thrown it,” said Maye about his three INTs. “The first one, I think I just got to see the guys deep, see the safety positions. The second one happens, maybe throw it a little farther. And the third one, they’re jumping cross routes, so I got to see in front.” Besides preventing three Patriots scoring opportunities, the interceptions also directly set up two Packers touchdowns. As a consequence, they were able to build a 24-7 advantage at one point. New England later turned the ball over a fourth time when Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble in the third quarter. The Patriots themselves registered no takeaways and are therefore now -11 on the year — tied for the league’s worst turnover differential through nine weeks. “When you’re playing a good football team, and when you turn the ball over like we did and give them plus field position, obviously it just wasn’t good enough,” said tight end Hunter Henry. “We’ve got to find a way to play a clean game offensively and not give them chances. It’s continued to bite us against the better teams that we play, and they’re going to take full advantage of that.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Packers
summary: The New England Patriots have already surpassed their 2025 loss total, getting beaten for a fourth time this year on Sunday by the Green Bay Packers. And it was a thorough beating as well with the team struggling to hold onto the football and prevent the big passing play. The end result was a 45-27 […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have already surpassed their 2025 loss total, getting beaten for a fourth time this year on Sunday by the Green Bay Packers. And it was a thorough beating as well with the team struggling to hold onto the football and prevent the big passing play. The end result was a 45-27 blowout loss at Gillette Stadium . Let’s see what the game taught us about the Patriots. Maybe they just aren’t good enough Look, we all want the Patriots to get back to the Super Bowl this year, and we hope that they are good enough to do that. The problem is, they have gone up against who I would consider the cream of the crop of the NFL in five games so far this season, and came away on the losing end four times, including two blowouts. I’m not saying that the Patriots won’t be a fringe playoff team, and I’m also not saying that they’re bad. But when all is said and done, they just might not be very good either. Yes, they are missing a lot of players, but at a certain point you just need to be able to win games, and they have not been able to do that against quality competition this year, outside of the Bills game in Week 4. There is still time for them to turn things around, but there should be real concern that they are simply not good enough throughout their roster to compete with the true contenders in the NFL in their current shape. Turnover woes continue The Patriots are now tied with the Colts for the worst turnover differential in the NFL. They are at -11 for the season after giving the ball away four times and forcing zero takeaways on Sunday. Obviously, this has a lot to do with the offense, as they have yet to have a game where they didn’t turn the ball over, which is unacceptable and a losing recipe. However, the defense has forced only eight turnovers in nine games, which ranks only 25th in the NFL. When you turn it over at a near-constant rate on offense, and you also can’t force turnovers on defense, you’re going to have a hard time winning games. The fact that the Patriots are 5-4 and have yet to win the turnover battle even once this season is therefore kind of incredible and indicative of the type of team and potential they do still have. However, they also have been undisciplined all year long, and the place where that shows up the most is the turnover department. Christian Gonzalez wasn’t worth the price tag on Sunday Christian Gonzalez is one of the best cornerbacks in the league, and the highest-paid. On Sunday, however, he didn’t look the part. He consistently got torched, and it didn’t matter who it was. Matthew Golden torched him, Christian Watson torched him, and the only reason no one else torched him is because he didn’t cover anyone else. When all was said and done, he was credited with 10 catches given up for 187. yards and a touchdown. There won’t be many games like this for the Patriots star, but one is too many for a player earning an average of $33.75 million per year. Drake Maye’s decision-making was puzzling Drake Maye has the potential to be one of the best quarterbacks in the league, and has played like it multiple times this season. He has also made some very questionable decisions, and that’s exactly what happened on Sunday as well. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The first drive of the game ended with him throwing an interception across his body; because he seemingly missed the fact that Mack Hollins had settled into a zone, threw it directly to a defender. Then, after Kyle Williams —we’ll get to him — dropped what should have been an easy touchdown, Maye tried to go back to him, but a bad ball ended in another interception. His third pick might have been his worst. He stared down Eli Raridon which allowed safety Xavier McKinney to read the throw and step in front of it for the interception. Maye can make all the throws, and has sky-high potential, but if he can’t cut down on the turnovers, the Patriots aren’t going anywhere this year. Kyle Williams is not ready for a big role I have defended Kyle Williams this season in part because even though he might be a one-trick pony, he is very good at that one trick. However, when you fail to consistently get open, and then drop touchdown passes when you actually do create some space, you are going to get criticized. Williams was supposed to be the Patriots’ WR5 or WR6 entering the season, and has been thrust into a bigger role because of injuries. His inability to consistently rise up to the occasion in that bigger role is still disappointing. Gabe Jacas needs to do some growing up After a less-than-ideal start to his Patriots career, second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas has been awesome this year. That said, he has had too many pre-snap penalties — and Sunday was more of the same. Twice in against the Packers he line dup offsides, with one of them giving the opponent a first down, and the other turning a manageable 3rd-and-6 into a much more difficult 3rd-and-1. He’s not always going to be a force rushing the passer — he wasn’t on Sunday — but the pre-snap penalties need to stop regardless of his production elsewhere. Mike Vrabel and Co. were thoroughly out-coached At times, the Patriots looked completely unprepared for this game. The Packers, on the other hand, never looked stressed and seemed to have all the answers on both offense and defense. Despite having been up and down this year, they they were a big up on Sunday, and, to me, it all starts with coaching. The Patriots might want to believe that they have a coaching advantage in a lot of matchups, and oftentimes they do. They definitely didn’t have one against Matt LaFleur and company, though. Injuries keep hitting the team Once again, the Patriots are unable to finish a game without multiple starters getting hurt. Ben Brown, Carlton Davis, Rhamondre Stevenson, Brenden Schooler and Will Campbell all left the game and didn’t return. While it will be seen how severe all of those injuries are, the team just keeps losing contributors. They did have a lot of injury luck last year, but they are on the the opposite end of the spectrum in 2026. The NFL season is a war of attrition, and the Patriots are losing that battle this season. More bad officiating We could say this every week, but the refereeing is not on a label worthy of a billion-dollar organization such as the NFL. On the first Drake Maye interception, Maye was clearly blocked in the back; they threw the flag, but then, inexplicably, picked it up. There was a defenseless receiver penalty on Pop Douglas, where, again, they picked up the flag after throwing it. There were other missed calls as well, including the first catch given up by Christian Gonzalez. A trip to Europe awaits The Patriots travel to Germany to face off against the Detroit Lions this coming Sunday. They will fly out on Wednesday, giving them some time to regroup before a game against a decent team. Despite their 6-3 record, the Lions are good but not great, and the Patriots should in theory be able to compete with them. I expect them to bounce back from the loss to the Packers, but whether that is enough to win the game or not, we’ll see.
author: Pat Lane

title: 4 winners and losers from Patriots loss to the Packers
summary: The New England Patriots were largely uncompetitive in a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-4 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 9 contest. Winners N/A Losers CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ top corner was not […]
full_text: The New England Patriots were largely uncompetitive in a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-4 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 9 contest. Winners N/A Losers CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ top corner was not his usual self on Sunday. Gonzalez was on scene for several explosive plays and took fault for a miscommunication that resulted in Matthew Golden’s 5-yard touchdown. Both Golden and Christian Watson posted 80-plus yards with Gonzalez in coverage while he surrendered 187 yards on a career-high 10 receptions in total. New England’s secondary is too talented to be playing at this level in recent weeks, and that begins with Gonzalez. QB Drake Maye: There were positive moments for Maye against Green Bay, but the quarterback ultimately struggled throwing three first-half interceptions that led to an early deficit. Maye’s interceptions came when he pushed the ball down the field, which was a concern entering the week against a zone heavy Packers defense that led the league in takeaways. Offensive line: Behind their fifth different starting combination, the pressure got to Maye early on Sunday. The Packers’ pressure schemes gave New England’s front fits as Maye was sacked four times and was forced into four throwaways. In total, Maye was under pressure on over 50% of his drop backs. RG Matt Pryor was initially charted with four pressures to lead the group. Injuries: As they have all season, the injuries continued to pile up. The Patriots lost CB Carlton Davis (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee), ST Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) in the loss. They did get positive news with starting left tackle Will Campbell, who would have returned in a closer game, but the roster is beaten down ahead of a trip to Germany — which could alter recovery timelines as the team departs Wednesday evening. Honorable mentions DeMario Douglas recorded his second career 100-yard game behind a beautifully-ran 36-yard corner-post route. Mack Hollins finished with three catches and a touchdown in his return. Efton Chism also found the end zone and had five catches. It was a down day for Kyle Williams, who failed to haul in a deep ball and was targeted on Maye’s second interception (which was on the quarterback). Rhamondre Stevenson’s fumble was the Patriots fourth turnover of the day. They now have a -11 turnover differential on the season. Milton Williams flashed throughout the day with three pressures and a TFL in the run game. Rookie cornerback Karon Prunty replaced an injured Carlton Davis at corner. While Prunty had an impressive gunner rep to help down a punt, the Packers immediately picked on him defensively. Packers were 4-of-5 in the red zone. The Patriots kickoff coverage continues to be shaky as they allowed a 48-yard return. Punter Mitch Wishnowsky continues to punt well and recorded four i20s.

title: Saints vs. Browns: Winners and Losers from New Orleans’ thrilling win
summary: The New Orleans Saints found their third win of the season on Sunday, beating the Cleveland Browns en route to taking the lead in the NFC South. The win wasn’t pretty, and there’s plenty to work on, but there is light at the end of the tunnel after New Orleans’ victory out of the bye. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Audric Estimé #30 of the New Orleans Saints rushes for a touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the second half of an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints found their third win of the season on Sunday, beating the Cleveland Browns en route to taking the lead in the NFC South. The win wasn’t pretty, and there’s plenty to work on, but there is light at the end of the tunnel after New Orleans’ victory out of the bye. Winner: RB Audric Estime Just two weeks ago, the Saints running backs ran for 11 rushing yards on 14 attempts. Going into the bye, that was the only conversation surrounding the Saints. They couldn’t run the ball all season, and it was on full display in another country. Coming out of the bye, the Saints lucked out and found a way to bring running back Audric Estime back on waivers. In his first game back with New Orleans, Estime ran for 72 yards on 15 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per carry and scoring a touchdown. While Travis Etienne’s return is on the horizon, Estime has likely found a role with the Saints where he’ll handle the bulk of the carries until he comes back. Winner: DE Carl Granderson Phew. The Saints have a dangerous pass rush combo. We all knew about Chase Young, who has 8 sacks in 8 games this season. But Carl Granderson has feasted off the attention Young brings and has brought his season sack total to 7.5 sacks. In the win against the Browns, Granderson logged 2 sacks and 2 tackles for loss. He was a game changer for the Saints on Sunday, and entered the week with a chip on his shoulder after a viral video of Shedeur Sanders seemingly laughing when asked a question about the Saints’ defense. While Sanders says he wasn’t laughing at the Saints’ defense, it opened the opportunity to add more motivation for the defense, and Granderson himself took it personally. If the former undrafted free agent can continue to play like this, New Orleans will end the season with two of the top three sack leaders. Loser: Saints’ Secondary Sunday’s matchup against the Browns was favored for the Saints secondary, who were facing a second-year quarterback in Sanders. The 2025 fifth-round pick got his first start of the 2026 season and faced the fierce Saints pass rush. The Saints pass rush did their job, but the secondary was outplayed in the biggest moments. From Denzel Boston missing Kool-Aid McKinstry to Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. failing to tackle KC Concepcion after allowing a big catch that turned into a touchdown, we didn’t see the plays we needed from the secondary against Tetairoa McMillan. Loser: The Turnover Battle What stands out the most for me, however, is the Saints’ inability to force takeaways. This was a prime opportunity to force takeaways and come away with a dominant win. New Orleans, however, lost the turnover battle, losing two fumbles and not forcing any turnovers themselves. From Jordyn Tyson’s first reception turning into a fumble three yards from the end zone, to Barion Brown running backwards before losing the ball himself, the Saints are beating themselves. The Saints are -6 on the season in the turnover battle, and it continues to get further away from them.

title: PFF grades and advanced stats for the Giants’ 19-11 victory over the Eagles
summary: The curse of The Linc has finally ended, and while it wasn’t pretty and it wasn’t dominating, it was a win, and a division win, nonetheless. The New York Giants now have about a two in three chance of winning the NFC East Division. That is probably their only avenue to the playoffs since most […]
full_text: Arvell Reese chasing Joe Milton on Sunday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The curse of The Linc has finally ended, and while it wasn’t pretty and it wasn’t dominating, it was a win, and a division win, nonetheless. The New York Giants now have about a two in three chance of winning the NFC East Division. That is probably their only avenue to the playoffs since most teams in the NFC North and NFC West are likely to finish with better records, but the Giants will take whatever they can get. Let’s take a look at Pro Football Focus grades and advanced stats to better understand who played well and who didn’t against the Eagles. PFF grades: Offense Jameis Winston showed why he is the ideal NFL backup quarterback. Pressed into action after J.J. McCarthy’s hip pointer in a game that was hanging in the balance with the Giants behind 8-6, Winston coolly led the Giants to the go-ahead touchdown that turned the game around. He finished 6 of 8 for 71 yards and the TD to Isaiah Likely and was credited with one big-time throw. J.J. McCarthy didn’t play great early on when the Eagles’ defense seemed to be taking away his first reads and they were getting pressure on him, but he came back onto the field and gutted it out after his injury and overall played pretty well, with two big-time throws credited by PFF. The flip side to the good quarterback play was the subpar offensive line play. The pass blocking was not bad. Bryan Hudson continues to play at least adequately at center, though he did surrender one sack. Jon Runyan gave up a hit and two hurries and Sisi Mauigoa a sack and a hurry, which are not terrible results against that tough Eagles interior defensive line. Andrew Thomas got an average pass block grade but only gave up one hurry, while Jermaine Eluemunor had a completely clean stat line and an excellent pass block grade. It’s in the run game that we see the offensive line’s shortcomings. Every starting lineman besides Hudson had a below average run block grade, and Mauigoa, Runyan, and Thomas all had terrible run block grades. If the Giants do manage to trade for Jonathan Taylor, don’t expect him to look like the JT that ran behind Quenton Nelson all those years in Indianapolis. Why was the line so bad Sunday when it looked good in Houston? Most likely because the Texans’ DL strength is on the edge, while the Eagles’ strength now is in the interior. The other reason the Giants’ running game is in tatters is because their two best running backs are injured. Devin Singletary didn’t do much in a starting role. The biggest excitement was from Greg Desrosiers, who actually bounced one outside for 9 yards, a rare sight this season, and showed some giddyup the Giants might consider making more use of if Cam Skattebo isn’t back by Thursday. As for the receivers, Malik Nabers was quiet yesterday (on the field, anyway) with only 43 yards and 5 receptions in 8 targets. That would have looked a lot better if he’d hauled in that beautiful end zone throw from McCarthy that was just a tad long but not impossible to catch for one of the NFL’s best receivers. The best news is that Darnell Mooney had his best game as Giant with three receptions in three targets for 54 yards; he got the best PFF grade of any Giants receiver. Isaiah Likely had a more quiet day than in some previous games but still caught the key TD pass that turned the game in the Giants’ favor, winding up with 53 yards. Malachi Fields didn’t have any spectacular plays like the one in Houston, but he had his usual day with three catches in five targets for 40 yards. Fields has had at least two receptions in every game this season. PFF grades: Defense You’ll probably be shocked to see that Arvell Reese was not the Giants’ most highly rated defensive player yesterday. That’s for one primary reason – pass coverage. It’s the one part of Reese’s game that is still under construction. Yesterday he gave up seven completions in eight targets for 55 yards including 26 YAC. Three of those completions were to wide receivers (Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper), and you can’t blame Reese for not making those plays; wide receiver on linebacker is always advantage, offense. When he was doing his day job, though, Reese excelled, getting an elite grade in pass rush because of his three sacks and his usual very good grade in run defense due to two run stops. Here’s a great angle on Reese’s obliteration of Eagles QB Joe Milton III with an interesting stat line from The Athletic’s Dane Brugler: This sack by Arvell Reese was the fastest (2.29 seconds) in the NFL since week 7 of last season, according to @NextGenStats Reese is the only NFL player with 65+ tackles, 8+ TFL, 1+ INT so far in 2026. pic.twitter.com/uaNi5EmRzC — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) November 9, 2026 Defensive Rookie of the Year? How about Defensive Player of the Year? (The latter won’t happen but you can make the case.) Elsewhere on the defense, Greg Newsome was the highest graded Giant with an elite 88.4 defense grade. Newsome’s game-by-grades as a Giant: 38.2, 51.9, 66.4, 63.7, 60.3, 71.5, 88.4. This is a reminder to us all not to judge players too quickly. Newsome seems to have progressively adjusted to Dennard Wilson’s defensive philosophy and is starting to play at a high level reminiscent of his early NFL career. No wonder the Giants extended him. Newsome made 6 tackles yesterday and gave up 2 receptions in 4 targets for only 13 yards. The rest of the cornerback room was less successful. Dru Phillips played his usual great game in run defense but was only adequate in pass coverage. Deonte Banks had a subpar score, mostly the result of his 30-yard pass interference penalty on a pass to Darius Cooper that set the Eagles up on the 3-yard line and led to their only TD. At safety, Ar’Darius Washington has taken on an increased role in recent games. He made three tackles and was targeted once, unsuccessfully. Jason Pinnock played adequately but uneventfully, with nothing on his stat line (including targets). Jevon Holland had an average stat line, with 2 tackles (both stops) and 3 assists and one 10-yard reception in 2 targets. The missing name? Tyler Nubin, now apparently a special teams player only – zero defensive snaps yesterday after only one in Houston. Some interesting things are happening on the interior defensive line. Darius Alexander had his best game of the season, with a sack, a hit, and a hurry and adequate run defense. Likewise sixth-round rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis is now getting a consistent 20-ish snaps per game (63 in the past three games after not playing on defense at all before that). As advertised, he provides nothing in the pass rush but he’s had six tackles, three of them stops, in the run game and hasn’t missed a tackle yet. D.J. Reader, now the stalwart of the IDL, had a sack, a hit and two hurries in addition to a tackle and an assist. If BJT further develops Shelby Harris may be the odd man out. Yesterday he played 35 snaps, typical of previous games, but had his second consecutive poor game because of his run defense (or lack thereof). He had one pressure yesterday, but that’s only his third of the year from a player who at one time was considered one the league’s better pass rushing IDLs. On the outside, Kayvon Thibodeaux was given only an average grade by PFF, but he had a good stat line, with two QB hits, two hurries and three tackles, two of them stops. Abdul Carter had one of his most quiet games, with no QB pressures and just one tackle (a stop). Shoutout to Dawuane Smoot in his first action as a Giant – he had a sack and a hurry in addition to one tackle (a stop), even though his overall grade was not great. Finally, with all the attention on Arvell Reese, let’s mention Micah McFadden, who had a sack and a QB hit yesterday in addition to five tackles (two of them stops) and four assists. He only gave up two receptions for 13 yards in five targets, but his coverage grade was low, suggesting that the players he was covering…

title: NY Giants planning ‘White Out’ game vs. Commanders
summary: The New York Giants are preparing to host Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, and they want to make it a unique experience at MetLife Stadium. With the Giants in first place at 5-2-1, the team wants to have a playoff-like atmosphere to give the players a homefield advantage. The Giants are wearing all […]
full_text: The New York Giants are preparing to host Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, and they want to make it a unique experience at MetLife Stadium. With the Giants in first place at 5-2-1, the team wants to have a playoff-like atmosphere to give the players a homefield advantage. The Giants are wearing all white against the Commanders, and they are encouraging the fanbase to do the same. From a press release issued by the team: “The Giants are set to wear their “Vintage White” uniforms and fans are strongly encouraged to wear white to the game to “White Out” MetLife Stadium. All attendees will receive a rally towel along with wearable light bands, which will be used for coordinated stadium-wide displays throughout the game. Fans are encouraged to arrive early and be in their seats by 7:45 p.m. for special player introductions, fireworks and a laser show,“ a press release read. “The Giants are also providing fans with an opportunity to gear up for gameday by visiting the “White Out” Shop, featuring a limited edition “White Out” collection from Starter along with other apparel including the “Vintage White” jerseys. The shop will be open for early access on Wednesday, Nov. 11 from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. outside MetLife Stadium between the MetLife and Verizon Gates. Parking for the Wednesday shop is free in Lot F, and no parking pass is required.“ The Giants wore their vintage white jerseys for their Week 9 win against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they hope they can go undefeated in those jerseys for the season. It’s the only time the vintage jerseys will be worn at home this season, and it’s meant to be a celebration of the 1980’s when the franchise won its first Super Bowl. “The Vintage White jerseys and pants resurfaced in 2016 as part of the NFL’s Color Rush concept, which commemorated 50 years of games being broadcast in color. The white jersey features blue numbers with a red outline, just like the Giants wore on the road for two decades.”
author: Jeremy Brener

title: Jaguars vs. Giants Week 11 contest gets scheduling change
summary: The New York Giants are preparing for their Week 10 matchup on Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, but the league has made some changes to their schedule for the following week. The NFL is flexing the start time for the game at MetLife Stadium between the Giants and the Jacksonville Jaguars to 4:25 […]
full_text: The New York Giants are preparing for their Week 10 matchup on Thursday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, but the league has made some changes to their schedule for the following week. The NFL is flexing the start time for the game at MetLife Stadium between the Giants and the Jacksonville Jaguars to 4:25 pm ET instead of 1 p.m. It is replacing the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Philadelphia Eagles, which takes its spot at 1 p.m. This change is largely being made for two reasons: The Jaguars and Giants are both in first place, making it one of the marquee matchups of the week. On top of that, the Eagles have struggled mightily, losing seven in a row. That streak has been capped off by the team’s most recent loss to the Giants, which sent them to 2-7 on the season. The Steelers and Eagles have a rare in-state rivalry in Pennsylvania that doesn’t get a lot of attention because they don’t play every year. The Giants and Jaguars, on the other hand, present a much more intriguing matchup in terms of overall football competition and playoff implications in both conferences. The Giants and Jaguars are joined in the late window by two other games on the West Coast. The New York Jets will face off against the winless Los Angeles Chargers, while the Las Vegas Raiders play a divisional matchup against Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos. This puts the Giants front and center for the national TV game of the week on Sunday afternoon. It is a testament to how well they have played over the first half of the season, and now they will get a chance to play in front of more eyeballs.
author: Jeremy Brener

full_text: Cam Skattebo | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cam Skattebo was “very close” to playing on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles and should be “full-go” Thursday against the Washington Commanders, according to New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh. “He was very close,” Harbaugh said on Monday morning. “We just decided to not take the risk that would go with it. There were some things that he was going to be limited just a bit, maybe. We decided not to go down that road because of the short week this week. “He should be full-go on Thursday night.” The Giants ran for just 80 yards on 31 carries vs. the Eagles, 2.6 yards per attempt. Devin Singletary had 21 carries for 31 yards, 1.5 yards per attempt. Skattebo had a career-high 124 yards on 17 carries in Week 7 against the Houston Texans. He leads the Giants with 418 rushing yards on 98 carries, 4.3 yards per rushing attempt. J.J. McCarthy ‘seems good’ Harbaugh said quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who is said to have suffered a hip pointer during the second half of Sunday’s game, is likely to be available vs. the Commanders. “He’s doing well,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll find out more during the course of the day and in a couple of days but it does look like he’s gonna play. We feel fairly good about that but don’t want to get out over my skis with it, but it seems good so far.”

title: Giants-Eagles: 5 plays that led to the Giants’ victory
summary: The New York Giants defeated the Philadelphia Eagles, 19-11, on Sunday to ascend to 5-2-1. The game featured 14 punts and 12 three-and-outs. The defenses dictated to two struggling offenses. New York faced adversity that was turned into their only touchdown drive of the game; J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game, and Jameis Winston entered […]
full_text: Arvell Reese | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants defeated the Philadelphia Eagles, 19-11, on Sunday to ascend to 5-2-1. The game featured 14 punts and 12 three-and-outs. The defenses dictated to two struggling offenses. New York faced adversity that was turned into their only touchdown drive of the game; J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game, and Jameis Winston entered to lead a 14-play, 76-yard drive that ended in an Isaiah Likely touchdown (more on that below). McCarthy returned to the game and threw a would-be touchdown to Malik Nabers that was not secured, which led to a field goal to conclude a 13-play, 54-yard drive. New York would only go up by eight, and the game was closer than it had to be after that. The game was not pretty, but a win is a win. Here are five plays, or sequences of plays, that were noteworthy and helped the Giants secure the victory. Play(s) 1: Arvell Reese is that guy Arvell Reese was EVERYWHERE once again! This time, though, he sacked the quarterback three times, including one where he received a free shot at Joe Milton: Arvell Reese 👀 pic.twitter.com/pcFmscdTtG — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) November 8, 2026 Reese picked up his second sack of the game by rushing initially, but then sliding off and spying. He saw Milton attempt to run, but he was there to stop Milton in his tracks: Arvell Reese with his second sack of the game. Dennard Wilson dialing it up against Joe Milton. pic.twitter.com/BpWz7zZpmL — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) November 8, 2026 Reese finished with 12 tackles, 10 solo tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble: Arvell Reese was absolutely TERRORIZING the Philadelphia Eagles ALL GAME LONG: • 12 total tackles (led team) • 3 sacks (led team) • 9 STOPS (led team) • 3 TFL (led team) • 3 QB hits (led team) The Giants rookie LB is one of the MOST DISRUPTIVE defenders in the NFL 😳🔥 pic.twitter.com/YbNoklQObA — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) November 8, 2026 Reese is playing unreal for a rookie, and every single week he seems to do something else that is beyond impressive. The Giants’ defense is excellent, coordinated by Dennard Wilson, and a big reason for that is the play of rookie linebacker Arvell Reese. Play (s) 2: Dominic Zvada! Zvada has struggled in recent games, and he found himself on the fans’ hot seat, but he went four-for-four to help the Giants secure a victory in Week 9 against Philadelphia. Zvada kicked 53, 38, and a pair of 49-yard field goals. Whatever was plaguing him mechanically seems to have been fixed, although time will tell. It was reassuring and important to see the undrafted rookie find his groove again. Play(s) 3: The Jameis Winston Experience Isaiah Likely WIDE OPEN TD to give the Giants the lead! NYGvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sVIaeJ0wU4 — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The Jameis Winston Experience was EXCELLENT in Philadelphia. Winston sparked the Giants’ offense on New York’s 14-play, 76-yard drive that ended with the five-yard touchdown catch to Isaiah Likely that is above. He converted a third-and-8 with a 7-yard catch-and-run by Devin Singletary, had a 16-yard strike to Malachi Fields on a third-and-15, and picked up 11 yards on a wacky—classic—Jameis Winston scramble where he looked dead to rights: Jameis will just do the most insnae shit I've ever seen out of nowhere hahaha pic.twitter.com/2UQj5cjv9p — Alex Wilson (@AlexWilsonESM) November 8, 2026 Winston also found Darnell Mooney for 27 yards on second-and-11, which got the Giants into the red zone for the first time all game: Jameis Winston delivers a strike to Darnell Mooney for 27 yards to finally get the Giants into the red zone pic.twitter.com/kn0wzBTy9p — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) November 8, 2026 The Giants are blessed to have Winston if something happens to McCarthy. New York isn’t 5-2-1, comfortably at the top of the division without Winston, who helped the Giants secure a victory as the backup. Play 4: 86-yard punt!? Eagles punter Brenton Mann punted 17 yards after Arvell Reese’s third-and-10 sack. The Giants’ offense did nothing with the positive field position, which was affected by a Nick Jones special teams penalty, but the dichotomy between Mann’s 17-yard punt and his next kick was stark! Jordan Stout punted the football 52 yards, and the Giants’ coverage team downed it at the Eagles’ two-yard line with 47 seconds left in the first half. New York wisely called timeouts and gave themselves an opportunity to put points on the board at the end of the first half. New York forced a three-and-out, where Mann took the field and booted a punt that ended as an 86-yard field flip. I love that Stout gave the Giants’ coaching staff the comfort of using their timeouts to try and take the lead in a tight 8-6 game; it’s one of the many reasons why a player like Stout is so valuable. However, Mann asked Stout to hold his beer in this situation, and the Giants’ attempt to establish the lead at halftime was squashed by an elite punt, resulting in the Giants just taking a knee. A normal punt would have given New York the ball with about 18 seconds left at around mid-field, but it was a special teams game to remember. Play(s) 5: Three-and-out! Prior to Week 9, Dennard Wilson’s defense led the league in three-and-outs. The Giants’ coaching is maximizing the personnel, and the aggressive — blitz-heavy — style has dictated to opposing offenses all season. That continued against the Eagles, as the Giants forced SIX three-and-outs, with an extra three-and-out that never saw fourth-down because of a forced fumble by Arvell Reese. Of course, if we’re going to mention the three-and-outs, we should also mention that the Giants’ offense went three-and-out five times. The game wasn’t an offensive showing, but one where the better football team won.
author: Nick Falato

title: NY Giants trade deadline: ‘Like a 9-year-old looking forward to Christmas’
summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told media in Philadelphia on Sunday night that if the team makes a move before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline it would have to “make sense short-term and long-term.” Harbaugh went even further in a post-game chat with Sports Illustrated NFL insider Albert Breer. Here is what Breer wrote […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | Getty Images New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told media in Philadelphia on Sunday night that if the team makes a move before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline it would have to “make sense short-term and long-term.” Harbaugh went even further in a post-game chat with Sports Illustrated NFL insider Albert Breer . Here is what Breer wrote about the Giants’ intentions at the trade deadline. Saying the Giants have been active on the phones with other teams would be like saying a 9-year-old is looking forward to Christmas. They made an offer to the Colts on Jonathan Taylor, they called the Ravens on Derrick Henry, they called the Titans on Jeffery Simmons (more than once) and inquired about guys who were never available. They dove hard into the defensive tackle market, working the Colts on DeForest Buckner (who wanted to go back to San Francisco and had his wishes honored), Grover Stewart and rising star Adetomiwa Adebawore (who was since extended); and the Patriots on Christian Barmore. All of that’s enough to give any playoff-starved fan of Big Blue a sugar high. And yet, they’ll tell you this isn’t about going all in on anything, happy as they are with where the team is. No, under Harbaugh, and with holdover GM Joe Schoen, this is now their default setting. Which, they’ll tell you, has little to do with adjusting any sort of preseason expectation. “No, that’s not how we look at winning,” Harbaugh texted me from the team bus, heading back to New Jersey on Sunday night. “You’re never ONE thing away. This is not addition and subtraction. The math is running on multiple levels of formulas and algorithms and humanity. You have to assess your options and opportunities. Seek value. What makes your team better shorter- and long-term and avoid what hinders your team, even in possibility. “It’s a case-by-case decision regarding options. The work is on finding and creating the options. That’s where the stones have to get turned over. We are building day-by-day for what’s coming tomorrow and in the future BOTH.” Which means not going all in on one thing, but being aggressive in looking at everything. “Always,” he continued. “Every single day. All the time. It’s not dependent on how close you think you are.” Will all that turning over of stones lead the Giants to making any moves? The clock is ticking as we all wait to find out.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NFC playoff picture: NY Giants solidify NFC East lead
summary: The New York Giants are crossing the halfway point in the 2026 season in first place in the NFC East. If the playoffs started today, the Giants would be the No. 3 seed as NFC East champions. There are nine games to play and a lot that can happen, but there is a lot of […]
full_text: Giants fans made themselves heard Sunday in Philadelphia. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are crossing the halfway point in the 2026 season in first place in the NFC East. If the playoffs started today, the Giants would be the No. 3 seed as NFC East champions. There are nine games to play and a lot that can happen, but there is a lot of optimism as the Giants chase their first division title since 2011. Here’s a look at the NFC playoff picture after the late slate of games on Sunday in Week 9. NFC playoff standings 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) Monday Night Football 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 1-1 NFCS) 5. Chicago Bears (7-2) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, win over ATL, 3-3 NFC) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) NFC East standings 1. New York Giants (5-2-1, 2-0-1 NFCE) 2. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 3. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 4. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) The Cowboys were able to keep pace with the Giants on Sunday as a result of their win against the Indianapolis Colts on the road. Meanwhile, the Commanders fell to the Los Angeles Rams at home, which has them desperately in need of a victory going into the team’s Week 10 Thursday Night Football contest at MetLife Stadium. The two teams will have a chance to settle the score after tying against one another at Northwest Stadium in Week 5. The game should be different for the Giants, as they will have J.J. McCarthy under center instead of Jameis Winston, who completed 33 of 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns during the game. The Giants hope to have leading rusher Cam Skattebo back after he missed the team’s Week 9 contest with a hamstring injury. As a team, the Giants managed to rush for only 80 yards throughout the game. Devin Singletary led the way with 31 rushing yards, but it came on 21 carries, just 1.5 yards per carry. Kickoff between the Commanders and Giants is scheduled for Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans can watch the game on Amazon Prime.

title: Jonathan Taylor trade: First-place NY Giants should take another swing
summary: Head coach John Harbaugh is right that the New York Giants are not at a place in their development where they should “go for a short term fix at an exorbitant cost.” But, yes, the Giants should make another run at getting star running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts. Harbaugh on Sunday night […]
full_text: Jonathan Taylor waving to fans in Indianapolis after Sunday’s game. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Head coach John Harbaugh is right that the New York Giants are not at a place in their development where they should “go for a short term fix at an exorbitant cost.” But, yes, the Giants should make another run at getting star running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts. Harbaugh on Sunday night did not deny reports that the Giants had pulled an offer of a 2027 second-round and 2028 fifth-round pick for Taylor off the table. “Things do change,” Harbaugh said. “Things change from day-to-day.” Things did change on Sunday when the Giants broke a 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia, further proving that these aren’t the same old Giants, and when the Colts lost yet another game. Perhaps after losing to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday to fall to 2-7 Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon and interim general manager Ed Dodds will come to their senses and realize the best thing they can for a franchise clearly in need of starting over is to capitalize on the best trade asset they have. The Colts have already parted with Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. They might part with quarterback Daniel Jones, wide receiver Josh Downs, and defensive tackle Grover Stewart before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. What good is hanging on to Taylor going to do them? Pro Football Talk is reporting that the Colts are expected to take the best offer they can get for Taylor between now and Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline. Taylor sounded Sunday like he knew he would be moving on: "I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display all of not only my hard work, but the team's hard work." @ADChernoff asked Jonathan Taylor what he hopes the fans will remember about him if this is Taylor's last game with the #Colts : pic.twitter.com/Z6bL4IMT0M — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) November 8, 2026 Taylor can’t rescue the Colts at this point. He can, though, do a lot for the Giants. Both this season and for a couple of years beyond 2026. He is signed to a reasonable for a top-tier running back contract through 2028. He would cost roughly $34 million in 2027 and 2028, plus the pro-rated portion of his $6.98 million base salary this season. With apologies to Cam Skattebo, the 27-year-old Taylor is a different class of running back. The Giants ran 31 times for 80 yards (2.6 yards per carry) against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. Devin Singletary, carrying the load without Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy, gained 31 yards on 21 carries (1.5 yards per carry). To be real, the Giants’ run blocking was horrid on Sunday. That has to get better or the Giants won’t be able to take full advantage of the talents of whoever they are handing the ball to. That shouldn’t stop the Giants from swinging a big deal for Taylor — if they are comfortable with the price tag. What is the price they should be comfortable surrendering? For me, the second- and fifth-round pick offer they previously made, perhaps sweetened by adding a player like Tracy, would be about as far as I would go. In my view, a first-round pick is a bridge too far. Still, the Giants have to remember they are sitting on the gold mine of two 23-year-old quarterbacks who look like starting-caliber NFL players in Jaxson Dart and J.J. McCarthy. One of them — probably McCarthy — could bring back a bounty of draft picks next offseason. “They were loud!” Coach Harbaugh on the fans today pic.twitter.com/YxmfgfUaIu — New York Giants (@Giants) November 9, 2026 Harbaugh’s Giants have an opportunity to win their first NFC East title since 2011. That isn’t a Super Bowl, but it would be quite an accomplishment. They should try to seize the moment. Could they win it without Taylor? Maybe, but their chances would be better with him. They have a chance to legitimize the five-year, $100 million contract they gave Harbaugh. They have a chance to give a 71-year-old owner fighting cancer a playoff team to be proud of. They have a chance to show their locker room that they recognize the players’ hard work and are willing to help them try to finish the job. They have a chance to show a clearly fired-up fan base that things are indeed different now. “The fans, they were great. We had a bunch of fans here, right? Wow. We had a bunch of fans here. They were loud. They were great. And I love our fans. This is a special place,” Harbaugh said. “You could just feel the passion and the excitement and the desire to win from the entire fan base,” said McCarthy. “It gives us so much motivation out there. I was telling the guys in the huddle, ‘Look around, see that blues are starting to fill up more than green.’ It just gives us that much more juice to go out there and execute that next play.” Harbaugh was also right on Sunday when he said “I never think that you’re one step away, one player away.” The Giants are not yet a Super Bowl team. There is no single move they can make that would put them in the class of the San Francisco 49ers or Chicago Bears in the NFC. A move for Taylor would get them closer, though, and would be another step toward putting the misery of the post-2011 Super Bowl stretch in the rearview mirror. Maybe the Giants won’t be able to get it done. They should, though, try. The players who have gotten them this far, the ownership group that went above and beyond to bring Harbaugh to New York, and the fans who have waited for a team to feel good about deserve it.

title: J.J. McCarthy ‘feeling pretty good’, aiming to be ready to face Washington Commanders
summary: For the first time in a decade, the New York Giants went into Lincoln Financial Center walked out winners. The Giants topped the Philadelphia Eagles 19-11 on the road, rising to 5-2-1 on the season and dropping the Eagles to 2-7 in the process. It wasn’t an easy game, and the Giants struggled to overcome […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy drops back to pass against the Philadelphia Eagles. | Getty Images For the first time in a decade, the New York Giants went into Lincoln Financial Center walked out winners. The Giants topped the Philadelphia Eagles 19-11 on the road, rising to 5-2-1 on the season and dropping the Eagles to 2-7 in the process. It wasn’t an easy game, and the Giants struggled to overcome the Eagles’ defensive line as well as their own mistakes. But they did overcome them, as well as an injury to quarterback J.J. McCarthy that sent him back to the locker room. But in the end it was McCarthy, and Jameis Winston, who ended the Giants’ decade-long winless streak in Philadelphia. “It means the world. The fact that [Jameis] and I got to do it, it’s just a testament of what this team’s all about,” McCarthy said. “I can’t thank the Mara’s, the ownership, just the organization for putting this group together because it’s a really special group. To get a gritty win like this and an environment like this and obviously the past was what it was, but to find a way to win, that’s all that matters is going 1-0 every week and we did that today.” ‘Gritty’ is probably the best way to describe a win that was in no way pretty, but they got the job done. That also describes McCarthy, who left the field with a hip injury suffered on a read-option run. “The play was quarterback-driven run, and I pulled it based on my read, and the goal is to get to the numbers, get out of bounds,” McCarthy said, describing the hit. “I pulled it back inside and kind of saw bomb late and tried to get my shoulder down, didn’t get it down enough and made a great hit. At the end of the day, I’ve just got to protect myself and do a better job of doing that.” “Football is a physical game,” McCarthy said. “I can’t thank the training staff enough for helping me get back on the field as fast as possible. But yeah, it’s feeling pretty good.” He was only out of the game for one drive — a drive in which Jameis Winston went 6 of 7 and picked up two first downs with his legs — and returned for the fourth quarter. “I feel good,” he added. “At the end of the day, [as] I said, it’s a physical game and a lot of guys are banged up, but we’re going to do our best to make sure we turn over as fast as possible and do whatever we can between now and then and make sure we’re as close to 100% leading up to a great opponent against Washington. They’re going to be hungry, and we’re really excited to go get this one.” After the game, head coach John Harbaugh said that McCarthy insisted on going back into the game for the fourth quarter. “He insisted on it,” Harbaugh said. “We weren’t pushing him back out there. He was able to play, but he insisted on playing. Even at the end we thought about putting Jameis in there for the last drive and he insisted on being out there. It says a lot about him for sure.” “I think it means a lot because I think it just demonstrates the heart we’re talking about,” Harbaugh added. “Every single player has the opportunity to lead and demonstrate that at some point in time. And to your point, the quarterback is doing it and that’s big. That’s big to fight through that kind of thing, fight through an injury, go back in, take care of it, get back out there. Now he’s going to have to fight to get ready to play on Thursday. That’s part of it, too. So pretty impressive. Darn impressive. Very impressive.” McCarthy was certainly anxious and excited to get back into the game after coming out of the locker room. “I’m able to walk, I’m able to throw. I want to get back out there as soon as possible,” he said. “Just like I said, I can’t thank the team enough – the athletic [training staff] for just really doing everything that was beneficial [to] me. They didn’t really push any lines or anything like that, and I just can’t thank them enough.” We all saw how fired up he was on the sideline after emerging from the locker room. JJ McCarthy has made his way back from the locker room and is fired up. He's back in the game. pic.twitter.com/pe4d5JVWGq https://t.co/mQvpOdpeYt — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 8, 2026 “I feel like it was definitely a moment where it was one of those things where you have to make that decision,” he said. “At the end of the day, no matter what, it’s about my brothers and I’ll do whatever I can to help them the best I can to be successful. And I felt like I was able to do enough to make sure that we could move the ball. Obviously, yes, put it all on the line for this organization and everything I can to help go get a win.” And McCarthy helped the Giants get the win, and he could feel the tide shift as the Giants pulled out to a two-score lead. “It was amazing,” McCarthy said. “You could just feel the passion and the excitement and the desire to win from the entire fan base. It gives us so much motivation out there. I was telling the guys in the huddle, ‘Look around, see that blues are starting to fill up more than green.” It just gives us that much more juice to go out there and execute that next play. I can’t wait to see the home fans Thursday night and be able to really give them a show because offensively we’ve got to do a better job with the defense playing fantastic today. Special teams played fantastic and we’re excited to make it right.”

title: Jets trade defensive back for 2028 draft pick
summary: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans evades pressure by Andre Cisco #8 of the New York Jets during the first half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. Payne also stands to benefit from the trade as he works his way back from a preseason injury that has kept him out of action so far this season.
