full_text: The Seattle Seahawks got the win they needed against the Arizona Cardinals, but they didn’t exactly get favorable results elsewhere in the NFC standings. As expected, the San Francisco 49ers dispatched the Las Vegas Raiders to temporarily assume control of the No. 1 seed again. While the NFC South tripped over itself like usual (except the New Orleans Saints), the NFC North was a perfect 3-0 on Sunday, with the Chicago Bears overcoming five turnovers to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a last-second field goal. Probably one of the biggest results of the day was the Green Bay Packers hammering the New England Patriots in a 45-27 romp, which is the result that currently keeps the Seahawks out of a playoff spot. NFC playoff standings entering Monday night 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) – Monday Night Football vs. Buffalo Bills pending 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 1-1 NFCS) 5. Chicago Bears (7-2) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, win over ATL, 3-3 NFC) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) If we’re being honest with ourselves, the NFC West title is on the cusp of being out of reach, and would be nailed on out of reach with a loss to the 49ers in Week 12. Even outside of the division race, the Seahawks’ Wild Card hopes rest on overtaking one of these red-hot NFC North teams and fending off the resurgent Rams, who’ve won three straight. It might be a bad thing if the Bears get dragged into the WC race given the head-to-head tiebreaker on Chicago, so a Bears NFC North title might be preferred in the long run. There’s a good chance that 10 wins might not be enough to get a Wild Card spot. Six wins might be enough to win the NFC South, but the Seahawks don’t play in that division, unfortunately.

title: Winners and Losers from the Seahawks’ latest sweep of Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks did what they had to do to get the W against the Arizona Cardinals. Fireworks were not needed on offense, while the undermanned defense held down the Cardinals offense after the opening drive. The dominance over Arizona continues, but there a far more big picture things to focus on beyond winning 11 […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks did what they had to do to get the W against the Arizona Cardinals. Fireworks were not needed on offense, while the undermanned defense held down the Cardinals offense after the opening drive. The dominance over Arizona continues, but there a far more big picture things to focus on beyond winning 11 in a row over arguably the most hapless franchise in the NFL. It’s time for Winners and Losers from Seahawks 17, Cardinals 3! Winners An undermanned defense steps up to the task Biggest winner for me was the defense, which took a kick in the teeth after giving up some big plays last week against the Chicago Bears. I know the Cardinals offense is bad when they’re not playing the Dallas Cowboys defense, but the Seahawks gave up an 89-yard drive to start the game and didn’t even let the Cards finish with 200 total yards. Sub-4 yards-per-play is excellent, and it’s not their fault that two perfectly fine turnovers were ruled out because of substandard officiating. Dante Fowler stepped up and got his first sack as a Seahawk, Byron Murphy II and DeMarcus Lawrence also got to Gardner Minshew, Derick Hall had three TFLs, Devon Witherspoon was a menace at the line of scrimmage, and Nick Emmanwori had a strong bounce-back performance after struggling versus Chicago. Above all else, this defense finally got some red zone stops, and perhaps it’s fitting that they got the red zone issues “fixed” for a day on both sides of the ball. A.J Barner gets more involved It’s not like Barner was the focal point of the Seahawks passing offense, but he caught his first touchdown of the season and turned three Barnyard sneaks into first downs and/or a touchdown. It’s the second multi-TD game of Barner’s career, and all of his touchdowns this season have come against Arizona. The fact that Seattle had Barnyard opportunities in itself was a relief and a sight for sore eyes. Drew Lock plays through pain, doesn’t turn it over It was a bit of a nervy start from Drew, but Lock gutted through the elbow and (later) oblique injuries to play mistake-free football. He wasn’t flashy and didn’t need to be, going 19/28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. Lock also scrambled for a first down and the only time there was a close shave on an interception was the screen pass that somehow got deflected to Cooper Kupp for eight yards. Also of note? No sacks. This was, in a non-patronizing way, a high-end backup quarterback performance. Lock didn’t do anything to put Seattle in jeopardy of losing the game, and made enough winning plays to get Seattle across the finish line. Now we wait to see if he plays in Week 10 . Zach Charbonnet gets closer to his old self Seattle’s run game wasn’t anything spectacular, but when it was time for the hammer to hit the nail, Charbonnet was called upon. He finished with 77 yards on 16 carries, including a spectacular 17-yard run to help bleed the clock. His 25-yard catch-and-run was wiped out due to a really iffy Jalen Sundell personal foul, otherwise he’d be north of 100 scrimmage yards. Having Charbonnet get into gear should help the offense across the run, pass, and pass pro. Jadarian Price makes noise as a receiver I can’t really vouch for Price having an effective game as a runner (9 carries for 24 yards), but he had a solid kick return to start the game, and led the Seahawks with 54 yards receiving on four catches. Yes, Jaxon Smith-Njigba had just 51 yards on seven catches, which gave us the rare sight of a non-JSN receiver leading the team in yards. Price wasn’t known as a receiving back in college, so this development was highly encouraging. Offensive line holds up after some nervy initial moments Lock was only hit three times and not sacked once. They got some movement in the run game albeit not consistently. Most of the pressures allowed were seemingly on blitzes and not four-man rushes. Some of the success I imagine is level of competition, but having your Week 1 starting OL + Josh Jones made for a calmer operation compared to the mess that was Monday night. Losers Clete Blakeman’s crew was a joke The Reggie Virgil catch not getting overturned for being out of bounds was astonishing, but that’s on the replay center since they make the call. For what it’s worth, I don’t think Barner’s touchdown was a catch but that’s one that might have been too closer to over turn. However… Deciding that Trey McBride’s forward progress was stopped on his fumble was amazingly bad officiating and indefensible. The Josh Jobe DPI was ludicrous and made it seemed like McBride was a lightweight when he just fell down from marginal contact. Two turnovers taken off the board because of those calls. I actually don’t have too much of an issue with the Devon Witherspoon taunting penalty, but having rewatched the Jalen Sundell unnecessary roughness I think that is a weak call. If it’s not after the whistle then I don’t think it was unnecessary roughness given Budda Baker was in the vicinity of where Charbonnet was tackled. It was a flag-fest; yet another one involving the Seahawks. There were a lot of deserved flags on both teams, but this trend of the NFL over-officiating games has to stop. Everyone knows A.J. Barner’s touchdown celebration except Jonathan Vilma Vilma was a great linebacker in the NFL and a Super Bowl champion. As an analyst? Yeah… Vilma on the call today and for the celebration dance AJ Barner does on EVERY SINGLE touchdown – he had 8 last year including in the Super Bowl – he comments "I think he forgot what he wanted to do" Grounds for contract termination I'm afraid — Carter Donnick (@CDonnick1) November 8, 2026 It was not an enjoyable broadcast to listen to, I’ll put it that way. Avery Smith is a liability on special teams This is not a major thing when we’re talking about special teams role players, but the rookie corner doesn’t get on the field on defense (nor should he), so he has to show his value on ST. He’s been culpable on a couple of big kick returns this season due to missed tackles and bad angles. Today was the second time he backed the Seahawks up due to a penalty. I wouldn’t be surprised to see some healthy scratches for him moving forward once the Seahawks are healthier. Final Notes What is Emanuel Wilson’s future on the Seahawks? The trade deadline is Tuesday. I can’t pretend Wilson has much trade value, but he’s been completely frozen out of the offense for two straight games. This week I am pretty sure he wasn’t even part of special teams, which at least he was last week. Obviously the injury concerns regarding Charbonnet and Price are enough to not leave yourself thin at running back, but it’s a bit unfortunate that Wilson has gone from a 100-yard game against the Kansas City Chiefs and a couple of other solid performances this season to an unofficial healthy scratch. George Holani stays on special teams, but doesn’t get any offensive reps . I’d say it’s about time that happened. If you can trust Zach in pass pro, Holani still provides something as a special teams guy. Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton get a little bit involved in the offense . A combined five catches for 59 yards for the other top receivers on the team. They each had successful third down conversions, which is a delight knowing how heavily Seattle relies on JSN. JSN goes full Golden Tate . Please don’t run backwards out of a first down again, JSN. No strong opinion on Brian Fleury’s play-calling . When you’re down two starting offensive linemen, your starting QB, a starting receiver, and your backup QB is hurt, there’s only so much you can do to make the offense functional. The execution generally looked better but this is a tough data point when assessing his future as OC. It was at least a relief to see Seattle stick with Price and Charbonnet and run more play-action again. Beat the fading Raiders and you can get some much-needed rest . Klint Kubiak has the Raiders at least looking more competitive than they have been in the past couple of years, but the Raiders…

title: Seahawks injury update: Drew Lock’s status ‘up in the air’ for Week 10 after hurting oblique
summary: It might be Jalen Milroe time for the Seattle Seahawks. While Drew Lock didn’t miss any game action during Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he has a new injury on top of the severe tendinitis he reportedly had been battling over the past couple of weeks. Lock was seen grabbing his right hip […]
full_text: It might be Jalen Milroe time for the Seattle Seahawks. While Drew Lock didn’t miss any game action during Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he has a new injury on top of the severe tendinitis he reportedly had been battling over the past couple of weeks. Lock was seen grabbing his right hip area during the third quarter of Sunday’s game, grimacing and walking gingerly as he got off the field prior to Seattle’s final scoring drive. Jalen Milroe warmed up on the sidelines while Lock went into the blue tent, but Lock stayed in for the rest of the afternoon and didn’t miss a play. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters at the post-game press conference that Lock’s status is “up in the air” after getting his oblique looked at. “We’re looking at him for an oblique, so we’ll assess it and go from there,” Macdonald said. “He made it out [of the game], but you know, like I’ve sat here before and told you a guy would be ready and then he wasn’t. So, leave my options open.” For what it’s worth, Lock said “we’ll get it looked at [Sunday night]” and that it “was not too bad.” When asked if the injury affected him, he said, “I wouldn’t say it did.” The Seahawks talk about having a “70-man roster,” knowing they’ll frequently need contributions from beyond the 53. With six starters down, this was one of those weeks. Mike Macdonald said it showed “the power of our 70” and called Drew Lock “a beast” for playing through injury. pic.twitter.com/rp7ZM3vgeo — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 9, 2026 Lock also said he felt “good” playing through the elbow injury. Odds are not sounding favorable for Sam Darnold to return against the Las Vegas Raiders, with ESPN’s Adam Schefter reporting what felt like a pretty obvious situation that he is in “jeopardy” of missing Week 10 with quad and rib injuries. If Darnold was listed as “week-to-week” by Mike Macdonald, this isn’t earth-shattering news as much as it affirms what’s already been said. If the news is negative on Lock, then we could see Jalen Milroe’s first career NFL start. But at the minimum, this is a very banged up Seahawks quarterback room and the bye week might be one of the most welcome byes in recent Seahawks history.

title: 49ers and Cowboys projected to be the highest-scoring game of the season
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are third in the NFL in points per game. The Dallas Cowboys are sixth in the NFL. So it shouldn’t surprise you when oddsmakers like FanDuel Sportsbook make the total for these two teams the highest projected total of any game this season. The projected total is set at 55.5. That […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are third in the NFL in points per game. The Dallas Cowboys are sixth in the NFL. So it shouldn’t surprise you when oddsmakers like FanDuel Sportsbook make the total for these two teams the highest projected total of any game this season. The projected total is set at 55.5. That ties for the highest total this season, with an October 12 matchup between the Bills and the Rams—a contest that ended 37-34. The Cowboys have had a couple of 54.5-point games. One was this month when they traveled to Arizona. That score was 30-33. The other 54.5 total came back in September against the Ravens, when the score was 34-31. The 49ers have had only one pre-flop game projected north of 50. However, they’ve been involved in a couple of games that went over 60 points. When the total is as high as 55.5, the oddsmakers are telling us no number is high enough. Low totals go under. High totals go over. “When it’s high, we go higher” is a saying in this market. That applies to two top-10 offenses. The 49ers are 4.5-point favorites. That’s because only the Raiders are worse defensively in EPA per play than the Cowboys. Dallas ranks 25th in defensive success rate. If you caught the Colts-Cowboys game on Sunday, the replays kept showing Daniel Jones throwing the ball underneath when receivers ran wide open at the intermediate and deep levels. Dallas was without cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown in Week 9. I’m not sure either will make much of a difference against the 49ers. The 49ers have done a great job at limiting the damage this season defensively. But they have not played an offense with the weapons Dallas has to date. The secondary will be tested in ways they haven’t been all season, because it’ll be the best quarterback Raheem Morris has seen. Per Sports Info Solutions, no quarterback has been more valuable than Dak Prescott this season. For as obnoxious as the total seems, it might be too low when you’re talking about these two high-powered offenses. This game should be on Sunday Night Football. It has all of the makings of being the most entertaining game of the month. Too bad it wasn’t flexed.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 3 defensive stars who helped pave the way for a 49ers win over the Raiders
summary: With how good the San Francisco 49ers offense is compared to the Las Vegas Raiders defense, it was thought the San Francisco offense would be making the big plays on Sunday. Instead, it was the San Francisco defense that threw the biggest punches of the game, forcing five second-half turnovers en route to a 38-17 […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images With how good the San Francisco 49ers offense is compared to the Las Vegas Raiders defense, it was thought the San Francisco offense would be making the big plays on Sunday. Instead, it was the San Francisco defense that threw the biggest punches of the game, forcing five second-half turnovers en route to a 38-17 win. The offense held its end of the bargain, scoring 31 of the 38 points; however, mistakes from the offense both kept the Raiders in the game and put the defense in some bad situations. But the defense never once broke, making big play after big play. While the offense exploded with plenty of points, all three stars from Week 9 come from the defense: 3rd Star: LB Jaden Dugger Dugger’s biggest play of the game felt like it was the beginning of the end for the Raiders but ended up being the beginning of the chaos that was the third quarter on Sunday. Dugger continued his solid rookie campaign as the 49ers super-utility man on defense finished with six tackles (all solo), but it was an early Christmas gift from Kirk Cousins that earned Dugger Sunday’s No. 3 star. The Raiders started the second half with the ball trailing by only 11 despite the 49ers scoring on three-of-four first-half drives. Any type of points from Las Vegas would have put the Raiders firmly in the game, and with that knowledge, Klint Kubiak wanted to start the drive hot, calling a play-action pass. Cousins took the snap and went to fake to Mike Washington Jr.; however, at the end of the fake, Washington’s elbow appeared to knock the ball out of Cousins’ hand. Cousins was able to quickly recover the ball but then decided one mistake on the play wasn’t enough. Instead of conceding on the play, Cousins was baited by Dugger, who got the quarterback to throw something that resembled a pass to Tre Tucker but looked like it was intended for Dugger. The rookie would do the rest of the work, taking the ball back for a touchdown, extending the 49ers’ lead to 18 points. 2nd Star: CB Upton Stout Dugger’s interception was canceled out just five minutes later with the Raiders responding to the turnover with a touchdown-scoring drive, putting Las Vegas within eight points. The two sides would then exchange turnovers (a 49ers interception followed by a Raiders lost fumble ending with a 49ers turnover on downs). The Raiders were one yard away from ending that stretch of drives with a touchdown. Upton Stout ensured the turnover streak continued. The San Francisco turnover on downs gave the Raiders the ball back at midfield down eight. An 18-yard pass to Tucker followed by a Deommodore Lenoir tackle for loss would have the Raiders at the doorstep of the red zone. Cousins would hit Michael Mayer on a strike near the goal line where Ji’Ayir Brown would initially greet Mayer, but Stout would follow closely behind with a punch that got just enough of the ball to knock it free. Fred Warner would pounce on it, and instead of a touchdown, it would be the 49ers’ ball. Even better, the 49ers offense would take the ball and score seven plays later. From one yard away to a four-point lead late in the third quarter to an 18-point lead as the fourth quarter begins. In a game of big momentum swings, none was bigger than the stretch that was started by Stout’s right hand. 1st Star: LB Fred Warner First and foremost, Fred Warner forced a loss of two on a quarterback sneak to prevent a Kirk Cousins touchdown. On a play that is designed to keep the quarterback moving forward, Warner alone forced the play to go backward. In a career of impressive feats, that might have been the best of Warner’s career. To make things even better, the stop would result in a Renardo Green interception to end a second Las Vegas drive at the goal line in a row. But before his goal-line heroics, Warner had another momentum-changing play in a wacky third quarter. The first turnover that started the stretch of turnovers mentioned above was an ugly Brock Purdy interception. Again, the Raiders would take the ball with a chance to get within four points with a short field. The drive started innocently enough, with a Cousins pass to Ashton Jeanty falling incomplete. They would follow with a quick pass to Brock Bowers. That’s where Warner comes in. The All-World linebacker would come in with that patented Warner Punch (the Peanut Punch is used so frequently around the league, but no one is better than Warner, so it’s his punch now) to knock the ball free to be picked up by Dre Greenlaw, giving the ball right back to the 49ers offense (to promptly give the ball back to Vegas four plays later). Several drives later, Warner would hold Cousins to the loss on the sneak, leading to the interception that would seal the deal. Week 9 might end up being example No. 1 in Warner’s Defensive Player of the Year campaign. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 9, the standings are: WR Mike Evans – 8 points QB Brock Purdy – 7 points LB Fred Warner – 6 points

title: Christian McCaffrey surpasses Hall of Famer to set new NFL record
summary: Sunday was a case of another week, another record for Christian McCaffrey, only this one was a biggy. McCaffrey had a quiet day in terms of yardage in the 49ers’ 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He had 87 total scrimmage yards, rushing for 67 on the ground, three fewer than rookie backup Kaelon […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers scores a second quarter touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday was a case of another week, another record for Christian McCaffrey, only this one was a biggy. McCaffrey had a quiet day in terms of yardage in the 49ers’ 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He had 87 total scrimmage yards, rushing for 67 on the ground, three fewer than rookie backup Kaelon Black. But he found the endzone twice, giving the 49ers a lead they never relinquished with a short-yardage plunge on the opening drive before scoring on a 12-yard reception in the second quarter. It was the latter touchdown that carried historical significance. McCaffrey’s touchdown reception marked the 37th of his illustrious career and took him ahead of arguably the finest dual-threat running back in the history of the sport. That score saw McCaffrey set the record the most touchdown receptions by a running back in the Super Bowl era, breaking his tie with Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk (36). Like Faulk, McCaffrey is destined to end up in Canton, having established himself as the pre-eminent do-it-all back of his era, his skills as both a runner and a receiver weaponized to an even greater degree in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. Of course, Faulk has the one thing McCaffrey is still chasing, having won Super Bowl XXXIV with the St. Louis Rams. But, having a backup in Black who can lessen the burden on him could be crucial in helping McCaffrey be at his best when it really counts in the postseason as he seeks to finally secure that Super Bowl ring. “We love our room. I think with KB, when he comes in it’s such a spark. When I can come in and come out and get my wind, he goes in, balls out, comes out, gets his wind. If we can just continue to do that, man, I think we can be really special,” McCaffrey said after the win over Las Vegas. “Jordan [James], also another guy who has been working so hard. When he touches the ball, he’s very dangerous as well. We’ve got a super high standard in that room and that’s because we know how good we can be. It’s because of guys like KB, because of guys like JJ and the rest of the guys who continue to push each other.”

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers stay atop NFC; Seahawks, Rams win ugly
summary: The San Francisco 49ers reached the halfway point with a 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, and for a hot second, it had the familiar 49ers play-with-their-food game feel. Then, thanks to a bad snap, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins opened the floodgates (and the second half) with this: From there, the 49ers manhandled the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers in the locker room before the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Commanders 23-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers reached the halfway point with a 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, and for a hot second, it had the familiar 49ers play-with-their-food game feel. Then, thanks to a bad snap, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins opened the floodgates (and the second half) with this: Jaden Dugger with a pick Six to start the second half! pic.twitter.com/QwOCfjaQiC — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) November 8, 2026 From there, the 49ers manhandled the Raiders. Yes, the Raiders scored another touchdown, but the 49ers were not blowing this lead. The win puts the 49ers at the No. 1 seed in the NFC, a half-game ahead of the Minnesota Vikings (6-1). They also lead the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams by 2.5 games in the NFC West. Since both of those teams won, the lead stayed put, but the 49ers took care of business. It came at a cost. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton broke his ankle and is out for the season. Cornerback Renardo Green also left with a back injury. Just when the pieces start coming back… Seattle Seahawks (5-4)/Arizona Cardinals (3-6) So that Minshew Magic we talked about last week? Well, it turns out that only lasts a single game. Last Sunday, quarterback Gardner Minshew II came off the bench in Dallas with 1:35 left in the third quarter and the Cardinals down 17-3. He threw three fourth-quarter touchdown passes, won in overtime, and took the starting job. Like the Dallas game, Minshew found himself down 17-3, and unlike the Dallas game, we didn’t get any fourth-quarter theatrics. We didn’t even get a single touchdown. Instead, the Cardinals sat at three points. That might be it for Minshew Mania, Magic, whatever we want to call it when he actually scores at least one touchdown. Seattle had their own offensive issues. With Sam Darnold not suited for this game due to injury, Drew Lock helmed the offense despite an elbow injury that had kept him inactive the previous two weeks and a hip issue that popped up in the third quarter. An offense that got only 17 points. Right, the Cardinals, who have their own litany of issues, held the Seahawks to that. Drew Lock, or no Drew Lock, that seems a bit small, but the Seahawks found a way to win. Minshew went 21-of-30 for 166 yards passing with no touchdowns and was sacked three times. Running back Tyler Allgeier ran for 147 yards in Dallas and managed 46 on 17 carries here. Meanwhile, Lock didn’t turn the ball over and finished 19-of-28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. The NFC West. Those games are slugfests. This one was a slugfest with 180 yards of penalties between the two teams. I guess it was entertaining? Los Angeles Rams (5-4) Myles Garrett finally showed up. In his debut against the 49ers in Melbourne, the defensive end didn’t record a tackle. Two months later, he came off injured reserve and had three sacks and a forced fumble in a 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The Rams needed every one of them, because the offense spent most of the day stuck in mud. Luckily, the Rams have defense and Garrett. Which means this: three sacks for this Myles Garrett guy pic.twitter.com/RpsM3zwHyd — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Sure, that defense was good, but the offense? Not so much. Puka Nacua was the entire passing game, with 14 catches on 19 targets for 150 yards receiving and a touchdown. No other Rams receiver had more than 20 yards. And the Rams might have more issues on offense now since Nacua hurt his knee on the Rams’ final offensive snap, a third-down jet sweep. He’ll get an MRI Monday, and the Rams don’t believe it’s a torn ACL , Friendly reminder that Davante Adams is already on injured reserve. And I thought the 49ers had wide receiver injuries. Sheesh. Onto Week 10 The 49ers go to Dallas to play the Cowboys (4-5). Dallas got past the 2-7 Colts on a Dak Prescott drive that took less than 30 seconds and a Caleb Downs interception. Really, all you need to know about that game is that the Cowboys’ defense isn’t that good and the offense is capable of things like this: A WILD play in Indianapolis! An untouched Lamb gets extra yards then fumbles in the red zone 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/rddAvGre0M — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 8, 2026 That is the drunken play of the year. The Rams visit the Cardinals. Arizona already beat Los Angeles 18-16 at Levi’s South SoFi Field in Week 6, via six field goals and no touchdowns. All I’m saying is, Cardinals, you’ve done it once. The Seahawks visit the Raiders, who just gave away four straight turnovers to the 49ers. Matchups matter, but I’m curious how the Raiders do against the Seahawks after what we saw with the 49ers today. Can they get four turnovers too? 1st: San Francisco 49ers ; Next: at Dallas Cowboys TIE-2nd: Seattle Seahawks ; Next: at Las Vegas Raiders TIE-2nd: Los Angeles Rams ; Next: at Arizona Cardinals 4th: Arizona Cardinals ; Next: vs. Los Angeles Rams

title: Ideal 49ers pass rush target asks his team to trade him
summary: The 49ers’ pass rush was not the force many might have expected on Sunday in their 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Though the 49ers forced five turnovers en route to victory, the miscues by the Raiders, for whom quarterback Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions, were not a product of overwhelming pressure from a […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The 49ers’ pass rush was not the force many might have expected on Sunday in their 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Though the 49ers forced five turnovers en route to victory, the miscues by the Raiders, for whom quarterback Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions, were not a product of overwhelming pressure from a defensive line boosted by the trade for DeForest Buckner. Indeed, Cousins was only pressured 31.3% of the time, which was 24th heading into Sunday Night Football in Week 9 among all quarterbacks. Not terrible, but not great for a team once again boasting Buckner’s prowess in that area and also getting Nick Bosa back from injury. The somewhat underwhelming showing underlined why the 49ers may feel the need to add further to their defensive line before Tuesday’s trade deadline. And an ideal target at the edge rusher spot has reportedly requested to be traded, according to NFL Network and ESPN’s Ian Rapoport . Will McDonald IV is projected as an outside pass rusher ideally suited to the wide 9 front often employed by the 49ers when he came out in 2023, a year in which San Francisco did not have a first-round pick. With an athletic profile that checked all the boxes , explosiveness that was crystal clear on tape, a well-refined pass rush arsenal, and positional versatility, having often played essentially on the interior in Iowa State’s 3-3-5 front in college, it was hard to think of a prospect better suited to the 49ers in 2023, and he remains an excellent fit. Despite the Jets’ continued struggles, McDonald has established himself as a consistently productive pass rusher. He has 24.5 sacks for his career, three of which have come this season as New York has slumped to a 2-7 start. McDonald had eight sacks last year and 10.5 in 2024. Now McDonald, under contract through 2027, wants out of New York, with Rapoport stating that the 27-year-old is unhappy with his usage by the Jets, having been utilized as more of a situational rusher this season. Rapoport added that teams have called on McDonald, but the Jets have not engaged in trade talks and do not plan to. However, things can change quickly in the NFL, and the prospect of adding another talented pass rusher under contract for next season should compel the 49ers to test their resolve. The season-ending ankle injury suffered by rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton could potentially complicate matters when it comes to the 49ers adding further pieces up front. But the acquisition of a player like McDonald would be a substantial boost to the edge rotation and enable the likes of Mykel Williams and Keion White to be used more frequently inside and help fill the void left by Halton’s injury. Buckner was a smart, cost-effective addition by the 49ers, but their former 2016 first-round pick should not be the final piece of the puzzle up front. There is a clear need on the edge, and McDonald is the ideal man to fill it.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 49ers News: Nothing sweeter than a Victory Monday
summary: Prayers up for all the injured players.  Brock Purdy finds a rhythm with 49ers’ unfamiliar and unproven wide receiving crew (paywall)“He did miss a few, but we scored on all those drives, too,” Shanahan said. “It was kind of awkward when he comes to the sidelines. I’m telling him what he did wrong, and then […]
full_text: Prayers up for all the injured players. Brock Purdy finds a rhythm with 49ers’ unfamiliar and unproven wide receiving crew (paywall) “He did miss a few, but we scored on all those drives, too,” Shanahan said. “It was kind of awkward when he comes to the sidelines. I’m telling him what he did wrong, and then it’s, ‘Awesome job scoring.’ He definitely missed a couple, but he made it up with plays to make back.” 49ers lose DT Gracen Halton to season-ending ankle fracture “In addition to Halton, the Niners also finished Sunday’s game without starting cornerbacks Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Renardo Green (back). Green injured his back when he landed on it during a fourth-quarter interception; Lenoir hurt his foot near the end of the game. Shanahan said the extent of those injuries is not yet clear as there will be more testing and monitoring in the next day or so. “Hoping they’re all right,” Shanahan said. “It wasn’t said that they were hurt for next week or anything, but we’re not sure when it’s a back and a foot. We’ve got to find out more tomorrow.” Kawakami: ‘We’ve got the guys to do it’ — Yes, the 49ers are in their abundance era (paywall) “Oh, of course: They saved Buckner for last — Fred Warner’s usual spot. And things got a little thunderous and, yes, emotional. “Some might say that was my idea,” George Kittle said later when asked about the drama of saving Buckner for the end. “Maybe.” You got Warner to approve the switch? “I went over Fred’s head,” Kittle said with a chuckle. Whether Kittle was being serious or not about making the call on this, the change-up was worth it — and set the tone for the 49ers’ eventual 38-17 victory and probably for the rest of this potentially very memorable season.” Fred Warner’s demolition of Raiders leaves 49ers in awe: ‘He’s playing out of his mind’ (paywall) “There was more. But Warner had to cut it short. He was on a tight deadline. He apologized — “Sorry, I’ve got to get going” — and he jogged to the locker room, where he later explained to a reporter why he’d looked a little harried. His wife, Sydney, was waiting with their 2-year-old son, Beau, and 10-month-old daughter, Bella. “I had to rush,” Warner explained, “because my wife tells me I always take too long to get to the fam.” The scene of Warner, a semi-flustered husband running behind, was proof: One of the NFL’s most instinctive defensive players can actually get out of position.” What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 38-17 win vs. Raiders “It doesn’t matter what they show you. That’s why I always joke about kicks. That’s why if I’m ever giving a lot of coaching on how to kick, I’m making stuff up. It either goes in or it doesn’t. They kick all the time. He had a good Bye Week from what he said, all the stuff he worked on. I know our special teams coaches, [special teams coordinator] Brant [Boyer], [assistant special teams coach] Colt [Anderson] and [special teams quality control coach Ronald Blair III] Ronnie gave all three of them assignments and things they needed to improve on. Those guys kept it real with us and worked at it and glad he had a real effective day today.” 9 winners, 2 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers win over the Raiders “Kirk Cousins was only pressured 31.3% of the time, which was 24th so far heading into Sunday Night Football in Week 9 among all quarterbacks. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers moved into first place on their bye last week, and this week they took control of the NFC with a convincing win. The Minnesota Vikings play Monday night and can tie the 49ers at 7-1, but San Francisco will stay in first place thanks to their strength-of-victory tiebreaker. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) Monday Night Football 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 3-3 NFC) (Wins tiebreaker over Saints based on best win percentage in division games 5. Chicago Bears (7-2, 4-2 NFC) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2, 4-1 NFC) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4) (Wins tiebreaker over Rams based on best win percentage in division games) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5, 1-3 NFC) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, wins over ATL+CAR) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) We’re a couple of weeks away from the top two teams in the NFC going head-to-head. The Vikings may not be long for the No. 2 seed, though. They host the Bills on Monday night, then travel to Lambeau Field before facing the Niners in their international matchup. The Seahawks and Rams have yet to meet. title: 9 winners, 2 losers, and 1 IDK from the 49ers win over the Raiders
summary: The San Francisco 49ers made it interesting after a wild third-quarter sequence that saw multiple turnovers in 10 minutes, but the offense was too much for the Raiders. Here are the winners and losers from the Niners’ high-scoring affair. Winners Jordan Watkins Watkins caught a 37-yard post from Brock Purdy for a touchdown. He caught […]
full_text: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers made it interesting after a wild third-quarter sequence that saw multiple turnovers in 10 minutes, but the offense was too much for the Raiders. Here are the winners and losers from the Niners’ high-scoring affair. Winners Jordan Watkins Watkins caught a 37-yard post from Brock Purdy for a touchdown. He caught all four of his targets for 86 yards. If Watkins can be reliable like he was in Week 9, it’ll make the loss of Mike Evans more tolerable if he’s out for multiple games. The Niners really don’t have that big-play threat. On Sunday, it was Watkins. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Watkins took a “huge step forward” on Sunday. Kaelon Black Black led the Niners in rushing with 70 yards. He had a couple of double-digit scampers. Black had 52 yards after contact. He was a beast on outside zone, with 40 yards on five carries. Black played fast, looked fast, and allowed the Niners to take some off the plate of Christian McCaffrey. Shanahan said, “I thought KB ran real hard today, and was real happy with him. He has been improving. Hope he keeps doing that.” Dre Greenlaw Greenlaw made a great diving play to recover Fred Warner’s forced fumble. It wasn’t an easy play, and didn’t look like he’d stay in bounds. Greenlaw led the team with eight tackles — three for loss — and had five impact plays. Greenlaw was excellent at limiting damage in coverage. He was targeted five times, gave up four receptions, but for -5 yards. Osa Odighizuwa Osa Odighizuwa had a pair of tackles for loss and quarterback hits. It was arguably his most impactful game of the season. He finished with a 17.6% pressure rate. Sumer Sports had Odighizuwa down for four impact plays, tying for second on the defense. Brock Purdy scrambling What a weapon it is when you have a quarterback who can bail you out of any situation, thanks to his legs. That was the case with Purdy on Sunday. Purdy ran for 40 yards on seven attempts. He had a couple of key first-down carries, including one for 18 yards. The 49ers ran for 190 yards, and their quarterback was a big reason why. Shanahan said, “He was effective with it,” about Purdy’s scrambling. “There were times when he missed a couple, where he probably didn’t wanna scramble. But once he starts that, you’re upset until he moves the chains or scores a touchdown, and then you get over it pretty quick. Brock has been a threat all year with his legs, and continues to do it.” Shanahan added later that Purdy made up for some of the missed throws earlier in the game with plays later in the game. Forcing turnovers Kirk Cousins threw the ball directly to Jaden Dugger for a pick-six. But he didn’t see Renardo Green in the end zone and underthrew another deep pass that fell into Malik Mustapha’s lap. If he continues this pace, the peanut punch will be named after Fred Warner. A bit of luck was involved on the fumble right at the goal line. That is the 49ers defense. Bend-but-don’t-break. They keep everything in front of you, prey on mistakes, and that’s what happened against the Raiders. Losers Everybody guarding Brock Bowers The 49ers had zero answers for Bowers, who caught seven of his eight targets for 111 yards, and had a receiving EPA of +0.72 every time the ball was in his hands. It’s one thing to give up a big play to a superstar player, but Bowers had two receptions for 50 yards on crossing routes, caught a 21-yarder on a post route, and a 20-yarder on a dig. It was big play after big play. If somebody else had beaten the Niners, that would have been respectable. But the other team’s best player got over on the defense, which is concerning. Penalties The 49ers were uncharacteristically sloppy, especially early on offense. The offense averages three penalties a game, and topped that by the second quarter. For the game, the 49ers had seven penalties for 59 yards. Vegas only benefited from those with one first down, but if you give a playoff team that many free yards, they’ll take advantage. Purdy overcame both penalties with his legs on one drive. While he’s playing at a high level, it’s not realistic to expect your quarterback to bail you out of those situations. IDKs The pass rush Kirk Cousins was only pressured 31.3% of the time, which was 24th so far heading into Sunday Night Football in Week 9 among all quarterbacks. It’s also about six percentage points below league average. Let’s add some context. When Cousins was pressured, it took 2.59 seconds, the 12th-highest mark. Cousins only threw the ball deep twice. Fifty-nine percent of his throws were short, and he averaged -1.75 air yards to the sticks. So, it’s not as if the pass rush had ample time to get after the Raiders quarterback. You’d still like to see at least one sack or more pressure, given the game script and knowing Cousins was going to drop back as often as he did. Odighizuwa had three pressures. DeForest Buckner had a couple of pressures. James Thompson and Garcen Halton had one. Nick Bosa had two, while Romello Height and Keion White had one. However, only Odgizhuwa had a double-digit pressure rate. It was Bosa’s first game back since September 20. Next week’s opponent and their passing attack will be a better gauge of the defensive line and pass rush. Cousins threw three interceptions, had only 216 passing yards, and posted a QBR of just 60.0. He didn’t play well. Winners The offensive line Trent Williams didn’t get beaten on the sack he allowed. It was a strange play. Williams and Connor Colby allowed a pair of pressures, while Colton McKivitz and Jake Brendel allowed one. The offensive line combined for 17 impact plays. Purdy was blitzed 43.3% of the time but was sacked only once and pressured 33.3% of the time. Kaelon Black averaged 1.64 yards before contact on 11 attempts. Christian McCaffrey averaged 1.0 yards before contact on his one carry, and Jordan James averaged 1.67 yards before contact on his one carry. Four carries of 10+ yards, and only three of the 43 carries were stuffed. The 49ers offensive line continues to excel. Ji’Ayir Brown Brown allowed a big play to Bowers, but he had two critical tackles in this game. The one nobody is talking about happened on the 54-yard kickoff return by the Raiders. That saved a touchdown. Las Vegas ended up kicking a 50+ yard field goal after that tackle. On Brown’s other tackle at the goal line, the Raiders didn’t score. Malik Mustapha Malik, too, allowed an explosive pass. All three safeties did. Mustapha made up for it with an interception and a pass breakup. He didn’t have to do much in the run game, but Mustapha played well in his deep quarter or third. He’ll be the X-factor on this side of the ball moving forward. I try to avoid listing the best players weekly. Take Trent Williams, for example. He held Maxx Crosby—arguably the best pass rusher in the game—to a 7.4% pressure rate. We heard from Crosby once all game. George Kittle should be on the winners list every week. He’s assumed Mike Evans’ role, judging by the workload. Purdy targeted Kittle on 37.5 of the late downs and another 25% in the red zone. Kittle had four receptions for 58 yards and set the tone early with a 37-yarder. He was arguably the 49ers’ most impactful player in Week 9. The broadcast said Warner had a quiet game, but he had a tackle for loss and a forced fumble when the Raiders were trailing by 11 and a first down away from the red zone. That was the game-changing play the defense needed. As long as the 49ers stars play like stars, they’ll be tough to beat against anyone in any stadium.

full_text: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers take on the 6-2 Chicago Bears. It’ll be one of the best defenses in the league taking on one of the top offenses. The Bears enter this game on a three-game winning streak, while the Bucs, who are somehow in first place in the NFC South, are on a two-game streak of their own. Tampa Bay has only allowed a team to score more than 26 points once since Week 1. On the flip side, it seems like whenever Caleb Williams is on the field, Chicago has a chance to score. If you can figure out how this game will go, then more power to you. It feels like it’ll be a reality check for the Bears offense after scoring 30 points in three straight games. If that’s true, even with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, Tampa Bay’s offensive line should give them enough room and movement for the running backs and Baker Mayfield to move the ball. I smell a Bucs upset.

Starting cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) both left Week 9 early. Shanahan was asked if there’s any concern at the position with both his starters suffering an injury. He said, “Hoping they’re all right. It wasn’t…said they were hurt for next week, or anything. We’re not sure when it’s a back and a foot. We’ll find out more tomorrow.” Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton broke his ankle. Shanahan confirmed that his season is over. That’s a big bummer for a player who was ascending and making splash plays every game. Halton nearly had an interception against the Raiders. Shanahan spoke about Halton’s season: Two things. He’s played at a very high-level as a rookie. He’s had an awesome seven or eight games here. We’re going to miss him a lot. Look forward to getting him back next year. I know the guys love him, too. He’s an awesome guy. The 49ers can’t seem to go a game without losing a player to a serious injury.

title: Buccaneers Week 9 Top Performers at Chicago Bears
summary: The Buccaneers steadied the ship after an early onslaught but did not receive what they needed from their offense as the Chicago Bears escaped with a narrow 27-24 victory Sunday night at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay’s defense got slugged for two quick touchdowns but impressively steeled their resolve to allow only 6 points the rest […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks to pass against Rueben Bain Jr. #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers steadied the ship after an early onslaught but did not receive what they needed from their offense as the Chicago Bears escaped with a narrow 27-24 victory Sunday night at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay’s defense got slugged for two quick touchdowns but impressively steeled their resolve to allow only 6 points the rest of the way while forcing 5 turnovers — one week after forcing 4. The unit harassed Caleb Williams and Co., who all looked like a top-3 offense in football over the better part of the last month. Unfortunately, the Buccaneers offense largely failed to capitalize on the opportunities provided to it. After the first three interceptions, the Bucs had 6 points to show for it, and while Bucky Irving carried them to a late game-tying touchdown, it just wasn’t enough to extend the contest in their favor. Baker Mayfield throwing two inexcusable interceptions, one of which being a pick-six, only further puts the onus on that side of the ball. As far as moral victories go, this contest is about as close as you will get in the NFL, but it’s still another tally in the loss column when it very well should’ve been a W. Tampa will need to shake it off during its bye week before another road trip north to face the Detroit Lions. Let’s do some shoutouts and enjoy that week off. Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving Bucky remains this team’s offensive engine, and it’s scary to think how anemic the entire operation would look without him slicing through defenses and bouncing off would-be tacklers like a yoked-up pinball. In the return to his hometown, Irving led all offensive players from either team in total yards (24 touches, 125 yards) and scored twice, taking the opportunity to showcase his talents on primetime. He’s well on pace for another 1,000+ yard season and already has 8 total touchdowns, proving an injured 2025 season was just a blip on the radar when it comes to his potential. Count the missed tackles 👀 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ntmUWIpeib — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 Kenny Gainwell contributed significantly again with 76 total yards on 8 touches, with most of that coming in the passing game. Over the last 3 weeks, Gainwell has resembled the reliable backup to Bucky the team envisioned when they signed him. Other than that, the not-so-fun part is that this passing offense is broken. Mayfield needed to throw the ball tonight after 15 total passes in the prior two weeks combined, and the results were largely poor. A huge 58-yard bomb to Tez Johnson offered some hope, but that really served as the only positive highlight as it was promptly counterbalanced by two horrific interceptions that actively dampened the Bucs’ chances. In a game where you lost by 3 points, a pick-six looms awfully large. Mayfield has 4 total touchdowns and 7 total turnovers on the year. Now it’s not all on him, as Zac Robinson looks incompetent in this area of the job and receivers keep dropping passes, but you expect more context-independent production from the guy you just gave $165 million. Defensive Top Performer: CB Jacob Parrish You could really go a number of ways with this one. Yes, Zyon McCollum got two interceptions and now has four total over the last three weeks, but I can’t ignore that he also got toasted the entire first quarter (including for a touchdown). He rebounded beautifully and he deserves credit for doing so, but that doesn’t erase the bad either. With that in mind, Parrish gets the big nod here for adding another pass deflection to extend his NFL lead — which also turned into yet another interception for Alex Anzalone, who played well again. Parrish delivered in coverage all night while also making critical tackles on Chicago’s dangerous open-field playmakers. Parrish has been such a stud anywhere he’s lined up, and he has a bright future as the Bucs’ next star cornerback. Alex Anzalone Picks Off Caleb Williams. He’s Thrown Four Interceptions Today. It Got Tipped Because Of Good Coverage And Ended Up Getting Taken Away. pic.twitter.com/Sv4QcM5fRl — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 9, 2026 The whole defense deserves so much praise for refusing to give in after a bad start and putting the team on its back — not just Sunday, but most of the year. It’s really hard to be mad at them for the end-of-game coverage flub that put the Bears in chip shot field goal range, as inexcusable as that mistake is, given how it wouldn’t have even been a close contest in the first place without them stymying an awesome Chicago attack. Tykee Smith nabbed a critical red zone interception, and Rueben Bain Jr. forced a fumble with a massive hit on Luther Burden to set the Bucs up for the late tying score. The latter also created some QB pressures as the rookie’s needle continues to point up. I maintained a first round grade on Rueben Bain Jr. during his final two college seasons. Here he is pressuring Caleb Williams. 2024 game film evaluation: https://t.co/TcEtndvtXj 2025 game film evaluation: https://t.co/ah3CKg9cNK pic.twitter.com/s4MDGrppSK — FIRST ROUND MOCK (@firstroundmock) November 9, 2026 Fellow rookie Josiah Trotter kept playing well and increased his team-leading tackle amount with an 8-stop effort, as well as adding a QB pressure as a blitzer. It’s easy to argue his immediate impact and elevation of the linebacker unit has significantly raised the entire defense’s floor. The turnover luck will likely dry up at some point, as it does for every team, but even then this is a unit Todd Bowles should be proud of. Special Teams Top Performer: P Riley Dixon You know the game flow is going your way when Riley Dixon’s performance is a net positive. Dixon loosed some critical punts to help maintain field position in the second half and allow the defense to keep its ears pinned back. Dixon placed two of his six punts inside the 20 and averaged a sturdy 48.8 yards per punt with a long of 54. In what has been another mediocre year overall for him, he chose a good night to provide his best effort of the season. Shoutouts, of course, also go out to Chase McLaughlin for all four of his chip shot kicks (3 field goals and 1 XP) to remain perfect on the year, as well as special teams maven Miles Killebrew for partially blocking a punt. Miles Killebrew blocks the punt for Tampa and the special teams come through! After a hot start to the game, the Bears have cooled off and continue to let the Bucs hang around. pic.twitter.com/XMQgTGMHZo — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) November 9, 2026 The coverage unit got bailed out by a questionable penalty on a would-be 92-yard kick return for a touchdown by Chicago’s Zavion Thomas, so that aspect needs to continue to improve, but overall a good night for a unit that’s been much-improved under the sage-like Danny Smith.

title: Week 9 Game Recap: Bucs fall despite forcing five turnovers
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took the primetime stage in week nine— Sunday Night Football on NBC. Not only would Cris Collinsworth be in the booth for the Buccaneers’ game but the team would take the field officially leading the NFC South. The first place Tampa Bay Bucs have dug themselves, with help, all the way […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker (94) sacks Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took the primetime stage in week nine— Sunday Night Football on NBC. Not only would Cris Collinsworth be in the booth for the Buccaneers’ game but the team would take the field officially leading the NFC South. The first place Tampa Bay Bucs have dug themselves, with help, all the way out of the 0-4 early season hole they dug themselves into. Week nine would be the team’s first chance to put some distance between themselves and their NFC South rivals, will Tampa Bay rise to the occasion or will they falter in the spotlight? First Quarter: Sunday night’s first drive was Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams versus Todd Bowles and his defense. Ben Johnson versus most would be a mismatch and in the game’s opening drive that looked to be the case as Tampa Bay fans had to watch Chicago coast down the field and into Tampa Bay’s end zone for ten first score of the game. Early concerns for Todd Bowles may stem, not only from the results of the drive (seven points allowed), but also from the fact that Caleb Williams consistently broke outside of the pocket without any noticeable restriction. 7-0, Bears. No glove for Baker Mayfield and no first downs either, though the Bucs’ quarterback did eclipse his completion total from a week ago on the Tampa’s opening drive the net result was a three-and-out. Chicago’s next drive started with more first downs than Bucs had earned the game thus far and finished in the end zone once again. 14-0, Chicago. The Buccaneers’ first six snaps all went to Bucky Irving before Zac Robinson remembered other players play for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers— The other player targeted? Cade Otton. Mayfield’s incomplete pass to Cade Otton set up the game’s first dose of Mayfield magic. Third and long and Baker Mayfield scrambled his way around the pocket buying time before eventually directing Kenny Gainwell downfield for a 44 yard gain. Second Quarter: The Bucs’ drive would stall out and Todd Bowles would opt for a conservative approach to surprise of the fanbase, kicking a short field goal. 14-3, Bears. Not much changed for Todd Bowles’ defense on the next Chicago drive, easy completions, no contain on the quarterback, and wide open receivers on most every play. The bleeding was finally stopped by a flagrant mistake when Chicago Bears’ rookie Zavion Thomas got frustrated and punched Jacob Parrish, pushed the Bears’ offense back 15 yards backwards. The ensuing play, Tykee Smith ruined the Caleb Williams showcase with a beautiful read undercutting a Williams throw to the end zone for for an interception. Converting turnovers into points are a necessity, however, Tampa converted the turnover into an awkward QB sneak for a failed fourth down conversion. Taking possession back in field goal range, Williams did it again— Rather Tampa’s defense did it again. Zyon McCollum followed Tykee Smith’s interception with one of his own. The Bucs’ offense was still struggling to offense so naturally a punt would follow. After the Bucs wasted each of their defense’s forced turnovers, Chicago knocked through a field goal— 17-3, Bears. Baker Mayfield and the Bucs’ offense got themselves back across a first down marker for the first time in quite while as Emeka Egbuka scooped a low pass over the middle, ticking the first half down to the two-minute warning. The first downs came in bunches (by the Bucs’ standards, multiple in one drive), but Tampa’s drive, momentum, and chances at scoring were swept away by an untimely Baker Mayfield interception. Right as Bucs’ fans were no doubt bracing for the worst, the flood gates did in fact not open. Zyon McCollum, who deserves praise for being the shiny example of how much development a player is capable of went low for a diving interception and hauled in his second Caleb Williams pass of the night. Back on offense with new life, Tampa Bay began with Emeka Egbuka for a huge catch and run, they found Bucky Irving and Cade Otton underneath to get themselves within striking distance. Another Chase McLaughlin field and another three points for the Buccaneers. 17-6, Chicago. Third Quarter: Zac Robinson went deep into his bag to start the second half. The Buccaneers started with two straight Bucky Irving runs, but after a chain-moving third down reception from Chris Godwin, Robinson dialed up a rare play action deep shot. Baker Mayfield dropped back and arched a beautiful pass into the striding arms of Tez Johnson all the way to the Bears’ two yard line. Two plays later, Bucky Irving would go on to score a touchdown in his homecoming— 17-13, Chicago. Amidst a lull, the game’s third consecutive punt created a highlight when special teams ace Miles Killebrew broke through the line of scrimmage and blocked Tory Taylor’s punt setting the Buccaneers’ offense near midfield. He also would indirectly set the Bucs’ offense up for another punt— Four consecutive. Bears’ offense had the ball back but that just meant they could give it away again— interception, Alex Anzalone. The short lived burst of enthusiasm from Tampa’s defense would be given a quick dagger and shut down by the Bears second interception of Baker Mayfield, a pick six, and a two-score lead for the Bears. 24-13, Chicago. Fourth Quarter: Tampa began the fourth quarter with Second down and Bucky Irving. Irving. Despite a slower day by recent standards, Irving took off to start the fourth quarter scampering past, under, and around Chicago defenders for 25 yards. Irving’s jolt burst Tampa into field goal and Todd Bowles, after a small bit of indecision, opted for a kick— 24-16, Bears. The next time Baker Mayfield and the Bucs’ offense would see the ball would be with 8:03 left on the clock and the ball on their own 15-yard line. Tampa would it make slightly passed their 30, before needing a punt and handing hope back over to Todd Bowles and their defense. 4:27 on the clock— Do or die for Tampa’s defense and they did. Rueben Bain Jr. hustling over to help make a tackle forced the ball which was recovered by Ifeatu Melifonwu. Inside the 20, needing eight to stay alive, the Bucs’ offense turned to Bucky Irving and Bucky Irving turned carries into points, crossing the goal line for the second time in the game. Two point conversion— Successful on a Baker Mayfield scramble. 24-24, All tied up. The Tampa Bay Buccaneer and Todd Bowles have had an outstanding defense though the last few games. Aside from Sunday night’s opening quarter, they had one again today. The group let up just three points between the first quarter and the final drive of the game, harassed Caleb Williams, and forced five turnovers. If there is one knock that Todd Bowles’ defense has had and continues to have it would be failing to close out close games. Bowles’ defense was lights out for nearly 75 percent of the game, but when the team needed them to pull out a stop they blew a coverage, left a player completely wide-open, and lost the game with ease on a short Cairo Santos field goal. 27-24, Chicago Bears.

title: Titans, Cam Ward’s Week 10 challenge gets more complicated
summary: The Tennessee Titans were on the Week 9 bye. Everyone is excited to watch Cam Ward play football again after his Week 8 breakout versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Week 10 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars will be difficult and is now more complicated following their trade for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III. Ward […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Cam Ward #1of the Tennessee Titans against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans were on the Week 9 bye. Everyone is excited to watch Cam Ward play football again after his Week 8 breakout versus the Cincinnati Bengals. The Week 10 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars will be difficult and is now more complicated following their trade for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III . Ward was excellent against the Bengals . The sophomore No. 1 overall selection was accurate, decisive, and aggressive with ideal ball placement. Ward threw for 300+ yards for the first time in his career, and also had two touchdown passes (to Chimere Dike and Wan’Dale Robinson) for the first time this season. Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/zsvYXRXj0P — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 9, 2026 Ward completed 26/40 attempts for 304 yards, the aforementioned two TDs, and zero interceptions (and a lost fumble). Here’s another fact we hadn’t seen mentioned. In addition to Ward enjoying his first-ever 300-yard throwing performance, his 26 completions tied his second-most in a single game (he was 28/42 versus the Seattle Seahawks last season). The 65% completion percentage versus the Bengals tied his previous season-high (vs. the Eagles) from earlier this year. Ward is now tasked with building on that performance versus the Jaguars. This Anthony Campanile-coached unit is playing elite football. The Jaguars rank second in points per game allowed (15.1) and fifth in rushing (89.3). If there’s an area they’ve struggled, it’s against the pass, where they rank 22nd in yards allowed (229/game). Hence the trade for Bates. The three-time Pro Bowl safety is among the most consistent ballhawks in the league. Bates has one interception this year, bringing his career total to 28 INTs. He ranks third among active NFL defenders in interceptions, behind just Harrison Smith and Titans legend Kevin Byard. Bates has two career interceptions versus the Titans, including one in the painful 2021 postseason defeat. He’ll now play against the Titans twice in the coming weeks following his trade to Jacksonville from the Atlanta Falcons. Ward will have to navigate this challenge while attempting to continue improving.

full_text: The Washington Commanders lost another game on Sunday, this one a 20-13 result against the Los Angeles Rams. Their record sits at 2-5-1 , putting their season on the brink if it isn’t over already. The 24-hour rule doesn’t even apply here despite extreme frustration with Washington’s inability to get out of it’s own way. Why? A defining matchup with the New York Giants is on the immediate horizon, scheduled for primetime on Thursday night football . While Quinn preached the fact that the Commanders must move on quickly, the Commanders head coach also addressed some missteps against the Rams in his Monday virtual press conference. Quinn backed offensive coordinator David Blough , whose play calling has taken sharp criticism from the fan base. He discussed the need for more consistent execution but also said there’s a need for better at the end of games. Quinn also outlined his communication routines with owner Josh Harris, the need for improvement in the. run game and why Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett got loose and wrecked Sunday’s game. Here’s the Quinn press conference in its entirety, plus some highlights from the virtual session: Dan Quinn Changes coming? title: Commanders Vs. Rams – Studs and Duds
summary: The Rams came to the nation’s capital with one plan in mind. Get Puka Nacua the ball. Washington had one job to do. Limit Puka’s impact in the game. THEY FAILED! Daronte Jones let a 38-year-old quarterback sit back in a relatively clean pocket and pick them apart by going to ONE MAN! This loss, […]
full_text: The Rams came to the nation’s capital with one plan in mind. Get Puka Nacua the ball. Washington had one job to do. Limit Puka’s impact in the game. THEY FAILED! Daronte Jones let a 38-year-old quarterback sit back in a relatively clean pocket and pick them apart by going to ONE MAN! This loss, coupled with a Giants win over the Eagles , all but seals Washington’s fate for the 2026 campaign. There should be NO trading for players at the deadline. The only thing that should come of this loss is SWEEPING CHANGES to both the staff and starting lineup! Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: WR Van Jefferson: After being signed from the practice squad out of necessity, Jefferson made the most of his opportunities by hauling in five receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown . He showed good hands and solid run-after-catch ability. Huge grab by Jefferson pic.twitter.com/vKttsK2rUp — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Nice job getting upfield to the the first down by Jefferson pic.twitter.com/9MnjSFpqIy — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Jayden with the STRIKE to Jefferson for the TD pic.twitter.com/isY3rRdOVz — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 LBs Frankie Luvu/Sonny Styles: The linebacker duo combined for 28 total tackles, a sack (Luvu), three tackles for a loss, two quarterback hits and four pressures. Styles had a nice pass defended that the refs INCORRECTLY called him for pass interference on. Styles with the TFL! pic.twitter.com/lKd3XS1bMX — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Luvu gets the sack on Stafford! pic.twitter.com/kjF1m2GKm3 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Horrible PI call against Styles. Higbee RAN INTO HIM😡 pic.twitter.com/ZP3JtA2V8F — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 S Nick Cross: Cross was all over the field making plays. He had eight total tackles (six solo), one tackle for a loss, three passes defended, a fumble recovery and a nice interception. When he’s been on the field, he’s been as advertised. Beautiful INT by Nick Cross! pic.twitter.com/TZRT8zJ2Ps — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 DQ challenged this play. He got it right. No catch pic.twitter.com/BKRui9K2cF — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Duds: Second-Half David Blough: I thought we were seeing some real growth from first-year offensive coordinator David Blough — and then the second half occurred. The Commanders offense was almost unwatchable, and Blough is the one who gets the blame. We saw more pre-snap penalties, limited help for his struggling offensive tackles and hardly any downfield shots. And it’s worth mentioning that two of the Rams top corners were not playing. That was a HORRIBLY called second half of offensive football by David Blough – in a must-win football game for the Commanders. Just inexcusably bad! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 This is what Blough dialed up for the last play of the game… pic.twitter.com/yNaOUHERMd — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 LT Brandon Coleman: I HAVE SEEN ENOUGH!!!!! Brandon Coleman has become unplayable. This “staff” benched Mike Sainristil for poor play. Now it’s time to do the same to Brandon Coleman. Esa Pole can’t be any worse… Brandon Coleman is almost unplayable at this point. pic.twitter.com/SOAtIBtbfL — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 2nd False Start of the game on Coleman – presnap penalties continue to haunt Washington pic.twitter.com/zFGqEw9KLi — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Horrible blocking by Brandon Coleman at LT. Luckily, Daniels is able to escape pic.twitter.com/dxF24loKlh — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 Another week, another FS by Brandon Coleman😡 pic.twitter.com/z5TcpHdo13 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 EDGE Odafe Oweh: For how much the Commanders are paying this guy to make an impact on our defense, he did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING against the Rams front. This may go down as yet another Adam Peters blunder. Daronte Jones: You knew the Rams had one player on offense who could hurt Washington, and Jones’ defense let him eat all game, to the tune of 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown. He also had two carries for 20 yards. So, ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY YARDS AND A SCORE!!! He’s good, I get it, but Jones’ defense literally let one may beat us. ONE MAN! Daronte Jones has absolutely NO ANSWER for Puka Nacua. This is embarrassing to watch — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 4th and 3 – Amos gives up WAY too much cushion pic.twitter.com/sUZbpO4RHx — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 CB Trey Amos: After an exceptional game against the Eagles last week, Amos came back down to reality. He was matched up often on Puka Nacua and he couldn’t stop the All-Pro receiver. I do pin a LOT of the blame on Daronte Jones, but guys need to step up and perform. Amos did not. The fourth-and-3 where Amos gave Nacua a 10-yard cushion was inexcusable! Puka Nacua comes down with the TD over Trey Amos, #Commanders now trail, 20-13 pic.twitter.com/LTMz41NJZi — Commanders Roundtable (@WSHRoundtable) November 8, 2026 GM Adam Peters: Hey Adam – You told fans and media all summer we were good at Center… Now, we get word that Nick Allegretti is no longer even playing center!!! I look around the NFL at all these young quarterbacks and the structure they have been given early in their careers; and then I look at Jayden Daniels. Notes: This was another game where QB Jayden Daniels didn’t look particularly sharp, but I’m going to absolve him of some of the blame due to complete incompetence by Brandon Coleman, poor play calling by David Blough in the second half, some untimely drops and being without many of his top receiving targets. He’s still misfiring on some throws and not connecting on ones where he has guys pretty open (Van Jefferson in the fourth quarter), and it’s fair to question some of his decisions. He did have his first turnover of the year — a fumble caused by Myles Garrett — on a poor blocking attempt. Count me unimpressed with all the check downs and his 274 passing yards. Quinn said the #Commanders ' final play had a check. The first read is to throw it to the end zone, but the second one is to throw it short if the defense sends an all-out blitz. The Rams showed that look presnap, which must be why Daniels went to Okonkwo, but they only sent 5. https://t.co/U5iRnJWqJ8 — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) November 8, 2026 Garrett causes Jayden to fumble. Rams recover pic.twitter.com/rLOpa1AxP4 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 8, 2026 TE Chig Okonkwo caught six of his seven targets for 57 yards and showed he’s not afraid to make tough catches in traffic. Commanders links Articles The Athletic Commanders’ mystifying final drive symbolic of an offense that keeps misfiring The Washington Commanders still had one more shot with eight seconds left, and if there was ever a team that desperately needed to show it could finally get things right with the game on the line in the final seconds, it was this one. Down by a touchdown with the ball at the Los Angeles Rams’ 31-yard line, Washington had time for at least one play, maybe two if necessary, to get the ball in the end zone. And somehow — somehow — the ball was not thrown there. Not once. Not on the Commanders’ first attempt, when Jayden Daniels’ deep pass over the middle sailed far over the head of receiver Stefon Diggs, and not on the second, when Daniels dumped the ball off on a crosser to tight end Chig Okonkwo, who broke a couple of tackles before the play sputtered. Okonkwo ran up against the sideline to about the Rams’ 11 and tried to pitch the ball backward to keep the play alive but instead tossed it onto the ground, at which point the play fizzled, along with one of Washington’s last hopes of keeping its season intact. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic The Commanders had a sixth-round rookie blocking Myles Garrett. How did we get here? Nick Allegretti remained on the sideline. He did not play a snap. In the past five games, the player the Commanders said for six months they were counting on to be their starting center has played a total of two snaps. “We went with how we’ve been practicing,” coach Dan Quinn said. And that’s with Matt Gulbin, that sixth-round rookie, backing up Lucas Patrick — the center the Commanders signed off the street in September — at center, and Allegretti backing up Chris Paul at left guard. Look, the Commanders didn’t lose to the Rams 20-13 solely because Patrick got dinged up and Gulbin had to replace him, tasked with trying to help block Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald when he hadn’t played in more than a month and had essentially just one game of experience in his NFL career. “It’s an excuse,” Gulbin said afterward. “I got to go out and do the expectations for the center position.
